## XI. He commands Alviso, bishop of Arras, to decide concerning the marriage of Baldwin of Rispens and Matilda of Albiniac.  
*(22 April 1145.)*

[D. BOUQUET, *Recueil*, XV, 426.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to our venerable brother ALVISO, bishop of Arras, greeting and apostolic blessing.

You have informed us both by letter and orally that certain of your parishioners, namely Baldwin of Rispens and Matilda of Albiniac, rashly attempted to contract marriage contrary to [Col. 1026B] your prohibition. When they had been summoned before your presence to administer justice in the matter, the husband’s party appeared before you under arms; and, before entering into the case, it demanded that the woman whom he had married contrary to the bishop’s prohibition be reinstated to him. Since the other party perceived that it was being wronged in these matters, it appealed to the Apostolic See and, at the appointed term—namely Laetare Jerusalem—sent its representative to our presence. The husband’s party neither appeared nor offered an excuse.

Since no one ought to gain advantage from absence, we command you by apostolic letters, with the case remaining in the same state, to summon both parties before you and, without any reinstatement, to hear the matter carefully on both sides and decide it canonically, setting aside the appeal. If, according to judicial procedure, that separation is confirmed, you shall cause what was given to the man as that woman’s dowry to be restored in full, as justice requires. But if either party contumaciously absents itself, you shall administer canonical justice concerning them. [Col. 1026C]

Given at Viterbo, on the tenth day before the Kalends of May [22 April].

## XII. Grant of privileges to the monastery of Saint Saviour in the diocese of Pavia, of the Cassinese order; it is declared subject to the Holy Roman Church alone.  
*(24 April 1145.)*

[MARGARINI, *Bullar. Casin.*, II, 162.]

[Col. 1026D]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son in Christ OBERTO, abbot of the monastery of Saint Saviour situated near Pavia, and to his successors canonically appointed, for ever.

God has entrusted us with the care of the pastoral office so that we ought, with fatherly concern, to provide for the peace and welfare of all churches and, lest they be harassed by the troubles of wicked men, fortify them by the authority of our See. Therefore, beloved son in Christ, Abbot Oberto, granting assent to your reasonable petitions, we receive under the guardianship of blessed Peter and the protection of the Apostolic See, and fortify by the privilege of this present writing, the monastery of the Lord Saviour over which, by God’s ordering, you preside, following the example of our predecessors of blessed memory, John, Benedict, Paschal, Callixtus, Honorius, Innocent, and Lucius, Roman pontiffs. [Col. 1027A]

We have learned that this monastery was restored by the most gracious piety of the Empress Adelaide Augusta and enriched through her liberality with very ample possessions. We therefore decree that whatever possessions or goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, God permitting, acquire through the grants of pontiffs, the benefactions of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought it proper expressly to specify:

The castle of Monticelli, with two chapels and all its appurtenances; the estate of Olona, with the chapel of Saint Anastasius and all its appurtenances; the estate of Baseregutia, with a baptismal church built in honour of Saint Mary and one chapel, with all its appurtenances; the estate of Frixinatia, with one chapel and all its appurtenances; the estate of Melaria, with the parish church of Saint Michael, the church of Saint Stephen, and Saint Martin, with all their appurtenances; half of the estate of Herbaria and the parish church of Saint Faustinus, with all that belongs to those halves and to the parish church; [Col. 1027B] the orchard situated within the gate of Saint John and near the Palatine gate, with two chapels—one built in honour of Saint Lawrence, [Col. 1027C] the other in honour of Saint Mary; the estate of Garlasco, with one chapel of Saint Mary, with jurisdiction and district extending two miles in every direction; at Marengo, a church built in honour of Saint Martin and a chapel built in honour of Saint Mary, with all that belongs to them; the cell of Saint Honorata, with all its appurtenances; half of the estate of Coriana, with one chapel and all its appurtenances; and the estate of Armentaria, with one chapel and all its appurtenances.

Upon your death, as the present abbot of the same monastery, no one shall presume to elect an abbot there through any craft of deception, except the person whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of their counsel, shall provide to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict. [Col. 1027D] The person elected, moreover, shall be consecrated by the Roman pontiff.

You may receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or churches, and the ordinations of your monks or canons who are to be promoted to sacred orders, from whatever bishop you prefer, provided he is Catholic and enjoys the favour of the Holy Apostolic See. Moreover, by apostolic authority we grant the right of baptism in the churches belonging to the same monastery—namely, the church of Saint Martin of Marengo, the church of Saint Anastasius of Olona, and the church of Saint Saviour of Monticelli—and in the other churches belonging to that monastery in which it is known to have been celebrated up to this time.

[Col. 1028A] No cleric or layman shall presume to demand from you tithes of the labour which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or of the sustenance of your animals. We also grant, by the liberality of the Apostolic See, the use of buskins, sandals, gloves, and the mitre, as this is known to have been granted to you and your successors through the authentic privileges of our predecessors. Furthermore, adding this present clause, we decree that the aforesaid monastery shall remain under the jurisdiction of no church, but shall be subject solely to the Holy Apostolic See.

We therefore decree that no bishop or any person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; [Col. 1028B] but that all shall be preserved whole for the complete benefit of those for whose governance and maintenance they were granted, saving in all things the authority of the Apostolic See. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to make amendment by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let him be subject at the last judgment to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, [Col. 1028C] so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.  
I, Theodewinus, bishop of Santa Rufina, have subscribed.  
I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed.  
I, Peter, bishop of Albano, have subscribed.  
I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Callixtus, have subscribed.  
I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Chrysogonus, have subscribed.  
I, Ubald, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed.  
I, Villanus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill, have subscribed.  
[Col. 1028D] I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed.  
I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed.  
I, Guido, cardinal deacon of the title of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed.  
I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in Carcere Tulliano, have subscribed.  
I, John, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary Nova, have subscribed.

Given at Viterbo, through the hand of Robert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the eighth day before the Kalends of May [24 April], in the eighth indiction, in the year 1145 of the Incarnation of the Lord, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

## XIII. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Peter at Perugia.  
*(25 April 1145.)*

[MARGARINI, *Bullar. Casin.*, II, 164.]

[Col. 1029A]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons BERNARD, abbot of the monastery of Saint Peter situated near the city of Perugia, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, for ever.

A desire shown to pertain to the purpose of religion and the salvation of souls is fittingly granted by us with a willing mind, and the desires of those who ask are to receive suitable support. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions; and, following in the footsteps of our predecessors, we fortify by the privilege of the Apostolic See the aforesaid monastery in which you are devoted to the service of God. We decree that whatever possessions or goods the same place now justly and lawfully possesses, or may hereafter, God permitting, acquire through grants of pontiffs, benefactions of princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors, in churches, cells, estates, parish churches, monasteries, lands, and farmsteads alike.

[Col. 1029B] Among these we have thought it proper to specify by name: the parish churches of Saint Constantius, Saint Rufinus, Saint Martin, and Saint John; the parish church of Saint Martyrius; the church of Saint Benedict at Agellione, with its appurtenances; [Col. 1029C] the church of Saint Justin, with its estate; the churches of Saint Andrew and Saint Angelo of Aliano, with their appurtenances; the church of Saint Mary at Petiniano and the church of Saint Clement; the estate of Casale; the estate of Petroniano; and what belongs to you from the estate and church of Saint Donatus in Civitella. Likewise, the land of Hugh, nephew of Berno of Monte Nigro.

By the protection of the Apostolic See we also confirm to you the churches of Saints Apollinaris, Blasius, and Montanus, with their appurtenances, saving the annual rent owed to the church of Farfa. We further confirm three estates in the county of Perugia: one called Pusulo, another Filontio, and the other Casalina, with churches, houses, vineyards, fields, gardens, cultivated and uncultivated mountains, and all their appurtenances; the monastery of Saint Angelo in the county of Assisi, in the place called Limisano, with its cells, chapels, and all that belongs to it; the church of Saint Michael the Archangel, situated near Perugia; the monastery of Saint Saviour at Potale; the monastery of Saint Peter at Poliano, with all their appurtenances; [Col. 1029D] the church of Saint Sylvester at Murcelle; the church of Saint Donatus; the right which you possess in the little field; the church of Saint Mary at Poggio, with its appurtenances; the church of Saint Paul at Monticello; the church of Saint Peter of Petroniano, with its estate; and also the hospital situated before the gate of Saint Peter, as it was restored to you by our predecessor of blessed memory, Pope Lucius [Col. 1030A]—saving the right of the Holy Sepulchre; the castle called Fracta of the sons of Azo.

You shall receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or churches, the ordinations of monks who are to be promoted to sacred orders, and of clerics belonging to the same monastery, from the diocesan bishop, provided he is Catholic and is willing to furnish these freely and without improper exaction. Otherwise, you may approach whatever Catholic bishop you prefer, who, supported by our authority, shall grant what you request.

Upon your death, the present abbot of the same place, or the death of any of your successors, no one shall be set over it through any craft of deception or violence, except the person whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of their counsel, shall elect according to the fear of God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict, to be consecrated by the Roman pontiff.

We absolutely forbid public Masses in the same monastery to be celebrated by a bishop, or stations or any ordinations to be held, without the will of the abbot and brethren, lest any occasion for popular gatherings be afforded in the retreats of the servants of God. Nor shall any bishop, except with the consent of the Roman pontiff, have power to burden, interdict, or excommunicate that monastery or its cells, or to impose new exactions. Nor may any secular magnate extort fodrum or any other service from the same monastery or its appurtenances, saving nevertheless the right and lordship of the Holy Roman Church. [Col. 1030B]

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may [Col. 1030C] rashly disturb the same church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, claim for personal use things unjustly given, or harass it with reckless vexations; but that all shall be preserved whole for the complete benefit of those for whose governance and maintenance they were granted. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to make amendment by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; [Col. 1030D] and let him be subject at the last judgment to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.  
I, Theodewinus, bishop of Santa Rufina, have subscribed.  
I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed.  
I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Callixtus, have subscribed.  
I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Lawrence and Damasus, have subscribed.  
I, Nicholas, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cyriacus, have subscribed.  
I, Manfred, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Sabina, have subscribed.  
I, Julius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus, have subscribed.  
[Col. 1031A] I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of the title of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed.

Given at Viterbo, through the hand of Robert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the seventh day before the Kalends of May [25 April], in the eighth indiction, in the year 1145 of the Incarnation of the Lord, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

## XIV. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Bertin at Sithiu.  
*(25 April 1145.)*

[Collect. des Cart., III, 320.]

[Col. 1031B] EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son LEO, abbot of Saint Bertin, and to his successors, etc., as above in the privilege of Pope Celestine.

[Note: [Col. 1031D] See under Pope CELESTINE, no. 30, *Patrologia*, vol. CLXXIX.]

Likewise, in the parish of Thérouanne, the village of Vinserna, with its lands and wastelands, extending to the boundaries of Edekin and Longuenesse; the church of Osclara; the church of Vuarnestun; the church of Saint Mary called Eggafrid’s Chapel; the church of Haveskerke; and the tithe of Saint Martin; the tithe of Saint Michael; the tithe of Longanessa; the tithe of Edekin; the tithe of Tilleke; etc. Again, as above in the said privilege of Pope Celestine.

What was reasonably determined by our venerable brother Milo, bishop of Thérouanne, concerning the chapel and cemetery of the lepers of Broburg, and confirmed by his written instrument, we confirm and judge to remain valid: namely, that in the said chapel the divine office shall be celebrated only for lepers and those serving them; that no one except a leper shall be buried in the cemetery; and that no one except a leper shall be received there for conversion. [Col. 1031C]

Likewise, in the diocese of Arras, the altar of Barlin, which our venerable brother Alviso, bishop of Arras, granted you; in the bishopric of Noyon, the altar of Runbeka, free of the rights of a personal benefice, saving episcopal rights. Stations, etc. To the end, as above in the privilege of Innocent.

[Note: [Col. 1032D] See among the letters of Innocent II, *Patrologia*, vol. CLXXIX, no. 398.]

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.

[Col. 1031D] Given at Viterbo, through the hand of Robert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the seventh day before the Kalends of May [25 April], in the eighth indiction, in the year 1145 of the Incarnation of the Lord, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

Signed with a circle.

Around its circumference is written: **“Make for me, O Lord, a sign for good”;** and in the middle of the said circle: **“Saint Peter. Saint Paul. Pope Eugenius III.”**

## XV–XVI. He confirms the exchange between the monastery of Saint Bertin at Sithiu and Thierry, count of Flanders, from Henchin to Berquaria; and the privilege of the same monastery concerning the election at Alchias.  
*(April 1145.)*

[Iperius, *Chronicle of Saint Bertin*, in MARTÈNE, *Thesaurus*, III, 640.]

[Col. 1032A]

Lord Abbot Leo went to Rome for the third time and obtained from Pope Eugenius a renewed confirmation of the aforesaid judgment and privileges. In it the pope confirms for us many matters by name: our election; the election at Alchias; the appointment of priests in our parish churches; and the prohibition against a bishop’s holding a station in this monastery; etc. [Col. 1032B] It begins thus: “EUGENIUS, etc. Of justice and exemption, etc.” Given in the year of the Lord 1145.

Likewise, another privilege confirming the exchange between us and Thierry, count of Flanders, from Henchin to Berquaria; it begins thus: “EUGENIUS, etc. Of the Apostolic See, etc.” Given as above.

Likewise, another concerning the election at Alchias, which begins: “EUGENIUS, etc. Of the Apostolic See, etc.” Given as above.

## XVII. He receives the monastery of Saint George at Prague under the protection of the Apostolic See and confirms its possessions.  
*(28 April 1145.)*

[BOCZEK, *Codex diplomaticus Moraviae*, I, p. 233.]

[Col. 1032C] EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ, BERTA, abbess of Saint George, and her sisters, present and future, professing the regular life, for ever.

It is fitting to grant ready assent to religious desires, so that faithful devotion may swiftly obtain its effect. Therefore, beloved daughters in the Lord, because through our venerable brother Henry, bishop of Moravia, a religious and honorable man, we have learned of your religious life and upright conduct, we receive his petitions for you with paternal kindness. We take under the protection of blessed Peter [Col. 1032D] and of ourselves the church of Blessed George, situated in the city of Prague, in which, having put aside secular entanglements and the allurements of the world out of desire for the heavenly kingdom, you live enclosed and devote yourselves to divine service; and we fortify it by the privilege of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions and goods you now justly and canonically possess through the gift or grant of the noble man Vladislaus, duke of the Bohemians, or may hereafter, God favoring you, acquire by grant of pontiffs, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid Church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, [Col. 1033A] diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved intact and shall be wholly beneficial for the use of you and of others for whose governance and support they were granted, without prejudice to the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the bishop of Prague. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our grant, should rashly attempt to act against it and disturb your enclosure or peace, then, having been warned a second or third time, if he does not make amendment by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself to be guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ; and at the final judgment let him be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve what is right for that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

*(Seal.)* I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.

I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Theodewinus, bishop of Santa Rufina, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Calixtus, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Gregory, have subscribed. I, Thomas, cardinal priest of the title of Vestina, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. [Col. 1033C] I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Octavianus, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed. Given at Viterbo through the hand of Robert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the fourth day before the Kalends of May, in the eighth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1145, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

## XVIII. To Bartholomew, Bishop of Laon, and U[rsio], Abbot of Saint-Denis of Reims.  
*(1145, April 29.)*

[D. Bouquet, *Recueil*, XV, 427.]

[Col. 1033D]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother BARTHOLOMEW, bishop of Laon, and his beloved son U., abbot of Saint-Denis of Reims: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is not unknown to your brotherhood that, just as our Redeemer is peace and truth, so he instructed that peace and truth be loved. It is therefore evident that the person who is ready to confess the truth—which is God—is loved by God. Accordingly, so that a proper end may be imposed upon the dispute long carried on between Alvisus, bishop of Arras, and G., abbot of Saint Nicholas, we command and strictly enjoin you by apostolic letters, under virtue of obedience, fully to declare in the presence of our venerable brethren Joscelin, bishop of Soissons, and Milo, bishop of Thérouanne, the truth which you know concerning the matter itself.

Given at Viterbo, on the third day before the Kalends of May.

## XIX. To Louis, King of the Franks: He replies that he received the king’s letters “with due kindness” and complied with his wish.  
*(1145, April 29.)*

[D. Bouquet, *Recueil*, XV, 427.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his most dear son in Christ, LOUIS, illustrious king of the Franks: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We received with due kindness your noble letters through our venerable brother Alvisus, bishop of Arras, a religious and honorable man, and willingly granted your requests concerning him. Moreover, we rejoice with paternal affection over what we have learned from him and from other religious men concerning the good beginnings of your youth; and we pray the Lord that perseverance in this good beginning may be granted you from above by the Father of lights, from whom all good things proceed. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, hold our aforesaid brother dearer than dear for reverence toward blessed Peter and ourselves; and, as befits royal excellence, show honor and reverence to the Church and to ecclesiastical [Col. 1034C] persons of the kingdom committed to you by the Lord. In the matter which he will communicate to you more privately on our behalf, hear him as though I myself were present, and carry it out in deed.

Given at Viterbo, on the third day before the Kalends of May.

## XX. He confirms for the monastery of Scheyern in Bavaria donations made by German nobles, bishops, and others.  
*(1145, April 30.)*

[Cocquelines, II, 287.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ULRIC, abbot of the monastery of Saint Mary of Scheyern, situated in the diocese of Freising, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

It is fitting to grant ready assent to religious desires, so that faithful devotion may swiftly obtain its effect. For this reason, beloved sons in the Lord, following the footsteps of our predecessors of happy memory, Paschal and Calixtus, Roman pontiffs, we graciously assent to your just requests. We take under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the church of the blessed Mother of God and ever-virgin Mary, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the page of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions and goods you now justly and canonically possess, [Col. 1035A] or may hereafter acquire by grant of pontiffs, generosity of kings, liberality of princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors.

We confirm to you in perpetuity, by the page of this present document, the places of Vispach and Usinhoven, in which you formerly lived, as they were confirmed by our aforesaid predecessors; likewise, whatever has been granted to you by bishops in parishes and tithes; and whatever Otto, Count Palatine, founder of the same place, with the consent of the noblewoman Countess Petrissa and of five other counts; whatever Haziga, with her sons Counts Eckard, Bernhard, and Otto; likewise Count Paichtold of illustrious memory, Count Conrad and his brother Otto, Bernhard, Ekkenaudus, and other faithful Christians are known to have offered from their own right to your community for the salvation of their souls.

You shall receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars and churches, and the ordination of monks to be advanced to holy orders, from the diocesan bishop, if he is willing to furnish them without misconduct; otherwise, you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer and receive from him the sacraments of consecration, provided that, supported by the authority of the Apostolic See, he grants what is requested. Upon the death of you, the present abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be set over it through any craft of deception or violence, except the person whom the brethren, by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren, shall determine ought to be elected, whether from their own community or, if necessary, from another, according to the fear of God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict. [Col. 1035C]

Moreover, we decree that the burial place of your house shall be entirely free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and final wish of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated. We grant you the right, according to your judgment and that of other religious persons and men of sound counsel, to choose whom you consider best as advocate, who, having regard to the fear and love of God, shall kindly provide for your interests in accordance with your will. If he proves burdensome to you, you may, by our authority, appoint another suitable person. Neither he nor anyone else, however, may claim the advocacy of your house as though hereditary, or hold it against your wishes. As a token of the protection received from the Apostolic See, you shall pay yearly to us and our successors one gold bezant.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid Church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved intact, wholly beneficial for the use of those for whose support and governance they were granted, without prejudice to the authority of the Apostolic See. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, having been warned a second or third time, if he does not amend by suitable [Col. 1036A] satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself to be guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and at the final judgment let him be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that Church may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Given at Viterbo through the hand of Robert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the second day before the Kalends of May, in the eighth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1145, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

## XXI. To R[otrou], Bishop of Évreux—That he grant to the nuns of Fontevraud a church given them by the abbot of Conques.  
*(1145, May 8.)*

[Pavillon, *Vie de Robert d’Arbrissel*, Proofs, p. 630.]

[Col. 1036B]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother R[OTROU], bishop of Évreux: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We do not believe that it is unknown to your brotherhood how the religious sisters of Fontevraud, having put aside temporal things, serve the Lord in a spirit of humility and contrition. Therefore it is fitting that all the faithful of God, and especially prelates of Churches, aid their weakness and poverty and mercifully grant them their desired consolation. Accordingly, by apostolic letters we request and command your brotherhood to grant them, for the love of God and out of reverence for blessed Peter and ourselves, the church which the abbot of Conques gave them. [Col. 1036C]

Given at Viterbo, on the eighth day before the Ides of May.

## XXII. To John, Archbishop of Braga—That he recognize the primacy of Toledo.  
*(1145, May 9.)*

[Mansi, *Concilia*, XXI, 671.]

Our predecessor Pope Lucius, of happy memory, commanded you orally to render due obedience to our venerable brother R., archbishop of Toledo, as to your primate; or, if you had any warrants or privileges against this, to present them, together with the documents, before our apostolic presence at the past Easter, and to answer the envoys of the same archbishop concerning his right. But you, as though distrustful of your cause, neither came nor advanced any reasonable excuse. Therefore, since, placed in the seat of justice, it is our duty to preserve intact the rights of every Church and ecclesiastical person, we command and strictly enjoin you by apostolic letters to render canonical obedience and due reverence to that archbishop as to your primate. If you disdain to fulfill this within three months after receipt of these letters, know that from that time you are suspended from episcopal office.

Given at Viterbo, on the seventh day before the Ides of May.

## XXIII. Privilege for the nunnery of Fontevraud.  
*(1145, May 9.)*

[Pavillon, *Vie de Robert d’Arbrissel*, Proofs, p. 630.]

[Col. 1037A]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ, P[ETRONILLA], abbess of Fontevraud, and her sisters, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

Since neither the unity of charity can subsist without the worship of true religion, nor service pleasing to God be rendered, it is fitting for apostolic authority to cherish religious persons and fortify their houses with pious protection. Therefore, beloved daughters in Christ, we graciously assent to your just petitions and fortify the aforesaid house of Fontevraud, in which you are dedicated to divine service, by the privilege of blessed Peter. We decree that whatever possessions and goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may hereafter, God favoring you, acquire by grant of pontiffs, liberality of kings, generosity of princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to state expressly: the place itself of Fontevraud, which is the head of the others, etc.

We prohibit any brother or sister, after making profession in your houses, from daring to depart without the permission of the abbess and chapter; and no one may presume to retain one who has departed without letters of dismissal. Since those who lead the religious life ought to live from the alms and beneficence of others, we decree that no one may presume to demand or receive tithes from you on the work which you cultivate at your own expense or from the upkeep of your animals. [Col. 1037C]

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions or goods, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved intact and wholly beneficial for the use of those for whose governance and support they were granted. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honor; let that person know himself or herself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let that person be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ; and at the final judgment let that person be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve what is right for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

Given at Viterbo through the hand of Robert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the seventh day before the Ides of May, in the eighth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation [Col. 1038A] 1145, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

## XXIV. Privilege for the Church of Saint Mary of Verona.  
*(1145, May 17.)*

[Ughelli, *Italia sacra*, V, 791.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother THEOBALD, bishop of Verona, and to his successors canonically promoted: in perpetuity.

A pious petition, etc. Therefore, venerable brother in Christ, Bishop Theobald, we graciously assent to your just petitions. We take under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the Veronese Church of the blessed Mother of God and ever-virgin Mary, over which by God’s authority you are known to preside, and fortify it by the privilege of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions and goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may hereafter, God favoring you, acquire by reasonable means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names:

The monastery of Saint Zeno; the monastery of Saints Fermo and Rusticus; the monastery of Saint Nazarius with all their appurtenances; the churches of the city itself; the fortress of Malcesine with all its lordship, jurisdiction, and appurtenances; the parish church of that fortress with all its chapels; our right in the castle called Tutis; the castle of Garda with all its appurtenances; the parish church of that place [Col. 1038C] with all its chapels; the parish church of Caprino with its chapels and tithes; that of Cisano with chapels and tithes; that of Gazizio with chapels and tithes; that of Teneri with chapels and tithes; that of Pavenguli with chapels, tithes, and castle; the monastery of Vemagazano with chapels and tithes; the parish church of the same place with its tithes and chapels; the estate of Lenzani with castle and all its appurtenances; Rivoltella with chapels and tithes; the parish church of Sitinii with chapels and tithes; the monastery of Saint Vigilius; the parish church of Puzolengo with chapels and tithes; the parish church of Saint Zeno Zodeldisco, with the church of Saint Michael situated by the Tartaro, with tithes; the church of Saint Peter in Carnario with tithes; the church of Saint Nazarius with tithes and estate; the church of Saint Ambrose of Casalialto with its appurtenances; the parish church of Valeggio with chapels and tithes; the monastery of Saint Mary near the *mensa*, so far as parochial right is concerned; the parish church of Ponto with chapels, tithes, and estate; the parish church of Saint Andrew with chapels, tithes, and estate; the parish church of Peschiera with chapels, tithes, estate, fisheries, and one half; the parish church of Cartholengi with chapels and tithes; the parish church of Palazzolo with tithes; the parish church of Sommacampagna with chapels and tithes; the parish church of Gregia with chapels, tithes, and estate; the parish church of Vico Attici with chapels and tithes; the parish church of Trinenzolo with chapels and tithes; the parish church of Bonfissio with chapels and tithes; the parish church [Col. 1039A] of Castellari; the parish church of Moratica with chapels and tithes; the church of Saint Peter in the monastery with tithes; the parish church of Saint Prosdocimus with chapels, tithes, and an estate extending to the old channel of the Tartaro; the church of Gatii with tithes; and the church of the royal estate with tithes and estate.

Parochial right in the parish church of Nogaria is to be held as was determined by the concord made in our presence between you and the abbot of Nonantola, and confirmed by our written instrument, together with the tithes which you canonically possess in the same village of Nogaria and in the other village called Aspum; the church of Casalavoni; the church of Salezole; the church of Ravanuance with tithes; the church of Vanferarii with tithes; the parish church of Ceredi with chapels, tithes, household dependents, and whatever else you justly possess there; the parish church of Leniacis with chapels, tithes, estate, and all its appurtenances; the parish church of Portaerem with chapels, tithes, estate, and appurtenances; the estate of Baasi with chapels and tithes; the parish church of Saint Zeno with chapels, tithes, and estate; the parish church of Englarii with chapel and tithes, and whatever else you justly possess there; the estate of Bonamdigni with churches and tithes; the church of Lasiae with tithes; the estate of Rupa Clara with parish church, chapels, tithes, household dependents, and its other appurtenances; the parish church of Cortiliani with tithes; the parish church of Boboloni with tithes and estate; the parish church of Tumba with chapels, tithes, estate, and its other appurtenances; the village of Casanova with all jurisdiction and the old castle; the parish church of Roncho with chapels [Col. 1039C] and tithes; the parish church of the Island of Porcharitia with chapels, tithes, and estate; the parish church of Opedani with chapels and tithes; the estate of Scardevaria with churches and tithes; the parish church of Geberti with chapels and tithes; the parish church of Azanensis with chapels and tithes; the churches of Porcilli with chapels and tithes; the parish church of Suardio with chapels and tithes, and whatever else you justly possess there; the estate of Galderii with churches, tithes, and household dependents; whatever right it has in the *me Mooe* called Sarmatiae [reading uncertain], in the woods situated near Monteforte, and in Fustalino, with all the appurtenances of that estate; the parish church of Colonione with chapels, tithes, household dependents, and half an estate; the parish church of Illati with chapels, tithes, and half an estate; the estate of Calavena with parish church, chapels, tithes, and household dependents belonging to it; the monastery of Saint Peter of Calavena; the parish church of Mezano with chapels, tithes, castle, and household dependents; half the estate of Lavanii with churches and tithes; the estate of Monte Aureo with parish church, chapels, tithes, and all its appurtenances; the parish church of Cretiana with chapels, tithes, and household dependents; the estate of Alzenagi and one half of Azagi; the parish church of Albatiani with tithes, chapels within the jurisdiction of the estate, and household dependents; the parish church of Saint Florian with chapels, tithes, and household dependents; the parish church of Higratio with chapels, tithes, household dependents, and half an estate; and the parish church of Saint George with chapels, tithes, household dependents, and half an estate.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may [Col. 1040A] rashly disturb the aforesaid Church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved intact, wholly beneficial for the use of those for whose governance and support they were granted, without prejudice in all things to the authority of the Apostolic See. If, therefore, in the future, etc.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Theod[ewinus], bishop of Santa Rufina, have subscribed. I, G[regory], cardinal priest of the title of Saint Callistus, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Chrysogonus, have subscribed. I, Ranerius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Prisca, have subscribed. I, Thomas, cardinal priest of the title of Vestina, have subscribed. I, Manfred, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Sabina, have subscribed. I, Villanus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian [Col. 1040B] Hill, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Oddo, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Peter, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed. I, Rodulphus, cardinal deacon of Saint Lucy in the Septa Solis, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Angelo, have subscribed. I, Hyacinthus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin, have subscribed. I, Bernard, cardinal deacon of the Holy Roman Church, have subscribed. I, Peter, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed. [Col. 1040C] I, Cintius, cardinal deacon of the Holy Roman Church, have subscribed.

Given at Viterbo through the hand of Robert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of June, in the eighth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1145, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

## XXV. He confirms the peace between Theobald, bishop of Verona, and A[lbert], abbot of Nonantola, made on the condition that one should possess “parochial right” and the other “right in the land” in the parish of Nogaria.  
*(1145, May 18.)*

[Tiraboschi, *Storia di Nonantola*, II, p. 259.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son A., abbot of Nonantola: greeting and apostolic [Col. 1040D] blessing.

Matters decided by the truth of judgment or settled by reasonable concord ought to be entrusted to the record of letters, lest they can hereafter be disturbed by the opposition of wicked persons. We therefore command that this present letter record how the controversy between you and our venerable brother Theobald, bishop of Verona, concerning the parish church of Nogaria was settled in our presence. Having heard the arguments of both parties and diligently investigated the matter before pronouncing judgment, we permitted you to choose a settlement for the sake of peace and the tranquility of both Churches.

It pleased both parties that henceforth the bishop of Verona should peacefully possess parochial right, while the abbot of Nonantola should possess right in the land, in the same parish of Nogaria. Having taken the counsel of our brethren concerning this, we gave our assent to the agreement; and lest any discord arise thereafter between these Churches, we have defined that parochial right as follows. When an archpriest is to be ordained in that parish, he shall be chosen by the clergy of that parish with the knowledge of the abbot of Nonantola. If suitable, the person chosen shall receive the care of the parish from the bishop of Verona; he shall be accountable to him for the care of the parish and promise obedience. To the abbot, however, he shall render an assurance by hand and due subjection in temporal matters. The bishop of Verona shall have the consecration of that parish, of its altars and chapels, and the ordination of the clerics belonging to it, and shall confer these freely and without difficulty. He shall also canonically correct the offences of those clerics.

When he comes to the council of the Roman pontiff, the archpriest and clerics of that parish shall pay him fifty Luccan solidi. If he comes to the Roman curia for a need or benefit of the Church of Verona, they shall provide him fifteen solidi of Luccan currency. But if he is summoned because accused of a crime, they shall not be compelled to give anything on this account. When, according to custom, they attend his synod, they shall pay ten synodal solidi [Col. 1041B] of Veronese currency, as is customary. When he visits the parish churches in accordance with custom, or if by any chance he happens to pass through that place, they shall receive him honorably in lodging according to the resources of that parish. But that parish shall remain altogether free and undisturbed from other burdens or exactions imposed by the bishop of Verona or his officials.

Given at Viterbo, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of June.

## XXVI. To Otto, provost, the brethren of Cappenberg, and the religious women of Wischlingen belonging to the same congregation: he grants exemption from tithes.  
*(1145, May 23.)*

[We have a summary of this unpublished privilege from Jaffé, *Regesta of the Roman Pontiffs*, p. 618.]

## XXVII. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Mary of Colomba.  
*(1145, June 3.)*

[Campi, *History of Piacenza*, I, p. 543, Proofs.]

[Col. 1041D]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons in Christ, JOHN, abbot of the venerable monastery situated in the place called Colomba, formerly named Caretum, and located in the diocese of Piacenza, and to his brethren professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

Whenever we are asked for something recognized as consistent with religion and uprightness, it is fitting for us to grant it with willing mind and to give appropriate support to the petitioners’ desires. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests. We take under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid monastery, in which you are dedicated to divine service, and fortify it by the privilege of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, God favoring it, acquire by grant of pontiffs, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names:

All the lands which the illustrious Marquis Pallavicino, together with his wife and sons; Marquis Conrad Cavalcaba with his wife; the vassals of those marquises; the church of Saint [Col. 1042B] Mary of Castellione; the church of Florentiola; the noble standard-bearer of the city of Piacenza; Malcoredus, vice-lord; Fulco, advocate; Bonizo of Andito; Ardengus, vice-lord; Grimerius and Baiamons, viscounts; Gislentio; brothers Bernard, John, and Calvus, sons of Salvus Arditionis; Malus Parens; Rainaldus Surdus; Malacria; the noble sons of Rainerius of the aforesaid city; and all other good men who have conferred them upon that place for devotion, sale, exchange, or reciprocal exchange. We decree that these lands shall remain peacefully and freely, in perpetual right, to the brethren of that place, exempt from every secular exaction.

And since those who live the common life ought to live from the alms and beneficence of others, we decree that no one may dare to demand or receive from the brethren of that monastery tithes upon the lands they cultivate with their own hands or at their own expense, or upon the animals they keep. We further decree that from the place called Barastalla to Siolo, from Siolo to Florentiola, from Florentiola to Butrium, from Butrium to Saint Andrew, and from Saint Andrew to the aforesaid Barastalla—boundaries which we know to have been specifically designated by our venerable brother Bishop Arduino, as well as by the clergy and people of Piacenza, and confirmed by Lothair, by the grace of God third Roman emperor Augustus—no church may at any time be built and no secular dwelling whatsoever established. [Col. 1042D]

We also confirm whatever the aforesaid bishop, by the counsel of his brethren, has justly granted you from lands belonging to the right of his bishopric and confirmed by his writing. Likewise, we confirm by apostolic authority the boundaries which the aforesaid Marquis Pallavicino, together with his wife, granted from lands of his own right to the aforesaid monastery of Colomba for the remedy of their souls, set in place with their own hands, and ratified by a written instrument; and we forbid anyone to presume to alter or transfer them. Namely: as the stream of Pontiore runs to the road which goes to Siolo; and as the boundaries themselves extend above Salicetum to the road which goes to Castellione; and as that same road runs above the tail-end of Luxerclo to the old stream; and as that stream runs to Bodracum; and as Bodracum itself runs as far as the enclosure of the same Burgundio; and as the stream of Frasaneto runs from that enclosure to the aforesaid place of Pontiore [lacuna].

No person whatsoever, therefore, may lawfully rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but all things shall be preserved intact and wholly beneficial for the use of those for whose governance and support they were granted, without prejudice to the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, having been warned a second or third time, if that person does not correct his offence by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honor; let that person know himself or herself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let that person be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and at the final judgment let that person be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve their rights for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Celsus, have subscribed. [Col. 1143C] I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Chrysogonus, have subscribed. I, Thomas, cardinal priest of the title of Vestina, have subscribed. I, Gilibertus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Mark, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Damaso, have subscribed. I, Hugh, cardinal priest of the title in Lucina, have subscribed. I, Villanus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. [Col. 1043D] I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Octavianus, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed. I, John, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Angelo, have subscribed.

Given at Viterbo through the hand of Robert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the third day before the Nones of June, in the eighth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1145, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

## XXVIII. He informs Otto, bishop of Prague, and Vladislaus, duke of the Bohemians, that certain persons have been excommunicated for seizing the goods of Henry, bishop of Moravia.  
*(1145, June 5.)*

[Theiner, *Disquisitiones eruditae*, p. 210.]

[Col. 1044A]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother OTTO, bishop of Prague, and his beloved son in Christ W., illustrious duke of the Bohemians: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It has been established by the Apostolic See that, if anyone, at the devil’s prompting, incurs the guilt of this sacrilege by laying violent hands upon a cleric or monk, he is subject to anathema; and no bishop may presume to absolve him, except when death is imminent, until he is presented before the apostolic presence [Col. 1044B] and receives its command. It has come to us that certain parishioners of our venerable brother Martin, bishop of Moravia, at the devil’s instigation, while he was travelling to the holy Roman Church, sacrilegiously assaulted his person and did not hesitate at all to carry off his goods. Therefore we, to whom it especially belongs not to allow so great a sacrilege and so grave an offence to pass unpunished, bound these same sacrilegious persons—namely Conrad, Wradizlaus, Depald, Micul, Jurata, Domazlaus, Slavebor, Ugo, Cuno, Roduik, and Bogdan—by the bond of excommunication at the recent feast of Pentecost, in the presence of a multitude of people, and separated them from the fellowship of all the faithful. Therefore, by these apostolic letters, we command [Col. 1044C] and enjoin you that you, brother bishop, publicly proclaim this same excommunication and cause it to be observed. But you, son W., duke, shall restrain them according to the power bestowed upon you by God, until they make satisfaction to our aforesaid brother for so grave an injury, and they themselves, in accordance with his command and counsel, come before us both for themselves and for the others, so that, as is contained in the aforesaid decree, they may receive our command concerning so grave a sacrilege.

Given at Viterbo, on the Nones of June.

### XXIX. To the abbots of Gradice and Třebíč, and likewise to Otto, duke of Moravia: he commands them, together with the duke of Bohemia, to compel the dukes Conrad, Wratislaus, and Theobald and their accomplices to make satisfaction to the bishop of Moravia.  
*(A.D. 1145, 5 June.)*

[BOCZEK, *Codex diplomaticus Moraviae*, I, 236.]

[Col. 1044D]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons . . . the abbots of Gradice and Třebíč, and to his beloved son in Christ OTTO, duke of Moravia: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It has come to us that certain parishioners of our venerable brother Henry, bishop of Moravia, at the devil’s instigation, while he was travelling with you, beloved son Duke Otto, to the holy Roman Church, sacrilegiously assaulted his person and did not hesitate at all to carry off his goods. Therefore we, to whom it especially belongs not to allow so great a sacrilege and so grave an [Col. 1045A] offence to pass unpunished, bound these same sacrilegious persons—namely Conrad, Wratislaus, Depold, Jurata, Domazlaus, Slavebor, Ugo, Cuno, Micul, Groznata, Radmilius, and Bogdan—by the bond of excommunication at the recent feast of Pentecost, in the presence of a multitude of people, and separated them from the fellowship of all the faithful. Therefore, by these apostolic letters, we command and enjoin you that you, sons . . . abbots, publicly proclaim this same excommunication. But you, son Duke Otto, according to the power bestowed upon you by God, shall, joining forces with our beloved son Wladislaus, duke of the Bohemians, restrain them until they make satisfaction to our brother for so grave an injury, and certain of them, in accordance with the command and counsel [Col. 1045B], come before us on behalf of themselves and the others and receive our command concerning so grave a sacrilege.

Given at Viterbo, on the Nones of June.

### XXX. At the request of Henry, bishop of Moravia, he receives the monastery of Litomyšl under the protection of the Apostolic See and confirms its possessions.  
*(A.D. 1145, 8 June.)*

[BOCZEK, *Codex diplomaticus Moraviae*, I, 237.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons . . . the abbot of the monastery at Litomyšl, of the Premonstratensian Order, and his brothers: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1045C] Considering with grateful mind the faithful devotion of our venerable brother Henry, bishop of Moravia, and readily assenting, with the paternal kindness proper to us, to his just petitions, in which he has earnestly interceded for you, we receive the church of Saint Mary, together with the place in which your monastery is seen to have been built, under the protection of Saint Peter and our own, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods your church now justly and canonically holds by the generous grant of the noble men Břetislav and Soběslav, former dukes of the Bohemians, as well as Duke Wladislaus, his brother Henry, Otto duke of Moravia, and our aforesaid brother [Col. 1045D] Henry himself, and of others; and whatever it may hereafter acquire, God favouring it, by grants of bishops, benefactions of princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for ever, now and in time to come.

Therefore let no person whatsoever be permitted to infringe this charter of our confirmation and protection, or rashly to oppose it. But if anyone presumes to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His apostles, the blessed Peter and Paul.

Given at Viterbo, on the sixth day before the Ides of June.

[Note: [Col. 1045] From a copy in the archive of the same monastery, which is preserved, inserted in the archive of Gradice, in the registry of the royal-imperial government of Moravia.]

### XXXI. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Saviour of Monte Acuto.  
*(A.D. 1145, 12 June.)*

[MITTARELLI, *Annales Camaldulenses*, III, Appendix, 420.]

[Col. 1046A]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons OFFREDUS, abbot of the monastery of the Lord Saviour in the territory of Perugia, in the place called below Mount Castellione, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: for ever.

It befits the mercy of apostolic governance to cherish religious persons and to foster their places by the safeguard of apostolic protection. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we grant due charitable assent to your petition, [Col. 1046B] and, following in the footsteps of our predecessor of good memory, Honorius, we fortify by the protection of the Apostolic See the monastery of Saint Saviour, in which you are devoted to the divine service. Therefore, by the authority of the Apostolic See, we decree through this charter of privilege that whatever goods and possessions appear to belong to the same monastery through grants of pontiffs, the liberality of kings, donations of the faithful, or other just means, and whatever it may hereafter, by the Lord’s bounty, justly and canonically acquire, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to record by their proper names:

Namely, the monastery of Saint Saviour, situated beside the River Carpino; the monastery of Saint Juliana with its chapels and appurtenances [Col. 1046C]; Saint Thomas’s, with its churches and appurtenances; the cell of Saint John at Monte Acuto, with its churches and appurtenances; the church of Saint Sylvester, with its churches and appurtenances; the church of Saint Paul of Herodina, with its appurtenances; the cell of Saint Julian on the island of Pulvensa, with its serfs, appurtenances, and fisheries; the church of Saint Florentius in the county of Arezzo, in the place called Mosanarii, with its appurtenances; the cell of Saint Mary at Colognola; the cell of Saint Florentius near the wall of the city of Perugia, with its appurtenances; the church of Saint Mary at Clevi, with its appurtenance; the cell of Saint Petronilla in the county of Todi; the church of Saint Donatus, with its churches and their appurtenances; the cell of Saint Simeon, with its churches and [Col. 1046D] appurtenances; the cell of Saint Peter at Antoniana; the churches of Saint Nicholas and Saint Paternianus, with all their appurtenances; the church of Saint Andrew at Fracta, with its hospital and their appurtenances; the cell of Saint Faustinus, with its churches and appurtenances; the cell of Saint Saviour at Jessiola, with its appurtenance; the cell of Saint Peter at Carpine, with its churches, castles, and appurtenances; the church of Saint Paternianus near the village called Farneto; the church of Saint Lawrence at Agello; the church of Saint Benedict at Carseta, and Saint [Col. 1047A] Andrew’s at Castro, with all their appurtenances; the cell of Saint Mary at Nicona, with its appurtenance; the church of Saint Christopher at Rufianula; the church of Saint Donatus on the mountain, with all their appurtenances; and the church of Saint Mary at Monteacuto, with its appurtenance.

In the county of Montefeltro: the church situated on Mount Cislo, with its appurtenance; the church of Saint Gaudentius near Mount Falcone; the church of Saint Saviour in Valle-Vienna, with their appurtenances; likewise the land at Sorbo, Favulla, Baxio, near the rock of Tifila, in the broad valley near Miratoria, and at Castagnola near Gattaria, with all things which appear in that county to belong to the said holy place; the cell of the Holy Trinity on Mount Nero, dedicated to the eremitical [Col. 1047B] life; the church of Saint Mary at Trivio, with their appurtenances; the church of Saint Matthew in the valley of the Lake, with all its appurtenances. In the county of the castle of Felicitas, whatever it possesses through the gift of Guicciardus, within or outside the city; and the parish church of Saint Peter on Mount Marciano, with its churches and all its appurtenances.

Further, upon the death of you, the present abbot of the same place, or of any of your successors, no one may be set over it by any craft of deception or violence, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren, shall elect in the fear of God and according to the Rule of Saint Benedict, to be consecrated by the Roman pontiff. You shall receive chrism, holy oil, the consecration of altars and churches, and the ordination [Col. 1047C] of monks and other clerics to be promoted to sacred orders, from the diocesan bishop, provided that he enjoys the grace and communion of the Apostolic See and is willing to supply these things freely and without abuse. Otherwise you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer and receive from him the sacraments of consecration, he being supported by the authority of the Apostolic See and granting what is requested. Moreover, we grant that you may retain the tithes of your labours for the use of the poor, without contradiction from any bishop. We also command and order that all agreements or charters made, contrary to law and right, by corrupt administrators or abbots from the goods of the monastery itself, to its detriment, shall be held altogether void and without force. We prohibit public [Col. 1047D] Masses or stations from being held in your monastery against the will of the abbot. Neither they nor any person may inflict molestation upon the goods of the monastery, or exact fodrum or forced services, so that, God granting, you may remain diligent and undisturbed in observing holy religion and enjoy the grace of Roman protection. Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the same monastery, remove its possessions, retain those removed, diminish them, or harass them in any manner; but that all shall be preserved intact, for the full benefit of those for whose governance they were granted, subject to the authority of the Apostolic See.

[Col. 1048A] If in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this charter of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after a second or third admonition, unless he corrects his offence by fitting satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be alienated from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Redeemer Jesus Christ; and let him be subject at the last judgment to stern vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

**Make for me, O Lord, + a sign for good.**

[Col. 1048B] I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Thomas, cardinal priest of the title of Vestina, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Damaso, have subscribed. I, Hugo, cardinal priest of the title in Lucina, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Bacchus and Sergius, have subscribed. I, Oddo, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Octavianus, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed. I, Rodulfus, cardinal deacon of Saint Lucy in Septa Solis, have subscribed.

Given at Viterbo by the hand of Robert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, [Col. 1048C] on the second day before the Ides of June, in the eighth indiction, in the year 1145 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### XXXII. Privilege for the Church of Saint Peter of Guastalla.  
*(A.D. 1145, 14 June.)*

[AFFO, *Istoria della città di Guastalla*, I, 338.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons RAINALD, archpriest of the church of Blessed Peter situated in the district of Guastalla, and his brethren, present and future, canonically appointed: for ever.

A pious request ought to be fulfilled by a corresponding result, so that the sincerity [Col. 1048D] of devotion may shine forth commendably and the advantage sought may undoubtedly acquire strength. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we mercifully assent to your just petitions. We receive under the care and protection of the Apostolic See, and commend to the patronage of Saint Peter, your church, which was raised from a chapel to a parish church by our predecessor of happy memory Pope Gregory V, and strengthened by privileges from his successors, the supreme pontiffs Paschal and Innocent II of holy memory. We decree that whatever possessions, tithes, and other goods the same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by grants of pontiffs, the liberality of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just [Col. 1049A] means, the Lord providing, acquire, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you.

We grant you unrestricted permission to receive chrism and holy oil, the ordination of clerics, and the consecration of churches from whatever Catholic bishop you choose. In addition, we decree that no one may presume, without your permission, to build a church within the bounds of your parish except one which ought to be subject to you; nevertheless, in all things the authority of the Apostolic See and the venerable dignity of the above-mentioned parish church are preserved. We also decree that the chapels of Saint Bartholomew, Saint George, and Saint Martin, belonging by right to your church and confirmed to you by our aforesaid predecessors, shall remain for ever subject to you. No archbishop, bishop, abbot, margrave, count, captain, [Col. 1049B] judge, or *guastaldio*, nor indeed any person whatsoever, may lawfully rashly disturb the aforesaid church, remove its possessions, retain those removed, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations. Rather, all shall be preserved intact for the full benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted.

If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this charter of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after a second or third admonition, unless he makes amendment by fitting satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be alienated from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ; and let him be subject at the last [Col. 1049C] judgment to stern vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Theodoricus, bishop of Santa Rufina, have subscribed. I, Ugolinus, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Oddo, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Octavianus, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Prison, have subscribed. [Col. 1049D] I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Angelo, have subscribed. I, Jacintus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Calixtus, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Chrysogonus, have subscribed. I, Thomas, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Vestina, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Damaso, have subscribed. I, Nicholas, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cyriacus, have subscribed. I, Hugo, cardinal priest of the title in Lucina, have subscribed. I, Julius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus, have subscribed. I, Villanus, cardinal priest of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill, have subscribed.

Given at Viterbo by the hand of Robert, cardinal priest of the holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the eighteenth day before the Kalends of July, in the eighth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation [Col. 1050A] 1145, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### XXXIII. Privilege for the abbey of Saint Mary of Châtillon.  
*(A.D. 1145, 16 June.)*

[PLANCHER, *Histoire de Bourgogne*, I, *Preuves*, p. 44.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons BALDWIN, abbot of the church of Blessed Mary of Châtillon, and the brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: for ever.

Whenever something is requested of us which is known to accord with reason and utility, it is fitting that we grant it gladly and provide appropriate assistance to the desires of those who ask. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we mercifully assent to your just petitions [Col. 1050B] and receive under the protection of Saint Peter and our own, fortifying it with the protection of this present writing, the aforesaid church of the blessed Mother of God and ever-virgin Mary, in which you are devoted to divine service. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, through grants of pontiffs, the liberality of kings, benefactions of princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, the Lord providing, acquire, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The church of Pomiliac; your right in the church of Brion; the church of Massay; the house of God at Châtillon with all its appurtenances; the whole parish [Col. 1050C] of that castle; the church of Saint Fidol; the church of Maisey; the church of Villota; the church of Bunciac; the church of Colomier; the church of Lairic; the church of Custeran; the church of Baclo; and the church of Empiliac, as these were canonically bestowed freely upon the same church, without *paratae* and *eulogiae*, by our venerable brother Geoffrey, bishop of Langres, and his predecessors—except that of Saint Fidol; two ovens in the same castle; half of the *minagium* [market-measure dues], both within and outside the market; the mill of Carcelles; also the tithes of the episcopal lands of that castle; likewise the annual *cruces* [processional offerings?] from Giey to Grancey and to Lentilly; from Lentilly to Colomier; [Col. 1050D] from Colomier to Salives, thence also to Bacelou and to Laignes. Likewise, from Colomier to Saint-Germain-Rocheux; from Saint-Germain to Aisey, and thence to the other Colomier; from these named villages as well as from all others lying within these bounds. Also the village called Poiseul; the village called Villeta, likewise near Dijon and Fleurey; Rotagium, with its wind-rights and toll, granted to your church from their own property by Odo and his son Hugh, dukes of Burgundy; the portion of the wood called Vicinum which Walter Burgarellus held therein; the meadow at Massay called Gruold’s meadow, which belonged to Hugh of Lairiac, son of Guido de Porta; and the mill of Empiliac, which is [Col. 1051A] beside the bridge and was granted to you by Willa, sister of Geoffrey, with the consent of her sons and nephews.

We also prohibit anyone from presuming to build a church or oratory within your parish without your consent, while the authority of the Apostolic See is in all things preserved. Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, remove its possessions, retain those removed, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but that all shall be preserved intact for the full benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the canonical reverence due to the diocesan bishop.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this charter of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it [Col. 1051B], then, after a second or third admonition, unless he makes amendment by fitting satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be alienated from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ; and let him be subject at the last judgment to stern vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Theodegninus, bishop of Santa Rufina, have subscribed. [Col. 1051C] I, Thomas, cardinal priest of the title of Vestina, have subscribed. I, Nicholas, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cyriacus, have subscribed. I, . . . cardinal priest of the title in Lucina, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Octavianus, deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed. I, Rodulfus, cardinal deacon of Saint Lucy in Septa Solis, have subscribed.

Given at Viterbo by the hand of Robert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of July, in the eighth indiction, in the year 1145 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### XXXIV. Bull in favour of Albert, abbot of Saint-Theudard.  
*(A.D. 1145, 23 June.)*

[*Gallia Christiana nova*, XIII, Instrumenta, 183.]

[Col. 1051D]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brothers ARNALD, archbishop of Narbonne, and RAYMOND, bishop of Toulouse: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Our son Albert, abbot of Saint-Theudard, appearing before us with testimonials in letters from certain of our brethren, laid before us a serious complaint: that Count Ildefonsus of Toulouse is violently destroying the abbey of Saint-Theudard; is causing the inhabitants of the village to rise against the abbot and monks and to move with their goods and houses to another place; is compelling the abbot [Col. 1052A] himself and the monks to flee and go about as exiles; is sacrilegiously building two castles on the allod of the monastery itself, and a third on land which he himself had sold to the same abbot for two thousand two hundred solidi; and, not content with this, is threatening them, to crown his wickedness, with still graver things—namely, punishment and death.

Since we do not believe that your brotherhood is unaware how sacrilegious it is to seize ecclesiastical property with such presumption, or how severe a punishment this deserves, by these apostolic letters we command you under obedience that, setting delay aside, you meet together and strictly admonish the aforesaid count on our behalf: he is to allow the aforesaid abbot and his monks to remain peacefully in their place; demolish the castles built on the monastery’s [Col. 1052B] allod; make fitting satisfaction to the abbot and brethren for the losses and injuries inflicted; and wholly abolish the evil customs which he is known to have imposed upon that abbey and its appurtenances.
