If, within forty days after your admonition, he disdains to comply, we prohibit the celebration of divine offices throughout the city of Toulouse itself and in the bishopric subject to his power, except baptism and penance for the dying. You shall cause this interdict to be firmly observed until he has made satisfaction in the manner stated above. But if he does not come to his senses and presumes to persist in the same malice, we cannot refrain from extending against his person the hands of blessed Peter and our own.

Given at Viterbo, on the ninth day before the Kalends of July.

### Chapter XXXV. To O[tho], bishop of Lucca.  
*(A.D. 1145, 30 June.)*

[BALUZE, *Miscellanea*, Lucchese edition, IV, 593.]

[Col. 1052C]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother O., bishop of Lucca: greeting and apostolic blessing.

A complaint has reached our ears that the prior of Saint Angelo and his brethren neglect to observe what our predecessor of happy memory, Pope Lucius, commanded concerning the church of Saint Saviour. Since we wish that his commands be observed as incontrovertibly as our own, by these apostolic letters we command you to order the same prior on our behalf that, just as that same predecessor of ours ordered him orally [Col. 1052D] under obedience, what Innocent and Celestine, our predecessors of holy memory, commanded, and what he himself confirmed by oath in the hand of our beloved son G., cardinal priest of Saints Lawrence and Damasus, he and his brethren shall observe without dispute. Moreover, hold as excommunicated those who threw stones at the same church of Saint Saviour or made an assault upon it, until they make satisfaction for so great a sacrilege. But if the aforesaid prior, his brethren, or his parishioners should ever presume to attack the brethren of Saint Fridian over that same church of Saint Saviour, or the persons or goods of that church, then from that time onward we prohibit the celebration of divine offices in the church of Saint Angelo itself.

Given at Viterbo, on the second day before the Kalends of July.

### XXXVI. To G., abbot of Saint Nicholas of Vedogio.  
*(A.D. 1145, 16 August.)*

[D. BOUQUET, *Recueil*, XV, 429.]

[Col. 1053A]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to G., abbot of Saint Nicholas of Vedogio: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Although you assert that you are burdened by poverty, we greatly wonder that you labour by every means to become poorer. For it ought not to have slipped your memory that we orally committed for determination to our venerable brother Alvisus, bishop of Arras, the dispute being litigated between you and the priest of Batpalms. In his presence, when you saw that the case was not proceeding according to your wishes, as [Col. 1053B] we have learned from that same brother of ours, you again appealed the aforesaid priest to the Apostolic See solely for the purpose of evasion and dilatory delay.

Since it is the duty of our office to provide with paternal care for those unjustly burdened, by these apostolic letters we command you that, when summoned by the aforesaid brother of ours, you shall appear before him, setting aside all pretexts. If the said priest proves by two or three suitable witnesses that his predecessors, who were priests, held a fourth part of the priestly benefice of Batpalms, you shall, setting aside every appeal, allow him thereafter peacefully to hold that fourth part, and restore in full the losses which he proves you have inflicted upon him in consequence. Otherwise, we shall by no means [Col. 1053C] be able to pass over your dilatory obstruction without administering fitting justice.

Given at Viterbo, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of September.

### XXXVII. To Alvisus, bishop of Arras: he commands him to judge between the abbot of Saint Nicholas of Vedogio and the priest of Batpalms.  
*(A.D. 1145, 16 August.)*

[Same work, p. 428.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother ALVISUS, bishop of Arras: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We are indeed grieved by the instability and fickleness which, as you have informed us by your letters, the abbot of Saint Nicholas of Vedogio displayed in your presence, and we have no doubt that this is utterly contrary to religious life. We remember [Col. 1053D] that we orally committed to your brotherhood, for determination in the following manner, the dispute between the aforesaid abbot and the priest who bears these presents: namely, that if the priest proves before you by two or three suitable witnesses that his predecessors, who were priests, held by the custom of the Church a fourth part of the priestly benefice of Batpalms, you should cause the same priest peacefully to hold that fourth part. When you wished to carry this into effect according to our command, the aforesaid abbot appealed the priest anew to our hearing, not, as you state, because of oppression, but solely for the purpose of evasion. Although in that appeal you proceeded outside the ordinary course, [Col. 1054A] nevertheless, since you deferred your judgment out of reverence for the Apostolic See, we commend your devotion in the Lord.

But since he ought not to profit by his dilatory obstruction and perverse contrivance, we again remit the case to your discretion. By these apostolic letters we command you, having associated with yourself prudent and discerning men, especially our venerable brother Milo, bishop of Moulins, to summon both parties before you. If the priest proves before you, as has been stated above, his claim regarding the fourth part, then, setting aside every appeal, you shall invest him in our stead with that fourth part and cause to be restored in full whatever he proves has been taken from him from that fourth part.

Given at Viterbo, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of September.

### XXXVIII. To Theobald, bishop of Verona.  
*(A.D. 1145, 12 September.)*

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, V, 784.]

[Col. 1054B]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother T., bishop of Verona: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It has come to us that certain nobles of your city are newly troubling the Church of Verona concerning a certain castle, which that Church had long possessed peacefully and held freely by grant of the emperors and confirmation of the Roman Church; and that you too have entered into litigation with them concerning this, against the will of your brethren and despite the prohibition issued on this matter. Since we do not wish the possessions and goods [Col. 1054C] of that Church to be lost through anyone’s injury or negligence, by these present letters we command you to enter into no judgment or agreement with them concerning it. Rather, without delay strictly admonish them to relinquish to it that castle and the other possessions which the Church of Verona has hitherto possessed peacefully, and no longer presume to trouble it concerning them. But if they are confident that they have a right, let them come with you before our beloved son G., cardinal priest, and there obtain what is just. If they refuse to do this and to desist from harassing the Church, administer justice against them as invaders of ecclesiastical property.

[Col. 1054D] Given at Monte Lubrico, on the second day before the Ides of September.

### XXXIX. He commands W[ido], cardinal priest, to settle the controversy concerning a certain castle which had arisen between the canons and certain nobles of Verona.  
*(A.D. 1145, 13 September.)*

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, V, 787.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son W., cardinal priest: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It has come to us that certain noblemen of the city of Verona are newly troubling the Church of Verona concerning a certain castle which that Church had long possessed peacefully [Col. 1055A] and held freely by grant of the emperor and confirmation of the Roman Church; and that our brother T., the bishop, has likewise entered into litigation with them concerning this against the will of his brethren and despite their prohibition. Since we do not wish the possessions and goods of that Church to be lost through anyone’s injury or negligence, we have instructed the same bishop by our letters to enter into no judgment or agreement with them concerning it, but rather, without delay, strictly to admonish them to relinquish to it that castle and the other possessions which the Church of Verona has hitherto possessed peacefully, and no longer presume to trouble it concerning them. But if they are confident that they have a right, let them come with him before you and there obtain what is just. We command you, however, by these present letters [Col. 1055B], at a suitable place and time, to summon before you both the same bishop, the archpriest and clergy, and the nobles; and, after carefully hearing the case from both sides, to decide it according to judicial procedure.

Given at Monte Lubrico, on the Ides of September.

### XL. Privilege for the Church of Reggio.  
*(A.D. 1145.)*

[MURATORI, *Antiquitates Italicae*, VI, 419.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother ALBERO, bishop of Reggio, and to his successors canonically appointed for ever.

A pious petition ought to be fulfilled with an effective result, so that both the sincerity of devotion may shine forth commendably and the benefit sought may assuredly acquire strength. Therefore, venerable brother Bishop Albero, we graciously assent to your just requests, and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the Church of Reggio, over which, by God’s appointment, you are known to preside; and we fortify it by the privilege of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods you now possess justly and canonically, or may hereafter be able, by God’s favor, to acquire by reasonable means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors, and through you to that same Church. Among these we have thought fit to set down expressly the following: [Col. 1055D] the monastery of Saint Prosper; the canonry of Saint Geminianus; the chapel of Saint Stephen and the other chapels of the same city; the monastery of Saint Thomas; the monastery of Saint Raphael; the parish church of Minotio; the chapel of Saint James of the Island of Bibio, with the other chapels of that same parish; the parish church of Thoano; the chapel of the hospital at Ponte de Cavella, with its possessions and the other chapels of that same parish; the parish church of Saint Vitalis, with its chapels and everything rightfully pertaining to it; the parish church of Campiola; the chapel of Saint Venantius of Bussina; the chapel of Valvesneria; the chapel of Saint Vitus, with the other chapels of that same parish; the parish church of Baysio, with its chapels; the parish church of the castle of Ariano, with its chapels; the parish church of Saint Eleucadius, with its chapels; the parish church [Col. 1056A] of Albineto, with its chapels; the parish church of Pulianello, with its chapels; the parish church of Lezulo, with its chapels; the parish church of Caviliano; the chapel of Fano; the chapel of Cirezula; the chapel of Saint Prosper of Graxiano, with the other chapels of that same parish; the parish church of Bibiano; the chapels of Bibianello, with the other chapels of that same parish; the parish church of Mutilena; the chapels of Curviaco; the parish church of Rivalta; the parish church of Foliano; the parish church of Cereto; the parish church of Banio; the parish church of Herberie; the parish church of Prato, with the chapel of Saint Martin of the Rivo and its other chapels; the parish church of Bagnolo; the parish church of Camporotondo, with the chapel of Corrigia, etc.; the parish church of Curte Nova; the parish church of Nuvelaria; the church of Campagnola; the parish church of Fabrica, with the chapel of Razolo; the parish church of Saint Mary [Col. 1056B] of Novis; the church of Gargatella; the parish church of Saint Stephen, with the chapel of Saint Possidonius, etc.; the parish church of Quarantula; the parish church of Saint Martin in Spina, with the chapels of Gavello and Maneronta; the parish church of Ceriano, with the chapel of Mulla; the church of Gonzagha; the parish church of Villula; the parish church of Pigugnaca; the parish church of Bondeno de Runculis; the parish church of Bondeno Arduini; the parish church of Suzaria; the church of Lettobenano; the church of Polisino; the church of Cizola; the parish church of Luzaria, with the chapel of Satta and its other chapels; the parish church of Guardestalla, with its chapels; the monastery of Marola; and the monastery of Canusio.

By the authority of this present decree we likewise establish that all the boundaries of the bishopric of Reggio shall henceforth be preserved wholly peaceable and intact for you and your successors. Following also in the footsteps of our predecessor, Pope Urban of happy memory, we decree that in parish churches held by monks within your bishopric they shall, with your assent, install priests who, if suitable, receive from you the care of souls and render account to you concerning the parish churches; but they shall show due subjection to the monks in temporal matters, the authority of the apostolic see being preserved in all things. If anyone therefore in the future, ecclesiastical, etc.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. [Col. 1056D] I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Calixtus, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Lawrence and Damasus, have subscribed. I, Albert, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Peter, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Angelus, have subscribed. I, Cinthius, cardinal deacon of the Holy Roman Church, have subscribed.

### XLI. Privilege for the Church of Berchtesgaden. (1145, October 9.)

[HUND, *Metropolis of Salzburg*, II, 160.]

[Col. 1057A]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons HUGH, provost of the Church of Berchtesgaden, and his brethren, both present and future, to be regularly appointed in perpetuity.

A desire shown to pertain to the purpose of religion and the salvation of souls ought to be granted by us with willing mind, and fitting assistance should be bestowed upon the desires of those who ask. Yet we ought to devote ourselves with ampler charity to the petitions of those whose religious foundations are known to belong more especially to the right of the holy Roman Church. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions, and, following the example of our predecessors of happy memory, the Roman pontiffs Paschal, Calixtus, and Innocent, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid monastery of Saint Peter, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the privilege of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods that same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by the concession of pontiffs, the generosity of kings, the gifts of princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, by the Lord’s aid, acquire, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. [Col. 1057C] Among these we have thought fit to set down expressly: the wood adjoining Cella; Niderheim; Sconenberg; Flozze; and all else which Count Berengar and his son Gebehard gave to that place; whatever you lawfully possess in the eastern district; Tetensteten; and the other things which Engelwanus, Henry, and Bernard of Mosa, William of Huba, and their other neighbours reasonably bestowed upon you; Rotehoven with its appurtenances; Hebingen, with the other things which Charles and his brothers likewise gave you; also those things which Rodulph of Lungowe in the same manner bestowed upon you; Fronehoven and the other things which Wolf Trigel and his brother Tiemo gave you from their own right.

[Col. 1057D] We likewise decree that no person may alter in your Church the order of canonical life which you have professed according to the Rule of blessed Augustine. Nor may any member of your profession, at the prompting of frivolity or under pretext of a stricter religious life, leave the cloister without the permission of the provost or the community. If he does leave, no bishop, abbot, or monk shall receive him without security furnished by common letters, so long, namely, as the observance of the canonical order continues in force in your church, by the Lord’s favor. You shall receive ecclesiastical sacraments from the diocesan bishop, provided that he enjoys the grace and communion of the apostolic see and is willing to administer them freely and without impropriety. Otherwise, for receiving those same sacraments, you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer; supported by our authority, he shall grant what is requested.

Moreover, we altogether forbid the advocacy of your house to be seized, without the consent of the provost and brethren, either by the heirs of the founders or by any other persons. If he to whom it has been entrusted appears burdensome or useless to that Church, and, having been admonished a second or third time, does not reform, we grant you free authority to expel him and appoint another suitable person in his place. Further, no cleric or layperson whatsoever shall presume to demand tithes from you on the produce which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or from the nourishment of your animals. We decree that the settlement of the dispute which had existed between you and the canons of Bamberg, and which was reasonably concluded before our venerable brother Conrad, Archbishop of Salzburg, shall remain valid.

When you, the present provost of the same place, die or are transferred to the government of another Church, or when any of your successors dies or is transferred, no one shall be placed over the house by any craft of deception or violence, unless he is one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren, shall canonically provide to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Augustine. We also grant that the burial place of that house shall be free, so that no one may oppose the final will and devotion of those who have decided to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated; provided, however, that the right of the mother church is preserved.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may [Col. 1058C] rashly disturb the aforesaid Church, remove its goods or possessions, retain what has been removed, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but that all shall be preserved intact for the use and benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, the authority of the apostolic see and the canonical right of the Archbishop of Salzburg being preserved. As a token of this protection received from the apostolic see, you shall pay to us and our successors each year one gold bezant.

If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this charter of our constitution, shall rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been admonished a second or third time, does not amend the offence by fitting satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour, know himself or herself liable before divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, and be subject at the last judgment to severe vengeance. [Col. 1058D] But upon all who preserve what is right for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Calixtus, have subscribed. I, Hubald, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. [Col. 1059A] I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in Carcere Tulliano, have subscribed. I, Guido, unworthy minister of the altar in the Roman Church, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Angelus, have subscribed. I, Berard, cardinal deacon of the Holy Roman Church, have subscribed.

Given at Viterbo through the hand of Robert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the seventh day before the Ides of October, in the eighth indiction, in the year 1145 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### XLII. He receives the monastery of Saints Peter and Paul of Hadmersleben under protection and confirms its privileges and possessions. (1145, October 26.)

[The original is at Berlin in the possession of D. G. B. J. Friedlander, says JAFFÉ, *Regesta of the Roman Pontiffs*, p. 619.]

### XLIII. He entrusts to Aribert, cardinal priest, Gregory, bishop of Bergamo, and the abbot of the monastery of Astino the investigation of the dispute between the canons of Saint Alexander and Saint Vincent. (1145, October 28.)

[LUPI, *Diplomatic Codex of Bergamo*, II, 1061.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brothers A[RIBERT], cardinal priest, and G[REGORY], bishop of Bergamo, and to his beloved son [Col. 1059C] the abbot of Astino: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The canons of Saint Vincent have complained to us that the canons of Saint Alexander do not observe those things which have been established by the apostolic see between the former and the canons of Saint Alexander, and confirmed by the privileges of our predecessors. Although they persist in discord contrary to our wishes, we nevertheless willingly devote ourselves, as the duty of our office requires, to their peace. By these apostolic letters we command you to assemble together, summon both parties before you, and diligently investigate and ascertain the claims and grounds of each party, both concerning the privileges and concerning the other complaints. You are to report the truth of the matter to us as quickly as possible by your letters. [Col. 1059D] But if the aforesaid cardinal cannot be present, you nevertheless shall hear the case in the manner stated above and notify us, as we have said.

Given at Viterbo, on the fifth day before the Kalends of November.

### XLIV. Confirmation or renewal, and new grant, of privileges to the monastery of Saint John the Evangelist, in the diocese of Parma, of the Cassinese Order. (1145, October 31.)

[MARGARINI, *Cassinese Bullarium*, II, 165.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son GUIDO, abbot of the monastery of Saint John, situated in the city of Parma, and to his successors to be regularly promoted in perpetuity.

[Col. 1060A] Since without the cult of true religion neither can the unity of charity endure nor service pleasing to God be rendered, it befits apostolic authority to love religious persons and to foster under the protection of the apostolic see the places in which they devote themselves to divine offices. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Guido, we graciously assent to your reasonable petitions and, following in the footsteps of our predecessor Pope Paschal of happy memory, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the church of Saint John, to whose government you have been assigned, and fortify it by the charter of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods the aforesaid monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by the grant of pontiffs, gifts of kings or [Col. 1060B] princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to set down expressly by name: in the same diocese of Parma, the church of Saint Stephen in the borough; the church of Saint Michael of Arcu; the church of Saint Stephen of Torano; the church of Saint Lawrence of Casella with its estate; the church of Saint Sabinus with its estate; the church of Saint Lawrence of Ramuscello; the castle of Ramuscello with its church; the castle of Saint Vitalis with its church and estate; the church of Saint John of Petrignano; the church of Saint Sylvester of Gambaletico; the church of Gainaco; the church of Saint Sylvester of Insula; the church of Saint Saviour of Sanguineo with its castle and estate; [Col. 1060C] two parts of the estate of Sacca and what is held in the church of the same place; the church of Saint Justina; the churches of Saint Prosper and Saint Anastasius in that same city; the church of Saint James at the bridgehead; the church of Saint Peter of the borough of Saint Domninus; the church of Provinciano; the church of Saint Matthew of Callio; the church of Saint Melanus with half the borough and four houses; the church of Paterno with its castle and estate; the church of Saint Michael of Filino; and whatever you possess in the church of Saint George of Pratis; the church of Saint Lucy of Cavagnano. In the diocese of Cremona, the church of Saint Justin of Delmona with all its appurtenances. In the diocese of Reggio, [Col. 1060D] the church of Saint Michael of Fossa. In the diocese of Luni, the church of Saint John and the church of Cavallana. In the diocese of Pistoia, the monastery of Saint Bartholomew with the church of Saint Mary outside the gate called the Gate of Lucca, the church of Saint George beyond the river Simbrona, the church of Saint Romanus, and the church of Saint Benedict of Massiano, with their estates and all their appurtenances; the church of Capitana with its estates and appurtenances; the church of Saint Bartholomew of Trivallo with its estate and all its appurtenances; the church of Saint Domninus of Smapolis with its estate and all its appurtenances; the church of Saint Angelus in the valley of Nebula with all their appurtenances; and the church of Saint Martin of Madia. We likewise confirm to you the tithes of the bishops of Parma granted to your monastery.

[Col. 1061A] Concerning those lands belonging to your monastery, wherever they may be, which are newly cultivated and which had not been cultivated for sixty, fifty, or forty years, or less, no one shall dare to claim tithes against you from their produce. We also prohibit the exaction of tithes on the produce which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or from the nourishment of your animals.

We grant permission to any free person who wishes to come to you and take the religious habit. We also grant that the burial place of that house shall be free, and no one shall obstruct the devotion and final will of those who decide to be buried there, unless they happen to be excommunicated. With respect to your monks and clerics, we grant you, your successors, and the priors of your monasteries leave to have hands laid upon them for ordination by whichever bishop you choose, provided that he is Catholic. We forbid anyone to elect an abbot in that monastery from outside monasteries unless the counsel and assent of the better and greater part of the brethren of the monastery of Saint John has been obtained. [Col. 1061B] No bishop or parish priest, wherever your churches may be, shall dare to introduce or remove any cleric in them without your consent and that of the priors established in various places. Likewise, no bishop shall dare to consecrate a church declared to belong by right to your monastery without the permission and invitation of the abbots of the monastery of Saint John and of the priors appointed in different places. We forbid all persons absolutely to presume to prohibit divine service in your chapels, wherever they may be, or to oppose the burial of those who wish to be buried there. We likewise altogether forbid all bishops and the persons subject to them to diminish, wherever they are known to be located, the honour or any goods belonging to you by right. If anyone attempts this and is known to persist in such obstinacy, we confidently grant you and your priors leave to appeal to the apostolic see.

We therefore decree that no person, cleric or lay, may rashly disturb the same monastery of Saint John of Parma, or any of the monasteries subject to it; remove [Col. 1061D] its possessions, retain what has been removed, diminish them, or harass or afflict it by reckless vexations. Rather, all shall be preserved intact for the use and benefit in every way of those for whose support and governance they were granted. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowing this charter of our constitution, shall rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been admonished a second or third time, does not make amends by fitting satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour, know himself or herself liable before divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, and be subject at the last judgment to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve what is right for that place may there be the peace [Col. 1062A] of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Ubald, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Nicholas, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cyriacus, have subscribed. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Hyacinth, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin, have subscribed. I, Jordan, cardinal deacon [Col. 1062B] of the Holy Roman Church, have subscribed.

Given at Viterbo through the hand of Robert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the second day before the Kalends of November, in the eighth indiction, in the year 1145 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### XLV. He confirms the possessions and privileges of the monastery of Molesme. (1145, November 18.)

[MABILLON, *Benedictine Annals*, VI, 392.]

At that time Gerald, or Giraud, abbot of Molesme, successor of Guido, had governed Molesme for five years. This year he obtained from Eugenius a most extensive privilege. In it are confirmed and enumerated all [Col. 1062C] the monastery’s possessions, churches, and dependent houses, including four monasteries of nuns dependent upon Molesme: two, indeed, in the diocese of Langres—Saint Mary near Jully and Saint Sulpicius near Oze; and likewise two in the diocese of Châlons—namely Andesisis (Andecies) and Blessed Mary of Valle-Onae. Given at Viterbo through the hand of Robert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of December, in the ninth indiction, in the year 1145 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of Lord Eugenius III’s pontificate.

The Robert, chancellor, who wrote these letters is Robert Pullus, an Englishman renowned for learning and writings, whom Bernard says (*Ep.* 362) was appointed as Eugenius’s assistant before his election. Bernard retained him at Paris, when he was not yet a cardinal, [Col. 1062D] a matter which offended the bishop of Rochester. The holy man placated him by letter (*Ep.* 203), praising Robert’s sound doctrine and valuing his writings highly.

### XLVI. He commands the bishops of Siena, Volterra, Florence, Lucca, and Luni not to permit obstruction of those who resort for prayer to the altar of blessed James the apostle, who works miracles in the church of Pistoia. (1145, November 22.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia Sacra*, III, 298.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brothers the bishops of Siena, Volterra, Florence, Lucca, and Luni: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We believe that there has come to your knowledge what great and numerous signs of miracles the almighty Lord has chosen at this time to display, through the merits of the blessed apostle James, at his sacred altar in the church of Pistoia. For this reason faithful people have begun to gather at that venerable place from diverse and distant parts of the earth, out of devotion and in search of remedies for their salvation. It is therefore fitting for Christian believers, especially those nearby, to give thanks to our Redeemer for so great a benefit bestowed, and faithfully to render to the blessed apostle James the services of devotion due to him. We therefore command and strictly enjoin you by apostolic letters to admonish your people and parishioners that they must not, on any pretext, impede men or women, wherever they may come from, who journey to so sacred an oratory for devotion and prayer; nor may they presume to inflict upon them any inconvenience or disturbance. [Col. 1063B] If any dare to do so, you shall publicly declare them excommunicated as sacrilegious persons and violators of the Truce of God; and you shall ensure that this same sentence of excommunication is firmly observed throughout your parishes until they have made satisfaction.

Given at Viterbo, on the tenth day before the Kalends of December, in the year 1145.

### XLVII. He grants an indulgence to those devoted to blessed James. (1145, November 22.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia Sacra*, III, 298.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to all God’s faithful who devoutly visit the oratory of blessed James the apostle, situated in the church of Pistoia: [Col. 1063C] greeting and apostolic blessing.

The ineffable greatness of divine mercy, which wills all people to be saved and to come to knowledge of the truth, has displayed at the most sacred altar of the blessed apostle James in the church of Pistoia many striking kinds of various miracles, for the compunction of the faithful. For, as we have learned from the testimony of our venerable brother Atto, devout bishop of that city, and many others, the blind, the lame, the crippled, and others weakened by various illnesses receive at that place, through the prayers and merits of the blessed James, as we have said, the remedies of health that they desire.

We therefore, giving thanks to almighty God for so great a manifestation of divine grace, have judged it fitting that Christian believers who devoutly visit the aforesaid venerable place out of piety may deserve to obtain from us some remission of their sins. Accordingly, trusting in the merits of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul and of that same James, we establish by apostolic authority that all who visit the aforesaid venerable oratory for devotion and prayer may rejoice that they have received an indulgence of seven days from the penance imposed upon them.

Given at Viterbo, on the tenth day before the Kalends of December.

### XLVIII. To Louis, king of the French—On undertaking an expedition to the Holy Land.  
[Note: Boczek published this letter in *Codex diplomaticus Moraviae*, I, 241, but addressed to all God’s faithful established throughout Gaul and dated at Trastevere, [Col. 1064D] on the Kalends of March 1146. We record the variants of the readings. EDITOR.] (1145, December 1.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 626.]

[Col. 1064A]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his dearest son LOUIS, illustrious and glorious king of the Franks, and to his beloved sons the princes and all God’s faithful established throughout Gaul: greeting and apostolic blessing.

From the accounts of the ancients and from what we find written in their deeds, we have learned how greatly our predecessors, the Roman pontiffs, laboured for the liberation of the Eastern Church. For our predecessor Pope Urban of happy memory sounded like a trumpet and took care to summon the children of the holy Roman Church from diverse parts of the world for its deliverance. At his call, the Transalpine warriors, especially the very strong and valiant men of the kingdom of the Franks, and those also from Italy, inflamed with the ardour of charity, assembled. Having gathered a very great army, and not without great shedding of their own blood, with divine assistance accompanying them, they liberated from the filth of pagans that city in which our Saviour chose to suffer for us and left us his glorious tomb as a memorial of his passion, as well as very many other places which, to avoid prolixity, we refrain from naming. Through the grace of God and the exertions of your fathers, who over successive periods strove according to their strength to defend these places [Col. 1064C] and extend the Christian name in those regions, they remained in Christian hands until our times; and the Christians also courageously stormed other cities of the unbelievers.

But now, because of the sins of ourselves and of that people—what we cannot say without great grief and lamentation—the city of Edessa, called Rohais in our language, which, it is said, when formerly all the land in the East was held by pagans, alone remained under Christian power in service to the Lord, has been captured by the enemies of Christ’s cross, and many Christian castles have been occupied by them. The archbishop of that city, together with his clergy, and many other Christians were killed there; [Col. 1064D] and relics of the saints were handed over to be trampled by unbelievers and scattered. We both understand the magnitude of the danger thereby threatening the Church of God and all Christendom, and do not believe that it escapes your prudence. For it is recognized as the greatest proof of nobility and worth that the gains acquired by the valour of fathers should be valiantly defended by you their sons. But if, God forbid, the contrary should occur, the courage of the fathers will be shown to have diminished in the sons.

Therefore we admonish, beseech, and command all of you in the Lord, and impose it upon you for the remission of sins, that those who belong to God, especially the more powerful and noble, should gird themselves manfully to confront the multitude of unbelievers, which almost always rejoices [Col. 1065A] at having gained victory over us [Note: Mansi: “which rejoices that it has gained the time of victory over us”], and should strive so to defend the Eastern Church, liberated from their tyranny by the shedding of so much of your fathers’ blood, as we have said, and to rescue many thousands of our captive brothers from their hands, that the dignity of the Christian name may increase in your time and your courage, praised throughout the whole world, may be preserved whole and unimpaired. Let that good Mattathias also be your example: for the preservation of his ancestral laws he did not hesitate to expose himself, with his sons and parents, to death and to leave behind whatever he possessed in the world; and at last, with divine aid cooperating, though only after many labours, he and his offspring valiantly triumphed over their enemies.

We, providing with paternal solicitude for your security and for the destitution of that same Church, grant and confirm by the authority given us by God to those who resolve, out of devotion, to undertake and complete so holy and necessary a work and labour that remission of sins which our aforesaid predecessor Pope Urban instituted. We decree, moreover, that their wives and children, and also their goods and possessions, shall remain under the protection of the holy Church, of ourselves, and of the archbishops, bishops, and other prelates of the Church of God. [Col. 1065C]

By apostolic authority we also forbid any claim henceforth to be raised concerning anything which they have peacefully possessed when they take the cross, until it is certainly known whether they have returned or died.

Furthermore, because those who serve the Lord in arms ought not to concern themselves with costly garments, elegant adornment, dogs, hawks, or other things that display frivolity, we admonish your prudence in the Lord that those who resolve to undertake so holy a work must by no means occupy themselves with colourful or grey furs, or with golden or silver arms, but must exert all their effort and diligence upon such arms, [Note: Mansi: “those who resolve to do so should not attend to these things, but to arms, etc.”] horses, and other things by which to fight the unbelievers.

[Col. 1065D] Whoever is burdened by debt and begins so holy a journey with a pure heart shall not pay interest accrued in the past. If they themselves, or others on their behalf, are bound by oath or pledged faith on account of interest, we absolve them by apostolic authority.

It shall also be lawful for them, once their relatives or lords to whose fief they belong have been notified and have either refused or been unable to lend money, freely to mortgage their lands or other possessions to churches, ecclesiastical persons, or other faithful persons, without any objection.

In accordance with the ordinance of our aforesaid predecessor, by the authority given us by God of almighty God and of blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, we grant such remission and absolution of sins that whoever devoutly begins and completes so holy a journey, or dies there, shall obtain absolution from all sins of which, with contrite and humbled heart, he has made confession, [Col. 1066A] and shall receive from the rewarder of all the fruit of everlasting recompense.

Given at Vetralla, on the Kalends of December.

### XLIX. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Stephen of Freising. (1145, December 7.)

[*Monumenta Boica*, IX, 501.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons SIGMAR, abbot of the monastery of Saint Stephen [Col. 1066B] of Freising, and his successors and brethren, both present and future, who profess the regular life, in perpetuity: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Because without the worship of true religion neither can the unity of charity endure, nor can service pleasing to God be rendered, it is fitting for apostolic authority to cherish religious persons and, with the Lord’s help, to provide for their peace. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we assent to your just petitions and receive the aforesaid monastery of Saint Stephen, in which you are devoted to divine service, under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing; decreeing that whatever possessions you now justly and canonically hold, or may hereafter be able to acquire, by the grant of pontiffs, the liberality of kings, the generosity of princes, the offerings of the faithful, or by other lawful means, through the Lord’s favour, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names: the monastery of Blessed Stephen, with its possessions and all its appurtenances; the churches, tithes, estates, and benefices of ministeriales which have been reasonably granted and given to you by our venerable brother Otto, bishop of Freising, and by his predecessors; the exchanges which have been reasonably granted and concluded between you and the same your bishop concerning Voltisigen, and others.

Moreover, we prohibit anyone, after making profession, from presuming to leave that monastery without the permission of the abbot and his brethren. We also grant that the burial-place of that same house shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who have resolved to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated, without prejudice to the rights of the mother church. Certainly, no cleric or layperson shall presume to exact tithes from you on the produce which you cultivate with your own hands, or from the sustenance of your animals. But upon the death of you, the present abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, let no one be set over it by any craft of fraud or violence, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren, according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Benedict, shall have judged to be elected.

[Col. 1067A] Therefore we decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb this place, or to take away its possessions, or retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass them with any vexations; but that all things be preserved whole for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they have been granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right and reverence due to the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing the text of this our constitution, shall rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been admonished a second and third time, does not correct his fault by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and honour, and know himself or herself liable before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let that person be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, and be subject, at the last judgment, to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of the same place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.

I, Humbaldus, priest-cardinal of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed, etc.

Given at Vetralla through the hand of Sabert [Robert], priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the seventh day before the Ides of December, indiction 9, in the year 1145 of the Lord’s Incarnation [Col. 1067C], in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

## L. Privilege for the monastery of Locus Restauratus (“the Restored Place”). (A.D. 1145, December 13.)

[Hugo, *Annales Praemonstratenses*, II, preface, 41.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to HAIMO, abbot of Locus Restauratus, and to his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, for ever.

Because without the worship of true religion neither can the unity of charity endure nor service pleasing to God be rendered, it is fitting for apostolic authority to cherish religious persons and, with the Lord’s help, to provide for their peace. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions and receive the aforesaid place, in which you are devoted to divine service, under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing; decreeing that whatever possessions and whatever goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may hereafter be able to acquire, by grant of pontiffs, liberality of kings, generosity of princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, through the Lord’s favour, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

From the gift of Count Ralph: arable land at Bonolio belonging to his demesne; likewise the *terragium* which he possessed there, on the condition that, if the peasants cease to cultivate it, it shall freely revert to your ownership; also pastures, uncultivated land, and the course of water for making a mill, while retaining for his succession the holdings and rents thereon; the church of Beriniac, which was conveyed to you through the hand of Manasses, bishop of Meaux, with the count’s consent and at his request; the tithe of Sineis (Seigneux), which the same count redeemed from the knights who held it in fee and which was granted to you through the hand of Peter, bishop of Senlis; the tithe of Burfantency; a third part of the tithe of Vamosey; the wood of Saint Medard, granted to you subject to an annual rent of seven and a half solidi payable to the monastery of Saint Medard; and the estate of Monte Bosonis (Morcourt), with its appurtenances.

[Col. 1068B] Certainly, no cleric or layperson whatsoever shall presume to exact from you tithes on the produce which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or on the sustenance of your animals. Therefore we decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid place, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass them with any vexations; but all things shall be preserved whole, for the benefit in every respect of those for whose governance and support they have been granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right and reverence due to the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowing the text of this our constitution, shall rashly attempt to act against it and, having been admonished a second or third time, does not correct that person’s fault by fitting satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and honour, and know himself or herself liable before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let that person be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ, and be subject at the last judgment to severe vengeance. But on all who preserve the rights of the same place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

[Col. 1068D] I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Guido, priest-cardinal of Saint Chrysogonus. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia. I, Rainerius, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Prisca. I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum. I, John, cardinal-deacon of Saint Adrian. I, Guido, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints Lawrence and Damasus.

Given at Verullae [Note: [Col. 1067D] Read “Vetrallae,” Vetralla. Jaffé.] through the hand of Robert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the said Roman Church, on the Ides of December, indiction 8, in the year 1145 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

## LI. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Remigius at Rheims. (A.D. 1145, December 14.)

[Varin, *Archives administratives de Reims*, I, I, 341, from the cartulary of Saint Remigius, p. 14.—Cartulary A of Saint Remigius, p. 6.]

[Col. 1069A]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons EDON, abbot of the monastery of Saint Remigius at Rheims, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, for perpetual remembrance.

[lacuna] Beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions and receive the aforesaid monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service, under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing; decreeing [Col. 1069B] that whatever possessions and whatever goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may hereafter be able to acquire by grant of pontiffs, liberality of kings, generosity of princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, through the Lord’s favour, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The very castle in which blessed Remigius is believed to rest, with every immunity and liberty granted to you by the kings of the Franks and confirmed by their charters, and with all its appurtenances; the borough outside it, with all jurisdiction and authority; likewise half the toll, market-charge, and road-toll; also the *minaticum* of the borough, with everything belonging to it, except five modii of grain which are annually paid by that church to the archbishop of Rheims for half of that *minaticum*, as was approved and confirmed by our predecessor Pope Innocent of happy memory, through the settlement and ordinance of the venerable persons G., bishop of Chartres and then legate of the Apostolic See, Joscelin of Soissons, Geoffrey of Châlons, A. of Arras, bishops, and Bernard, abbot of Clairvaux, and Hugh, abbot of Pontigny, between Archbishop Renaud and Abbot Odo; the market from the feast of Saint Celinia, mother of blessed Remigius, until the vigil of the apostles Simon and Jude.

In the diocese of Rheims: the church of the holy martyrs Timothy and Apollinaris, with all belonging to it; [Col. 1069D] the church of Saint Julian, without a personal benefice; Satiacum with its church; Colunnas with its church; Genevereyum, Sarpeicurt, Dussellum, Grauhenna, Corbiniacum with their appurtenances; Gerson; the church of Saint Mary in the borough of Regiteste, with its appurtenances, namely the church of Viniac [variant: Viniacri], the church of Avention, the church of Barbeium, the church of Pertis, and the church of Tennion, with everything belonging to those churches; Erpeium with its church; Villare of Saint Remigius with its church; Salix of Saint Remigius and Roseium with their churches; the basilica, estate, island, and Pumachem with their churches; Baina, Nocerium, and Moscherium with their churches; Villare in the wood; Condatum with its church; Gehennevilla and [Col. 1070A] Poaria with their churches; the cell of Caniacum and Alendusium with their churches; Bairona, Pont Bairi, and Tassiacum with their churches; Tassiacum, Hermundivilla, Crusniacum, and Serzeium with their churches.

In the personal benefice: Irbroys (Braux, marginal note of the cartulary), with its church; Villare with its church; Beloium with its church; Aisencella with its church; Furneium, Valerias, and Lupincont with their churches.

In the diocese of Laon: Moncellum with its church.

In the diocese of Arras: the church of Saint John the Baptist of Hosdan with its appurtenances; Beldin with its church; the altar of Monci; the chapel of Lueres.

In the diocese of Meaux: Nelis with its church, with complete liberty.

In the diocese of Avignon: the church of Saint Martin and half the village called [Col. 1070B] Saint-Remigius.

In the diocese of Aix: the church of Saint Martin of Triola; the church of Saint Martin of Marcilliana; the church of Saint Mary of Ventebran; the church of Saint Michael of Finistella, now called Volta, with its appurtenances.

In the diocese of Liège: Lucarna with its church and appurtenances; the chapel of Ambe; the chapel of Squincorte; the chapel of Heustan and of Bunna; Sclumanz with its church; the church of Squina; the church of Olobergis; Litta with its church and appurtenances; Covorna, Retinas, and Angledura with their appurtenances.

In the diocese of Mainz: Coslam with its churches and appurtenances; the church of Blessed Martin in the village of Saint Remigius, as it was adjudged to you by our predecessor [lacuna] Pope Calixtus and confirmed by his charter, together with half of that village; the church of Marsna, as granted to you by our predecessor [lacuna] Pope Innocent; furthermore, the judgment reasonably rendered between the matron Gisela and the church of Blessed Remigius by J., bishop of Soissons, M., bishop of Thérouanne, and other honourable persons, in the presence of Samson, archbishop of Rheims.

[Col. 1070C] Moreover, we prohibit anyone from presuming, without your consent, to build a new church or chapel within your parishes to the detriment of your ancient churches. We decree that all churches known to belong by right to the same monastery shall remain free from every personal succession. Therefore we decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid monastery, to take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass them by any other vexations; but that all things be preserved whole, for the benefit in every respect of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the archbishop’s canonical right. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowing the text of this our constitution, shall rashly attempt to act against it and, having been admonished a second or third time, does not make amends by fitting satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and honour, and know himself or herself liable before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let that person be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ and be subject at the last judgment [Col. 1071A] to severe vengeance. But on all who preserve what is just for the same place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have signed. I, Guido, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Chrysogonus, have subscribed. I, Rainerius, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Prisca, have subscribed. I, Julius, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Marcellus, have subscribed. I, Nicholas, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Cyriacus, have subscribed. [Col. 1071B] I, Wido, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints Lawrence and Damasus, have subscribed. I, Ubaldus, priest-cardinal of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Villanus, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill, have subscribed. I, Aribertus, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Anastasia, have subscribed. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum, have subscribed. I, Odo, cardinal-deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, John, cardinal-deacon of Saint Adrian, have subscribed. I, Hyacinth, deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin, have subscribed. I, Jordan, cardinal-deacon of the Roman Church, have subscribed. [Col. 1071C] I, Cinthius, cardinal-deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed.

Given at Vetralla through the hand of Robert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the Kalends of January [Note: [Col. 1071D] Read: the nineteenth day before the Kalends of January], indiction 9 [Note: [Col. 1071D] This indiction has been altered in the two cartularies of Saint-Remi. What we believe we read was *indict. VIIII*; the X was erased and a V substituted, so as to make VIIII.], in the year 1145 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

## LII. Privilege granted to the Carthusians of Mont-Dieu. (A.D. 1145, December 16.)

[Marlot, *Metropolis Remensis*, II, 314.]

[Note: [Col. 1072D] The words “and Saint John the Baptist” are added in this bull; they are absent from Innocent II’s bull for the same monastery, because the church of Mont-Dieu had in the preceding year been dedicated by Samson to the Blessed Virgin and Saint John.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons in Christ, the brethren of Saint Mary and Saint John the Baptist of Mont-Dieu, serving Christ, [Col. 1071D] present and future, professing the regular life, for ever.

It is fitting that we gladly grant a request which is known to pertain to the purpose of religion and the salvation of souls, and afford suitable support to the desires of petitioners. Therefore, beloved sons in God, wishing with paternal solicitude to provide for your peace, we receive the aforesaid monastery of the Blessed Mother of God, in which you are devoted to divine service, under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and fortify it by the privilege of this present [Col. 1072A] writing; decreeing that the monastic order according to the Rule of blessed Benedict, and likewise the rule and institutions of the Carthusian brethren, shall be kept there inviolably for all time.

Moreover, we confirm to you and your successors by the text of this present writing the place itself, and whatever has been bestowed upon you by lawful means in lands, woods, waters, pastures, or other things by Odo, abbot of the Church of Blessed Remigius and founder of your monastery; Ursio, abbot of Saint-Denis; Richard, abbot of Mouzon; Nicholas of Bourg; William of Seton; Guido of Altrey, knights; or other faithful of God; and whatever shall hereafter, God being propitious, be bestowed. We have also thought fit to specify the boundaries of the place by their own markers: namely, from Mont-Dieu itself, etc., [Col. 1072B] as in the bull of Innocent of the year 1136, no. 246, *Patrologia*, vol. CLXXIX.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia. I, Odo, cardinal-deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Guido, cardinal of the title of Saint Chrysogonus. I, Raynerius, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Prisca. I, Hyacinth, deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Jordanus, cardinal of the Roman Church. I, Cinthius, cardinal-deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Julius, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint [Col. 1072C] Marcellus.

Given at Vetralla through the hand of Robert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of January, indiction 8, in the year 1145 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

## LIII. Privilege for the monastery of Belleval. (A.D. 1145.)

[Hugo, *Annales Praemonstratenses*, I, 207.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons PHILIP, abbot of Belleval, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, for ever.

It is fitting that we gladly grant protection which is known to pertain to the purpose of religion or the salvation of souls, and afford suitable support to the desires of petitioners. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your petitions and receive the aforesaid place, in which you are devoted to divine service, under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing; decreeing that whatever goods that place now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter be able to acquire through grants of pontiffs, generosity of kings [Col. 1073A] or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

Namely, the place which was called Wamelis and is now called Belleval, with all its appurtenances, which Alwidis, abbess of the church of Saint Peter at Avenay, by the common consent and counsel of her entire chapter, granted to you and your successors subject to an annual rent of one pound of wax; the place called Orvans, with all its appurtenances and with every tithe, according to the grant and confirmation of Renaud, archbishop of Rheims; the land which Simon Taschet and his brother Elias gave you; the place called Dulnch, with all its appurtenances; the mill beside the village of Noaz, which Renaud the knight and all his heirs gave you; half of the place called Lunasnils, given to you by Hugh and his brother of Sacey, and Wamherus and his brother of Salmoncey; the place called Fosreth, given to you by Bartholomew and Renaud of Grandpré, and the sons of Warin of Urcisci and his wives [lacuna] of Briola and his wife and their sons; the place called Anementh with all its appurtenances, and all that the church of Mouzon possessed within its boundaries, whether in tithes or in any uses, all of which Abbot Richard, by the common counsel and consent of his entire chapter, granted and conveyed to you to possess in perpetuity, subject to an annual rent of one modius of grain [Col. 1073C] according to the measure of Mouzon; mills on the Meuse; the land which Herbert Lupus and his wife and daughters gave you, and that which Roger, his wife Oldiardis, and their heirs gave you; the place called Crissen, which Haylidis of Grandpré and her son John, her brothers and sisters, and Warnerus of Brixey and his heirs gave you, with all its appurtenances; mills on the Aisne, fishing rights, and sufficient use of the wood for building and burning.

Everything which John and Walter of Brixey possessed in the tithe of the aforesaid place, and everything possessed there by the church of Saint-Denis, Ursio, abbot of that place, by the common counsel of his chapter, granted to you subject to an annual rent of three Rheims solidi; fishing rights and land at Asne adjoining Crissey, which Elias and his son of Bourg gave you, a fourth part of which land Odola, her husband Haricus, and her son gave you; and the land which Renaud of Grandpré gave you; the land which Guido of Saint Mary gave you; and meadows and the place called Fontenelles, with all its appurtenances. The gift and reasonable agreement concerning the mills on the Aisne, between [lacuna], which Odo, abbot of Saint Remigius, made with you by the common counsel of his chapter, according to the terms of the common chirograph of both churches. Also the chapel situated on the river Arne [Col. 1074A] and the house [lacuna], with everything belonging to it, and the land which Dudo of Diona gave you subject to a rent of ten sextarii of grain.

Certainly, no cleric or layperson whatsoever shall presume to exact tithes from you on the produce you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or on the sustenance of your animals. We also decree that the canonical order according to the Rule of Saint Augustine and the reasonable institutions of the Premonstratensian brethren shall be reasonably preserved there for all time; and that no brother or lay brother, after making profession, may leave that cloister without the permission of the abbot and the whole chapter, while no one shall dare to retain one who has left.

Therefore we decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever [Col. 1074B] rashly to disturb the aforesaid place, to take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass them with any vexations; but that all things be preserved whole, for the benefit in every respect of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing the text of this our constitution, shall rashly attempt to act against it, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and honour, know himself or herself liable before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ, and be subject at the last judgment [Col. 1074C] to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve what is right for the same place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Guido, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Prisca. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia. I, Ramerus [Raynerius], priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Prisca. I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum. I, Guido, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints Lawrence and Damasus. I, John, cardinal-deacon of the title of Saint Adrian.

Given at Vetralla through the hand of Robert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman [Col. 1074D] Church, on the eighteenth day before the Kalends of December [Note: [Col. 1073D] The chronological data are corrupt. Jaffé.], indiction 8, in the year 1145 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

## LIV. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Mary of Cuissy. (A.D. 1145.)

[Hugo, *Annales Praemonstratenses*, I, part I, p. 68.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons LUKE, abbot of the church of Saint Mary of Cuissy, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, for ever.

[Col. 1075A] The authority of our office exhorts us to cherish religious persons with paternal affection and to foster their places by the protection of the Apostolic See. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions and receive the aforesaid Church of the Blessed Mother of God and ever-Virgin Mary, in which you are devoted to divine service, under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing; decreeing that whatever possessions and whatever goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may hereafter be able to acquire by grant of pontiffs, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, through the Lord’s favour, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit [Col. 1075B] to specify the following by their proper names:

Namely, a third part of the tithe of Vassonia; the wood called Chabrel, with the adjacent cultivated and uncultivated land belonging to that wood; the *vinagium*—a levy on wine as well as on your other goods—which Count Hugh of Roucy and his wife Ricantia gave you; the land of Gerard and Drogo of Curi, purchased from them and donated to you by Bartholomew, bishop of Laon; the meadow adjoining the river called Ausona; fishing rights for two boats, given you by Bertrand and Peter, sons of Roger of Maisy; a third part of the tithe of Apelli, canonically granted to you with the assent of Simon, bishop of Noyon; the alms granted to you by Hugh Furnerius at the place called Chanetencurt and at another place called Noerellus; the benefice of Godo, likewise conferred on you by Godo, which is called the Lord’s Vineyard; the field of Gaher, with two parts of the tithe of that same allod; the cultivated land adjoining your grange; two meadows; a third part of the tithe of Geniac; a third part of the tithe of Ulliac, with all its appurtenances.

The estate of Altavilla; the altar of the same village; the altar of Son; the estate of Gland; the estate of Segniac, with all its appurtenances; the estate of Eurisis; the altar of the same village; the estate of Longavalle; a fourth part of the village called Disiacus, given by Ralph; the land beside the aforesaid village, which you purchased from Goswin, castellan of Pierrepont, together with the adjacent wood for all your necessary uses; vineyards in [Col. 1075D] the village called Arsy; the estate of Saint Aldebert, with all its appurtenances; the estate of Roez, with all its appurtenances; three mills in the valley below Commi; five mills situated in the valley of Juminiac; the mill below Cerniac; half of a certain mill which you hold in the village called Ambliniac; there certain *vinagia*; two parts of the wood which Bartholomew, bishop of Laon, bestowed upon you, one part lying below Boconvilla and the other above Vallemclara. By gift of Louis, king of the French, whatever has lawfully been given to you from his fief. Certainly, no cleric or layperson whatsoever shall presume to exact from you tithes on the produce which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or on the sustenance of your animals.

[Col. 1076A] Therefore we decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb your aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass them with any vexations; but that all things be preserved whole, for the benefit in every respect of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right and reverence due to the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing the text of this our constitution, shall rashly attempt to act against it, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and honour, know himself or herself liable before divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God [Col. 1076B] and of our Lord Jesus Christ, and be subject at the last judgment to severe vengeance. But on all who preserve their rights for the same place may there be the peace of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia. I, Ismarus, bishop of Tusculum. I, Raynerus, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Prisca. I, Hubaldus, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Praxedis. I, Nicholas, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Cyriacus. I, Hubaldus, priest-cardinal of the title of Holy Cross in [Col. 1076C] Jerusalem. I, William, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, John, cardinal-deacon of Saint Adrian. I, Jordan, cardinal-deacon of the Roman Church.

Given at Vetralla through the hand of Robert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, in the year 1145 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

## LV. He commands archbishops and bishops to bless elected provosts of the Premonstratensian order as abbots without delay. (A.D. 1145, December 18.)

[Le Paige, *Bibliotheca Praemonstratensis*, 626.]

[Col. 1076D] EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brethren, the archbishops and bishops to whom these letters shall come: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The religious brethren of the Premonstratensian order, by God’s grace, are advancing in religious life and, by the example of their good conduct, turn many persons devoted to the pleasures and carnal desires of this present age toward right living. It is therefore fitting that good prelates of churches should endeavour to assist them, foster them in so holy a purpose, and provide them aid and counsel in their needs. As we have learned, they have determined by common counsel, not through ambition but for the fuller observance of religion, to make the provosts of their houses abbots. Therefore, by these apostolic letters we command you that, when they are presented to you by the abbot of Prémontré, or by his letters, together with the brethren whom they are to govern, you shall invoke the grace of the Holy Spirit and bless them as abbots.

Given at Sutri, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of January, in the first year of our pontificate.

## LVI. Privilege for the church of Saint John the Evangelist at Ravenna. (A.D. 1145, December 24.)

[Fantuzzi, *Monumenta Ravennatia*, V, 285.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons RODULF, abbot of the monastery of Saint John the Evangelist situated in the city of Ravenna, and to his [Col. 1077B] brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, for ever.

In the governance of the apostolic see, placed there by the Lord’s disposition, it is fitting that we heed with due kindness the prayers of religious persons and preserve the justice of the churches in which they are known to serve God, so that, just as we are called Fathers in name, we may likewise be shown to be such in deed. For this reason, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service, strengthening it by the protection of this present writing; decreeing that whatever possessions and goods you now justly and canonically [Col. 1077C] possess, or may hereafter, by the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings, the liberality of princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, acquire by the Lord’s favour, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names: the parish church of Saint Martin at Barisano; moreover, all the possessions and appurtenances which are known to belong by proprietary right to your monastery in that same parish; the church of Saint Mary at Grezi, with all its appurtenances; the parish church of Polenta, with all its chapels and appurtenances; whatever you possess in the diocese of Faenza; the church of Saint Nicholas at Taurese, with all its appurtenances; the church [Col. 1077D] of Saint Gervasius, with all its appurtenances on both sides of the river; the church of Blessed Mary on the seashore at Rimini, and all possessions and appurtenances which you justly hold in that city or in its diocese; the parish church of Saint Mary at Bonta, with all possessions belonging to you by right in that parish; the church of Saint John the Evangelist at Capo Sandali, with the riverbank as far as the middle of the river; whatever you possess at Massa di Navegalicio; on the bank of Persico; in the parish of Saint Mary at Porto; at the allotment of Mauro; at Romolago; on the estate of Tethro; at the port of Vethraria; at Viguenza; at Ducentula; at Quartizana; and at Limbaula.

[Col. 1078A] We further confirm to you and your successors the ordering and administration of the aforesaid parish churches with their chapels, as they were reasonably granted by the bishops in whose dioceses your churches are situated and confirmed by their writings. We therefore decree that absolutely no person may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the apostolic see and the canonical right of the diocesan bishops. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowing this charter of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after a second or third warning, unless he makes suitable amends by satisfaction, [Col. 1078B] let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be separated from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and at the final judgment let him be subject to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve the just rights of that place, may there rest the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive the fruit of good action. Amen, amen, amen.

Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, subscribed. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia, subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Callixtus, subscribed. I, Hubald, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, subscribed. [Col. 1078C] I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Laurence and Damasus, subscribed. I, Julius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus, subscribed. I, Ubald, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem, subscribed. I, Villanus, cardinal priest of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill, subscribed.
