I, Oddo, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, subscribed. I, Jacintus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin, subscribed. I, Peter, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, subscribed.

[Col. 1078D] Given at the Lateran through the hand of Robert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the ninth day before the Kalends of January, in the ninth indiction, in the year 1146 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

## LVII. He receives the Church of Blessed Peter at Regensburg under protection and confirms its possessions.  
*(A.D. 1145, December 30.)*

[RIED, *Codex diplomaticus*, I, 213.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ADALBERT, dean of the Church of Regensburg, and his brethren, present and future, to be canonically appointed, for ever.

It is deemed fitting and consonant with honour that we, who have been raised to the governance [Col. 1079A] of churches, should defend them against the malice of wicked men and fortify them with the protection of the apostolic see. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions, receive under the protection of that same prince of the apostles and of ourselves the aforesaid Church of Blessed Peter, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may hereafter, by the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings, the liberality of princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, acquire by the Lord’s favour, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names:

[Col. 1079B] The Church of Blessed Peter of Regensburg itself, with all its possessions and appurtenances; the estate of Gislingen, with all its possessions and appurtenances; your cloistered houses; the building-plots of houses situated in the city of Regensburg; the church of Illinchoven; the church of Hovechirchen; the church of Waltkeringen; the church of Pfafenberg; the church of Hitinchoven; the church of Pfolenchoven; the church of Lirendorf; the church of Leuchingen; the church of Punnechoven; the church of Otelthaim; the church of Chirphinholze; the church of Hazenchoven; the tithe of Wimtingen; the tithe of Samtingen; tithes in Toenkove; tithes in Norkoune; the estate which you possess in the village called Holzen; the estate which you possess in [Col. 1079C] the village called Heitemchoven; the estate which you possess in the village called Strazze; and the holding which you possess in the village called Talmazzingen.

Further, we decree that the administration of the archdeaconries of that church shall be entrusted to none other than the canons of your church. We therefore decree that absolutely no person may rashly disturb the aforesaid place, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the apostolic see and the canonical right and due reverence of the diocesan bishop.

If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular [Col. 1079D] person hereafter, knowing this charter of our constitution, should attempt to act against it, then, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects his offence by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be separated from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and at the final judgment let him be subject to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place, may there rest the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that both here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, subscribed.

[Col. 1080A] Eleven cardinals subscribed.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Robert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the third day before the Kalends of January, in the eighth indiction, in the year 1145 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

A lead seal is appended: EUGENIUS PP. III.

## LVIII. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Mary at Springiersbach.  
*(A.D. 1145, December 31.)*

[GUNTHER, *Codex Diplomaticus Rheno-Mosellanus*, I, 291.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons RICHARD, abbot of the Church of Saint Mary at Sprenckersbach, and his brethren, present [Col. 1080B] and future, professing the regular life, for ever.

Since without the worship of true religion neither the unity of charity can endure nor service pleasing to God be offered, it is fitting for apostolic authority to cherish religious persons and, with God’s help, provide for their peace. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the holy church of the blessed Mother of God and Virgin Mary, in which you are devoted to divine service, strengthening it by the privilege of this present writing.

First, indeed, we decree that the canonical order according to the Rule of blessed Augustine shall be kept there inviolate for all time. Moreover, whatever possessions and goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may hereafter, by the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings, the liberality of princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, acquire by the Lord’s favour, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: [Col. 1080C] the Church of the Blessed Virgin Mary at Sprenckersbach itself, with its possessions and all appurtenances; the Church of Blessed Mary situated near Andernach; the Church of Blessed Nicholas of the Island, which place lies on the bank of the Moselle; the church of Keymetam, situated on the mountain called Mary’s Castle, as our venerable brother Albero, archbishop of Trier, [Col. 1080D] reasonably granted and gave it to you and confirmed it by the charter of his writing; and the church situated in the Valley of the Martyrs, with its possessions and all appurtenances.

Furthermore, no cleric or layman whatsoever shall presume to exact tithes from you on the produce of the lands which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or from the increase of your animals. We likewise decree that the burial-ground of that place shall be free, so that none may oppose the devotion and last will of those who have chosen to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated, saving the right of the mother church. Moreover, we prohibit anyone, without the common consent of the brethren, from accepting any fief from the same church or the advocacy of that place, or from presuming to transfer by any succession [Col. 1081A] to another what he has accepted.

When you, the present abbot of that place, or any one of your successors dies, no one shall be set over it by any cunning of intrigue or by force, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren, shall provide to be elected in the fear of God and according to the Rule of blessed Augustine.

We therefore decree that absolutely no person may rashly disturb the aforesaid place, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the apostolic see and the canonical right and due reverence of the diocesan bishop. [Col. 1081B] If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowing this charter of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects his offence by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be separated from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and at the final judgment let him be subject to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place, may there rest the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that both here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. [Col. 1081C] I, GG., cardinal priest of the title of Callixtus. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Oddo, cardinal of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia. I, Humbald, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul. I, Wydo, cardinal priest of Saints Laurence and Damasus. I, Arebert, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia. I, Bernhard, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Clement. I, Villanus, cardinal priest of Saint Stephen on the [Col. 1081D] Caelian Hill. I, Jordanis, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. I, Gg., cardinal deacon of Saint Angelus. I, Jacinctus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Peter, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata.

Given at the Lateran by the hand of Robert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the second day before the Kalends of January, in the eighth indiction, in the year 1145 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

## LIX. He commands Bernard, bishop of Hildesheim, and his successors not to alienate Wincenburg Castle; he forbids the Goslar men, who had seized a certain provostship, to be let go unpunished; he commends Provost C. and Canon R.  
*(A.D. 1145–46, May 27.)*

[Orig. Guelf., III, 449.]

[Col. 1082A]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother B[ERNARD], bishop, and to his beloved sons the clergy and people of the Church of Hildesheim: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Just as our predecessors, the Roman pontiffs, are known to have loved the Church and city of Hildesheim as renowned and noble in the German kingdom, so we too, following in their footsteps, wish to love and foster it with a fuller affection of charity and to devote more diligent attention to its honour. With this purpose, our predecessor Pope Innocent, of blessed memory, commanded you, brother bishop, that you should never grant as a benefice, nor in any manner alienate, Wincenborgh Castle, which is recognized as belonging by right to the Church of Hildesheim, but that it should remain for all future times for the benefit of that church.

We therefore, whose special concern it is to confirm good acts, forbid by apostolic authority that either you or any of your successors shall have authority to enfeoff or in any way alienate the aforesaid castle; rather, we decree that it shall remain free for ever for the benefit of that church and without anyone’s encroachment. But if anyone at any time, by rash presumption, should presume to enfeoff or alienate that castle, or to receive or occupy it as a benefice, let him know that, together with his supporters, he is to be bound by the bond of excommunication for so grave an offence.

Nevertheless, brother bishop, we command you that within forty days you render canonical justice to our beloved son C. against the men of Goslar, who, as we have learned, violently seized his provostship while he was in our service. We also earnestly commend to your charity that same provost and our beloved son R., a canon of your church.

[Col. 1082D] Given at Viterbo, on the sixth day before the Kalends of June.

## LX. To Gregory, bishop of Bergamo.  
*(A.D. 1145–46, July 12.)*

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, IV, 459.]

EUGENIUS, etc., to GREGORY, bishop of Bergamo, etc.

Since it belongs to your office to love and preach peace, and to restore it among those at discord, especially among your subjects, we grieve that you show yourself the author and instigator of the discord which has long been agitated between the clerics of Saint Vincent and Saint Alexander. This we infer from the fact that, as we have heard, you delayed making this evident until the octave of Pentecost. [Col. 1083A] Although this deserved grave punishment, nevertheless, for the present, bearing it in the mildness of the apostolic see, we command you by apostolic letters that, upon receiving these letters, you shall publicly declare before all clergy and people that the priests who remain rebellious in rendering the oath of fidelity, according to the command of our predecessors and ourselves, to the clerics of Saint Alexander, have been deprived by us of every ecclesiastical benefice, just as we have already deprived them of office; and you shall ensure that this sentence of deprivation is firmly observed until they satisfy the aforesaid clerics of Saint Alexander concerning the said fidelity. Otherwise, for as long as you delay fulfilling this command of ours, you shall abstain from every episcopal office. We likewise require you to take such care in this matter that we are not compelled to punish your [Col. 1083B] negligence and their contumacy with a more severe sentence.

Given at Viterbo, on the sixth day before the Ides of July.

## LXI. To P., prior, and the brethren of Saint Frigdian at Lucca.  
*(A.D. 1145–46, September 4.)*

[BALUZ., *Miscellanea*, ed. Luc., IV, 594.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons P., prior of Saint Frigdian, and the brethren: greeting and apostolic blessing.

If injury or molestation is inflicted upon you by the monks of Saint George or by others, we grieve, since we love your church and yourselves as special [Col. 1083C] sons of the apostolic see with true charity in the Lord, and we regard whatever prosperity or adversity befalls you as our own. Therefore, having received your complaint against the monks of Saint George and learned, through examination of your letters, of the injury they inflicted upon you, we have forbidden the celebration of offices in their monastery until they make worthy satisfaction to you for so great an injury.

Given at Viterbo, on the second day before the Nones of September.

## LXII. To the abbot and brethren of Saint George at Lucca.  
*(A.D. 1145–46, September 4.)*

[Ibid.]

[Col. 1083D] EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the abbot and monks of Saint George of Lucca: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Although those who despise the decrees of the apostolic see are by no means deemed worthy of apostolic blessing, nevertheless, considering rather the mildness of the Roman Church than your presumption, we have not yet decreed in paternal kindness to withdraw it from you. Our predecessor Pope Innocent, of blessed memory, as we have learned from his writing, concerning the dispute over the parish between you and our beloved sons, the canons of Blessed Frigdian, after your many absences and prolonged contumacy, summoned a council of his brethren, restored in full to the Church of Blessed Frigdian the parish which you had [Col. 1084A] invaded, and freely adjudged it to that church. He completely removed you from the usurpation or invasion of that parish, decreeing and confirming by his privilege that henceforth they should hold and possess that parish whole and entire, and that neither monks, nor you, nor anyone else might bury their parishioners without their consent or against their objection.

But you, as we have learned from the complaint of those same sons of ours, secretly carried under the silence of night to your monastery one of their parishioners, named Fridicione, after illness had wholly deprived him of speech, and clothed him in the monastic cowl. Although those same canons forbade this before it was done, and although they subsequently forbade it on our behalf, you thought it so trivial that you even disdained to hear them. [Col. 1084B] There can be no doubt that in this you acted against the privileges of the apostolic see, against the prohibition made on our behalf, as we have said above, and against the decrees of the holy Fathers. For it is either willing devotion or one’s own profession that makes a monk. But we have learned that neither was present in this case. Since, therefore, we can neither can nor ought to allow so great a presumption on your part to go unpunished, we forbid the celebration of divine offices in your monastery until you make worthy satisfaction to our aforesaid sons, P., prior, and the other brethren of Saint Frigdian, for so great an injury.

Given at Viterbo, on the second day before the Nones of September.

## LXIII. Privilege for the Church of Saint John at Kaltenborn.  
*(A.D. 1145–46, October 22.)*

[SCHOETTGEN and KREYSIG, *Diplomata*, II, 698.]

[Col. 1084C]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GODESCHALC, provost of the Church of Blessed John the Evangelist at Caldenborn, and his brethren: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is fitting readily to grant consent to religious desires, so that faithful devotion may attain a speedy result. For this reason, beloved sons in the Lord, having great confidence in your religious devotion and upright life, and wishing to provide for the future peace and welfare of your church, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves that church, with all goods known to belong to it canonically or which it may hereafter, by reasonable means [Col. 1084D] and the Lord’s favour, acquire; and we strengthen it by the charter of this present writing. By apostolic authority we forbid any ecclesiastical or secular person, at any time, to rashly disturb the aforesaid church, its goods, or the brethren serving God there, or harass them with any vexations. But if anyone presumes to attempt this, let him incur the indignation of almighty God and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul; let him be separated from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and at the final judgment let him be subject to severe vengeance. Amen.

Given at Viterbo, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of November.

## LXIV. To Peter, bishop of Riez, and Bertrand, bishop of Fréjus.  
*(A.D. 1145–46, October 27.)*

[D. BOUQUET, *Recueil*, XV, 429.]

[Col. 1085A]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brethren P., bishop of Riez, and B., bishop of Fréjus: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The Church of Barjols belongs to the right of Blessed Peter and pertains especially to his ownership and protection. Therefore we are under an obligation to cherish and foster it and other churches belonging to it, and to inflict upon them no injury or molestation. Accordingly, we command and order you by apostolic letters to impose no new exactions, receptions, [Col. 1085B] hospitality demands, or other unusual burdens upon the churches which it possesses in your bishoprics, nor to exact them from their priests; but freely to leave them in the liberty in which they are known to have existed in the time of your predecessors, namely Augerius and Berengarius.

Moreover, we suspend from the orders which they have received those priests or clerics subject to you who knowingly bury excommunicated persons in a cemetery, until they present themselves before us to make satisfaction for so grave a presumption. You, however, shall announce our suspension to them and ensure that it is firmly observed.

Given at Viterbo, on the sixth day before the Kalends of November.

## LXV. He intercedes with Henry, bishop of Moravia, for brethren who departed without permission from the monastery on Mount Strahov.  
*(A.D. 1145–46, November 21.)*

[BOCZEK, *Codex diplomaticus Moraviae*, I, 238.]

[Col. 1085C]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, bishop of Moravia: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The bearers of this letter, coming to us, informed us that, seduced by certain brethren, they departed without your permission, and without the permission of their abbot and brethren, from the religious house called Mount Sion, founded by your devotion. But when they later returned to that same place, the brethren refused to receive them. Since it is fitting that, just as we desire our own debts to be remitted by the Lord, so we should mercifully forgive our brethren [Col. 1085D] even when they offend against us, we request and command your belovedness by apostolic letters that, for the love of God and of ourselves, if those brethren are tolerable to them, you shall cause them to be received in that place out of regard for charity and mercy.

Given at Viterbo, on the eleventh day before the Kalends of December.

## LXVI. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Mary in Regula.  
*(A.D. 1146.)*

[FANTUZZI, *Monumenta Ravennatia*, VI, p. 46.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons RODULPH, abbot of the monastery of Saint Mary in Regula, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, for ever.

[Col. 1086A] Whenever a request is made of us which is recognized as consistent with religion and honour, it becomes us readily to grant it and to give fitting support to the desires of petitioners. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your petitions and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid church of the blessed and ever-Virgin Mary, in which you are devoted to divine service, strengthening it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may hereafter, by the grant of pontiffs, the liberality of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, acquire by the Lord’s favour, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors.

[Col. 1086B] Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: the estate of Bimbani, with its church and all appurtenances; likewise, we confirm to you the tithes of that same estate, as they were reasonably granted by your bishops; the church of Monsignani, with the enclosed place in which it was built, and other possessions in the court of Morethani; the church of Mura, with four adjoining estates and its other possessions; your right in the church of Saint John at Pomtogase; a certain tract of land at Capo Silicum, where tombs have been built; also, a fishery with the adjoining cugullaria [term uncertain]; Campiani Castle with its entire court; half of Turigini Castle with half [Col. 1086C] of that court; certain possessions in the court of Tausignani; and the church of Rivisalsi with its entire court.

In the diocese of Bologna: the church of Saint Thomas in the village of Fasani, with all its possessions; the church of Saint Martin in Podio, with all its possessions; all your possessions in the parish of Saint Laurence. We also grant that the burial-ground of that place shall be free, so that none may oppose the devotion and last will of those who have chosen to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated, saving the right of the mother church.

We therefore decree that absolutely no person may rashly disturb the aforesaid Church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved [Col. 1086D] whole for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the apostolic see and the canonical right of the diocesan bishops. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowing this charter of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects his offence by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be separated from the most precious body and most sacred blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and at the final judgment let him be subject to severe [lacuna]. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place, may there rest the peace of our Lord [Col. 1087A] Jesus Christ, so that both here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Callixtus, subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, subscribed. I, Albix [reading uncertain; perhaps Alberic], bishop of Ostia, subscribed. I, Oddo, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, subscribed. I, Heribald, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal priest of Saints Laurence and Damasus, subscribed. [Col. 1087B] I, Julius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus, subscribed. I, Ubald, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem, subscribed. I, Julian, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill, subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, subscribed. I, Jacintus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin, subscribed. I, Peter, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, subscribed.

Given [lacuna] in the year 1146 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the year [lacuna] of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

## LXVII. He receives under protection the monastery of Saint Peter at Ghent, or Blandinium, and confirms its goods and privileges.  
*(A.D. 1146, January 1.)*

[MIRAEUS, *Opera diplomatica*, III, 41.]

[Col. 1087C]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons SIGER, abbot of the monastery of Saint Peter at Ghent, or Blandinium, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, for ever.

Since without the worship of true religion neither the unity of charity can endure nor service pleasing to God be offered, it is fitting for apostolic authority to cherish religious persons and fortify their places with pious protection.

Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just [Col. 1087D] petitions and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service, strengthening it by the privilege of this present writing.

We decree that whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings, the liberality of princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, acquire by the Lord’s favour, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors.

Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: in the diocese of Tournai, the altar of the church of Saint Mary, built in the precinct of Saint Peter, with its appurtenances; the chapel of Saint John the Baptist at Burgo; [Col. 1088A] the chapel of Saint James; the chapel of Saint Nicholas; the chapel of Swynaerde (today the collegiate church of Saint Pharaildis); the altar of Oostburch, with all its appurtenances; the altar of Leka; the altar of Vlaersloo, with its appurtenances; the altar of Oudeghem; the altar of Hossene; the altar of Westrem; the altar of Lovendegem; the altar of Themseka; the altar of Kemseke; the altar of Calfsuorde; the altar of Beveren (in Waas, no longer extant); the altar of Desselgem; the altar of Anseghem; the altar of Autrive; the altar of Avelgem; the altar of Ooteghem; the altar of Bossuyt; the altar of Hollain; the altar of Annetieres; the altar of Campinio; and the altar of Carvin, free from persons and from every personal succession, as these were canonically entrusted to you by Simon, bishop of Tournai, and confirmed in his written instrument [Col. 1088B] (in the year 1140).

In the diocese of Cambrai: the altar of Meerlebeke, with its appurtenances; the altar of Materen; the altar of Bost, with its appurtenances; the altar of Hillegem; the altar of Dulciac, with its appurtenances. In the diocese of Arras: the altar of Harnes, with its appurtenances. In the diocese of Rochester: the altar of Lewisham; the altar of Greenwich.

Furthermore, following in the footsteps of our most holy predecessor Pope Gregory (VII), we absolutely forbid public masses to be celebrated by a bishop in that monastery, lest in the retreats and dwellings of the servants there be occasion for popular gatherings or a new entrance be made for women, unless the abbot of the place has requested him.

[Col. 1088C] We also forbid anyone to build within your parishes to the detriment of your churches, saving nevertheless the authority of the apostolic see and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. We therefore decree that absolutely no person may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any other vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowing this charter of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects it by suitable [Col. 1088D] satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be separated from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and at the final judgment let him be subject to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place, may there rest the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that both here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia. I, Marcus, bishop of Tusculum. [Col. 1089A] I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Chrysogonus. I, Reynerius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Prisca. I, Julius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus. I, Nicholas, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Lawrence and Damasus. I, Aribert, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia. I, Waldus, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Villanus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, Oddo, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Velum [Col. 1089B] Aureum. I, John, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian. I, Hyacinthus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Jordan, cardinal deacon of the Roman Church. I, Cinthius, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus.

Given at the Lateran, etc., on the Kalends of January, in the ninth indiction, in the year 1145 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Eugenius III.

### LXVIII. Privilege for the convent of Faremoutiers. (1146, January 3.)

*[Gallia Christiana nova*, VIII, *Instr.*, 550.]

[Col. 1089C] EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ, RISENDIS, abbess of the monastery of Faremoutiers, and her sisters, present and future, who profess the regular life, in perpetuity, etc.

Therefore, beloved daughters in the Lord, moved by the prayers of our venerable brother Alberic, bishop of Ostia, we graciously assent to your just petitions; and we receive under the protection of Saint Peter and our own the aforesaid monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future acquire, by the grant of pontiffs, the liberality of kings, the gifts of princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through the Lord’s favor, shall remain secure and undiminished for you and your successors. Among these, we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names.

In the district of Meaux, the estate itself which was formerly called Eboriacus, but is now Faremoutiers, with churches, tithes, cultivated and uncultivated lands, winepresses, woods, meadows, mills, waters and watercourses; the markets held each week, the rights of way, and the entire jurisdiction of the whole town; together with the surrounding villages, namely Morou with its church and tithe; the chapel of Saint Adalberga; Pont-Mucre with its church and two portions of the tithe; Poncello; Dammartin [Col. 1090A] with the mills belonging to that same village; Tremis; Mesmillo; Calueto-faico; Vicinis; Busseto; Chessuto; Mesura Triangulo; Montebon; Invito; Campogeneste; the aforesaid village of Montmartin; Monterainard; Belteil with five portions of the tithe; Raoul’s village; Montelavandria; Bellumvidere; Rogo; Salceio; Alba; Berrinniis; Mesnil-Risendis; Mancello; Mesoarcheriis; Favergis; Plessero; Melo; Curtervello; and Mesegierii, with all appurtenances of those same villages; Alpineium with its appurtenances, cultivated and uncultivated lands, waters and watercourses, forests, meadows, and woods; the church of Blessed John the Evangelist, with all tithes, situated at Plesseto Arnulphi, with its appurtenances.

In the district of Troyes, Bulliacum with its lands and other [Col. 1090B] appurtenances; the church of Bonoloco Curfelix. In the district of Paris, Corlegen with all appurtenances; the tithe of Marcheingen. In the district of Sens, Tumba with all appurtenances, namely its church, tithes, cultivated and uncultivated lands, woods, mills, waters and watercourses; the chapel situated in the village called Balacrium; the chapel situated at Montemintelli. In the territory of Gâtinais, the estate called Gaicus with all appurtenances; whatever rights you possess in the church of Noem, in the church of Damnaria, at Montecrescone and Monteboi, and in the church and village of Saint Firmin. In the district of Provins, the church of Saint Bartholomew of Curte Euroldi. Likewise, in the district of Meaux, twenty solidi of rent payable at the [Col. 1090C] castle of Columbario, which are paid to that church by the lord of that castle.

We also confirm by the tenor of this present writing the liberties and immunities which were justly granted to that monastery—and also to its villages, lands, people, and other things belonging to it—by our most illustrious son Louis, renowned king of the Franks, and confirmed by his charter. Upon the death of you, the present abbess of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be set over it by deceit, cunning, or violence, except one whom the sisters by common consent, or the sounder part of their counsel, shall, in the fear of God and according to the Rule of Saint Benedict, have provided to be elected.

You shall receive chrism, holy oil, the consecration of altars or churches, the ordination [Col. 1090D] of clerics to be promoted to holy orders, and the blessings of nuns from the diocesan bishop, provided that he is Catholic, enjoys the favor of the Apostolic See, and is willing to provide these things for you freely and without any improper demand. Otherwise, you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer, who, supported by our authority, shall grant what is requested.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, remove its possessions, retain those removed, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved inviolate and whole, for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted—subject to the agreement [Col. 1091A] reasonably made and confirmed by his document between Bishop Manasses and Abbess Risendis, through Hugh, bishop of Auxerre, and Geoffrey, bishop of Châlons, at the command of our predecessor Pope Innocent of happy memory, and strengthened by the documentary guarantee of the bishop of Meaux; while the authority of the Apostolic See is also reserved, as is the canonical jurisdiction of the bishops in whose dioceses the other churches belonging to the monastery are situated. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowing the tenor of this our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, etc. Amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia. Ymarus of Tusculum. B., cardinal priest of the title of Calixtus. [Col. 1091B] Guido, cardinal of the title of Saint Chrysogonus. Hubaldus, cardinal of Saint Praxedes. Hubaldus, cardinal of the title of Saints John and Paul. Gilebertus, cardinal of Saint Mark. Aubertus, cardinal of Saint Anastasia. Nicholas, cardinal of the title of Saint Cyriacus. Bernard, cardinal of Saint Clement. Julius, cardinal of Saint Marcellus. Villanus, cardinal of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill. Jordan, cardinal of Saint Susanna. I, Odo, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Velum Aureum. Guido, cardinal of Saints Cosmas and Damian. [Col. 1091C] Octavian, cardinal of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. John, cardinal of Saint Adrian. Gregory, cardinal of Saint Angelo. Becardus, cardinal of the holy Roman Church. Guido, cardinal of Saint Mary in Portico. Hyacinthus, cardinal of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. Cynthius, cardinal of Saints Sergius and Bacchus.

Given at the Lateran by the hand of Robert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the third day before the Nones of January, in the ninth indiction, in the year 1145 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### LXIX. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Lambert at Suben. (1146, January 4.)

*[Monumenta Boica*, IV, 524.]

[Col. 1091D]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, JOHN, provost of the Church of Blessed Lambert at Suben, and his brethren, present and future, who profess the regular life, in perpetuity.

Whenever a request is made of us which is known to accord with religion and uprightness, it is fitting that we grant it willingly and give suitable aid to the desires of those who petition us. For this reason, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions and receive under the protection of Saint Peter and our own the aforesaid church, in which you are devoted to divine service; and we strengthen it by the protection of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may in future acquire through grants of pontiffs, the liberality of kings, gifts of princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through the Lord’s favor, shall remain secure and undiminished to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: the church of Saint Margaret the Virgin at Hengst, with its stable-yard and all its appurtenances; the church at Mallentin, with all its appurtenances, as these were reasonably confirmed to you in writing by our venerable brother Conrad, archbishop of Salzburg.

Given at the Lateran by the hand of Robert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the holy Roman [Col. 1092B] Church, on the day before the Nones of January, in the ninth indiction, in the year 1146 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### LXX. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Michael of Bergen. (1146, January 7.)

[THORKELIN, *Diplomatarium Arna-Magnæanum*, II, 1.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, ORMO, abbot of the monastery of Saint Michael of Bergen, and his brethren, present and future, who profess the regular life, in perpetuity.

The care of the universal Church has been entrusted to us by God, the provider of all good things, so that we may love religious persons and strive by every means to spread religion pleasing to God. For no service is ever rendered acceptable to God unless, proceeding from the root of charity, it is preserved in the purity of religion. Therefore all lovers of the Christian faith ought to cherish religion and support more attentively venerable places, together with the persons devoted therein to divine service, so that they may not be troubled by the annoyances of wicked people or burdened with oppressive exactions.

Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions, and receive under the protection of Saint Peter and our own the aforesaid monastery of Blessed Michael the Archangel, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. First, indeed, we decree [Col. 1092D] that the monastic order according to the Rule of Saint Benedict shall be preserved there inviolate for all time. Moreover, whatever possessions and goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may in future acquire through grants of pontiffs, the liberality of kings, gifts of princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through the Lord’s favor, shall remain secure and undiminished to you and your successors. Among these, we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: the monastery of Blessed Michael itself, with its lands, possessions, tithes, meadows, woods, fisheries, and other appurtenances; the islands called Aumas, with the church of Saint Clement; the church of Saint Nicholas of Hardla, with the islands belonging to it; and all other [Col. 1093A] things whatsoever belonging to the same monastery, which shall be preserved forever under the protection of the supreme keeper of the keys and our own.

Furthermore, we prohibit anyone who has made profession there from presuming to depart from that monastery without permission of the abbot and his brethren. We further decree that whenever you need to visit the Apostolic See, you shall have free liberty to do so. Upon the death of you, the present abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be set over it by any deceitful contrivance or violence, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of their counsel, shall in the fear of God and according to the Rule of Saint Benedict have provided to be elected.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid [Col. 1093B] place, remove its possessions, retain those removed, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall remain whole, for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, with the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical jurisdiction and reverence due to the diocesan bishop reserved. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowing the tenor of this our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not amend his offense by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer; and let him be subject to severe vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Given at the Lateran by the hand of Robert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the seventh day before the Ides of January, in the eighth indiction, in the year 1145 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### LXXI. Confirmation of all goods and privileges granted to the monastery of Tournus by the supreme Roman pontiffs. (1146, January 9.)

[JUENIN, *Nouvelle Histoire de Tournus*, proofs, p. 157.]

[Col. 1093D]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, PETER, abbot of the monastery of Tournus, and his brethren, present and future, who profess the regular life, in perpetuity.

Although by the authority and benevolence of the Apostolic See we stand in obligation to all members of the holy Church, it is fitting that we extend a more earnest concern of charity to those places and persons which adhere especially and more intimately to the holy Roman Church. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions; and, following in the footsteps of our predecessors, the Roman pontiffs Urban, Paschal, Calixtus, [Col. 1094A] Innocent, and Lucius, of happy memory, we receive under the protection of Saint Peter and our own the monastery of Tournus, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future acquire through grants of pontiffs, the liberality of kings, gifts of princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through the Lord’s favor, shall remain secure and undiminished to you and your successors.

Moreover, following the example of our aforesaid predecessor Pope Calixtus of blessed memory, we decree by the authority of this present decree that henceforth no bishop shall have power to impose any burden in respect of altars and churches, [Col. 1094B] tithes, or anything duly belonging to them, which you are known to have possessed before the prohibitions of our predecessor Pope Urban of holy memory, or which you acquired thereafter by grant of bishops; but just as you held certain things in full through their permission, so you shall hold them forever in the future.

We also confirm by the authority of the Apostolic See, for your support and that of the poor, the tithes of the churches which you now possess and which are held by laymen, if reverence for your religious order can withdraw them from lay control: namely, between yourselves and the monastery of Saint Florent, those of the churches of Lausduni, that is, Holy Cross and Saint Nicholas, as was done and confirmed in writing by our aforementioned predecessors Urban and Calixtus of happy memory. We command that henceforth the monks of Saint Florent shall not presume to inflict upon you or your church any trouble on this account; but that you and your successors shall possess the aforesaid churches forever without their disturbance.

We further add that the same place in which rest the bodies of Blessed Valerian the martyr and Saint Philibert the confessor shall forever remain free of every yoke of secular power. Nor may a bishop, whatever his diocese, disturb that place under pretext of excommunication, absolution, or any other administrative act; nor impose crosses or any new exactions upon the borough or other possessions [Col. 1094D] of the monastery. We prohibit public Masses from being celebrated in that monastery, or a station from being held there by a bishop, apart from the will of the abbot or brethren, as was established and confirmed in writing by our predecessors.

Upon the death of you, the present abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be set over it by any deceitful contrivance or violence, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of their counsel, shall, according to God and the Rule of Saint Benedict, have provided to be elected and consecrated by the pontiff of the Apostolic See or his legate. We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, remove its possessions, retain those removed, diminish them, or harass it by any [Col. 1095A] vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole, for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, with the authority of the Apostolic See of course reserved. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowing the tenor of this our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not amend his offense by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer; and let him be subject to severe vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve what is just for that place, may there be the peace of our Lord [Col. 1095B] Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Alberic, bishop, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Calixtus, have subscribed. I, Ubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes, have subscribed. I, Nicholas, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross, have subscribed. I, Ubaldus, cardinal priest of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the [Col. 1095C] Velum Aureum, have subscribed. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Angelo, have subscribed. I, Astaldus, cardinal deacon of Saint Eustace beside the Temple of Agrippa, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed. I, Hyacinthus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin, have subscribed. I, Peter, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran by the hand of Robert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the holy Roman [Col. 1095D] Church, on the fifth day before the Ides of January, in the ninth indiction, in the year 1145 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### LXXII. To the bishops of Angoulême and Limoges—That they should settle by canonical judgment the dispute between the Cluniacs and the clerics concerning Roche-Beaucourt. (1146, January 16.)

[D. BOUQUET, *Recueil*, XV, 435.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brethren LAMBERT, bishop of Angoulême, and GERALD, bishop of Limoges, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have carefully heard the dispute long conducted between our beloved sons, the [Col. 1096A] monks of Cluny and the clerics of Roche-Beaucourt (*Roca-Bovis-curtis*, La Roche-Beaucourt), concerning the church of that place; and we have long deliberated upon it with our brethren. Therefore, having heard the arguments of both parties and made more diligent inquiry, since from the confession of both parties we have learned that the monks were in possession, we have judged that, if the monks can prove in our presence by two or three suitable witnesses that the clerics then in that church, or someone acting through them, violently expelled them from possession of that church, that possession shall be restored to them. Once full restitution has been made, summon both parties before you within two months, carefully investigate the case concerning ownership on either side, [Col. 1096B] and bring it to an end by canonical judgment.

Given at the Lateran, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of February.

### LXXIII. Bull confirming the possessions of the monastery of Crisenon. (1146, January 19.)

[*Gallia Christiana nova*, XII, *Instr.*, 117.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ, ELIZABETH, abbess of Crisenon, and her sisters, present and future, who profess the regular life, in perpetuity.

Since without the worship of true religion neither the unity of charity can endure nor a service pleasing to God be offered, it is fitting for apostolic authority to cherish religious persons [Col. 1096C] and protect their places by a pious safeguard. Therefore, beloved daughters in Christ, moved by the prayers of our venerable brother Hugh, bishop of Auxerre, we graciously assent to your just petitions and receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and our own the aforesaid place, in which you are devoted to divine service; and we strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may in future acquire through grants of pontiffs, the liberality of kings, gifts of princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through the Lord’s favor, shall remain secure and undiminished to you and your successors.

Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: the mills of Cren; in the diocese of Sens, the tithe of Chasciacum; the oven at Auxerre with vineyards; vineyards at Varzy; the territory of Lucy; the grange of Nertennac with its territory; in the diocese of Nevers, the monastery of La Ferté, in which you have established a community of your sisters; and, for the use of those sisters, whatever Hugh of Limo and his wife Petronilla, Seguinus and his wife Agnes, and Ogerus and his wife Christiana have given you of their right in the village called Lunum, at Luguen, Chalma, Coenni, Suenci, Tribus Aquis, Cigoniis, Chassennis, and Ruenni. The tithe which William Carolus and his wife held at Linum. A tenth part of the fish of the enclosure of Count William [Col. 1097A] at Disisa. The aforesaid monastery of La Ferté shall always remain under your governance and obedience.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid place, remove its possessions, retain those removed, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole, for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, with the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical jurisdiction of the diocesan bishop reserved. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowing the tenor of this our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not amend his offense by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer; and let him be subject to severe vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve what is just for that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find in the future the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Calixtus, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Chrysogonus, have subscribed. [Col. 1097C] I, Jordan, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum, have subscribed. I, Wido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed. I, Astallus, cardinal deacon of Saint Eustace, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran by the hand of Robert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of February, in the eighth indiction, in the year 1145 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### LXXIV. Bull in favor of the monastery of Saint Marian. (1146, January 19.)

[*Gallia Christiana nova*, XII, *Instr.* 118.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, RAINERIUS, abbot of Saint Mary Rotunda outside the walls of the city of Auxerre, and his brethren, present and future, who profess the regular life, in perpetuity.

Since without the worship of true religion the unity of charity cannot endure, nor service pleasing to God be offered, it is fitting for apostolic authority to cherish religious persons and, with the Lord’s help, make salutary provision for their peace. Therefore, beloved [Col. 1098A] sons in the Lord, moved by the prayers of our venerable brother Hugh, bishop of Auxerre, we graciously assent to your just petitions; and we receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and our own the aforesaid place, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may in future acquire through grants of pontiffs, the liberality of kings, generosity of princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through the Lord’s favor, shall remain secure and undiminished to you and your successors.

Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: the churches of Saint Mary Rotunda and Saint Marian, situated in the suburb of Auxerre, with everything belonging to them, except those things which appear to belong to the bishop’s ownership and lordship; the grange of Oisella with all lands belonging by right to the church of Blessed Mary in that place and in the surrounding parishes; the grange of Bosculo with its lands; the grange of Capella with its lands; the mill of Scoquo; the grange of Bunost with its territory; an entire prebend in the church of Saint Stephen, provided, however, that in the celebration of the daily Mass for deceased canons, and also in that Mass which the priest-canons celebrate in due order during the appointed weeks, you render the service owed to that church. Certainly, no one shall presume to demand tithes from you on the produce which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or from the increase [Col. 1098C] of your animals.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid place, remove its possessions, retain those removed, diminish them, or trouble it by any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole, for the benefit solely of those for whose governance and support they were granted, with the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical jurisdiction of the diocesan bishop reserved. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowing the tenor of this our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not amend his offense by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer; and let him be subject to severe vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve what is just for that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the most strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Odo, cardinal deacon of Saint George. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. [Col. 1099A] I, Octavian, cardinal deacon in the Tullian Prison. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Gregory. I, Hyacinthus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, William, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Calixtus. I, William, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen at Belmonte. I, Bernard, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Clement.

Given by the hand of Robert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of February, in the ninth indiction, in the year 1145 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### LXXV. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Zeno at Reichenhall. (1146, January 28.)

*[Monumenta Boica*, III, 532.]

[Col. 1099B]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, LANZO, provost of Hall, and his brethren, present and future, who profess the regular life, in perpetuity.

Whenever a request is made of us which is shown to accord with religion and uprightness, it is fitting that we grant it willingly and give suitable aid to the desires of those who petition us. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions; and, following in the footsteps of our predecessor Pope Lucius of happy memory, we receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and our own the aforesaid church of Hall, in which you are devoted to divine service, [Col. 1099C] and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that in that church the canonical order according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine shall be preserved inviolate for all time, as our venerable brother Conrad, archbishop of Salzburg, ordained and confirmed by his charter.

Moreover, whatever possessions and goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may in future acquire through grants of pontiffs, the liberality of kings, gifts of princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through the Lord’s favor, shall remain secure and undiminished to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: the tithe-salt; the estate called [Col. 1099D] Suvant, with all appurtenances belonging to it, which the aforesaid archbishop granted to the aforesaid church; the water at the spring of Halla, given by Ebo; the water given by Facco; the estate given by Sigiboto Occheim; and the estate given by Henry Nutzpoum.

Certainly, no cleric or layman whatsoever shall presume to demand tithes from you on the produce which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or from the increase of your animals. We also forbid anyone of your profession, through an impulse of fickleness or under pretext of stricter religion, to leave the cloister without permission of the provost or community. Should anyone depart, no bishop, abbot, or monk shall receive him without the guarantee of letters from the community, [Col. 1100A] so long as, through the Lord’s favor, the observance of the canonical order remains in force in your church. But if, having been summoned a second or third time, he scorns to return, it shall be lawful for the provost of that place . . . . or when he passes to the governance of another church, or upon the death of any of your successors, no one shall be set over or substituted there by deceitful contrivance or violence, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of their counsel, shall canonically provide to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of Blessed Augustine.

We also grant that burial in that place shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and final wish of those who decide to be buried there, unless perhaps they are excommunicated; nevertheless, the rights of their mother church are reserved. Moreover, we confirm to your governance and right the chapels founded within the bounds of the parish [Col. 1100B] church, or which may hereafter, by God’s favor, be founded; and by apostolic authority we prohibit any cleric from holding them without your consent, or ministering in them contrary to your prohibition, just as this is known to have been prohibited by the privilege of our aforementioned predecessor Pope Lucius of good memory.

We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid church, or to take away its goods or possessions, or to retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any unlawful exactions or molestations; but let all things be preserved intact for the use and benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the [Col. 1100C] Apostolic See and the canonical right of the Archbishop of Salzburg. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing the text of this our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, having been warned a second or third time, unless he correct his offence by appropriate satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself to stand guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be separated from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer; and let him be subject to stern vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve what is just for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

[Col. 1100D] Given at Trastevere through the hand of Robert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the fifth day before the Kalends of February, in the ninth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1146, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### LXXVI. He notifies Saint Alexander of Bergamo of the definitive judgment rendered by him upon several articles of controversy.  
*(Year 1146, January 30.)*

[LUPI, *Codex diplomaticus Bergomensis*, II, 1063.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons LANFRANC, provost of the Church of Saint Alexander at Bergamo, and his brethren: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1101A] By the exercise of the office of apostleship entrusted to us by the Lord, we ought to remove scandals from among the churches and, with paternal solicitude, provide for their peace and tranquillity. Therefore, concerning the controversy which has for some time been disputed between you and the canons of Saint Vincent over certain specific and expressly stated articles, when you and they had appeared before us, we carefully investigated and fully understood the arguments and allegations of both parties, together with the privileges and other documents of our predecessors of happy memory—Innocent, Celestine, and Lucius, Roman pontiffs—which were issued at different times concerning this same controversy. With the assent and counsel of our brethren, we have thus put an end to the aforesaid dispute by a definitive judgment.

First, indeed, [Col. 1101B] whatever was ordained or decided concerning the same controversy by our aforesaid predecessors, we have likewise confirmed by apostolic authority and decreed to remain valid. Namely: priests of the diocese of Bergamo who were ordained after the judgment issued by our predecessor Pope Innocent of happy memory, and those who shall hereafter be ordained, shall render fidelity to both churches; and if the canons of Saint Vincent refuse to receive it, we nevertheless command that the same be rendered to your church.

Concerning penances, we command this to be observed between you: whenever priests from the whole diocese of Bergamo bring their parishioners to penance for public crimes, they shall endeavour to summon both parties; and penance for the aforesaid crimes shall by no means be imposed without the presence of your provost or of one priest of your church. [Col. 1101C] Further, at the bishop’s table the provost of your church shall hold the first place on the left side and shall have his clerics beside him.

We further decree that whenever, in the customary processions for celebrating the solemnities of Mass, the canons of Saint Vincent come to your church, they shall peacefully occupy the four walls of the choir in that church; and on the vigil and feast of Blessed Viator, and in the Gregorian Litanies, you shall honourably receive them through your representatives, with incense, holy water, and ringing bells. But whenever they meet with you in that church, whether for funerals or for other matters, you shall hold the whole choir of your church [Col. 1101D] jointly with them. And whenever you meet with those same canons of Saint Vincent, whether there or elsewhere, the provost of your church shall occupy the first place on the left side of the choir, while the remaining brethren shall sit jointly with those clerics.

The chaplains of the churches of Saint Saviour, Saint Agatha, Saint John, Saint Grata, and Saint Vigilius shall come to your church for High Mass on Sundays and principal feasts. On the Lord’s Supper, at baptism, and at other solemnities, we command that the divine offices be peacefully observed by both parties as you have customarily celebrated them according to established practice.

And, by apostolic authority, we impose perpetual silence concerning this matter upon the aforesaid canons of Saint Vincent and upon all others, admonishing [Col. 1102A] and commanding that you be content with this our determination and observe our command without contradiction. But if anyone should attempt to act against this document of our determination and confirmation, he shall be liable to the loss of his power and honour.

Given at Trastevere, on the third day before the Kalends of February.

I, Abricus, notary of the lord Emperor Frederick, have seen and read the authentic original of this copy and have subscribed in confirmation.

I, Alborinus, notary of the Sacred Palace, etc.

I, Peter, notary of the Sacred Palace, have seen and read the authentic original of this copy, and wrote it as it was contained therein, with more or less outside the letter.

### LXXVII. Privilege for the monastery of Casa Dei.  
*(Year 1146, February 1.)*

[MABILLON, *Annales Benedictini*, VI, 698.]

[Col. 1102B]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons STEPHEN, abbot of the monastery of Saint Robert of Casa Dei, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

It is fitting that we readily grant a desire known to pertain to the purpose of religion and the salvation of souls, and afford suitable support to the wishes of petitioners. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we willingly assent to your just requests and take the aforesaid monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service, under the protection of Saint Peter and ourselves, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. [Col. 1102C] We decree that whatever possessions and goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may hereafter acquire, by the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings, the benefactions of princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, by the Lord’s favour, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have judged it proper to specify by their own names:

The priories of Cornillon and Saint-Sauveur, with their churches, tithes, and appurtenances; the priories of the church of Canteogeol and of Montferrand, with their churches, tithes, and appurtenances; the priories of Saint Mary of Mont-Pilosi and of Bouillon, with their churches, tithes, and appurtenances; the priories of Saint [Col. 1102D] Libérata, Bargiac, and Leuciac, with all their appurtenances; the priories of Andria, Sepeio, Jaliniac, and Tecleda, with all their appurtenances; the priories of Saviniac, Bellomonte, Vecellis, and Saint Tréveri, with their churches, tithes, and appurtenances; the priories of Audancia, Vera-Villa, and Veracco, with the churches of Saint Veranus and their appurtenances; the monastery of the Cross, with the churches of Flavin, Aidoschia, Longacanal, Bisonas, Saint Desiderius, Saint Mary of the Road, Leschas, Saint Hilary, Saint Ursus, and Fratta; with the parish of Monte, as the stream divides it; with the chapel of Bescosello, with tithes and all their appurtenances; the priory of Portus Dei, with its churches, tithes, and all its appurtenances; the cell [Col. 1103A] of Belli-Cadro, with its appurtenances; the churches of Fischeo, Monte-Ayraldo, Balgro, and Sabran; likewise the church of Saint Liberius with its appurtenances. We also confirm to you in perpetuity those abbeys in which you have customarily installed abbots. We therefore decree, etc.

I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia. I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum. I, Odo, deacon-cardinal of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Guido, deacon-cardinal of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Gregory, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Lawrence in Damaso. [Col. 1103B] I, Jordan, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Susanna. I, Artald, deacon-cardinal of Saint Eustace beside the temple of Agrippina. I, Hyacinth, deacon-cardinal of Saint Mary in Cosmedin.

Given at Trastevere through the hand of Robert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the Kalends of February, in the ninth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1146, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### LXXVIII. Privilege for the monastery of Nantua.  
*(Year 1146, February 9.)*

[COCQUELINES, II, 294.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the prior of the monastery of Nantua and his brethren, [Col. 1103C] present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

It accords with the clemency of apostolic governance to love religious persons and fortify their places with pious protection. For it is known to be worthy and consonant with honour that we, who have been assumed to the governance of churches, should defend them from the wickedness of evil people and support them by the patronage of the Apostolic See. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we mercifully assent to your just petitions and, following the example of our predecessor Pope Lucius of happy memory, take the aforesaid monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service, under the protection of Saint Peter and ourselves, and strengthen it with the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions [Col. 1103D] and goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings, the benefactions of princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, by the Lord’s favour, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have judged it proper to specify by their own names:

Pomerium, Trefortium, Calorum, Trevorgias, Rumiliacum, Calmum, Cintriacum, Calargias, Talussiacum, Mozerias, Breynodum, Saint Alban, Saint Martin of Fraxinum, Villeta near Ambronay, Saint Germanus of Vallebona, Buencum, Lovenna, Ardunum, Astinenum, the estate near Geneva, Saint Martin of Veretalia, and Serveriacum.

[Col. 1104A] We further prohibit and, by apostolic authority, forbid anyone within the bounds of that monastery—namely, Saint Martin, Salas, Senochias, Carisium, the place of Silvanus, and Poisat—from presuming to seize or assault any person, or to make an attack or any injury whatsoever, as has been reasonably ordained and prohibited by the venerable brother Amadeus, Archbishop of Lyons and legate of the Apostolic See.

We decree that the monastery itself, together with the chapel of Saint Michael situated within its cemetery, shall remain in that liberty which was granted to it by Saint Gregory and in which it is known to have remained peacefully for sixty years; but both the place itself and the brethren shall remain perpetually under the obedience and disposition of the Abbot and monastery of Cluny.

[Col. 1104B] We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but let all things be preserved intact for the use and benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing the text of this our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, having been warned a second or third time, unless he correct his offence by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before divine [Col. 1104C] judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be separated from the most sacred body and blood of God and the Lord, from the most sacred body and blood of God and the Lord our Redeemer Jesus Christ; and let him be subject to stern vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve what is just for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Given at Trastevere through the hand of Robert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the fifth day before the Ides of February, in the ninth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1145, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### LXXIX. Privilege for the monastery of Mortemer.  
*(Year 1146, February 14.)*

[*Neustria pia*, 780.]

[Col. 1104D]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ADAM, abbot of Mortemer, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity, etc.

A pious petition should be brought to fulfillment by a consequent effect, etc.

Given at Trastevere through the hand of Robert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of March, in the ninth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1145, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### LXXX. Privilege for the monastery of Cluny.  
*(Year 1146, February 15.)*

[*Bibliotheca Cluniacensis*, col. 1386.]

[Col. 1105A]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his dearest son in Christ PETER, Abbot of Cluny, and to his successors to be regularly appointed in perpetuity.

Although, by the authority and benevolence of the Apostolic See, we stand indebted to all children of the holy Church, it is especially fitting that we protect with a more ardent zeal of charity venerable persons and places—above all those which have always adhered more particularly and devotedly to the Apostolic See and which excel in a fuller religious observance.
