For our predecessors of holy memory—namely John XI, likewise John XIX, Agapetus, Benedict VI, likewise Benedict VII, Leo VII, likewise Leo IX, Gregory VI, likewise Benedict VII, Leo VII, likewise Leo IX, Gregory VI, likewise Gregory VII, Alexander II, Stephen, Victor III, Urban II, Paschal II, Gelasius II, Calixtus II, Honorius II, and Lucius II, pontiffs of the Roman Church—have endowed the monastery of Cluny with the prerogative of singular affection and liberty, and have fortified all that pertains to it by the enactments of their privileges. [Col. 1105B] Following in their footsteps, we decree that all churches, cemeteries, monks, etc., as in the diploma of Lucius, *Patrologia*, vol. CLXXIX, no. 49, down to these words: “Likewise, the church of Rua, which belongs to the monastery of Abbeville,” to which are added:

[Col. 1105C] The island of Gravelonge with its appurtenances. We prohibit, moreover, etc.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum, have subscribed. I, Gregory, priest-cardinal of the title of Calixtus, have subscribed. I, Wido, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Chrysogonus, have subscribed. I, Hubald, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Praxedes, have subscribed. I, Hubald, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Gilbert, unworthy priest of the Holy Roman [Col. 1105D] Church, have subscribed. I, Guido, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints Lawrence and Damasus, have subscribed. I, Nicholas, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Cyriacus, have subscribed. I, Manfred, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Sabina, have subscribed. I, Aribert, priest-cardinal of Saint Anastasia, have subscribed. [Col. 1106A] I, Hubald, priest-cardinal of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Villanus, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill, have subscribed. I, Bernard, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Clement, have subscribed. I, Jordan, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Susanna, have subscribed. I, Odo, deacon-cardinal of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Guido, deacon-cardinal of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Octavian, deacon-cardinal of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed. I, Gregory, deacon-cardinal of Saint Angel, have subscribed. [Col. 1106B] I, Astald, deacon-cardinal of Saint Eustace beside the temple of Agrippa, have subscribed. I, John, deacon-cardinal of Saint Mary the New, have subscribed. I, Berard, deacon-cardinal of the Holy Roman Church, have subscribed. I, Guido, deacon-cardinal of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed. I, Peter, deacon-cardinal of Saint Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed. I, Cinthius, deacon-cardinal of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed.

Given at Trastevere through the hand of Robert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of March, [Col. 1106C] in the ninth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1145, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### LXXXI. To H., prior, and the brethren of Saint Marcellus of Salseto.—He confirms to them the gift of the church of Savatia made by Eustace, Bishop of Valence, before he became disobedient to the Roman Church.  
*(Year 1146, February 15.)*

[D. BOUQUET, *Recueil*, XV, 436.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons H., prior of Saint Marcellus, and his brethren: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Compelled by the authority of the Apostolic See, we mercifully assent to the just prayers of religious persons and preserve their right for them. Therefore, granting favourable assent to your just petitions, we likewise confirm to you by apostolic authority the church of Salvatia with its appurtenances, as it was reasonably granted to you and confirmed by his writing by our venerable brother C., [Col. 1106D] Bishop of Valence, with the consent of his entire chapter, before he became disobedient to the Roman Church.

> **Note:** [Col. 1105D] Correct “E,” that is, Eustace, concerning whom one reads in the *Life of Saint John, Bishop of Valence*: “For it pleased apostolic severity that Eustace, bishop of that see, be deposed, and that the clergy and people be granted, so far as lay in its power, free authority to elect a pastor. That man was illustrious by noble lineage and exceedingly pleasing to thousands of soldiers, whom he had either girded with swords or [Col. 1106D] generously supplied from his own resources . . . Relying upon evil persuasions, he delays the election by threats and terrors; he insists by his own authority that the decrees of the supreme pontiff, to whom he had already then begun to be disobedient, should cease; and for seven years the Church of Valence, at the command of Lord Pope Innocent, was deprived of divine office,” etc.

If anyone, knowing this document of our grant, [Col. 1107A] should attempt to act against it, let him know that he shall incur the wrath of Almighty God and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Trastevere, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of March.

### LXXXII. To Odo, prior, and the brethren of Saint Martin of the Fields, he grants “that, when the canons of Blessed Gervasius of Encre die, monks shall be substituted there.”  
*(Year 1146, February 20.)*

[MARRIER, *Histoire de Saint Martin des Champs*, p. 303.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ODO, prior of Saint Martin of the Fields, and his brethren: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1107B] Concerning the controversy which has long been disputed between you and the canons of Blessed Gervasius of Encre over this matter, we have carefully heard the arguments and allegations of both parties and, by the counsel of our brethren, have thus put an end to that controversy. Whatever was ordained concerning this case by Gaurin, Bishop of Amiens of good memory, with the counsel of religious men, and confirmed by the writings and authority of our predecessors of happy memory, Innocent and Lucius, Roman pontiffs—namely, that, when the canons die, monks shall be substituted there, while preserving the prebends of those who survive—we likewise confirm by apostolic authority and decree to remain valid; and concerning [Col. 1107C] this case we impose perpetual silence upon the canons.

Given at Trastevere, on the tenth day before the Kalends of March.

### LXXXIII. Privilege for the Church of Saint Martin of Beuron.  
*(Year 1146, February 23.)*

[PETRI, *Suevia ecclesiastica*, 216.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons FREDERICK, provost of the Church of Blessed Martin of Beuron, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

Since neither the unity of charity can endure without the worship of true religion nor service pleasing to God be rendered, it is proper for apostolic authority to love religious [Col. 1107D] persons and, with the Lord’s help, provide for their peace. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, following in the footsteps of our predecessor Pope Innocent of happy memory, we mercifully assent to your just petitions, take the aforesaid Church of Blessed Martin—in which you are devoted to divine service—under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever persons and goods you now justly and canonically possess, both from the gift of Peregrinus of good memory, a nobleman and founder of your house, and from other faithful servants of God, or may hereafter acquire, by the grant of pontiffs, benefactions of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, by the Lord’s favour, shall remain secure [Col. 1108A] and unimpaired to you and your successors.

We also decree that in your church, in which brethren who have professed the canonical life dwell, after canonical profession has been made there, no one whatsoever may leave thence without permission of the whole community; and no one shall dare retain one who leaves. So that you may serve Almighty God more peacefully, we prohibit anyone from presuming to claim the advocacy of your place as a hereditary right, nor may any advocate be appointed over you except one whom your superior has chosen by the common counsel of his brethren, as was established by that same predecessor of ours, Pope Innocent.

We likewise decree that burial at that place shall be free, so that no one may obstruct the devotion and final will of anyone who chooses to be buried there, unless he is excommunicated, saving the right of the mother church. When you, the present provost of that place, or any of your successors dies, no person may be set over it by any craft of surreptitiousness or violence, unless he is one whom the brethren, by common consent or by the sounder part of the brethren’s counsel, in the fear of God and according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine, have provided to be elected.

[Col. 1108B] We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid place, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but let all things be preserved intact for the use and benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See [Col. 1108C] and the canonical right and reverence due to the diocesan bishop. As a sign of this protection received from the Apostolic See, you shall pay one gold piece annually to us and our successors.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person should violate the text of this our constitution or knowingly attempt to act against it, then, having been warned a second or third time, if he does not correct his offence by appropriate satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself to stand guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be separated from the most holy body and blood of God and our Lord Jesus Christ; and let him be subject to stern vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve their rights for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

[Col. 1108D] I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia. I, Odo, deacon-cardinal of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Wido, deacon-cardinal of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Ismarus, bishop of Tusculum. I, Gubernator, cardinal of the title of Calixtus. I, Hubald, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Praxedes. [Col. 1109A] I, Gilbert, unworthy priest of the Holy Roman Church. I, Barido, priest-cardinal of Saints Lawrence and Damasus. I, Bernard, priest-cardinal of Saint Clement. I, Jordan, priest-cardinal of Saint Susanna. I, Octavian, deacon-cardinal of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. I, GG., deacon-cardinal of Saint Angel. I, Ostald, deacon-cardinal of Saint Eustace. I, Guido, unworthy minister of the altar in the Roman Church. I, John, deacon-cardinal of Saint Mary the New. I, Gerard, deacon-cardinal of the Holy Roman Church. [Col. 1109B] I, Peter, deacon-cardinal of Saint Mary Inviolata.

Given at Trastevere [Note: [Col. 1109D] Read: “at Trastevere.”] through the hand of Robert, priest-cardinal and vice-chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the seventh day before the Kalends of March, in the ninth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1145, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### LXXXIV. Bull for Saint Evurtius of Orléans.  
*(Year 1146, February 24.)*

[*Gallia Christiana nova*, VIII, 507.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ROGER, abbot of the Church of Saint Evurtius of Orléans, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

[Col. 1109C] The care of the universal Church has been entrusted to us by God, the provider of all good things, for this purpose: that we may love religious persons and endeavour in every way to spread religion pleasing to God. For service acceptable to God is not rendered unless, proceeding from the root of charity, it is preserved in purity of religion. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we mercifully assent to your just requests, take the aforesaid church—in which you are devoted to divine service—under the protection of Saint Peter and ourselves, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing.

First, indeed, we decree that the canonical order, according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine and the institution of the brethren of Saint Victor of Paris, [Col. 1109D] which by God’s grace is known to have been established in that church, shall be preserved there inviolate for all time. Nor shall any brother, after making profession there, be permitted to depart from that cloister without the permission of the abbot and the whole community; and no one shall dare retain one who departs without letters of the whole community. The abbot who is in office may, however, pronounce canonical sentence upon one who has departed without your knowledge or against your will, if, after being admonished a second or third time, he refuses to return.

Further, whatever possessions and goods the same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by the grant of pontiffs, benefactions of kings [Col. 1110A] or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through God’s favour, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have judged it proper to specify by their own names:

The church of Seneliac (Seneli) and Seneliac itself; the estate of Baldric (Baudreville), with arable lands and all belonging to that estate, and the jurisdiction of that authority—that is, the vicariate—as the privilege of Charles, king of the Franks, attests it was anciently given to your church by that king; the church of Artheniac (Arthenai), with arable lands, on which there was formerly an estate called *Peculiaris villa* (“the private estate”), and the tithes of those lands, and the house situated in that estate, which the king freed from every customary due and exaction.

Likewise, [Col. 1110B] the estate called Boiletum (Baulai), with its adjoining territory, the land-rent of the same estate, and other customary dues; the estate called Cunita (Cuni), with everything belonging to it, both persons and arable lands, tithes, and the other customary dues of that land; the lands which you have at Marolium (Mareau), beside Piveris (Pitiviers); the lands which you have at Romeliacum (Roumilli); the lands which you have at Sironville; the lands which you have at Moncellos (Monceaux), and beside them the wood called Cantamerula (Chantemêle); the lands which you have in the estate called Mantelii; the lands which you have at Merelatum (Merelay), and others at Geminiacum (Gemigni); and whatever you have [Col. 1110C] at Fayacum (Fay); the estate called Ursella (Oursel), near the town of Balgentiacum (Baugenci), with arable lands, land-rent, the dues and jurisdiction of the whole estate, and other customary dues; a prebend in the Church of Holy Cross, as you have hitherto held it peacefully; the rent of twelve solidi which Hugh, son of Ernaud, [source incomplete]; and the immunity which Charles the Great, king of the Franks, bestowed upon all your lands and possessions, namely that, wherever they are situated within his realm, they shall be free from all customary dues and exactions which the king’s officials were accustomed to levy upon them.

When you, the present abbot of that place, or any of your successors dies, no one may be set over it by any audacity of surreptitiousness or violence, unless he is one whom the brethren from the community of that place, or from another community of the same order, have canonically provided to be elected. [Col. 1110D] Certainly, no one whatsoever may presume to exact tithes from you on the produce which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or on the sustenance of your animals. We likewise grant you free authority to acquire or even redeem from lay hands those tithes which are known to belong by right to your churches.

We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, diminish or retain what has been taken, or harass it with any vexations; but let all things be preserved intact for the use and benefit in every way of those for whose governance [Col. 1111A] and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing the text of this our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, having been warned a second or third time, if he does not amend by fitting satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself to stand guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be separated from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Redeemer and Lord Jesus Christ; and let him be subject to stern vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and [Col. 1111B] before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Given at Trastevere through the hand of Robert, priest-cardinal and chancellor, on the sixth day before the Kalends of March, in the ninth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1146, and in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### LXXXV. Privilege for the Church of Saint Mary of Parma.  
*(Year 1146.)*

[AFFO, *History of Parma*, II, p. 363.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons AICARD, provost of the Church of Parma, and his brethren, present and future, to be canonically appointed: in perpetuity.

[Col. 1111C] A pious request ought to be fulfilled with an effective result, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth worthily and the benefit sought may undoubtedly acquire force. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, following in the footsteps of our predecessor Pope Innocent of happy memory, we graciously assent to your just requests. We receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid church, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may in future acquire, by concession of popes, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, God being favourable, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors.

Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names: the monastery of Saint Quentin, with the church of Saint Mary of the Plain and all other appurtenances belonging to it by right; the church of Saint Christina; the church of Saint Nicholas; the church of Saint Antoninus; the parish church of Saint Pancras, with the church of Saint Nicholas and its hospital beside the Taro, with the church of Saint Anastasius within the city, and all other appurtenances belonging to that parish church; the parish church of Saint Martin with its tithes; the parish church of Saint Prosper with its tithes; the parish church of Purpurano with its chapels; the parish church of Malandriano; the parish church of Saint Cassian with its tithes; the chapel of Viliguano; the chapel of Marano; the chapel of Meletulo; the chapel of Ballone; the chapel of Corviaco, situated within the castle; the chapel of Barca; the chapel of Marzaliis; the chapel of Azano; the chapel of Lower Vallera; the chapel of Travagnano; the chapel of Terentio; the chapel of Saint Secundus; the chapel of Pizzo; the chapel of Palazione; the chapel of Vicolongo; the chapel of Sala; the right which you have in the chapel of Saint George of the Meadows, the chapel of Ponticello, and the chapel in the village of Paul; the chapel of Ulmo; the chapel of Calerno with its hospital; the chapel of Saint Lawrence of Meletulo, with all appurtenances belonging by right to the aforesaid parish churches and chapels; the tithes of all who dwell in that city and its suburbs, as you have lawfully possessed them down to these times according to the division of the parish churches; and your share of the offerings made on the vigil and feast of Saint Domninus of the Borough, and at the Assumption of Blessed Mary, in the parish church of Cornilio. [Col. 1111D–1112B]

We therefore decree that no ecclesiastical or secular person whatsoever may rashly disturb that community, or take away, retain, diminish, or harass with any unjust exactions your goods or possessions. Rather, all things are to be preserved intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the canonical right and reverence due to your bishop. As a token of this protection received from the Apostolic See, you shall pay yearly to us and to our successors one gold bezant.

If, therefore, anyone in future, knowing the tenor of this our constitution, should rashly attempt to contravene it, and, after a second or third warning, should fail to make fitting reparation, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour, know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the wrong committed, be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer, and be subject at the last judgment to severe vengeance. [Col. 1112C]

But may the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all who preserve the rights of that place, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Imerius, bishop of Tusculum, have subscribed. [Col. 1112D] I, G.G., priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Callixtus, have subscribed. I, Guido, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Chrysogonus, have subscribed. I, Hubaldus, priest-cardinal of Saint Praxedes, have subscribed. I, Guido, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints Lawrence and Damasus, have subscribed. I, Odo, cardinal-deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal-deacon of Saint Angelo, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed.

Given at Trastevere through the hand of Robert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on 25 February, in the ninth indiction, in the year 1145 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

LXXXVI. Privilege for the church of St Andrew of Rochester. (A.D. 1146, 25 February.)

[WHARTON, *Anglia Sacra*, I, 344.]

[Col. 1113A]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons BRIEN, prior of the church of Blessed Andrew of Rochester, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

The care of the universal Church has been entrusted to us by the Lord, the Provider of all good things, in order that we may love religious persons, etc. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we assent to your just requests, receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid church of the Apostle Andrew, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions and goods you now justly and canonically possess, whether by gift or grant of Lanfranc, Anselm, Ralph, and Theobald, archbishops of Canterbury of blessed memory; Gundulf, bishop of Rochester; William and Henry, kings of the English; and other faithful persons; or may acquire in future, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. [Col. 1113B]

We also judge to be confirmed and valid the grant reasonably made to you by your bishop Ernulf concerning synodal pennies, and the charter recording it. Furthermore, we decree to be valid and firm the agreement justly and canonically made between you and our venerable brother Ascelin, your bishop, through the aforesaid Theobald, archbishop of Canterbury, concerning Lambeth and certain other possessions. [Col. 1113C] We also confirm to you the reeveship of that city, just as until now you have reasonably held, over your men and those of the bishop and of the king’s reeve, a fourth part; likewise sake and soke, toll and team, and infangthief, together with your other customs and liberties, etc.

Given at Trastevere through the hand of Robert, priest-cardinal of the Holy Roman Church and chancellor, on 27 April, in the eighth indiction, in the year 1146 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the second year of the pontificate of Pope Eugenius III.

LXXXVII. He approves the establishment of regular canons in the church of Tarentaise. (A.D. 1146, 26 February.)

[*Gallia Christiana nova*, XII, Instr. 382.]

[Col. 1113D]

EUGENIUS, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother PETER, archbishop of Tarentaise, and his brethren: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The authority of our office urges us to heed just prayers and by every means to promote the religious life pleasing to the Lord. Accordingly, we have confirmed by the protection of the Apostolic See the establishment in the church of Tarentaise of an order of canons according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine, made by concession of our predecessor Pope Innocent of happy memory. We decree that, when any of the canons there dies, no one except a professed regular canon shall be appointed in his place. [Col. 1114A]

We command that all who, after our predecessor’s said concession, have been installed contrary to the terms of that establishment be removed. We annul and declare void the gifts or alienations of the goods of that church made subsequently by Israel, once its archbishop. And because Peter, archbishop of Tarentaise of blessed memory, forbade under excommunication that the churches of Saint Maurice, Landriac, Rastheco, and Peseto be granted to Wibert and his brother Peter, or to anyone of their family, we confirm this provision as valid, just as it was confirmed by our predecessor Pope Lucius of pious memory.

Given at Trastevere, 26 February, in the eighth indiction, in the year 1145 of the Lord’s Incarnation. [Col. 1114B]

LXXXVIII. He confirms the rights and possessions of the regular canons of the church of St Peter of Tarentaise, and decrees that the regular order according to the Rule of St Augustine shall always be observed there. (A.D. 1146, 26 February.)

[Ibid.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the present and future canons of the church of Tarentaise professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

Since without the worship of true religion neither the unity of charity can endure nor service pleasing to God be offered, it is fitting for apostolic authority to love religious persons and, with the Lord’s help, provide for their peace. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, moved by the prayers of our venerable brother Peter, archbishop of Tarentaise, we graciously assent to your just requests. Following in the footsteps of our predecessor Pope Innocent of happy memory, we receive under the protection of the prince of the apostles and of ourselves the aforesaid church of Blessed Peter, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present document. First, indeed, we decree that the canonical order according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine shall be preserved there inviolate for all time. [Col. 1114C]

Moreover, whatever possessions and goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may in future acquire, through grants of popes, generosity of kings, gifts of princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, the Lord granting it, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. We also decree that, upon the death of any canon known to belong to your church, no one except a canon professing the regular life shall be appointed in his place. [Col. 1114D]

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid place, take away its possessions, retain things taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations. Rather, all things are to be preserved intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right and reverence due to the archbishop of Tarentaise. [Col. 1115A]

If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowing the tenor of this our constitution, should rashly attempt to contravene it, and, after a second or third warning, should fail to correct his offence by fitting satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour; let that person know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the wrong committed; let that person be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let that person be subject at the last judgment to severe vengeance. But may the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all who preserve the rights of that place, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen. [Col. 1115B]

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic See, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, G.G., priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Callixtus, have subscribed. I, Odo, cardinal-deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal-deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Raynerius, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Prisca, have subscribed. I, Octavian, cardinal-deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed. [Col. 1115C] I, Guido, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints Lawrence and Damasus, have subscribed. I, Bernard, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Clement, have subscribed. I, Cinthius, cardinal-deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed.

Given at Trastevere through the hand of Robert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on 26 February, in the ninth indiction, in the year 1145 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

LXXXIX. He exhorts all the faithful of God established throughout Gaul to undertake the holy war. (A.D. 1146, 1 March.) [Col. 1115D]

[BOCZEK, *Codex diplomaticus Moraviae*, I, 241, from a fourteenth-century quarto parchment codex in the archive of the chapter of Olomouc, titled: “Letters of Blessed Bernard of Clairvaux, etc.”, no. CXXVI.—This letter, with a few changes, is printed above under no. 48, but addressed to King Louis and dated at Vetralla, 1 December 1145. The variants are noted there.]

XC. Privilege for the monastery of Saints Peter and Paul of Westminster. (A.D. 1146, 8 March.)

[RYMER, *Foedera*, I, 14, from the original in the Cotton Library, Aug. II, 50.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son GERVASE, abbot of Westminster, and his successors regularly appointed: in perpetuity.

[Col. 1116A] Although, by the authority and benevolence of the Apostolic See, we are indebted to all sons of the holy Church, it is especially fitting that we should devote a more earnest concern of charity to those places and persons known to belong particularly to the ownership and defence of the Apostolic See, and provide with fatherly care lest they be troubled by the molestations of wicked men.

Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Gervase, we graciously assent to your just requests. Following in the footsteps of our predecessors, the Roman pontiffs, we decree that the monastery of Westminster, known to have been founded in honour of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul, shall remain solely under the protection and ownership of the prince of the apostles himself and of the Holy Roman Church, to whose jurisdiction it has been shown to belong; and we strengthen it by the privilege of this present document. [Col. 1116B] We decree that everything which that monastery has obtained from its beginning to the present by grant and donation, and also by the liberality of privileges and charters, through the bounty of ancient noble kings—namely Edgar and the glorious King Edward, restorer of that church—their successors William and Henry, or Stephen, other princes, or faithful persons; and whatever it may obtain in future, shall be entirely free and exempt from every invasion or disturbance by persons of any rank or power.

Furthermore, by the authority of God and of the holy apostles Peter and Paul, and of this Holy Roman See and of ourselves, we renew, grant, and permit, and confirm in perpetuity: the charters and privileges of the aforesaid kings and all written instruments of any nobles; likewise, those writings which Saint Dunstan, archbishop, conferred upon that church for the safeguarding of that place—so that the place may forever be wholly separated from every service and episcopal jurisdiction. [Col. 1116C]

We apostolically confirm, by divine and most firm authority, and decree to remain valid and uninjured forever, all possessions and benefactions in the city and outside it, of lands or churches, gifts of tithes, dignities, and all things given or hereafter to be added, which ancient kings or any other persons have piously bestowed for the liberty and exaltation of that place and in the honour of God; likewise the privileges and charters drawn up concerning them, in every respect as the holy charters and privileges of that church attest. Thus no one may dare to act against the goods of the aforesaid church, strengthened by the grant of the Holy Roman Church and our confirmation, or thereafter presume in any manner to infringe or diminish them. [Col. 1116D]

We also decree and, in the name of holy authority and obedience, command that the dependent cells adjoining that aforesaid place shall in every way be subject to it as to their own mother; and that whomever the entire community of the mother church has chosen jointly shall be placed over them as their guardian, as persons subject in all respects.

[Col. 1117A] If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowing the tenor of this our constitution, should rashly attempt to contravene it, and, after a second or third warning, should fail to make fitting reparation, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour, know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the wrong committed, be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer, and be subject at the last judgment to severe vengeance. But may the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all who preserve the rights of that place, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. [Col. 1117B] I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum. I, G.G., priest-cardinal of the title of Callixtus. I, Rainerius, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Prisca. I, Octavian, cardinal-deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. I, Gregory, cardinal-deacon of Saint Angelo.

Given at Kanstiberi [Note: [Col. 1117D] Read *Transtiberim*, “at Trastevere.”] through the hand of Robert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on 8 March, in the ninth indiction, in the year 1145 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

XCI. To the chaplains of the Church of Piacenza. (A.D. 1146, 10 March.)

[CAMPI, *History of the Church of Piacenza*, I, p. 144. *Book of Privileges of the Cathedral of Piacenza*, p. 46 verso.]

[Col. 1117C]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the chaplains of Saint Euphemia, Saint Gervasius, Saint Protasius, Saint Peter of the Forum, Saint Julian, Saint Martin of the Forum, Saint Domninus, Saint Alexander, Saint Martin of the Borough, Saint Vincent, Saint Stephen, Saints John and Paul, Saint Zeno, Saint Faustinus, Saint Michael, Saint Agatha, Saint Mary of Sperono, and Saint Mary of Porta Gariverti: greeting and apostolic blessing.

A complaint has reached our ears that, although according to the ancient custom of your mother church of Piacenza and of your chapels you ought to perform baptisms in the greater church on Holy Saturday, you now wish to withdraw that customary service from the aforesaid church and deny the obedience due to your mother. Since we do not wish an ancient and reasonable custom to be abolished, we command you by apostolic letters that you humbly render the aforesaid service of your devotion to that church, and presume to make no objection thereto; otherwise, we shall by no means leave your contempt unpunished. [Col. 1117D]

Given at Trastevere, 10 March.

XCII. To Abbot Suger.—That he should assist before the king the monastery of St Medard, burdened by the count of Soissons. (A.D. 1146, 11 March.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 647.]

[Col. 1118A]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son SUGER, abbot of Saint Denis: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It cannot be unknown to you that the monastery of Blessed Medard at Soissons belongs to the jurisdiction of blessed Peter and pertains especially to his defence and that of the Holy Roman Church. Since, as we have learned, that monastery is greatly burdened by Ivo, count of Soissons, on account of money which he demands from the abbot of that place, we request and command your discretion by apostolic letters that, out of reverence for blessed Peter and for us, you help and support that abbot and his brethren in this matter and in others in which they need your aid. [Col. 1118B] Act also as their intercessor and helper before the majesty of the royal dignity, whose favour and counsel you are known to enjoy, so that you may merit greater favour from blessed Peter and the Apostolic See.

Given at Trastevere, 11 March.

XCIII. To Egelbert, bishop, and the canons of the Church of Bamberg.—Concerning the sanctity, miracles, and canonization of Emperor Henry. (A.D. 1146, 14 March.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 630.]

[Col. 1118C]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother EGELBERT, bishop, and to his beloved sons, the canons of the Church of Bamberg: greeting and apostolic blessing.

As we remember having notified you through your letters and messengers, we delegated from our side our venerable brethren N., bishop of Santa Rufina, and N., priest-cardinal, to those regions on various affairs; and we charged them orally to visit your Church, make a careful inquiry into the truth concerning the life and miracles of King Henry, and report it to us in writing. [Col. 1118D]

Now, from the testimony of those our brethren and of many religious and prudent men, we have learned much concerning his chastity; the foundation of the Church of Bamberg and many others; the restoration of certain episcopal sees; his manifold generosity in almsgiving; the conversion, with the Lord’s cooperation, of King Stephen and all Hungary accomplished through him; his glorious death; and the many miracles divinely displayed in the presence of his body after his death. Among these matters we give particularly earnest attention to this chief and most memorable fact: though he had received the diadem and sceptre of empire, he lived not imperially but spiritually. [Col. 1119A] Although in a lawful marriage, he preserved intact until the end of his life the purity of chastity—something recorded of few.

Weighing all these things together, and carefully considering your devotion and that of the Church of Bamberg, which is known to be subject solely to the Holy Roman Church, we assent to your requests by the authority of the Holy Roman Church, the foundation of all councils, although a petition of this kind is not usually admitted except in general councils. Having taken counsel with our brethren, the archbishops and bishops present, we decree that from henceforth the commemoration of that memorable man whose exaltation you request shall be observed among the saints, and that his anniversary shall be celebrated solemnly. [Col. 1119B] It concerns you, therefore, to persevere in obedience and fidelity to the Holy Roman Church and to render it the service of fitting devotion, so that you may be found worthy of more abundant favour from blessed Peter and from us.

Given at Trastevere, 12 March.

XCIV. To Peter, archbishop of Bourges.—Concerning primacy over the provinces of Bourges and Bordeaux. (A.D. 1146, 15 March.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 668.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother P., archbishop of Bourges, and to his successors canonically appointed: for perpetual remembrance.

The authority of our office urges us to exercise fatherly concern for the condition of churches and, with the Lord’s help, beneficially provide for their tranquillity and peace. It is just that we too should preserve firm and inviolate, God being the author, the dignity granted by the generosity of the Apostolic See to churches or persons. Therefore, dearest brother in Christ, Archbishop Peter, observing your devotion toward us and toward the Holy Roman Church—of which you are a special son and in which you are known to have received holy orders—we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the noble church of Bourges, over which you preside by God’s appointment, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present document. [Col. 1119C–D]

By this present privilege we confirm that you shall hold primacy over two provinces, namely Bourges itself and Bordeaux, as you are known hitherto to have held it. We decree that the dioceses situated within the province of Bourges shall remain under the authority and jurisdiction of you and your successors: Clermont, Limoges, Rodez, Albi, Cahors, and Mende. The bishops of those cities shall recognize the church of Bourges as mother and teacher, and shall humbly render obedience and reverence to you and your successors as to their own metropolitan. [Col. 1120A]

Moreover, we confirm to you and your successors the use of the pallium. For greater honour, we grant that the banner of the Lord’s Cross may be borne before you throughout the aforesaid provinces, as the ancient custom of your predecessors also obtained. Furthermore, whatever possessions and whatever goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may acquire in future, etc. Upon the death of you, the present archbishop of that church, or of any of your successors, no one shall be placed there by any craft of deceit or violence, except the person whom the canons of the aforesaid church shall canonically provide to be elected according to God and the statutes of the Apostolic See. We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb that church or your person, etc.

XCV. Bull confirming the goods and immunities of Tongerlo. (A.D. 1146, 15 March.)

[HUGO, *Annals of the Premonstratensian Order*, II, 593.]

[Col. 1120B]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons HENRY, abbot of the church of Blessed Mary of Tongerlo, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: for perpetual remembrance.

A desire shown to pertain to the purpose of religion and the salvation of souls ought to be gladly granted, and fitting assistance should be afforded to the petitioners’ wishes. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions. We receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid church of Tongerlo, of the Blessed Mother of God and ever-virgin Mary, in which you are devoted to divine service; and we strengthen it by the privilege of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future acquire, through concessions of popes, generosity of kings, gifts of princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, the Lord granting it, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. [Col. 1120C]

Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names: two parts of the tithe of that church and the demesne, namely forty *bonaria* with one mill; land in the same parish yielding annually nineteen *sextaria* of malt, together with ten vessels of barley; moreover, land there yielding twelve shillings and one penny with the other dues of the land, and one holding yielding a fourth sheaf, and in addition one holding; the holding at Wimple, yielding five shillings with its other dues; the holding at Lanchem, yielding five shillings with its dues; land at Vuele yielding three and a half shillings with the remaining dues; the land which you received from Engelbert, for which you pay him annually two and a half *sextaria* of malt and twelve pence. [Col. 1120D]

All Hubert’s property at Evuin, granted to you both in allod and inheritance; land yielding twelve pence to the canons of Lyra; land yielding one penny upon the altar of Saint Gummarus; land yielding two shillings in the coinage of Leuven to the canons of Brussels. From Arnold’s gift, one half of Calmelholt. From Conrad’s gift, one holding at Lifterde, yielding a fourth sheaf and six pence; all Arnold’s allod at Nile, granted to you by him; from the gift of the brothers Gerard and Wibert, half the site of the church at Beinthem; and from the gift of that same Wibert, half the site of the church of Orbeca. We likewise confirm to you the tithes which you canonically possess. [Col. 1121A]

We prohibit anyone from usurping the advocacy of that place. Rather, the lord of Leuven for the time being, as has reasonably been established by our dearest son Conrad, king of the Romans, shall provide protection to you and your goods without any exaction.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb that church, take away its possessions, retain things taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations. Rather, all things are to be preserved intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. [Col. 1121B]

If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowing the tenor of this our constitution, should rashly attempt to contravene it, and, after a second or third warning, should fail to correct that person’s offence by fitting satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour, know that person guilty before the divine judgment for the wrong committed, be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer, and be subject at the last judgment to severe vengeance. But may the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all who preserve the rights of that place, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen. [Col. 1121C]

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. [Col. 1121D] I, Scribens, cardinal-deacon, of the title . . . [lacuna] I, Octavian, cardinal-deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. I, . . . priest-cardinal of the title of Callixtus. I, Guido, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Chrysogonus. I, Hubaldus, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Praxedes. I, Manfred, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Tu . . . [lacuna] I, Haribert, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Anastasia. I, Villanus, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill.

Given at Trastevere through the hand of Robert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the Ides of March [15 March], in the eighth indiction, in the year 1145 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

XCVI. To the clergy and people of Tournai.—He sends them a bishop, Anselm, restored to the Church of Tournai and consecrated by himself. (A.D. 1146, 15 March.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 663.]

[Col. 1122A]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his dearest sons, the clergy and people of Tournai: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The Church of Tournai has suffered greatly for a long time through the absence of its own shepherd. As we have learned from the testimony of many religious and prudent men, it has sustained many losses of souls and bodies and serious injuries. For we have heard that many thousands of persons in that bishopric never saw a bishop; but, as though they had no bishop, they departed this present world without the anointing of sacred chrism which the faithful, who must fight against the snares of the devil, receive through the hands of bishops. [Col. 1122B]

Accordingly, compelled by the duty of our office, by the frequent exhortations of many religious persons from your regions, and inflamed with zeal of charity, we have resolved, with the Lord’s help, to meet such great evils. Having taken counsel with our brethren, and invoking the grace of the Holy Spirit, we have consecrated for you as bishop our beloved son Anselm, abbot of Saint Vincent at Laon. Sending him back to his proper see with the favour of the Apostolic See and the authority of our letters, we ask, exhort, and command your whole body by apostolic letters to receive him reverently, love and honour him, and humbly render to him obedience and reverence as to your own shepherd and bishop of your souls. [Col. 1122C]

By apostolic authority, we absolve from that allegiance, oath, or obedience all those who, on account of the bishopric of Tournai, have been bound by oath, fealty, or obedience to our brother S. [Simon], bishop of Noyon. We command that they shall be bound by the same fealty and obedience to our aforesaid brother, Bishop Anselm. If anyone should presume to be rebellious or disobedient to him, we shall, with the Lord as author, hold valid the sentence which that same our brother the bishop shall canonically pronounce against that person. [Col. 1122D]

Given at Trastevere, on the Ides of March [15 March].

XCVII. To Louis VII, king of the French.—He commends Anselm, bishop of Tournai, consecrated by himself. (A.D. 1146, 15 March.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 664.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his dearest son in Christ, LOUIS, illustrious king of the French: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is fitting that we should be solicitous for those who, by the Lord’s ordering, are entrusted to our governance, and should think of their salvation as of our own; for at the final judgment, if we have been negligent regarding their salvation, we shall render an account for them to the Lord. As we do not believe you are unaware, the Church of Tournai is known to have lacked its own pastor from times long past. Hence, as we have learned from the truthful report of many religious and discerning men, apart from other losses, many thousands of persons have departed this present world without that anointing of sacred chrism which believers, when about to contend against the snares of the devil, receive through the hands of bishops; and through this and in various other ways, very great losses, both to souls and bodies, have arisen in that bishopric through the absence of its proper pastor.

Therefore, wishing to provide both for ourselves and for them, we have resolved, with the Lord’s help, to meet such great evils; and, having invoked the grace of the Holy Spirit, we have consecrated our beloved son Anselm, abbot of Saint Vincent of Laon, as bishop of Tournai. We believe that this will result in a great increase to the kingdom entrusted to you by God and to your crown. We therefore admonish your nobility and exhort you in the Lord that no perverse suggestion may move your heart in this matter; but that you receive with cheerful countenance and glad spirit what has been done because of so great a necessity and for the salvation of so many thousands of persons, and that, out of reverence for blessed Peter and for us, you strive to assist and uphold the same bishop by the counsel and aid of your greatness. For whatever honor and benefaction may be bestowed upon him by your generosity, we reckon as bestowed upon ourselves.

Given beyond the Tiber, on the Ides of March.

XCVIII. To Alvisus, bishop of Arras, and Milo, bishop of Thérouanne.—That they should ensure that Anselm, consecrated by him bishop of Tournai, is received by the king of France and the count of Flanders. (Year 1146.)

[BOUQUET, *Recueil*, XV, p. 437.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brothers A[LVISUS], bishop of Arras, and M[ILO], bishop of Thérouanne, greeting and apostolic blessing.

By your representation, brother A., bishop of Arras, and that of many other religious and discerning men, we have learned that, if the Church of Tournai had its own bishop, the honor of God would there be increased and salvation would thereby come to many thousands of souls, who are endangered without episcopal care and the provident care of their own pastor. Therefore, inflamed with zeal for charity and justice, and moved by your exhortation as though it were that of the Lord Jesus Christ himself, we have wished to meet such great evils and, with the Lord’s help, have completed what our predecessor Pope Innocent of happy memory began concerning the establishment of a bishop there.

> [Note: Col. 1123C. Herimannus recounts at length the course of events under Innocent, ibid., p. 408: “At the same time,” he says, “that is, in the year 1142, a dispute arose between Pope Innocent and King Louis, son of the aforesaid Louis, and the kinsmen mentioned above—namely Simon, bishop of Noyon, and Count Ralph of Vermandois—on account of which the king and the count were deprived of communion and remained so for a year; while the bishop was suspended from episcopal office for some time [lacuna].
>
> “When this dissension between the pope, the king, and the bishop of Noyon became known, Provost Theoderic, who succeeded Gunther, burning with desire, together with the clergy of Tournai, that his church should recover its former dignity, privately addressed Lord Herimannus, who had formerly been our abbot, urging him to go to Rome and cautiously sound out the pope’s mind in this matter. Lord Herimannus, favoring their prayers, went to Rome, showed Pope Innocent the letters which Pope Paschal had formerly sent to the people of Tournai, and set forth the entire course of the matter described above. At last he also received letters from him, in which he admonished the people of Tournai and commanded them by apostolic authority, after taking counsel with religious and discerning men, to elect their own bishop without delay and to present the elect to the metropolitan of Reims for consecration; but if he should refuse to perform this, they were to bring him into the pope’s presence [lacuna].
>
> “Having therefore taken counsel with religious men, we unanimously elected Absalon, abbot of Saint-Amand, a religious man, to be our bishop. The election was immediately reported to the archbishop of Reims; but he said that he did not dare consecrate him through fear of the king and Count Ralph. We were therefore compelled by necessity to refer the matter to Rome. The elect himself, however, being a wise man, refused to go, fearing—as later occurred—that the Roman curia might be turned from its judgment by money,” etc.
>
> Thus Herimannus—or another contemporary of his—who adds concerning Eugenius: “When this man was reported to us all not to be greedy for money, having been informed through intermediaries about our affair and asked what he intended to do in it, he replied that he would do whatever the abbot of Clairvaux should direct him by letter.”]

We therefore ask your charity and exhort you in the Lord that you labor most diligently, both with our dearest son L[ouis], illustrious king of the Franks, and Count T[heoderic] of Flanders, and with such others as you recognize to be expedient, for the peaceable and honorable reception of that bishop; and that you take care, in brotherly charity, to provide for his quiet and tranquillity. (The remainder is lacking.)

XCIX. To Bernard, abbot of Clairvaux.—He signifies that at Bernard’s request he consecrated Anselm bishop of Tournai, and commands him to strive to work for his peace. (Year 1146.)

[D. BOUQUET, XV, p. 438.]

[Col. 1124C]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his dearest son in Christ BERNARD, abbot of Clairvaux, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Inflamed with zeal for charity, and moved especially by your exhortation and that of many other religious and discerning men, we have completed, with the Lord’s help, what our predecessor Pope Innocent of happy memory began concerning the appointment of a bishop in the Church of Tournai; and, having invoked the grace of the Holy Spirit, we have consecrated our beloved son Anselm, abbot of Saint Vincent of Laon, as bishop there. We therefore admonish your charity, in which we have great confidence in the Lord, that you should strive to labor both with our dearest son Louis, king of the Franks, and with such others as you recognize to be expedient, for his peace; and that by the counsel and assistance of your goodness, according to the Lord, you support and uphold him, lest any perverse suggestion be able to corrupt the heart of the Most Christian king in this matter. In this act we intend no diminution whatever of that king; rather, we believe that we have proceeded in this cause for the honor of God and the increase of his kingdom. (The remainder is lacking.)

> [Note: Col. 1125D. “He also sent other letters,” says Herimannus, “to the bishop of Noyon, in which he exhorted him to bear patiently the fact that the people of Tournai had a bishop of their own, and not to presume, either in person or through anyone subject to him, to inflict any molestation upon him. He also commanded the metropolitan of Reims and the bishops of the province to uphold him and assist him in all things, to admonish the bishop of Noyon to desist from every presumption, and to be reconciled with him in peace. But Simon himself was a most gentle man and did not know how to repay evildoers with evil; and therefore it came about that he did not attempt, either in word or deed, to act against the pope’s command. This also accorded with the nobility of his lineage.” We do not possess those letters of Eugenius.]

XCIX *bis*. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Peter at Salzburg. (Year 1146, March 25?)

[*Nov. Chron. S. Petri Salisburg.*, 231.]

[Col. 1125B]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons BALDERIC, abbot of the monastery of Saint Peter at Salzburg, and his brothers, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

It is fitting that we readily grant a desire that is known to concern the purpose of religion and the salvation of souls, and extend suitable support to the desires of petitioners. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions; and we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and our own the aforesaid monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods have been reasonably granted to your church by the archbishops of Salzburg and confirmed by their charters, and whatever else you now possess justly and canonically, or may hereafter be able to acquire, by the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings, the gifts of princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through the Lord’s favor, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. We have considered it proper to specify among them the following in their own names:

the church of Saint Michael, situated at the city gate, with its tithe and endowed manor; the church at Walmes, with the tithe of Prettinave, Peirheimin, Meniwisin, and Munichus; likewise tithes from sixteen estates; in Chiemgau, from ten *hubae*; in Carinthia, from half a *huba* and eight estates; also tithes from three fisheries—at Fusculfe, and at Abersee; tithes of cheeses given to bishops at Torlagowa, Hoiberga, and Elsinwanc; the island named Appanowa beside the river called Lamera, one half of which has been apportioned for the use of the poor and the other half for the sustenance of the brothers, in equal division, by our venerable brother Conrad, archbishop of Salzburg; ten manors which Duke Henry, son of Engelbert, and six manors which his brother Engelbert, margrave, left to the aforesaid archbishop, and which he himself gave to your monastery out of piety; the benefice of the widow Gerviga at Rakkingin; the benefice of Berthold at Wengi and Ramiside; the benefice of Megingoz of Sulberch at Pinzgau; the benefice of Piligrin of Schalheim at Walabingin and Haselpach; the benefice of Eticho of Blase above Yagara; the benefice of Eberhard of Fritelingin, at Copingin and Talehusen, with its mill; one plot within the city; a vineyard situated on the hill neighboring Riesttinpurch; a plot and vineyard with their appurtenances at Arnsdorff; the benefice of Eruto the blind at Holzhusen; the benefice of Henry of Pongau at Tomerespach; the benefice of the two brothers Adalbert and Cotescalch at Lingheringin and Haldenwanc, at Tiufinpaha and Chunohingin; one *patella* with all its appurtenances, which you transferred from the aforesaid our brother the archbishop; and the benefice of Wolfram of Ossinwane, reasonably bequeathed to your church by that same man and granted by the archbishop.

We decree, therefore, that it shall be lawful for no one at all to rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, seize its possessions, retain what has been seized, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things be preserved intact for the benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted, to be useful to them in every way, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right and reverence due to the archbishop of Salzburg.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly attempts rashly to act against this page of our constitution, after a second or third admonition, unless he makes good his offense by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ; and at the last judgment let him be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ rest, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Odo, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. I, John, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary the New. I, G[?], cardinal priest of the title of Calixtus. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Chrysogonus. I, Rainerius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Prisca. I, Hubald, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes. I, Ubald, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross. I, Bernard, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Clement.

Given beyond the Tiber through the hand of Robert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the eighth day before the Kalends of April, in the eighth indiction, in the year 1145 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the second year of the pontificate of Pope Eugenius III.

C. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Nicasius at Reims. (Year 1146, March 25.)

[VARIN, *Archives administratives de Reims*, I, I, 316.]

[Col. 1127B]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son JOHN, abbot of Saint Nicasius, and to his successors, present and future, to be regularly appointed in perpetuity.

From the letters of our venerable father Samson, archbishop of Reims, we have learned that Count Henry, with his wife and sons, and Clarembald of Roseto, likewise with his wife and sons, inflamed with the fire of divine love and stirred by the exhortations of our dearest son Bernard, abbot of Clairvaux, freely and absolutely renounced into the hands of that archbishop, for the remission of their sins, the church of blessed Mary of the castle of Port, which they possessed hereditarily against justice and the salvation of their souls; asking him to grant that church to the monastery of Saint Nicasius and establish a monastic order there. He willingly accepted their request, granted the same church with all its appurtenances to the aforesaid monastery for the establishment of a monastic order there, and confirmed it by his charter [lacuna]. We confirm the same grant or donation [lacuna].

Moreover, whatever Arnulf of Gest, with the counsel and assent of our predecessor Pope Innocent of happy memory and likewise of our venerable brother Albero, bishop of Liège, has justly and canonically granted you from his own right in allods and other property, we likewise confirm to you and your church: namely, all the land which Arnulf himself and his brother John possessed by hereditary right; in addition, half an allod in fields, meadows, woods, and whatever he possessed there; the allod in the village of Vesana; the allod of Resbais; the allod of Hesbinis; and the allod of Rumestat with the tithe of Guzencurt.

If anyone knowingly attempts rashly to act against this page of our confirmation, after a second or third admonition, unless he corrects his offense by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ; and at the final judgment let him be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ rest, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

Given at Sutri, on the eighth day before the Kalends of April.

CI. To Samson, archbishop of Reims.—He rebukes him because he presumed to crown the king of France in the city of Bourges, contrary to the right of the archbishop of Bourges, and therefore forbids him the use of the pallium. (Year 1146, March 26.)

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XXI, 666.]

[Col. 1128B]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother SAMSON, archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Nearly the whole world has known, and your prudence ought not to have been unaware, how greatly the holy Roman Church and our predecessors of happy memory—namely Innocent, Celestine, and Lucius—labored for the peace of the Church of Bourges and of our venerable brother Peter, archbishop of that church. But now, when through God’s grace and the effort of those same predecessors of ours it had come to a haven of tranquillity, you, who ought to have rejoiced with your brother, have instead, in reverse fashion, burst forth in rash audacity to his injury and disturbance. You presumed to crown our dearest son Louis, illustrious king of the Franks, in the city of Bourges despite an appeal to the Apostolic See—a thing which neither you nor any of your predecessors is known to have done. Rather, the archbishops of Bourges—Leodegarius, Vulgrin, and Alberic, all of good memory—are known to have possessed this right peacefully and undisturbed down to these times.

Nor did that final refuge of the afflicted—the appeal to the Apostolic See—avail the same archbishop; nor did the fact that he had dutifully visited his mother, the Holy Roman Church, and our presence, and stood before us that very day. Indeed, in greater contempt of blessed Peter and of us, you sacrilegiously invaded the Church of Bourges, though it was under interdict from divine offices, together with Gossenus, bishop of Soissons, other suffragans of your church, abbots, and many others of your province; and you rashly presumed there to celebrate divine offices and carry away offerings. At the appointed term of appeal, moreover, you neither came yourself nor sent to our presence adequate representatives to answer for you.

Had you weighed with careful reflection how greatly you offended and how greatly you diminished the dignity of your mother, the Holy Roman Church, you would never have burst forth into such audacity. The greater the dignity which you have received from your mother, the Holy Roman Church, the greater was the honor and reverence you ought to have shown her. Nor have we thought it right to leave unmentioned that this same brother of ours, Archbishop Peter, was promoted to holy orders in the Roman Church by our predecessor Pope Innocent of happy memory, and was sent by him to govern the Church of Bourges. We therefore wish you to know that we regard injuries done to him and to the Church entrusted to him by the Lord not as alien but as our own, and as inflicted upon ourselves.

Although, for so great an offense and so manifest a contempt, we might by the rigor of justice have pronounced a graver sentence against you and your accomplices, nevertheless, from the clemency of the Apostolic See we have judged that the sentence due should be deferred. Yet, lest we seem to dissemble so great an offense and pass over it, as it were, in silence, after taking counsel with our brothers we prohibit your use of the pallium. By this apostolic writing we command and order you that within forty days after receiving the present letter, you return in their entirety to the Church of Bourges, through suitable and honorable persons, those offerings—and especially those candles—which you received in that church, and cause them to be restored openly upon the altar, just as the injury was open.

Concerning so great a contempt of blessed Peter and of us, you shall present yourself before the apostolic tribunal, to answer and make satisfaction, together with your accomplices: G[oslenus], bishop of Soissons; A[lvisus], bishop of Arras; O[do], bishop of Beauvais; T[heoderic], bishop of Amiens; S. [corrected to P., Peter], bishop of Senlis; S[imon], bishop of Noyon; G[uy], bishop of Châlons; Bartholomew, treasurer of Laon; and Boso of Reims, who stood with you in such presumption, on the octave after the coming feast of Saint Martin (18 November).

Given at Sutri, on the seventh day before the Kalends of April.

CII. He writes to the consuls of Laon that “it is clear that the document which the bishop of Laon, under the name of Robald, archbishop of Milan of blessed memory, produced in the presence of his predecessor Lucius concerning the case being conducted between himself and the brothers of Cerreto, was rejected by that pope himself.” (Fragment—Year 1146, April 8.)

[GIULINI, *Memorie di Milano*, V, 449.]

CIII. He grants privileges to the monastery of Fleury. (Year 1146, April 15.)

[Col. 1129D]

[Only mention of this privilege survives in SAUSSEY, *Annales de l’Église d’Orléans*, 200 and 226.]

CIV. To Henry, bishop of Moravia.—Concerning a certain matter of establishing peace entrusted to him. (Year 1146, April 22.)

[BOCZEK, *Codex diplomaticus Moraviae*, I, 240.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to HENRY, bishop of Moravia, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since it is the office of apostolic dignity, over which, though unworthy, we preside, to love, shape, and strengthen concord in the kingdom, and diligently to watch over the daily progress in the Lord of the whole Church, we have determined that it is always useful to share with you also, our dearest faithful co-worker, some labor, however small, to be borne for the necessity and advantage of the Church. We have therefore entrusted to your solicitude the word of peace, the saving word, so that, like a prudent steward, you may sow the seed of the Lord’s grain in good soil, in fertile ground; from which, through the fruit of your labor, a crown of righteousness may grow both for us and for you, on account of your cultivation and love of the divine law.

If, therefore, you faithfully dispense to faithful soil, which yields fruit in its seasons, the seed of the word received from reverence for apostolic authority, and if indeed you nourish it so that it produces fruit—or, if it has not yet produced fruit, whether it must still be awaited for some time—we desire to be informed by your charity.

[Col. 1130B] Given at Sutri, on the tenth day before the Kalends of March.

> [Note: Col. 1129D. Read: “the tenth day before the Kalends of May.” JAFFÉ.]

CV. To R., bishop of Bazas, concerning the abbey of Saint Fremerius. (Year 1146, April 22.)

[*Gallia Christiana*, new ed., I, Documents, 190.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to R., bishop of Bazas, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Our beloved son Matthew, abbot of Saint-Florent, has complained to us that the abbot and monks of Saint Fremerius withhold from him their due and customary obedience and by no means observe their profession according to the Rule. Since we desire that justice be rendered to each church and ecclesiastical person, by this present apostolic writing we command you to admonish those monks strictly on our behalf: they are humbly to render to the same abbot of Saint-Florent their due and customary obedience without contradiction, and beneficially correct their offenses in accordance with that abbot’s admonition; otherwise, we shall not leave their disobedience and laxity unpunished.

Given at Sutri, on the tenth day before the Kalends of May.

CVI. Privilege for the nunnery of Blessed Mary in the forest of Nidi-Merli. (Year 1146, April 24.)

[PAVILLON, *Life of Robert of Arbrissel*, Preface, p. 570.]

[Col. 1130D]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ, MARY, abbess of the monastery of Blessed Mary situated in the forest of Nidi-Merli, and to the sisters, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

Since without the observance of true religion neither the unity of charity can endure nor service pleasing to the Lord be offered, it is fitting for apostolic authority to cherish religious persons and provide for their peace with paternal solicitude. Therefore, beloved daughters in the Lord, following in the footsteps of our predecessors of happy memory, the Roman pontiffs Calixtus and Innocent, and likewise moved by the prayers of our venerable brother Geoffrey, archbishop of Bordeaux, we graciously assent to your just petitions. We receive under the protection of blessed Peter and our own the aforesaid monastery of the Blessed Mother of God Mary, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the aforesaid monastery now possesses justly and canonically, or may hereafter be able to acquire, by the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through the Lord’s favor, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors.

We have considered it proper to specify the following in their own names: the church of Saint Mary in Scotia, situated in the diocese of Nantes; in the same diocese, the church of Saint Radegund and the church of Saint Honorina with their appurtenances; in the diocese of Cornouaille, the church called the Place of Mary (*Locus Mariae*) with its appurtenances; in the diocese of Aleth, the church of Saint Santonius of Teloio and the church of Saint Germanus with their appurtenances; in the diocese of Rennes, the church of Saint Macutus in the forest called Tilia, with its appurtenances; in the diocese of Le Mans, the church of Saint Mary called the Fountain of Saint Martin, with its appurtenances; in the diocese of Tours, the church of Saint Mary Magdalene called Fraxinea; in the diocese of Angers, the alms-estate of Halenodium with its appurtenances, the church of Saint James of Lutrium, and the church of the same apostle called Petra Alberiae, with its appurtenances; in the diocese of Poitiers, the church of Saint Mary called Fulgerosa, with its appurtenances, etc.

We also forbid anyone, after making profession in the same monastery, to depart without the permission of the abbess and her chapter; and no one may dare retain one who has departed. We decree, therefore, that it shall be lawful for no one at all rashly to disturb the aforesaid monastery, seize its possessions, retain what has been seized, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things be preserved intact for the benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted, to be useful to them in every way.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly attempts rashly to act against this page of our constitution, after a second or third admonition, unless she corrects her offense by suitable satisfaction, let her be deprived of the dignity of her power and honor; let her know herself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let her be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ; and at the last judgment let her be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ rest, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given on the eighth day before the Kalends of May, in the ninth indiction, in the year 1146 of the Lord’s Incarnation.

CVII. To the bishops of the province of Bordeaux.—Concerning ecclesiastical and canonical liberty. (Year 1146, April 24.)

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XXI, 679.]

[Col. 1132A]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brothers GEOFFREY, archbishop of Bordeaux, and his suffragan bishops—namely those of Agen, Angoulême, Saintes, Poitiers, and Périgueux—and to all abbots established throughout the same province, present and future, in perpetuity.

Privileges bestowed upon the most holy churches, for the sake of liberty, by Roman pontiffs or Catholic kings ought not to be overthrown by any rashness or disturbed by any change of times.
