For just as the Catholic mother Church shines in spiritual matters without spot or wrinkle, with the manifold fragrance and brightness of virtues, so in temporal matters it is fitting that she be subject to no servitude and to no worldly condition. This being so, we, following in the footsteps of our predecessors of good memory, the Roman pontiffs Innocent and Lucius, strengthen by the assertion of our favor the liberty conferred upon the churches of the province of Bordeaux by the illustrious men Louis the father, of distinguished memory, and his son Louis, kings of the Franks, and confirmed by their privileges; and we command that it be observed in future times as valid and inviolable.

That is: both in the see of Bordeaux and in the other episcopal churches or abbeys of the same province, in elections of bishops or abbots, you are to possess canonical liberty, without an obligation of homage, oath, or faith pledged by the giving of hands.

Moreover, what our predecessors decreed in general councils—that all the property and goods of a deceased archbishop of Bordeaux, suffragan bishop, or abbot be preserved whole and inviolate for the use of successors—we likewise decree by apostolic authority. We further add that all churches established within the aforesaid province shall possess intact and undisturbed their estates, possessions, and everything belonging to them, according to their privileges, rights, and good customs; and that, as has been said, in all your churches, their ministers, and your possessions, you shall possess canonical liberty in all things, saving the authority of the Apostolic See.

Let no one, therefore, presume rashly to disturb you or your churches concerning this constitution of ours, or inflict upon you any opposition thereby. But if anyone attempts in rash audacity to oppose this constitution of ours, unless he suitably amends his offense, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor, incur the indignation of almighty God and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul, and be subject to excommunication. But those who preserve it shall obtain the blessing and favor of the same apostles. Amen.

[Col. 1133A]

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, Imar, bishop of Tusculum, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Chrysogonus, have subscribed. I, Hubald, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Lawrence and Damasus, have subscribed. I, Jordan, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna, have subscribed. I, Odo, cardinal deacon of Saint Gregory at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Angel, have subscribed.

Given at Sutri through the hand of Robert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the eighth day before the Kalends of May, in the ninth indiction, in the year 1146 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius.

CVIII. Privilege for the canons of the church of Saint Ursus of Aosta. (Year 1146, April–May.)

[*Historia patriae Monumenta*, Charters, I, 790.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ARNALD, prior of the church of Saints Peter and Ursus at Aosta, and his brothers, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

Since without the observance of true religion neither the unity of charity can endure nor service pleasing to God be offered, it is fitting for apostolic authority to cherish religious persons and, with the Lord’s aid, to provide for their peace. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions. We receive under the protection of blessed Peter and our own the aforesaid Church of Saints Peter and Ursus, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods you now possess justly and canonically, or may hereafter be able to acquire by the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings, the gifts of princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through the Lord’s favor, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors.

We likewise decree that burial in that place shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who decide to be buried there, unless perhaps they are excommunicated, saving the right of the mother church. Upon the death of you, the present prior of that place, or of any of your successors, no one may be placed over it by any trickery of subreption or violence, except one whom the brothers by common consent, or the sounder part of the brothers, shall provide to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Augustine.

We decree, therefore, that it shall be lawful for no one at all rashly to disturb the aforesaid Church, seize its possessions, retain what has been seized, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things be preserved intact for the benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted, to be useful to them in every way, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right and reverence due to the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly attempts rashly to act against this page of our constitution, after a second or third admonition, unless he corrects his offense by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ; and at the last judgment let him be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ rest, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Hubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes, have subscribed. I, Humbaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Aribertus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint [Col. 1134C] Anastasia, have subscribed. I, Jordanus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna, have subscribed.

Given at Sutri, through the hand of Robert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, in the ninth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1146, in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

## CIX. Privilege for the monastery of Reichersberg.  
*(1146, May 4.)*

*[Monumenta Boica, IV, 412.]*

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GEROH, provost of the Church of Reichersberg, [Col. 1134D] and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

It befits us willingly to grant a desire shown to concern the purpose of religious life and the salvation of souls, and to afford suitable support to the requests of petitioners. For just as no effect is to be granted to those asking what is unjust, so no petition ought to be delayed for those desiring what is lawful and just. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, following in the footsteps of our predecessor Pope Innocent, of happy memory, and likewise moved by the prayers of our venerable brother Conrad, Archbishop of Salzburg, we mercifully assent to your just petitions. We receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and strengthen by the privilege of this present writing, your monastery, situated in the diocese of Passau upon land belonging to the Church of Salzburg, [Col. 1135A] where you are devoted to divine service.

First, indeed, we decree that in both your own house and the monastery of nuns subject to you, the canonical order, according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine, shall be preserved inviolate for all time. Furthermore, whatever possessions and goods that same church now rightfully and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by the grant of pontiffs, the liberality of kings, the bounty of princes, the offerings of the faithful, or by other just means, through the Lord’s favour, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their own names:

[Col. 1135B] Namely, the estate and parish of Reichersberg, with its tithe and parochial right; the chapel of Saint Martin with its appurtenances; vineyards at Ascha; the village of Chrouvat; and the remaining estates offered to you by Werher, founder of that place; the tithes of the church of Bramberg and of the newly cultivated lands of the Passau Forest, belonging from the aforesaid parishes as far as the Hungarian boundaries, confirmed to you by the privilege of our venerable brother Conrad, Archbishop of Salzburg; a pan of salt and other estates given by the same bishop; Hefstat and other estates rightfully offered by Ruodbertus; estates given by Fridericus; the estates formerly belonging to Egelolfus and Eberhardus, with their tithes, reasonably granted to you by the Bishop of Freising; vineyards purchased at Chremesa; [Col. 1135C] and what Duke Luipoldus conveyed from his own right.

Certainly, no one at all shall presume to exact tithes from you upon the produce of your labour which you cultivate with your own hands or resources, or upon the produce of your animals. You shall receive ecclesiastical sacraments from the diocesan bishop, or from the Archbishop of Salzburg, provided that he enjoys the favour and communion of the Apostolic See and is willing to confer them upon you freely and without improper exaction. Otherwise, for receiving those sacraments, you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer, who, supported by our authority, shall grant what you have requested.

And since the place appears to have been established such that the principal advocate of the Church of Salzburg is the same person, [Col. 1135D] neither he nor anyone else may be permitted to harass that place with unjust burdens. If he does so and, upon your complaint, does not make amends, then, by counsel of the aforesaid archbishop, that advocacy shall be taken from the unfit holder and another substituted in his place.

Upon the death of you who are now provost of that place, or should you pass to the governance of another church, or upon the death of any one of your successors, no one shall be placed or substituted there through any crafty device or violence, except one whom the brethren, by common consent or by the sounder part of the council, shall canonically provide to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of Blessed Augustine. We further forbid anyone of your profession, prompted by fickleness or under pretext of a stricter religious life, to depart without the permission of the provost [Col. 1136A] or the community. Should anyone depart, no bishop, abbot, or monk shall receive him without the security of letters shared between the parties, so long, that is, as the observance of canonical order continues in force in your church, by the Lord’s favour. But if, having been summoned a second or third time, he scorns to return, the provost of that place may pronounce canonical sentence against him.

We also grant that the burial-place of that house shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict, without prejudice to the right of the mother church.

Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid Church, take away its [Col. 1136B] possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but that all shall be preserved whole for the benefit of those for whose governance and maintenance they were granted, and shall be of use to them in every way, without prejudice to the authority of the Apostolic See and to the canonical right of the Archbishop of Salzburg and the Bishop of Passau. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been admonished a second or third time, should fail to correct the offence by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and honour, know himself or herself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed, be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer, [Col. 1136C] and be subject to strict vengeance at the final judgment. But let all who preserve the just rights of that place have the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Albericus, Bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, Imarus, Bishop of Tusculum, have subscribed. I, Octavianus, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed. I, Rainerius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Prisca, have subscribed. I, Ubaldus, cardinal priest of Saints John and [Col. 1136D] Paul, have subscribed. I, Aribertus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia, have subscribed. I, Manfredus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Sabina, have subscribed. I, Villanus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill, have subscribed. I, Bernardus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Clement, have subscribed. I, Ubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed. I, Petrus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed. [Col. 1137A] I, Cinthius, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed.

Given at Sutri, through the hand of Robert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the fourth day before the Nones of May, in the ninth indiction, in the year of the Lord 1146, in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

## CX. Privilege for the monastery of Saints Peter and Paul at Paderborn.  
*(1146, May 7.)*

*[SCHATEN, Annals of Paderborn, I, 765.]*

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons CONRAD, abbot of the monastery of the blessed apostles [Col. 1137B] Peter and Paul, situated in the city of Paderborn, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: for perpetual remembrance.

It befits the clemency of apostolic governance to love religious persons and fortify their places with pious protection. For it is recognized as worthy and becoming to honour that we, who have been appointed to govern the churches, should both protect them from the wickedness of evil men and sustain them by the patronage of the Apostolic See. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we mercifully assent to your just petitions, receive the aforesaid monastery, where you are devoted to divine service, under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. [Col. 1137C] We decree that whatever possessions and goods you now rightfully and canonically possess, or may hereafter acquire, through grants of pontiffs, the liberality of kings, the bounty of princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through the Lord’s favour, shall remain firm for you and your successors. [lacuna]

Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their own names: Widun with its church; Merbeke with its church; Gelsendorp; Rumbeke; Fuclon; Dotenhusen; Waltmannenghuson; Halle; Thensin; Rime; Deheim; Bekehuson; Habergo; Edekehuson; Nederc; Ossendorp; Curbike; Messere; Bullenghuson; Menne; Andepo, with its church. Likewise, in lower Andepo: Volpethenhuson; [Col. 1137D] Fornholte; the church at Haltenghuson, with episcopal ban and three chapels; Bellede; the tithe at Wilbodessun; Bethengdorp; Hese; Sturenbrug; Suinveld; Weplede; Burgnon with its church and a tithe from the manor; Butenen; Unnenscare with its tithe; Nortburgnon with its tithe; Alfnon; Meslete; Hedmere; Hengeldere; Atlon with its church and a tithe from the manor; Butenen; Balhorn; Burele, which was Sundra, with its tithe; Helsen and its mill with fishpond; Lessethe; Scarheim; Wambeke; Ermescenhuson; Cethslere; Hohensele; Rederbruggon; Radengheim with its chapel and a tithe from half the village of Putthen; the manor and church, with half a tithe, and the chapel at Vorthuson belonging to the same church; Appele; Weshle in Thesterbrant; [Col. 1138A] the manor with its entire household; the church at Duilon with four chapels, namely Niwelen, Hellue, Hasten, and Gamberen, with half a tithe.

Upon the death of you who are now abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be placed there through any crafty device or violence, except one whom the brethren, by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren’s council, shall provide to be elected from that cloister according to the fear of God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict—or, if necessary, from another. You may also choose priests for the parish churches which you hold and present them to the diocesan bishop; if they are suitable, the bishop shall commit the care of souls to them, so that they may answer to the bishop for the care of the people, but render to you due subjection in temporal matters. [Col. 1138B]

Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but that all shall be preserved whole for the benefit of those for whose governance and maintenance they were granted, and shall be of use to them in every way, without prejudice to the authority of the Apostolic See and to the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it and, having been admonished a second or third time, should fail to correct the offence by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and honour, know himself or herself guilty before divine judgment [Col. 1138C] of the iniquity committed, be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer, and be subject to strict vengeance at the final judgment. But let all who preserve the rights of that place have the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church.

**MAKE FOR ME, O LORD, A SIGN FOR GOOD.**

I, Albericus, Bishop of Ostia. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint Gregory at the Golden Veil. [Col. 1138D] I, Rainerius, cardinal. I, Aribertus, cardinal priest. I, Ubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Octavianus, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. I, Jordanus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna. I, Petrus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata.

Given at Sutri, through the hand of Robert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the Nones of May, in the ninth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1146, in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

## CXI. He commends the writings of Gerhoh, provost of Reichersberg, “against the most pernicious innovations,” and exhorts him to persevere.  
*(1146, May 16.)*

*[PEZ, Treasury of Anecdotes, I, II, 169.]*

[Col. 1139A]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son G., provost of Reichersberg: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have graciously received the writings of your devotion and, by examining them, have plainly recognized the fervour of your religious commitment: “My heart grew warm within me, and in my meditation a fire shall blaze”; your utterance also is exceedingly inflamed. Therefore, since we have learned that you burn with the zeal of charity against the most pernicious innovations and the disturbances [Col. 1139B] arising against the Church of God, we rejoice with paternal affection and commend your devotion in the Lord. But because it is good to begin, though much better to bring matters to completion, we admonish your belovedness in the Lord to persevere steadfastly in your good purpose. For we love your person with paternal charity as a learned and religious man, and we desire, insofar as we can according to God, to honour and support you.

Given at Sutri, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of June.

## CXII. Privilege for the church of Saint Lawrence at Clarholz.  
*(1146, May 23.)*

*[HUGO, Annals of Prémontré, I, 396.]*

[Col. 1139C] EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ERMERPARD, provost of the church of Blessed Lawrence of Clarholz, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

It befits the clemency of apostolic governance to love religious persons and fortify their places with pious protection. For it is recognized as worthy and becoming to honour that we, who have been appointed to govern churches, should both protect them from the wickedness of evil men and sustain them by the patronage of the Apostolic See. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we mercifully assent to your just petitions. We receive under the protection of [Col. 1139D] blessed Peter and ourselves, and strengthen by the privilege of this present writing, the aforesaid church in which you are devoted to divine service. We decree that whatever possessions and goods you now rightfully and canonically possess, or may hereafter acquire, by grant of pontiffs, liberality of kings, bounty of princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through the Lord’s favour, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their own names:

One chapel at Clarholz; two manors; five holdings in the village called Lette; one chapel; three holdings at Mackenberge; two holdings at Gunewich; one holding at Velnceringterpe; three holdings at Rupelo; one holding at Behlen; one holding at Veiiterpe; one holding at [Col. 1140A] Eslere; one holding in the marshy place called Ullenho; twenty-seven portions called Warscharp, with all their appurtenances, woods, meadows, pastures, common pastures, waters and watercourses, fishing rights, mills, roads, trackless places, exits, and entrances. Likewise, twenty-six solidi from a certain tithe, given by the Bishop of Münster; a chapel at Belhem with all its appurtenances; four solidi of tithe at Hultinghausen; a small wood near Hombrinke, held as a fief from Count Egebert, with one holding situated within that same wood. Furthermore, one holding at Behlenholte, two at Clarholz, one at Meicherne, one at Edelinckausen, and one at Molenhem, which you redeemed for sixteen marks of silver from a ministerial named Gyselbert, whose fief they had been; [Col. 1140B] and further, one holding which you bought at Duninghausen.

Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but that all be kept entire for the benefit of those for whose governance and maintenance they were granted, and be of use to them in every way, without prejudice to the authority of the Apostolic See and to the canonical right and reverence due to the diocesan bishop. If any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it and, having been admonished a second or third time, should fail to correct the offence by suitable [Col. 1140C] satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and honour, know himself or herself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed, be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer, and be subject to strict vengeance at the final judgment. But let all who preserve the rights of that place have the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Given at Viterbo, through the hand of Robert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the tenth day before the Kalends of June, in the ninth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1146, in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

## CXIII. He confirms the canonical order established in the church of Saint Wigbert at Quedlinburg by Thomas, cardinal priest and legate of the Apostolic See.  
*(1146, May 24.)* [Col. 1140D]

*[ERATH, Diplomatic Codex of Quedlinburg, 87.]*

## CXIV. To Henry, Bishop of Moravia.—He consoles him amid adversity. He commends Theobald, brother of Duke Wladislaus, absolved from excommunication. He reports that certain priests have been deprived of benefices for performing sacred rites in the territory of the excommunicated Conrad. He permits him to absolve Wladislaus.  
*(1146, May 25.)*

*[THEINER, Critical Investigations, 209.]*

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, Bishop of Moravia: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1141A] We sympathize with paternal affection in the tribulations and distresses which, as we know, you have long suffered at the hands of those unbelievers, although we too, by the Lord’s permission, are afflicted by many tribulations. Yet your discretion does not fail to know that all who wish to live devoutly in Christ Jesus must endure the tribulations of this age. For our Lord Jesus Christ himself was sent by the Father not for the world’s joys but to endure sufferings and even death for us. We must therefore imitate him, our head, since if we suffer persecution for his sake, we shall be blessed, assured of his promise.

Take courage, then, dearest brother in Christ, and act manfully; for our Saviour will not forsake his own even to the end. We are ready to give you help and counsel in all matters in which we can do so according to God. [Col. 1141B] We have received Theobald, brother of our beloved son W., the illustrious Duke of the Bohemians, who attacked your person and those who were with you, together with certain of his companions; and, after receiving from him an oath that he would make satisfaction for so grave an offence according to our command, we caused him to be absolved. After his absolution, we commanded him henceforth neither to seize a cleric or monk nor to give assent to one who does so. Then, having imposed upon him a fitting penance, we sent him back to your discretion, that you might deal mercifully with him according to the devotion and contrition which we recognized in him. We have also admonished and earnestly requested him to show himself so devout and humble toward you [Col. 1141C] that he may deserve pardon from the Lord and from you for so great an offence.

As for Wladislaus, excommunicated for this same offence, since, being detained by a severe illness, he cannot, as we have learned, come into our presence, we entrust him to your discretion and grant you authority to absolve him and impose a fitting penance upon him. Furthermore, following the judgment of blessed Gregory concerning disobedience to the commands of the Apostolic See, we wholly depose from office the three presumptuous priests, namely Bolemilus, Ballus, and Sorith, who, as has been reported to us, presume to celebrate divine offices in the land of Conrad, excommunicated by us and interdicted by our authority from divine offices; and we forbid them ecclesiastical benefice.

Moreover, since we need religious and discreet persons, by apostolic letters we command you to present yourself to us as soon as it is convenient for you; and then we shall take care to answer you more fully concerning the matter which you reported to us through our beloved son D., provost of Prague. [Col. 1141D]

Given at Viterbo, on the eighth day before the Kalends of June.

## CXV. He confirms the rights of the monastery of Varlar concerning the election of a provost and the conferral of advocacy.  
*(1146, May 25.)*

*[HUGO, Annals of Prémontré, II, Preface, p. 652.]*

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ALBERT, provost of the Church of Varlar, and his brethren: greeting, in perpetuity.

[Col. 1142A] Since we desire the rights of all churches to be kept unimpaired. [lacuna] etc. Upon the death of you who are now provost of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be placed there by any crafty device or violence; rather, you may elect a provost without anyone’s opposition, by common counsel or by the sounder part of the council, according to the fear of God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict. Moreover, no one shall presume to seize or usurp the advocacy of your place except one whom the provost and brethren unanimously provide to be elected according to God and the advantage of that place. And since you were first confirmed in the Premonstratensian order according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine, you must obey Prémontré itself, as your mother, in all matters required by the order, [Col. 1142B] and in no way depart from it in the right of filial relationship. Certainly, lest a later age, which God forbid, should devise anything to the contrary, we confirm by apostolic authority, through this page of the present writing, the provisions which we have established. Therefore let all who preserve the rights of that place have the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen, amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Conradus, Bishop of Sabina. I, Octavianus, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. I, Guido, cardinal priest of Saint Chrysogonus.

Given at Viterbo, through the hand of Robert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the eighth day before the Kalends of June, in the ninth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1146, in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius [Col. 1142C] III.

## CXVI. He receives under protection the church of Saints Mary and Blaise at Fridesel and confirms its possessions.  
*(1146, May 25.)*

*Unpublished.—JAFFÉ, Registers of the Roman Pontiffs, p. 623.*

## CXVII. To Villanus, Archbishop of Pisa, he confirms, by renewed liberality, all grants which Innocent II formerly made to Baldwin, in the year 1146, on the Kalends of June, in the eighth indiction. “Given at Viterbo through the hand of Robert, cardinal chancellor of the Holy Roman Church.”  
*(1146, June 1.)*

*[UGHELLI, Sacred Italy, III, 394.]*

## CXVIII. He exhorts Henry of Moravia and Otto of Prague, bishops; Duke Wladislaus; and all clergy and people established throughout Bohemia and Moravia, to restrain clerical incontinence.  
*(1146, June 2.)*

*[THEINER, Critical Investigations, 208.]*

[Col. 1142D]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brethren HENRY, Bishop of Moravia, and OTTO, Bishop of Prague; and to his beloved sons in Christ, Duke WLADISLAUS and all clergy and people established throughout Bohemia and Moravia: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The administration of the Apostolic See, in whose service we are unworthy servants by the Lord’s disposition, makes us debtors to those nearby and those far away alike. Understanding this, our predecessor Pope Innocent, of happy memory, and exercising paternal concern for you, sent our beloved son Guido, cardinal deacon, [Col. 1143A] into those regions. Through him he announced to you and commanded you firmly to observe what he promulgated in the general council concerning the incontinence of clerics and priests and other enormities. Since you, brother bishops, and you, beloved son in Christ W., as we have learned from Guido’s report, stood resolutely by him in these matters, we thank you and commend your devotion in the Lord.

But because virtue consists not merely in beginning but in completing, we ask and exhort your whole community in the Lord, and impose it upon you for the remission of your sins, that you, to whom power has been entrusted by God in that land, shall cause the provisions concerning clerical incontinence and other enormities, issued there by the aforesaid cardinal under the authority of our said predecessor, [Col. 1143B] to be observed with your counsel and assistance. You shall restrain the contemptuous with due correction, according to the discretion granted you by God and the statutes of the holy Fathers. We also give thanks to your belovedness for the fidelity and devotion which you bear toward blessed Peter and ourselves, and for the frequent visitation conveyed to our predecessors and ourselves through our beloved son Daniel, provost of Prague, whom we have recognized as faithful to you and devoted to your honour.

Given at Viterbo, on the fourth day before the Nones of June.

## CXIX. He commends Wladislaus, Duke of the Bohemians, as zealous for ecclesiastical affairs. He adds greetings for his wife Gertrude. He commends Henry, Bishop of Moravia.  
*(1146, June 2.)*

*[THEINER, ibid., 209.]*

[Col. 1143C]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son in Christ W., illustrious Duke of the Bohemians: greeting and apostolic blessing.

If, according to the testimony of Sacred Scripture, one who offers himself as a helper of good works shares in their reward, you deserve a greater merit, since you are not merely a helper but also an agent. Therefore it is pleasing to us that, as we have learned from reports of our venerable brother Henry, Bishop of Moravia, and our beloved sons Guido, cardinal deacon, and Daniel, provost of Prague, you love and honour churches, ecclesiastical persons, and especially religious people; and you strive to advance religion and all else known to pertain to the honour of God in the land entrusted to you by God. You also labour resolutely to root out from not only your own chapel but the entire land those enormities which have prevailed greatly because of sins, especially the incontinence of clerics, which is abominable to God. For since clerics ought to be the temple of God, vessels of the Lord, and sanctuary of the Holy Spirit, it is most unworthy that they should serve beds of lust and indecencies. [Col. 1143D]

We likewise commend your devotion in the Lord because, although that people is corrupted by an ancient custom of excessive drinking and drunkenness, you yourself love the sobriety opposed to that vice and, as a Catholic prince [Col. 1144A] fearing God, oppose these and other enormities with the steadfastness of a manly spirit. Since a crown is promised not merely to one who begins but to one who perseveres, we ask and exhort your nobility in the Lord, and impose it upon you for the remission of sins, that you steadfastly persevere in your good purpose, so that, by God’s provision, you may live happily in the present and receive in the future the fruit of everlasting recompense.

We greet and bless our beloved daughter Gertrude, your duchess and wife, and admonish her in the Lord to persevere, in accordance with her good beginning, in the love of God and affection for religion. Finally, we particularly commend to your and her nobility the aforesaid Bishop of Moravia and D., the provost—prudent and discerning men who sincerely love your persons and your honour. [Col. 1144B] We thank your belovedness for the visitation frequently rendered to our predecessors and ourselves. We truly love your persons in the Lord and desire to honour and heed you in all matters in which we are able according to the Lord.

Given at Viterbo, on the fourth day before the Nones of June.

## CXX. Privilege for the monastery of Stavelot.  
*(1146, June 6.)*

*[MARTÈNE, Amplified Collection, II, 121.]*

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons WIBALD, Abbot of Stavelot, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: [Col. 1144C] in perpetuity.

“It befits the clemency of apostolic governance to love religious persons and fortify their places with pious protection,” etc., as in the privilege of Pope Lucius, dated in 1144. See *Patrologia*, vol. CLXXIX, no. 67.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Conradus, Bishop of Sabina. I, Albericus, Bishop of Ostia. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Chrysogonus. I, Hubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes. I, Hubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul. I, Manfredus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint [Col. 1144D] Sabina. I, Albertus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia. I, Ubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Jordanus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Octavianus, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. I, Gregorius, cardinal deacon of Saint Angelo. [Col. 1145A] I, Petrus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata. I, Cinthius, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus.

Given at Viterbo, through the hand of Robert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the eighth day before the Ides of June, in the ninth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1146, in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

## CXXI. To Henry, Bishop of Moravia, he commands that Duke Wladislaus of Bohemia be admonished to make satisfaction for the damage inflicted upon the Church of Regensburg.  
*(1146, July 2.)*

*[BOCZEK, Moravian Diplomatic Codex, vol. I, p. 250.]*

[Col. 1145B] EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, Bishop of Moravia: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The more fully we trust in your prudence, religious devotion, and integrity, the more confidently we make known to you the things which we love or hate, hoping that you will love with equal affection the things which we love and will likewise hold in hatred, with the zeal of charity, those which we hate. We believe that the devastation and ruin of the Church of Regensburg, committed in tyrannical fashion by Duke Henry, Duke of Bohemia, Frederick the advocate, count palatine, the sons of the prefect, and their other accomplices, have already come to your attention. Therefore our venerable brethren C., Archbishop of Salzburg, and [lacuna], Bishop of Regensburg, [Col. 1145C] having zeal for God and love of justice, pronounced a sentence of excommunication upon the aforesaid incendiaries and evildoers; and we confirm by apostolic authority that sentence, canonically pronounced by those same brethren of ours against their parishioners.

And because we love the Duke of Bohemia with paternal affection for your sake and wish no burden to be inflicted upon him, by apostolic letters we command your brotherhood diligently to meet with him on our and your behalf and strictly admonish him: that he permit all those whom he or his men have carried off into captivity in the atrocity of that crime to depart free; that he make satisfaction for such great acts of sacrilege; and that he desist from disturbing that church.

Given at Viterbo, on the Nones of July.

## CXXII. He receives the Church of the Holy Sepulchre at Jerusalem under protection and confirms its possessions.  
*(1146, July 13.)*

*[Eugène de ROZIÈRE, Cartulary of the Holy Sepulchre, 36.]*

[Col. 1145D]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons PETRUS, prior of the church of the Holy Sepulchre of the Lord, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

If the gentleness and liberality of the Apostolic See ought to provide fitting consolation to all Christians throughout the world, it is especially fitting that it should bestow this upon those who lead the religious life and seem more closely to cleave to almighty God [Col. 1146A]. Since, therefore, you have resolved to live according to the Rule of blessed Augustine, and, worshipping in the place where the Lord’s feet stood, you serve under rule at his glorious Sepulchre and in the places in which that same Redeemer of the world endured death, we judge you worthy of greater goodwill and favor, and we desire to cherish you with paternal affection. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, graciously assenting to your just petitions, and following the example of our predecessors of happy memory, Calixtus, Honorius, and Innocent, Roman pontiffs, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and our own the most holy church of the Lord’s Sepulchre, in which, devoted to divine service, you continually commemorate the Lord’s Passion and the triumph of the most victorious Cross; and we also receive [Col. 1146B] your persons under that protection, and fortify them by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods you now justly and canonically possess, whether by the gift of Duke Godfrey of distinguished memory and of each King Baldwin, and also of Arnulf, patriarch of Jerusalem, and his successors, or whatever you may hereafter acquire, by God’s favor, through grants of pontiffs, the liberality of kings, the benefactions of princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors.

Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names: in the diocese of Bethlehem, the village of Thecue with all its appurtenances, as it was granted to you by Fulk [Col. 1146C], king of Jerusalem of good memory, and confirmed by the text of his charter; the castle of Mahomerie with its church and all its appurtenances; in the diocese of Caesarea in Palestine, the castle of Feniculi with its church and all its dependencies; in the city of Joppa, the church of Saint Peter with all its adjacent lands; in the city of Tyre, the church of Saint Mary of the ancient see with all its appurtenances; the village of Saint Erina in the diocese of Tyre with its appurtenances; the castle of Gith with its appurtenances; in the diocese of Tripoli, the church of the Holy Sepulchre near Mount Peregrinus with all its appurtenances; in the same diocese, the church of the Holy Sepulchre or of George, which is in the hill country, with all its dependencies; likewise the village called [Col. 1146D] Bivora with all its appurtenances, and the exchange-property of Megine; in Apulia, the church of the Holy Sepulchre near Brindisi and the church of Saint Lawrence with all their appurtenances; the church situated outside the castle of Barulum, in honor and under the name of that same Holy Sepulchre, on the southern side near the public roads, with all its dependencies; likewise the church of the Holy Sepulchre outside the walls of the city of Troia, with all its appurtenances; the church of blessed Theodore situated in the suburb of Benevento; in the diocese of Embrun, the church of the Holy Sepulchre of Kahorcas, the church of Saint Peter and Saint Pontius of Sedena, the church of Saint John of Conspinacis, and the church of Saint Peter of Avanzo, with all their appurtenances; [Col. 1147A] in the diocese of Maguelonne, the church of Saint Saviour of Rubo with all its dependencies; in the diocese of Albi, the church of Saint Mary of Sepfacta with all its adjacent lands; the estate called Lugan; the holding called Cantol; the holdings Lubuscketh and Dei; the holding Alaphemaze, with the church of Saint Mary and all its appurtenances; the holding Las Cruces of Saint Amarantus; the holding Castandel; the holding Viarlar; the holding called Villa Godor; the church of Saint Osmerius with all its appurtenances; in the diocese of Saintes, the church of Saint Peter of Mancapzhana with all its appurtenances; in the diocese of Bazas, the church of Saint Osbert with all its dependencies; in the diocese of Barcelona, [Col. 1147B] the church of the Holy Sepulchre of Latablata with all its appurtenances; in the same diocese, at Palma, the church of Saint Peter and the church of Saint John with all their appurtenances; in the diocese of Vic, the church of Saint Mary of Coseoliis with all its dependencies, the church of Saint Mary of Pratis, and the church of Saint Andrew with all their appurtenances; in the diocese of Urgell, half of the castle of Mirabel with its appurtenances; in the diocese of Nájera, the church of Saint Mary of Gronio with all its dependencies, and the hospital of Villa Rubea with all its appurtenances; in the diocese of Burgos, the church of Saint Clement of Covas with all its adjacent lands, and the church of Saint Michael of Quantana with all its [Col. 1147C] appurtenances; in the castle of Sorith, the church of Saint Andrew and the church of Saint Marina with all their adjacent lands; in the village called Clunia, the church of Saint Andrew with all its appurtenances; in the diocese of Palencia, the church of Saint Mary of Pisorga with all its appurtenances, and the church of Saint Alexander of Valtanas with all its dependencies; in the castle of Verde, the church of Saint Michael and the monastery of Saint Romanus with all their appurtenances; in the castle of Corel, the church of Saint Marina and the church of Saint Eugratia with all their appurtenances; in the castle of Portel, the church of Saint Michael of Vega with all its appurtenances; in the city of Palencia, the church of Saint [Col. 1147D] Emilianus of Veruesca with all its appurtenances, the church of Saint Pelagius of Valle de Pero with all its appurtenances, the church of Saint Mary of Sandronas with all its appurtenances, and the church of Saint Mary of Pilelas with all its appurtenances; in the village of Feles, the church of Saint Michael with all its dependencies; in the diocese of Segovia, the church of the Holy Sepulchre at Coca, the church of Saint Saviour, and the church of Saint Mary called Bovada, with all their appurtenances; in the city of Ávila, the church of Saint Mary the New with all its appurtenances; at Arévalo, the church of Saint Peter in the old town with all its appurtenances; in the diocese of Salamanca, the church of Saint Christopher situated outside the city [Col. 1148A] with all its appurtenances; at Medina, the church of Holy Cross with all its dependencies; in the diocese of Zamora, the church of the Holy Sepulchre with all its appurtenances; in the castle called Toro, the church of the Holy Sepulchre with all its appurtenances; in the village of Lali, the church of Saint Eugenia with all its dependencies; in the city of León, the church of the Holy Sepulchre with all its adjacent lands; at Rivo Sicco, the church of Saint Justus of Paralelos with all its appurtenances; at Medina, the church of Saint Peter with all its appurtenances, and the church of Saint Lawrence of Oterolo with all its appurtenances; in the village of Morel, the church of Saint Pelagius with its appurtenances, and the church of Saint Justus of Villa Vela with all its [Col. 1148B] appurtenances; in the same diocese, the village of Golpigar with all its appurtenances, and the village of Versadam with all its adjacent lands; at Masella, the hospital with all its appurtenances, the church of Saint Mary of Nava with its appurtenances, and the church of Saint Peter of the castle of Olfereth with its appurtenances; in the diocese of Astorga, the church of Saint Peter of Cabaneros with all its appurtenances, and the church of Saint Mary of Zothes with all its appurtenances; in the diocese of Santiago, the church of Saint Sebastian of Tavairoas with its hermitage and other appurtenances, the monastery of Saint Mary of Nogaria with all its appurtenances, and the monastery of Saint Saviour of Sobradel with all its appurtenances; in the diocese of Tui, [Col. 1148C] the church of Saint Peter of Nogaria, called Sardonia, with all its appurtenances.

Upon the death of the patriarch of that place, no one shall be set over it through any crafty deception or violence, except one whom the brethren of that place, by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren’s counsel, shall canonically provide to be elected according to the fear of God and the statutes of the holy Fathers.

We therefore decree that absolutely no person may rashly disturb the aforesaid place, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations whatsoever; but that all shall be preserved intact for the benefit in every respect of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right and reverence due to the diocesan bishops.

If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowing this text of our constitution, shall presume rashly to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not amend his offence by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself liable before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, Redeemer; and let him be subject to strict vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of the same place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action [Col. 1149A] and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Chrysogonus, have subscribed. I, Hubaldus, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Praxedes, have subscribed. I, Hubaldus, cardinal-priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Gillibertus, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Mark, have subscribed. [Col. 1149B] I, Guido, cardinal-priest of the title of Saints Lawrence and Damasus, have subscribed. I, Aribertus, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Anastasia, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal-priest of the title of the Shepherd, have subscribed. I, Bernardus, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Clement, have subscribed. I, Jordanus, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Susanna, have subscribed. I, Odo, cardinal-deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal-deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Octavianus, cardinal-deacon of Saint Nicholas [Col. 1149C] in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed. I, Rodulfus, cardinal-deacon of Saint Lucy in Septa Solis, have subscribed. I, Gregorius, cardinal-deacon of Saint Angel, have subscribed. I, Joannes, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary the New, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed. I, Jacinctus, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin, have subscribed. I, Petrus, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed.

Given at Viterbo, through the hand of Robert, cardinal-priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman [Col. 1149D] Church, on the third Ides of July, in the ninth indiction, in the year 1146 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### CXXIII. He commends Bishop Theobald because, on account of property of the canons occupied by citizens, he prohibited the celebration of divine services in his city. He directs him to ensure that a sentence of excommunication, pronounced for the same reason against certain nobles by Guido, cardinal-priest, be observed. (Year 1146, July 19.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, V, 785.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother T., bishop of Verona, greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1150A] You should know that the common sons, the canons of Verona, have informed us that, because of the offences of the citizens of that place, who violently occupy their goods and possessions and hold them contrary to justice, you have prohibited the celebration of divine offices in that city. Since we approve this interdict, canonically imposed by you, we command and direct you by apostolic letters to ensure that it is firmly observed until those same usurpers fully restore to the aforesaid canons everything unjustly taken away, or reach an amicable agreement with them concerning the same complaint. But if any priest of that place should presume to celebrate divine offices contrary to the interdict of that place, restrain him by canonical censure in such a manner that the others may be afraid.

[Col. 1150B] Furthermore, strictly admonish Eleazar and his son Pil.; also Alderic, Redaldus, Conrad, son of Muget, Bachel, Regrigius, Gilbert, and Ulbert, brothers of Alberic the shepherd, who, as the canons’ complaint shows, unjustly hold their goods and revenues, to restore all these things unlawfully withheld and henceforth cease harassing them. If, after your admonition, they prove contemptuous, administer canonical justice upon them. Finally, ensure throughout your diocese [Col. 1150C] that the sentence of excommunication which, by command of G., cardinal-priest and then legate of the Apostolic See, you canonically pronounced against Gir. Grassus and his sons, also against Albert the Deaf and his brother, and certain other usurpers of the property of the Church of Verona, is firmly observed until they make satisfaction; and do not absolve them in any way until you have entirely freed those same canons from their harassment. Likewise, strictly admonish those who recently burned their castle of Pruno and plundered the people of that place, to restore in full everything taken and the damages unjustly inflicted, and to desist altogether from harassing them. But if, within forty days after receiving the present letters, they scorn to do so, pronounce against them a sentence of excommunication and ensure that it is firmly observed throughout your diocese until they make satisfaction.

Given at Viterbo, the fourteenth day before the Kalends of August.

### CXXIV. He commands A[rnold] of Trent, L[othair] of Vicenza, and B[ellinus] of Padua, bishops, to compel certain nobles to restore the property of the canons of Verona which they have occupied. (Year 1146, July 19.)

[UCHELLI, *Italia sacra*, V, 785.]

[Col. 1150D]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brothers A., bishop of Trent, L., bishop of Vicenza, and B., bishop of Padua, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have received a complaint from our sons, the canons of Verona, that Count Od. and his son Pastro, and his relatives, as well as heirs and kinsmen, Hen. of Vico Aedri, and certain other parishioners of yours, violently occupy and unjustly retain the goods and possessions of the Church of Verona. [Col. 1151A] Therefore, because it is our duty to render them due justice, we command and direct your brotherhoods by apostolic letters that, within forty days after receiving these letters, you strictly admonish your aforesaid parishioners to restore in full to them the said goods and possessions unjustly taken away, and henceforth not presume to do anything of the kind against the Church of Verona. If, after your admonition, they prove contemptuous, restrain them by canonical censure.

Given at Viterbo, the fourteenth day before the Kalends of August.

### CXXV. To the canons of Verona he affirms that the castle of Cereta was adjudged to them by Guido, cardinal-priest. (Year 1146, July 19.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, V, 783.]

[Col. 1151B]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GILBERT, archpriest, and the other canons of the Church of Verona, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The authority of our office exhorts us to cherish churches and ecclesiastical persons with paternal affection and, with the Lord’s help, to provide beneficially for their peace and welfare hereafter. Beloved sons in the Lord, willingly assenting to your just petitions, we decree that the determination of the case, canonically made by Guido, cardinal-priest, [Col. 1151C] in the dispute between you and our venerable brother Theobald, your bishop, concerning the castle of Cereta, the village, and the jurisdiction of that place, shall remain valid. By apostolic authority we confirm that castle, together with the said village and jurisdiction, as they were reasonably adjudged to you. If anyone, knowing this text of our confirmation, shall rashly presume to act against it and, having been warned a second or third time, does not amend by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor and incur the indignation of almighty God and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Viterbo, the fourteenth day before the Kalends of August.

### CXXVI. At the request of Bishop Anselm, he confirms the bishopric of Tournai, exempted from the authority of the bishops of Noyon. (Year 1146, July 24.)

[MARLOT, *Metropol. Rem.*, II, 350.]

[Col. 1151D]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother ANSELM, bishop of Tournai, consecrated by our hands, and to his successors canonically appointed, in perpetuity.

It has always been lawful, and always shall be lawful, for the most holy Roman Church, by the heavenly privilege conferred upon it, to unite divided episcopal sees, etc. The Church of Tournai is known from ancient times to have been an episcopal see and to have had its own shepherd. Although the bishop of Noyon held its care and administration for a long time, it is nevertheless not recorded that it was subject or united to the Church of Noyon. [Col. 1152A] In it the multitude of people has grown so greatly that it necessarily ought to have its own bishop, even if it had not possessed one in antiquity; and, because of the distance, these churches cannot be governed by one shepherd without grave peril to souls. Moved by the enactments of the holy canons and by the earnest action of our predecessors of happy memory, Urban, Paschal, and Innocent, who deliberated upon this very matter, we, after taking counsel with our brethren, have, with the Lord’s cooperation, provided you as shepherd for the Church of Tournai; we have consecrated you to the episcopate, as it were by the hands of blessed Peter himself, and, with the Lord’s help, sent you to govern that people. By the text of this present privilege we therefore establish as lawful and perpetual [Col. 1152B] that henceforth the Church of Tournai shall be free from every subjection to the bishop of Noyon and shall always have its own bishop. We also decree that whatever possessions and goods the Church of Tournai now justly and canonically possesses, and which are known to belong to it by right, or whatever it may hereafter acquire, by God’s favor, through the benefactions of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors, and through you for that Church.

We therefore decree that no one may rashly disturb the aforesaid Church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations whatsoever; but that all shall be preserved intact [Col. 1152C] for your benefit and that of Christ’s poor, saving the authority of the Apostolic See. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowing this text of our constitution, shall presume rashly to act against it and, having been warned a second or third time, does not correct his offence by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself liable before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, Redeemer; and let him be subject to strict vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that Church, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here also they may receive the fruit of good action [Col. 1152D] and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have signed. I, Guido, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Chrysogonus, have signed. I, Hubaldus, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Praxedes, have signed. I, Jordanus, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Susanna, have signed.

Given at Viterbo, the ninth day before the Kalends of August, in the ninth indiction, in the year 1146 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### CXXVII. To Raymond, bishop of Périgueux, that by excommunication he compel the clerics of Rochebeaucourt to restore that church to the Cluniacs. (Year 1146, September 9.)

[D. BOUQUET, *Recueil*, XV, 441.]

[Col. 1153A]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother RAYMOND, bishop of Périgueux, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We believe that it has come to your knowledge that we carefully heard the controversy, long disputed between our beloved sons the Cluniac monks and the clerics of Roche-Boviscurtis (La Rochebeaucourt), concerning the church of that place, and discussed it at length with our brethren. [Col. 1153B] Having heard and diligently investigated the arguments of both parties, since from the confession of both parties we learned that the monks had been in possession, we judged that, if the monks proved before our venerable brethren Lambert, bishop of Angoulême, and Gerald, bishop of Limoges, by two or three suitable witnesses that they had been violently expelled from possession of that church, that possession should be restored to them.

But now, as the aforesaid brethren have informed us by their letters, the Cluniac monks completed this proof in their presence in accordance with the tenor of our letters; yet those monks, who, in accordance with our judgment, ought to have obtained [Col. 1153C] restitution of possession from him who is called abbot and from the other clerics then present, were, as they have informed us by letter, repelled with threats and insults and sent back to us with a renewed complaint. Therefore, because we must not fail the justice of the monastery of Cluny and can no longer tolerate the disobedience and contumacy of those clerics, we command and direct you by apostolic letters to restore fully to the Cluniac monks, within thirty days after receiving these letters, that church with its ornaments and all its other appurtenances. If the clerics should presume to oppose this, publicly declare them excommunicated and keep them excommunicated until, in accordance with our command, [Col. 1153D] restitution is completed. Once restitution has been made, if the clerics who had been ordained in that church before the monks’ expulsion wish to litigate concerning ownership, let the case be heard in the presence of the aforesaid bishops, in accordance with the tenor of our other letters, and be concluded by a canonical judgment. But we do not wish any other clerics, who were intruded into that church after the expulsion of the monks, to be admitted at all to an action concerning ownership.

Given at Viterbo, the fifth Ides of September.

### CXXVIII. Bull for the monastery of Gellone. (Year 1146, September 18.)

[Gall. Chr. nov., VI, Instr. 280.]

[Col. 1154A]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son HUGH, abbot of Saint William, and to his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

By the office of the apostolate entrusted to us, we are debtors to those nearby as well as those far away; and although we ought commonly to honor and love all brethren and preserve due justice for the churches entrusted to them, we ought nevertheless to cherish with a more earnest zeal of charity those whom, through God’s [Col. 1154B] grace, we know to be distinguished by a fuller integrity of life and the brightness of religion. For this reason, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Hugh, we graciously assent to your just petitions and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and our own the monastery of Saint William, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by God’s favor, through grants of pontiffs, the liberality of kings, the benefactions of princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names: in the diocese of Lodève, the estate of Saint Genesius of Litenis, and the church of Saint John [Col. 1154C] with its village, fortification, and other appurtenances; the church of Saint Martin with the estate of Castris; the church of Saint Saturninus of Seiraz with its estate; the church of Saint Felix; the church of Saint Martin of Monte Petroso with its chapels, namely Saint Peter of Monte Petroso and Saint Mary of Guarringa. In the diocese of Béziers, the estate of Miliac with the church of Saint William; the church of Saint Paragorius; the church of Saint Genesius of Campaniano; the church of Saint John of the Old Wall, with the chapel of that castle, its tithes, and appurtenances; the church of Saint Vincent of Popiano with its appurtenances. In the diocese of Nîmes, the priory of Saint Peter of Salve with all its churches and appurtenances; [Col. 1154D] the church of Saint Peter of Mayrois with its appurtenances; the church of Saint William of Esperone; the church of Saint Martin of Beers with its appurtenances. In the diocese of Agde, the church of Saint Martin of Caux with its tithes and other appurtenances; the church of Saint Peter of Fontemartis with its appurtenances. In the diocese of Maguelonne, the church of Saint Martin of Lundras, with the chapel of Saint Gerard of the castle of Lundras, together with its tithes and other appurtenances; the church of Saint Michael of Grimiano with its appurtenances. In the diocese of Viviers, the church of Saint Hilary and Saint Martin with its dependencies at Spedonia. In the diocese of Gap, the church of Saint Desiderius of Ortamota; the church of Saint Peter of Ulmobel, with its dependencies united to the nuns’ monastery of Gap. [Col. 1155A] In the diocese of Rodez, the church of Saint Mary of Cornutio with its chapel and other appurtenances; the church of Saint Stephen of Larzac; the church of Saint Eulalia; the church of Saint Mary of Cisterna; the church of Saint Martin of Mauriac; the church of Saint Amantius of Bruxa; the church of Saint Caprasius; and the church of Saints Saturninus and Julian of Creyssel, with all their appurtenances. In the provinces of Spain: in the diocese of León, the village called Vallesalis with all that belongs there to blessed William. In the diocese of Astorga, the church of Saint Vincent with all its appurtenances. In the archdiocese of Braga, the church of Saint Mary of Arriano with all its appurtenances, and all other possessions belonging by right to blessed [Col. 1155B] William in the provinces of Spain.

You shall receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or churches, ordinations of those who are to be promoted to holy orders, blessings of abbots, and all ecclesiastical sacraments from the bishop of Lodève, provided that he is Catholic, is in the favor and communion of the Holy Apostolic See, and is willing to confer these freely and without any improper exaction. Otherwise, you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer, who, supported by our authority, shall grant what is requested. We also grant that burial at that place shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and final wish of those who have resolved to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated, saving the right [Col. 1155C] of the mother church. On the death of you, the present abbot of that place, or of any one of your successors, no one shall be set over it through any crafty deception or violence, except one whom the brethren, by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren’s counsel, shall provide to be elected according to God and the Rule of blessed Benedict. We decree that the sentence which our predecessor Pope Urban of happy memory pronounced between you and the monks of Aniane and confirmed by his writing shall remain valid and inviolable. We add, moreover, that neither the bishop nor any of his officials may burden that monastery. Furthermore, out of reverence for blessed William we prohibit [Col. 1155D] any bishop, cleric, or other person from having authority forcibly to draw back from the route leading to the church of that same Saint William any traveler going or returning, or to disturb him by deceitful contrivances. We also grant that the abbot or monks of that Saint William may freely appeal to the Apostolic See in their grievances, and that, in accordance with the enactment of our predecessors, that monastery shall be free from every condition or secular lordship. Moreover, if the diocesan bishop should wish improperly to burden the churches of Saint Bartholomew and Saint Lawrence, we permit them free recourse to appeal to the Apostolic See. Once an appeal has been lodged, no one may prohibit divine offices in those places.

We therefore decree that absolutely no person may rashly disturb [Col. 1156A] that same place, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, or diminish them, etc.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have signed. I, Guido, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Chrysogonus, have signed. I, Umbaldus, cardinal-priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, have signed. I, Aribertus, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Anastasia, have signed. I, Julius, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Marcellus, have signed. I, Jordanus, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Susanna, have signed. I, Theodewin, bishop of Santa Rufina, have signed. I, Odo, cardinal-deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have signed. I, Octavianus, cardinal-deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have signed. I, Joannes, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary the New, have signed. I, Petrus, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, have signed.

Given at Viterbo through the hand of Baro, subdeacon of the Holy Roman Church, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of October, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1146 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### CXXIX. Privilege for the Church of Saint Zeno at Hall. (Year 1146, September 22.)

[*Monumenta Boica*, III, 534.]

[Col. 1156C]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons HENRY, provost of the Church of Saint Zeno at Hall, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

For since neither can the unity of charity endure without the worship of true religion, nor can service pleasing to God be rendered, it is fitting for apostolic authority to cherish religious persons and, with the Lord’s help, to provide for their peace. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, moved by the prayers of our venerable brother Conrad, Archbishop of Salzburg, we graciously assent to your just petitions; and we take under the protection of Blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid church of St. Zeno, [Col. 1156D] in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. We establish, first of all, that the canonical order according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine shall be inviolably observed there for all time. Moreover, whatever possessions and goods you now justly and canonically possess, whether from the gift of the aforesaid archbishop, founder of your house, or of other faithful people of God, and whatever you may in the future acquire, by the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings, the benefactions of princes, the offerings of the faithful, or by other lawful means, by the Lord’s favor, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors.

Among these, we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names: the estate situated before the [Col. 1157A] gate of that same church, with its appurtenances; and the property called Suante, given by the archbishop himself; whatever right you possess in the tithe of salt boiled from the spring of Halla; from the gift of Ebo, Facco, and Babo, the waters which you possess in that same spring for boiling salt; the property situated in the place called Occhein, with its appurtenances; from the gift of Sigboto, the property called Unchen; from the gift of Henry, son of Etecho, and of his brother, the property called Nuterppoiim, with all its appurtenances.

We decree that, in your churches in which brothers professing the canonical life dwell, no one whatsoever, after making canonical profession in your houses, may leave thence without the permission of the community as a whole; and no one may dare retain one who has left. If, after a second or third admonition, he has scorned to return, the provost of that place may pronounce canonical sentence against him. Moreover, the people of Halla themselves, as has been canonically established by the aforesaid archbishop, shall not be taken away from you by any of his successors, but shall remain under the authority of your provost. Further, we decree that the chapels founded within the boundaries of the parochial church of Halla, as has reasonably been provided by that archbishop himself, shall be subject to the same mother church. In future, however, we forbid new chapels to be built in that parish without the assent of your provost, without prejudice, of course, to the authority of the Apostolic See and of the proper bishop. [Col. 1157C]

We also decree that the burial-place of that house shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who have determined to be buried there, unless they are perhaps excommunicated or under interdict, while preserving the rights of the mother church. Upon the death of yourself, the present provost of that place, or of any one of your successors, no one shall be set over it by any cunning of fraud or by force, except one whom the brothers, by common consent, or the sounder part of the brothers’ counsel, shall provide to be elected in the fear of God and according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid place, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations whatever; but that all things shall be preserved intact [Col. 1157D] for the use and benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right and reverence due to the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowingly disregarding this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after a second or third admonition, unless he correct his offence by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ; and at the last judgment let him be subject to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, [Col. 1158A] so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Given at Viterbo through the hand of Baro, subdeacon of the holy Roman Church, on the tenth day before the Kalends of October, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1146 of the Incarnation of the Lord, and in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### CXXX. Privilege for the Church of St. Donatian at Bruges.  
*(A.D. 1146, October 25.)*

[Miraeus, *Opera diplomatica*, III, 44.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ROGER, provost, and the other brethren of the church of St. Donatian at Bruges, present and future, canonically to be appointed, in perpetuity.

[Col. 1158B] The authority of the Apostolic See entrusted to us exhorts us to extend the aid of protection to places and persons that implore it with due devotion. For, just as no effect ought to be granted to those asking for unjust things, so no petition of those desiring what is lawful ought to be deferred—especially those who, with honorable life and commendable moral conduct, rejoice to serve almighty God. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions and take under the protection of Blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid church of Blessed Donatian at Bruges, in which you are devoted to divine service; and we strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. We establish that whatever possessions and goods [Col. 1158C] that same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may in the future acquire, by the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings, the benefactions of princes, the offerings of the faithful, or by other lawful means, by the Lord’s favor, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors.

Among these, we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names: in the diocese of Tournai, the altars of Dudasela, Utkerca, and Orscamp, with their appurtenances; the altars of St. Michael and of the Holy Cross; Suenkerka, Clemeskerka, Zuevenzela, and Arricta. In the diocese of Thérouanne: Widescat and Kemla, with all tithes and lands belonging to them; Hema with its appurtenances; Dixmutha and Clarck; two parts of the tithe from Formasela and [Col. 1158D] Diesbusc, and from the newly cultivated lands of that same estate. Likewise, the chancellorship of the Count of Flanders, as it was granted to your church in pious devotion by Count Robert and confirmed by his charter, and as the church itself has hitherto held it peacefully.

Upon the death of yourself, the present provost of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be placed over it through any artifice of fraud or by force, except one whom the brothers of that church shall canonically provide to be elected according to the Lord.
