### CLIII. He confirms the possessions and privileges of the monastery of Vivo. (A.D. 1147, January 13.)

[MURATORI, *Antiquitates Italicae*, III, 233.]

[Col. 1185C] **EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons RUSTICUS, prior of Vivo, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.**

A pious request ought to obtain the effect of its will, etc. We strengthen by the page of this present writing the monastery of Vivo, in which you devote yourselves to divine service. We decree that whatever possessions, etc. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following in their proper names: namely, the monastery of Saint Peter in Campo; the monastery of Saint Benedict of Mojano; the monastery of Saint Peter in Arnano, with all its goods and possessions, as these were canonically granted to you by our brother Martin, bishop of Chiusi, for the reform of religious life, [Col. 1185D] and confirmed by his written instrument.

Since monks and religious men ought to live from the alms and beneficence of other faithful persons, we establish by apostolic authority that you are not to be compelled to pay tithes to anyone from the produce which you gather by your own hands and at your own expense. We also enact by a decree to remain in force for ever through God’s grace that you may freely receive for conversion clerics or laymen fleeing from the world, provided that they are bound by no obligation to anyone and that permission has been sought from their bishops; and that you may grant them the habit of monastic profession, without anyone’s opposition or molestation. Thus, freed from the harassment of all men, you may devote yourselves freely and without disturbance to the service of almighty God.

We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may, etc., saving the apostolic authority and the canonical right of the bishop of Chiusi. If anyone, therefore, etc. [Col. 1186A]

### CLIV. Privilege for the monastery of Raitenhaslach. (A.D. 1147, January 28.)

[HUNDIUS, *Metropolis Salisburgensis*, III, 197.]

[Col. 1186C] **EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GERON, abbot, and his brethren of Raitenhaslach, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.**

It is fitting readily to grant assent to religious desires, so that faithful devotion may obtain a swift result. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously grant your just requests and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and our own the aforesaid place in which you are dedicated to divine service. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the monastery justly and canonically possesses at present, or may hereafter acquire, by grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, through God’s favor, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors.

Among these we have thought fit to specify the following in their proper names: the place itself, as it was bestowed upon you in pious devotion by our venerable brother Conrad, archbishop of Salzburg; Windeberge with all its appurtenances; one *mansus* at Tierolfingen, with pastures, cultivated and uncultivated lands, lawfully acquired or to be acquired; in the forest commonly called Ampfnigersfort, the pastures of Portena and the site of Sulingen. In the diocese of Regensburg, the estate in the place called Mosuolgen, as it was reasonably granted to you by the nobleman Wolfher, his wife, and his sons.

Further, no one shall presume to demand tithes from you on the produce of your labor which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or on the sustenance of your animals. [Col. 1187A] We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away or diminish its goods, or burden it with any harassments; but that all things be preserved intact for the use and benefit in every way of those for whose governance and maintenance they have been granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishops.

If any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, after a second or third admonition, unless he makes amendment by fitting satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity perpetrated; let him be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and of the Lord our Redeemer Jesus Christ; and let him be subject to strict vengeance at the final judgment. But upon all who preserve what is just for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

[Col. 1187B] Given at the village of Bovianum [variant: Pronianum], through Guy, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of February [18 January], in the tenth indiction, in the year 1146 of the Incarnation of the Lord, and in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### CLV. Bull for the Camaldolese congregation. (A.D. 1147, February 6.)

[MITTARELLI, *Annales Camaldulenses*, III, 437, from an old manuscript of Saint Michael in the borough of Pisa.]

[Col. 1187C]

**EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons AZO, prior of Camaldoli, and his brethren professing the regular life: in perpetuity.**

It is fitting readily to grant assent to religious desires, so that faithful devotion may obtain a swift result. For no service is ever rendered pleasing to God unless, proceeding from the root of charity, it is preserved in the purity of religion. All lovers of the Christian faith, therefore, ought to love religious life and diligently foster venerable places together with the persons dedicated in them to divine service.

Accordingly, dearest sons in the Lord, granting assent to your just petitions, we receive your place, with all that pertains to it, under the guardianship of blessed Peter and our protection, and strengthen it by the patronage of the Apostolic See. Following in the footsteps of our predecessors of blessed memory, the Roman pontiffs Honorius and Innocent, we decree by the present enactment that the hermitage of Camaldoli shall remain for all future times in the vigor of its condition and religious life, and that the order of monastic observance established throughout your congregation shall not be altered by the insolence of any person or by any superstition.

We further add that, after making monastic profession, no brother of your congregation may leave without permission of the prior and the reasonable consent of the brethren. If he presumes to leave and, after a second or third admonition, scorns to return, we subject him to a sentence of excommunication until he has made fitting satisfaction. We further forbid any of those governed by brethren of your congregation to be prohibited from divine service by any bishop without canonical examination. Moreover, during a general interdict of a city or parish, with the doors closed and diocesan persons not admitted, the monks of your churches shall by no means be forbidden to celebrate divine offices. Whoever, for the service of the servants of God dwelling in the hermitage of Camaldoli, travel to any regions shall not be molested by anyone whatsoever, whether going, returning, or staying. [Col. 1188A]

Moreover, whatever goods or possessions you justly and canonically possess at present, or may hereafter acquire, by grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, through the Lord’s aid, shall remain secure and unimpaired for ever to you and to your successors remaining in the same religious life. Among these we have appended the following, to be noted by their proper names:

In the diocese of Arezzo: the church of Saint Donatus, called Fons Bonus (“Good Spring”), with its hospital and all its goods; in that city, the monastery of Saint Peter Piccolo and the church of Saint Michael; the monastery of Silva Munda; the monastery of Saint Mary at Agnano; the monastery of Saint Peter at Rota; the monastery of Saint Saviour of the Berardingii; the monastery of Saint Quiricus at Rosa; the estate of Lupon with its church; the hermitage of Fleri; the monastery of Saint Virian; the monastery of Saint Bartholomew at Anglari, with the castle and all its appurtenances; the village of Monthione, which you bought from the abbot of Saint Flora, and the church of that village; the village of Modiana, which you bought from Henry the provost and the remaining canons, as is contained in your charters, and the church of that village with its tithe; the tithes of the village of Agna, its church, and the tithe of Largnano.

In the diocese of Fiesole: the monastery of Saint Mary at Poplena.  
In the diocese of Castello: the monastery of Diciano; the monastery of the Holy Sepulchre with the whole borough.  
In the diocese of Florence: the monastery of Saint Peter at Luco; the monastery of Saint Saviour near the city.  
In the diocese of Lucca: the monastery of Saint Peter at Puteoli, with the chapel of the borough of Porcaria and the chapel of the castle; the monastery of Saint Saviour at Cantiniano; the hospital near the borough of Saint Genesius.  
In the diocese of Volterra: the monastery of Saint Justus near the city; the monastery of Saint Peter at Cerreto; the monastery of Saint Mary at Puliciano; the monastery of Saint Peter at Fontiano.  
In the diocese of Pisa: the monastery of Saint Stephen at Cintoria; the monastery of Saint Sabinus at Montione. In the city itself: the monastery of Saint Michael, the monastery of Saint Fridianus, and the monastery of Saint Zeno, saving the right of the Roman Church.  
In the diocese of Chiusi: the monastery of Saint Peter at Vivo on Mount Amiata, [Col. 1189A] as was determined by our predecessor of happy memory, Pope Celestine.  
On the island of Sardinia: the monastery of the Holy Trinity at Saccaria; the church of Saint Eugenia at Samanar; the church of Saint Michael and Saint Lawrence at Vanari; the church of Saint Mary and Saint John at Altasar; the church of Saint Mary at Contra; the church of Saint John and Saint Simon at Salvenaro; the church of Saint Nicholas at Trulla; the church of Saint Peter at Scano; the church of Saint Paul at Controniano; the church of Saint Peter at Heolin.  
In the March of Camerino: the monastery of Saint George; the monastery of Saint Martin at Accole, with the church called Eremita (“the Hermitage”).  
At Galiata: the monastery of Saint Mary on the island; the hermitage of Fajoli.  
In the diocese of Populonia: the church of Saint Paternianus at Ferracciano.  
In the diocese of Faenza: the monastery of Saint Hippolytus near the city.  
In the diocese of Ravenna: the monastery of Saint Apollinaris in Classe.  
In the diocese of Bologna: the monastery of Saint Michael; the monastery of Saint Christina; and, in the city itself, the church of Saint Damian.  
Likewise in the diocese of Arezzo: the church of Saint Sabinus at Clio; the church of Castillione; likewise, the monastery of Morrona. [Col. 1189B]

All these things, together with everything belonging to the said monasteries, we establish and decree by the authority of the Apostolic See to remain for perpetual times as one body under one head—that is, under the prior of the Camaldolese hermitage—and to persevere in the observance of that discipline. Under that prior, I mean, who shall be regularly elected, through the Lord’s aid, by the abbots or priors of the congregation itself and by the hermits. Further, we decree that the congregation itself shall be fostered perpetually under the guardianship of the Apostolic See in such a way that no bishop may excommunicate any of these monasteries or prohibit it from divine offices without the consent of the prior or permission of the Apostolic See. The brethren of the hermitage of Camaldoli, however, may receive the sacraments of consecrations and ordinations from whichever Catholic bishop they choose. [Col. 1189C]

We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid hermitage, take away its possessions or retain them when taken away, diminish them, or burden it with any harassments; but that all things be preserved intact for the use and benefit in every way of those for whose governance and maintenance they have been granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishops. If any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity perpetrated; let him be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and of the Lord our Redeemer Jesus Christ; and let him be subject to strict vengeance at the final judgment.

[Col. 1190A] But upon all who preserve what is just for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

**“Work for me, O Lord, a sign for good.”**

### CLVI. Privilege for the nunnery of Saint Peter at Luco. (A.D. 1147, February 7.)

[MITTARELLI, *Annales Camaldulenses*, III, 440.]

**EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughter in Christ . . . . abbess of the monastery of Saint Peter situated at Luco . . . . . . . .**
Because without the observance of true religion neither the unity of charity can endure [Col. 1190D], nor service pleasing to God be rendered, it is fitting for apostolic authority to cherish religious persons and, with the Lord’s aid, to provide salutarily for their peace. Therefore, beloved daughters in the Lord, we graciously grant your just requests, and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service; and we strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and canonically holds through the offering of Gotidius of blessed memory and the grant of Rodulf, prior of Camaldoli, or may hereafter acquire, by the grant of popes, the bounty of princes, the offerings of the faithful, [Col. 1191A] or other just means, through the Lord’s generosity, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and those who succeed you.

Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names: a share in the town of Luco with its appurtenances; a share in the estate of Larciana with its appurtenances; possessions at Tiliano, Fortunio, and Prata; a share in Cantamerulo; a share in Rivofrigido with its appurtenances; a share in Rivocornoclario with its appurtenances; a share in the estate of Castro, in the estate of Silva, and in the estate of Frena, with their appurtenances; and the church of St Christina near the castle of Seven Fountains, with its appurtenances.

Moreover, no one whatsoever shall presume to exact tithes [Col. 1191B] from you on the produce of the lands which you cultivate at your own expense, or on the sustenance of your animals. We also grant that the burial-place of this house shall be free, so that no one may obstruct the devotion or last wishes of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict, without prejudice to the rights of the mother church. Further, the place itself shall always remain under the lordship and supervision of the prior of Camaldoli; neither a bishop nor the bishop’s officers may excommunicate or interdict the community of this place or its priests, or harass them concerning any other matter, unless he has first approached the prior of Camaldoli in a spirit of charity.

We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the same monastery, take away its possessions [Col. 1191C], retain possessions taken away, or harass it with reckless vexations; rather, all things shall be preserved whole for the benefit in every way of the uses for which they were granted, namely, the governance and support of the women, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop.

If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowing this document of our decree, shall rashly presume to act against it, and, having been warned a second and a third time, does not make amendment by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour; let such a one know that he or she stands guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let such a one be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of the Lord and Redeemer, Jesus Christ; and at the last judgment let such a one be subject to severe vengeance. [Col. 1191D] But upon all who uphold the just rights of this place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Lawrence and Damasus, have subscribed. ### CLVIII. Privilege for the monastery of St Peter at Puteoli, in the diocese of Lucca.

*(A.D. 1147, 11 February.)*

[MITTARELLI, *Annals of Camaldoli*, III, Appendix, p. 435, from the autograph of the canons of Lucca.]

[Col. 1192C]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son ALBERT, of the monastery of St Peter of Puteoli, and to his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, for ever.

It is fitting readily to give assent to religious desires, so that faithful devotion may obtain a swift effect. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Albert, we graciously grant your just requests and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid monastery over which, by God’s appointment, you preside. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the same monastery justly and canonically holds, or may hereafter acquire, by the grant [Col. 1192D] of popes, the bounty of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, God being favourable, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors.

Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: namely, the land which you hold in the parish of St Paul; the land which you hold in the parish of Lunata; the land which you hold in the parish of Brancalo; the land which you hold in the parish of St Januarius; and the land which you hold in the estate of Gragnano. Moreover, no one shall presume to exact tithes from you upon the produce which you rear at your own expense or upon the sustenance of your animals. We also grant that the burial-place of this house shall be free, so that no one may obstruct the devotion and last wishes of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated [Col. 1193A] or under interdict, without prejudice, however, to the rights of the mother Church.

We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain or diminish possessions taken away, or harass it with any vexations; rather, all things shall be preserved whole for the benefit in every way of the uses for which they were granted, namely, the governance and support of those concerned, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop.

If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowing this document of our decree, shall rashly presume to act against it, and, having been warned a second and a third time, does not make amendment by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour; let such a one know that he or she stands [Col. 1193B] guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let such a one be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of the Lord, our Redeemer Jesus Christ; and at the last judgment let such a one be subject to severe vengeance. But upon all who uphold the just rights of this place may there be the peace of the Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

“Make for me, O Lord, a sign for good.”

### CLIX. To Gregory, bishop of Lucca.—That he introduce the canons of St Frigdian into the Church of St Pantaleon.

*(A.D. 1147, 17 February.)*

[BALUZE, *Miscellanies*, Lucca edition, IV, 593.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother G., bishop of Lucca: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The Roman [Col. 1194A] Church looked for the correction of the clerics of the Church of St Pantaleon in the time of our predecessors and in our own time. But, as their sins deserved, their hearts were hardened more violently, and they refused to receive the yoke of the Lord under religious observance. Therefore, desiring to consult their benefit rather than their will, we command you in this present writing, just as we enjoined you orally, to introduce our beloved sons, the canons of St Frigdian, into the aforesaid Church of Blessed Pantaleon, and, with manly firmness and prudence, to ensure that there they may peacefully devote themselves to divine service. But if anyone proves a reckless opponent in this matter and, after being warned three times by your brotherhood, refuses to desist, pronounce upon him a sentence of excommunication.

Given at Pontremoli, on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of March.

### CLX. Privilege for the monastery of St Dionysius at Milan.

*(A.D. 1147, 3 March.)*

[GIULINI, *Memories of Milan*, V, 586.]

[Col. 1194B]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ARIALD, abbot of the monastery of St Dionysius at Milan, and his brethren, professing the regular life, for ever.

It is fitting readily to give assent to religious desires, so that faithful devotion may obtain a swift effect. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Ariald, we graciously grant your just requests and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the monastery of St Dionysius, over which, by God’s appointment, you preside; and we strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. [Col. 1194C] We decree that whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and canonically holds, or may hereafter acquire through the grant of popes, the bounty of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through the Lord’s favour, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors.

Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: the church of St Michael of Pescallo, in which you have authority to establish a monastery, should it be expedient, as our venerable brother Oberto, archbishop of Milan, has granted you by reasonable provision; the whole parish of the suburb of the gate called Porta Nuova, as it was lawfully adjudged to you by the judgment of that archbishop; [Col. 1194D] the church of St Mary in Solario, now called St Fidelis; the church of St Lawrence, next to the house of Tasso, with all their appurtenances; the estate of Meleate, with three chapels—namely, St Bartholomew, St Dionysius, and St Mary of Sabioncello—and two castles, namely those of Melate and Sabioncello; the estate of Lierni, with two chapels, namely those of Blessed Maurice and Blessed Michael; one third of the estate of Talamona with its tithe, and your right in the two chapels situated in that estate, namely those of St Mary and St Martin, with all appurtenances belonging to them; the chapel of St Martin of Gradi with all its possessions; the church of Blessed Michael of Pescallo, [Col. 1195A] with all its appurtenances; the tithe of the lands lying next to the monastery itself and of the lands on either side of the River Seveso, in all the appurtenances of the people dwelling in the gate called Porta Nuova and in Porta Orientale, which are now cultivated or were formerly cultivated, as it was canonically granted and confirmed to you in writing by Eribert, archbishop of Milan; possessions held by you at Sacrate, Sesto called Giovanni, Affori, the bridge of Ourion, Gorgonzola, Aronio, Pescallo, Lomacio, Casalego, Calulate, Romano, Quinto, Surdi, and Casale, at Casinis, and in Valle-Saxia, with all the liberties and customs of the aforesaid possessions, as you have hitherto peacefully held them by royal grant and as they have been confirmed to you by the aforesaid Archbishop Oberto.

Moreover, the four clerics of the same monastery who belong to the order of the Decumani of the Church of Milan shall be appointed and ordained in that church by the abbot in office, for the honour of God; and they shall obey him as their father and lord, as they are known to have done hitherto and as is contained in the writing of the said archbishop. Furthermore, whatever Adalbert, the usurper of that monastery, unlawfully alienated from the same Church of St Dionysius through sales, pledges, grants in fief, investitures, written leases (*libelli*), exchanges, lettings, or any other means, we declare void; and we grant you authority to reclaim it for the Church of Blessed Dionysius, just as this was lawfully adjudged by the sentence of the consuls of Milan and confirmed by Rubald, archbishop of blessed memory. [Col. 1195C] Moreover, no one shall presume to exact tithes from you on newly cleared lands which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or on the sustenance of your animals. We likewise confirm to you the tithes which you canonically possess.

We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain or diminish possessions taken away, or harass it by any vexations; rather, all things shall be preserved unimpaired and whole for the benefit in every way of the uses for which they were granted, namely, the governance and support of those concerned, saving the authority of the Apostolic See [Col. 1195D] and the canonical right of the archbishop of Milan. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowing this document of our decree, shall rashly presume to act against it, and, having been warned a second and a third time, does not correct that presumption by worthy satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour; let such a one know that he or she stands guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let such a one be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of the Lord, our Redeemer Jesus Christ; and at the last judgment let such a one be subject to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of this place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, [Col. 1196A] the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, … Avinus, bishop of St Rufina, have subscribed. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, Ubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Hugh, priest of the title in Lucina, have subscribed. I, John, cardinal deacon of St Mary the New, have subscribed. I, Hyacinth, cardinal deacon of St Mary in Cosmedin, have subscribed.

Given at Vercelli through the hand of Guido, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the fifth day before the Nones of March, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1146 [1147] of the Lord’s Incarnation, [Col. 1196B] in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### CLXI. He confirms the privileges and possessions of the abbey of Saints Solutor, Adventor, and Octavius at Turin.

*(A.D. 1147, 7 March.)*

[*Monumenta of the History of the Fatherland*, Charters, I, 791.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons WILLIAM, abbot of the Turin monastery of the Holy Martyrs Solutor, Adventor, and Octavius, and to his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, for ever.

Whenever that which is known to accord with religion and uprightness [Col. 1196C] is sought from us, it is fitting that we gladly grant it and give suitable support to the desires of petitioners. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously grant your just requests and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid monastery in which you are dedicated to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and canonically holds, or may hereafter acquire through grants of popes, the bounty of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, God being favourable, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names. [Col. 1196D]

Within the city itself: the church of St Paul and the church of St Brictius, with building-sites, houses, vineyards, holdings, and other property possessed within and outside the same city. In the valley of Breduno: the church of St Martinian, once a monastery, with lands, tithes, and the churches of St Mary, St Donatus, and St Julian. In that valley and at Monasteriolo: the church of St Mary, with the whole estate and tithe; the church of St Martin with the whole tithe; the church of St John of Collo, with the whole estate, tithes, and its appurtenances; the church of St Stephen of Cermagna; at Ciriaco, St Lawrence; at Spinariano, the church of St Martin; at Burgaro by the Stura, the church of St Mark; at Settimo, [Col. 1197A] the church of St Peter, and nearby outside the village, the church of St Saviour with all lands and tithes belonging to it.

The estate of Calbica with its churches, half of the whole tithe, and its appurtenances, from the River Nono as far as the middle of the River Po, and the Great Rock below Mairano, and half of the port on that river. At Moncalieri, ten *iugera* of land. At Testona, four holdings and vineyards, and other property which you possess there. At Cargnano, the church of St Martin, 304 *iugera* of land, and other property which you possess there. The estate of Sangano, with its parish church and dependent churches, tithes, fisheries, and villages with their appurtenances. The tithe of Trasma. At Giaveno, the church of St Martin, with lands and other property which you possess there. At Convaciis, the church of St Mary, [Col. 1197B] half of that entire estate, and one third of the tithe. At Onorio, the church of St Mary; at Ripolis, lands, vineyards, and other property which you possess there. The church of St Mary of Strata. At Vinalasco, the church of St Peter with its appurtenances. At Planicia, the church of St Solutor with lands and other property which you possess there; at Castagnole, the church of St Peter with half the tithe. Within the castle, the church of St Mary. At Doaso, the church of St Mary and St Peter, with lands, their appurtenances, and one third of the tithe. At Polengaria, the churches of St Mary and St Desiderius with their appurtenances. At Scalenga, the property which you possess there. At Salciasco, the church of St Mary with holdings and lands. At Bulgari Cornaliso, the church of St Mark with tithes and its appurtenances. [Col. 1197C] At Tegerone, the churches of St Peter, St John, and St Mary, with lands, tithes, and their appurtenances. At Stadegarda, the churches of St Saviour and St Mary, with the tithes of that valley. In Monferrato, the church of Saints Victor and Corona, of St Thomas, and the church of St Eusebius. At Baldesedo, the church of St Julian with its appurtenances. At Montecuco, at the place called “At the Saints,” a church with its appurtenances, and nearby the church of St George; at Montefia, the church of St Marcian with its appurtenances. At Piacenza, the monastery of St Alexander with all its appurtenances within that bishopric. At Gavellana, the church of St Leonard with its appurtenances. In Provence, [Col. 1197D] at the place called Reilana, the church of St Michael with its appurtenances near the city, and the church of St Pancras with its appurtenances.

Moreover, no one whatsoever shall presume to exact tithes from you on the produce which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or on the sustenance of your animals.

On the death of you, the present abbot of this place, or of any one of your successors, no one shall be placed over it by any stratagem of deception or by force, except the person whom the brethren, by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren, [Col. 1198A] shall provide to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict. We also decree that the burial-place of this house shall be entirely free, so that no one may obstruct the last wishes and devotion of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated, without prejudice, however, to the rights of the mother Church.

If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowing this document of our decree, shall rashly presume to act against it, and, having been warned a second and a third time, does not make amendment by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour; let such a one know that he or she stands guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let such a one be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of the Lord, our Redeemer [Col. 1198B] Jesus Christ; and at the last judgment let such a one be subject to severe vengeance. But upon all who uphold the just rights of this place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia. I, John, cardinal deacon of St Mary the New. I, Hulbaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul. I, Hyacinth, cardinal deacon of St Mary in Cosmedin. I, Hugh, priest of the title in Lucina. [Col. 1198C] I, Jordan, cardinal priest of the Church of St Susanna.

Given at Susa through the hand of Guido, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the seventh day before the Nones of March, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1146 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

[Note: [Col. 1197D] The year 1146 corresponds neither with indiction X nor with the third year of Eugenius’s pontificate, for on 10 March of that year Eugenius consecrated Anselm bishop of Tournai at Rome [Col. 1198D]; but the date is reckoned from the Incarnation and corresponds to the year 1147 of our era, and thus all the dates agree.]

### CLXII. Privilege for the monastery of Bonneval, of the Cistercian Order.

*(A.D. 1147, 26 March.)*

[MANRIQUE, *Cistercian Annals*, II, 82.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GOZEVIN, abbot of Bonneval, and his brethren, [Col. 1198D] present and future, professing the regular life, for ever.

It is fitting that we willingly grant the desire known to pertain to the religious purpose and the salvation of souls, and give suitable support to the desires of petitioners. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously grant your just requests and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid place in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may hereafter acquire through grants of popes, the bounty of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or also other just means, God being favourable, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. [Col. 1199A] Moreover, no one whatsoever shall presume to exact tithes from you on the produce which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or on the sustenance of your animals.

We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb that place, take away, retain, or diminish your goods or possessions, invade or violate your barns or storehouses, or harass you with any molestations. Rather, all things shall be preserved whole for the benefit in every way of the uses for which they were granted, namely, the governance and [Col. 1199B] support of those concerned, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical reverence due to the diocesan bishop.

If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowing this document of our decree, shall rashly presume to act against it, and, having been warned a second and a third time, does not make amendment by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour; let such a one know that he or she stands guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let such a one be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of the Lord, our Redeemer Jesus Christ; and at the last judgment let such a one be subject to severe vengeance. But upon all who uphold the just rights of this place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action [Col. 1199C] and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, John, cardinal deacon of St Mary the New. I, Humbaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia. I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum. I, Hyacinth, cardinal deacon of St Mary in Cosmedin. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Lawrence and Damasus.

Given at Cluny through the hand of Guido, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, [Col. 1199D] on the seventh day before the Kalends of April, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1147 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### CLXIII. Privilege for the nunnery of Tart.

*(A.D. 1147, 3 April.)*

[PLANCHER, *History of Burgundy*, I, preliminary matter, p. 47.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ, ELIZABETH, abbess of Tart, and her sisters, present and future, professing the regular life, for ever.

It is fitting that we willingly grant the desire known to pertain to the religious purpose and the salvation [Col. 1200A] of souls, and give suitable support to the desires of petitioners. Therefore, beloved daughters in Christ, we graciously grant your just requests and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid place in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the same place now justly and canonically holds, or may hereafter acquire through grants of popes, the bounty of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, God being favourable, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors.

Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: the place [Col. 1200B] of Tart itself; the place called Marmot with its appurtenances; and full rights of use in all the woodland of Villers; the grange of Lamblento with its appurtenances, which Humbert of Bissey, together with Peter the Elder and his heirs, freely gave you, with the assent of Hugh of Beaumont, from whose holding it was, and full rights of use in all the woodland of Villers; the grange of Haute-Silve with its appurtenances and full rights of use in fields, woods, and pastures; and the tithes which its possessors relinquished before the dedication of the church of that grange, in the presence of the lord bishop of Chalon. Moreover, no one shall presume to exact tithes from you on the produce which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or on the sustenance of your animals.

[Col. 1200C] We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid place, take away its possessions, retain possessions taken away, or harass it with any vexations; rather, all things shall be kept whole, for the benefit in every way of your uses, saving the canonical reverence due to the Apostolic See and the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowing this document of our decree, shall rashly presume to act against it, and, having been warned a second and a third time, does not make amendment by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour; let such a one know that he or she stands guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let such a one be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of the Lord, our Redeemer Jesus [Col. 1200D] Christ; and at the last judgment let such a one be subject to severe vengeance. But upon all who uphold the just rights of this place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given at Maisnil-Lambert, through the hand of Guido, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the third day before the Nones of April, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1147 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### CLXIV. To the archbishops of Lyons and Besançon, etc.—He confirms the constitution of Pope Calixtus II concerning the peace and security of the territory of Trinorc, within fixed boundaries marked by crosses.

*(A.D. 1147, 4 April.)*

[D. BOUQUET, *Collection*, XV, 443.]

[Col. 1201A]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brethren the archbishops of Lyons [AMEDEUS] and Besançon [HUMBERTO], and the bishops of Mâcon [PONTIUS] and Chalon [GUALTER]: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Our predecessor, Pope Calixtus of happy memory, as we have learned from his letter—see Calixtus’s letter in *Patrologia*, vol. CLXIII, no. 7—came to Trinorc; and, wishing in fulfilment of his office to provide for the peace and security of that place, [Col. 1201B] he ordered boundaries to be set up all around. Within these boundaries, marked by crosses in accordance with the custom of the land, he entirely prohibited seizures, plundering, assaults, or anything of that sort. Following in his footsteps, we confirm by the authority of the Apostolic See what he established in this matter and command its observance. Therefore, if anyone with bold rashness presumes to oppose his constitution and our confirmation, that person shall be suspended from divine offices until satisfaction has been made. Whoever proves an observer of it, however, shall receive the blessing and grace of almighty God and His apostles.

Given at Maisnil-Lambert, on the second day before the Nones of April.

### CLXV. Privilege for the Church of St Pancras at Ranshofen.

*(A.D. 1147, 10 April.)*

[HUND, *Metropolis of Salzburg*, III, 208.]

[Col. 1201C]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons MANEGOLD, provost of the Ranshofen Church of Blessed Pancras the Martyr, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, for ever.

By the care of the universal Church entrusted to us by God, the provider of all good things, we are bound to love religious persons and to strive by every means to promote the religious life pleasing to God. For no service is ever rendered acceptable to God unless, proceeding from the root of charity, it is preserved in the purity of religion. Therefore, beloved sons in [Col. 1201D] the Lord, moved by the prayers of Henry, illustrious duke of the Bavarians, we graciously assent to your just petitions; and we receive under the guardianship and protection of blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, and strengthen by the privilege of the apostolic see, the aforesaid church of blessed Pancras the martyr, in which you devote yourselves to the divine office. First, indeed, we decree that the canonical order known to have been established in that place according to the Rule of blessed Augustine shall be preserved there inviolate for all time.

Moreover, whatever possessions or goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, God being favourable, by grant of pontiffs, gift of kings or princes, offering of the faithful, [Col. 1202A] or other lawful means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: namely, the church of St Michael, with its tithe and parochial right; the chapels of Neu-Kirchen, Hantenberge, and Geroltesperge, with their appurtenances. Certainly, no one whatsoever shall presume to exact tithes from you on the produce of lands which you cultivate with your own hands or at [Col. 1202A] your own expense, or on the sustenance of your animals.

You shall receive ecclesiastical sacraments from the diocesan bishop, provided that he is Catholic, enjoys the favour and communion of the apostolic see, and is willing to administer them to you freely and without any improper exaction. Otherwise, you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer; supported, indeed, by [Col. 1202B] our authority, he shall grant what is requested. When you, the present provost of this place, die or are transferred to the government of another church, or when any one of your successors dies, no one shall be set over the place through any crafty deceit or violence, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of their counsel, shall provide to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Augustine.

Furthermore, since your house has been established on the understanding that the advocate of the goods of the aforesaid duke in those parts shall also be advocate of this place, we prohibit both him and any of his subordinate officers from harassing the place itself with unjust burdens. If he does so and, having been admonished a second and third time, does not make amends, then, by the counsel and aid of the duke himself, that advocacy shall be [Col. 1202C] taken from the unfit holder, and another suitable person substituted in his place. We also grant that the burial-place of the said house shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who have decided to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict, the right of the mother church being preserved.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or oppress it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole, to serve in every way the use and benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the apostolic see and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly attempts rashly to act against [Col. 1202D] this page of our constitution, and, after a second or third admonition, does not make suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let him be subject to strict vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve what is right for this place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good works and find with the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Given at Troyes through the hand of Guy, deacon-cardinal and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the fourth day before the Ides of April, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1147 of the Lord’s Incarnation [Col. 1203A], in the third year of the pontificate of Pope Eugenius III.

## CLXVI. He exhorts the peoples to a holy expedition against the Slavs in Pomerania. He also writes to the king of Spain to prepare war against the Saracens of Iberia.

*(A.D. 1147, 11 April.)*

[BOCZEK, *Codex diplomaticus Moraviae*, I, 244.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to all the faithful of God: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We believe that it has come about by the ordering of divine counsel that so great a multitude of the faithful from different parts of the world is arming itself for the defeat of the unbelievers, and that almost the whole land of Christians is being exhorted to so praiseworthy a [Col. 1203B] work. For among the other princes and powerful men, the kings themselves, who rule over other nations, having taken up the sign of the life-giving cross, are preparing for the liberation of the Eastern Church; and, with God’s aid, they intend mightily to overcome the enemies of Christ’s cross, who, as our sins deserved, have cruelly slaughtered our brethren at Edessa and in many other places in those regions.

The king of Spain also is powerfully arming himself against the Saracens of those regions, over whom he has already, by God’s grace, often triumphed. Certain of you likewise, desiring to become participants in so holy a labour and reward, intend, with the Lord’s help, to go against the Slavs and other pagans dwelling toward the North and to subject them to the Christian religion. Considering their [Col. 1203C] devotion, we grant, by the authority bestowed upon us by Almighty God and blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, to all who have not taken the same cross for Jerusalem but have resolved to go against the Slavs and remain in that expedition, as decreed, out of devotion, that remission of sins which our predecessor Pope Urban of happy memory established for those setting out for Jerusalem. By the same authority, under pain of excommunication, we prohibit anyone from accepting money or any other ransom from those pagans whom he is able to subject to the Christian faith, so as to permit them to remain in their unbelief.

Moreover, because we recognize that it is expedient for there to be among you some religious, prudent, learned person who may provide for your peace and [Col. 1203D] tranquillity, preserve unity among you, and remind you to advance the Christian religion, we have appointed for this purpose our venerable brother A[nselm], bishop of Havelberg, a religious, prudent, and learned man, and have imposed this charge upon him. Therefore, by these apostolic letters we command and direct you to love and honour him for reverence of blessed Peter, of ourselves, and for the salvation of you all; and humbly to obey his salutary counsels, admonitions, and commands, so that God may thereby be honoured and concord and brotherly love, with the Lord as author and through his own diligent cooperation, may be preserved among you.

We further decree that those who [Col. 1204A] take the cross for so holy an expedition, and their goods, shall remain under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves.

Given in the territory of T[royes], on the third day before the Ides of April, in the second year of our pontificate.

## CLXVII. Privilege for the monastery of Foigny.

*(A.D. 1147, 15 April.)*

[*History of the Monastery of Foigny, of the Cistercian Order*, by the work and study of John de LANCY, prior of the same monastery; Bonne-Fontaine, 1670, quarto, p. 24.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to GOSWIN, abbot of Foigny, and to his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

It is fitting readily to grant [Col. 1204B] assent to religious desires, so that faithful devotion may obtain a swift result. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid place, in which you are dedicated to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions or goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may hereafter acquire, God being favourable, by grant of pontiffs, gift of kings or princes, offering of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors.

Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: the place itself of Foigny; that part of the wood of Étréaupont, according to the defined boundaries, [Col. 1204C] which you peaceably possess by right of ownership, while in the remaining part you have only a right of use; the tithes of the land of Étréaupont; the place called Aubenton, with all things pertaining to it; half of the land called Flignies; the land called Landouzy, with the great tithe and all things belonging to it, except the inhabitants; the estate called Vilers and the second called Watigny; likewise the third called Agnis; the land of Foucouzy and the fourth part of Tibiis; the territory of Vilercelli, with its tithe and certain other adjoining lands; the place called Evezcania; pastures throughout all the land of Robert of Montaigu; the estate called Arcuzot; and the vineyards of Culpetra. Certainly, no one shall presume to exact tithes from you on the produce of lands which you cultivate with your own hands or at [Col. 1204D] your own expense, or on the sustenance of your animals.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the place itself, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole, to serve in every way the use and benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the apostolic see and the canonical reverence due to the diocesan bishops. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly attempts rashly to act against this page of our constitution, and, after a second or third admonition, does not make suitable [Col. 1205A] satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ; and let him be subject to strict vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve what is right for this place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good works and find with the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Guy, priest-cardinal of the title of St Chrysogonus. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia. I, Ismarus, bishop of Tusculum. I, Hyacinth, deacon-cardinal of St Mary in [Col. 1205B] Cosmedin [lacuna], etc.

Given in the territory of Meaux through the hand of Hugh, priest-cardinal, acting in place of Lord Guy, deacon-cardinal and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of May, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1147 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the third year of the pontificate of Pope Eugenius III.

## CLXVIII. He commands G[regory], bishop of Lucca, to install the brethren of St Frigdianus in possession of the church of St Pantaleon within twenty days.

*(A.D. 1147, 24 April.)*

[BALUZE, *Miscellanies*, ed. Lucca, IV, 593.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother G., bishop of Lucca: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1205C] We believe that you remember how we enjoined upon you orally, and afterwards ordered by letter, that you should introduce the religious brethren of St Frigdianus into the church of St Pantaleon and provide for their peace and tranquillity. We are therefore greatly astonished that, as the result shows, you have not yet carried our command in this matter into effect. Accordingly, by these repeated letters we command and direct you that, all excuse set aside, within twenty days after receiving this present writing you shall introduce those brethren into that church and so provide for their peace and tranquillity that they may serve the Lord there in quiet and remain free from the disturbance of wicked persons. If anyone [Col. 1205D] attempts to hinder you or them in this matter, then, if he is a cleric, suspend him from ecclesiastical office and benefice; if a layman, exclude him from entry into churches.

Given at Paris, on the eighth day before the Kalends of May.

## CLXIX. At the request of Henry, bishop of Toul, he forbids the reimposition of “the custom of the Frostrarii, commonly called the *Probatio*, within the ban of Wischeri or Tracoldis-villa,” relinquished by Hugh, count of Vaudémont, and the building by the duke of Lorraine of a castle “within four leagues near the church of Toul.”

*(A.D. 1147, 28 April.)*

[D. CALMET, *History of Lorraine*, II, Documents, p. 324.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable [Col. 1206A] brother HENRY, bishop, and to the beloved sons, the canons of the Church of Toul: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is our duty to labour for the condition of churches and, with the Lord’s help, beneficially to provide for their peace and welfare. The nobleman Hugh, count of Vaudémont, intending out of devotion to set out for Jerusalem, as we have learned from his writing, relinquished, abjured, and surrendered, for the salvation of his soul, together with his wife and sons, that custom of the *Frostrarii*, commonly called the *Probatio*, which he had hitherto unjustly held within the ban of Wischerc or Tracoldis-villa, and also the commendations of the inhabitants of both bans, all occasion being removed. He acknowledged this act in the presence of our venerable brother A., archbishop of Trier; [Col. 1206B] he freed those same villages from every wrongful custom about which you had complained; and strengthened the same freedom by the protection of his written instrument.

Therefore, desiring to provide henceforth for your peace, we confirm that same freedom by this present document; and, lest anyone should presume thereafter to violate it or to trouble the Church of Toul in this matter, we prohibit it by apostolic authority. If anyone presumes to attempt it, let him be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, and let both he and his land be placed under interdict as regards the divine offices. We command the same to be done if the duke of Lorraine, or any of his heirs, presumes to build a castle or [Col. 1206C] any fortification within four leagues near the church of Toul, since this has generally been forbidden by kings, and we confirm the prohibition by apostolic promulgation.

Given at Paris, on the fourth day before the Kalends of May.

## CLXX. Privilege for the monastery of St Mary of Thélu.

*(A.D. 1147, 28 April.)*

[HUGO, *Premonstratensian Annals*, II, 583.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons WALFRID, abbot of the church of Thélu, and his brethren, present and future, professing the canonical and regular life, in perpetuity.

A desire shown to concern the purpose of religion and the salvation of souls ought, with God as author [Col. 1206D], to be fulfilled without delay. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the church of Blessed Mary of Thélu, in which you are dedicated to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. First, indeed, we decree that the canonical order according to the Rule of blessed Augustine and the institution of the Premonstratensian brethren shall be observed in your church inviolate for all future time.

Whatever possessions or goods the aforesaid church now justly and canonically possesses, as they have been confirmed by our beloved son Bartholomew, bishop of Laon, or may hereafter acquire, God being favourable, by grant of pontiffs, [Col. 1207A] gift of kings or princes, offering of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: namely, the place itself of Thélu, and the entire tithe of that territory with its due liberty [lacuna]. We decree, moreover, that the canonical order according to the Rule of blessed Augustine and the institutions of the Premonstratensian brethren shall be observed there inviolate for all time. No brother, after making profession in that place, may leave that cloister without the permission of the abbot and the whole community; and no one shall dare retain a departing brother without a common letter of authorization.

[Col. 1207B] We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may lawfully rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or oppress it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole, to serve in every way the use and benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the apostolic see and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly attempts rashly to act against this page of our constitution, and, after a second or third admonition, does not make suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood [Col. 1207C] of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ; and let him be subject to strict vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve what is right for this place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good works and find with the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given at Paris through the hand of Hugh, priest-cardinal, acting in place of Lord Guy, deacon-cardinal and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the fourth day before the Kalends of May, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1147 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the third year of the pontificate of Pope Eugenius III.

## CLXXI. Privilege for the monastery of Ferrières.

*(A.D. 1147, 28 April.)*

[MABILLON, *Benedictine Annals*, VI, 708.]

[Col. 1207D]

EUGENIUS [lacuna] to the beloved son JOHN, abbot of the monastery of Ferrières, and to his successors professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

A desire shown to concern the purpose of religion and the salvation of souls ought, with God as author, to be fulfilled without delay. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot John, we graciously assent to your just petitions and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves and our successors the aforesaid monastery over which, with God as author, you are known worthily to preside; and we strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. [Col. 1208A] We decree that whatever possessions, estates, or goods that monastery now canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, God being favourable, by grant of pontiffs, gift of kings or princes, offering of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors in the same monastery. Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names:

the church of St Eligius, situated opposite the aforesaid monastery; the church of St Andrew of Château-Landon, with its benefices and appurtenances; the church of St Peter of Arreville; the church of St John of Prodais-Fontaine; the church of St Germanus of Nergiat; the church of St Victurius of Fontanet; the church of the Holy Saviour of Cella; the church of St [Col. 1208B] Martin of Courtemand; the church of Holy Cross of Longiaca; the church of St Dionysius of Mulment; the church of St Lupus of Branslis; the church of Parchis; the church of Vallibus; the church of Polliniac; the church of St Genulfus of Brusciac; the juniorate of the church of Bugliniac; the church of Mundreville; and the church of Bursiac.

In the parochial churches which you hold and from which you receive benefices, you shall elect priests and present them to the diocesan bishop. If they are suitable, the bishop shall entrust the care of souls to them, so that they may render account to the bishop for the care of the people, while rendering to you due subjection in temporal matters belonging to your monastery. We also decree that the burial-place of this house and that of St Andrew of Château-Landon [Col. 1208C] shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and pious will of those who desire to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict.

We also prohibit any bishop from performing ordinations in the same monastery or, unless invited by the abbot of that house, from celebrating public Masses. Moreover, we prohibit anyone from presuming to establish a church or cemetery on the property of that same house, except with the assent and will of the abbot and chapter. When you, the present abbot of this place, die, or when any of your successors dies, no one shall be set over it through any crafty deceit or violence, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren’s counsel, shall provide to be elected according to God and the Rule of blessed [Col. 1208D] Benedict. The person elected may receive blessing from whatever bishop he chooses and may enjoy all else according to the privileges of our predecessors.

Finally, if it happens that an abbot is accused of any crime, the judgment of a single bishop shall not determine the sentence; rather, the censure of a provincial council shall be awaited, or, should he prefer to appeal, the matter shall be referred to the hearing of the Roman pontiff. We further decree that neither the aforesaid church nor the church of Blessed Mary within your fortification nor the church of Blessed Andrew of Château-Landon shall cease from the divine offices because of a general interdict of the province. Instead, with doors open and excommunicated and interdicted persons excluded, you may lawfully celebrate the divine offices aloud [Col. 1209A]. Moreover, we confirm to you all churches which belong by right, firm possession, and fee to the church of Ferrières. We decree, however, that no person, etc.

Given at Paris through the hand of Hugh, priest-cardinal, acting in place of Lord Guy, deacon-cardinal and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the fourth day before the Kalends of May, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1147 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the fourth year of the pontificate.

## CLXXII. Privilege for the monastery of Grimbergen.

*(A.D. 1147, 1 May.)*

[HUGO, *Premonstratensian Annals*, I, Preface, 510.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved [Col. 1209B] sons HUMBERTO, abbot of Grimbergen, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

It is fitting readily to grant assent to religious desires, so that faithful devotion may obtain a swift result. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your petitions, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid place, in which you are dedicated to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions or goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may hereafter acquire, God being favourable, by grant of pontiffs, gift of kings or princes, offering of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your [Col. 1209C] successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names:

[Col. 1209C] namely, the altar of Wamblini with its dependencies, Berchem, Radelgem, and Ramesdunk; the altar of Strumbeca. Walter, called the Great, gave fifteen holdings (*mansi*) to the church of Grimbergen. His son Gerard gave one. Alveric and his son Reimer gave two and the court of Everchen. The venerable widow Adeloïa conveyed to the aforesaid church the allod at Kerberghe with its tithe, four solidi at Vicele, the land called Bochult, and half a mill at Grimbergen. Walter Berthold, with his heirs Gerard and Walter of Eme, gave land at Steilo and fishing rights. Volfundis gave the aforesaid church a portion of the land of [Col. 1209D] Botolengem, and one holding at Amelrengem to the church of Strumbeca. Lambert of Ossele, a free man, devoutly offered himself, his allod, and his dependants. Osto of Leuve and his coheirs gave the eighth part which they possessed at Macha. Hugh and Adanghem gave the ninth part of their tithe at Herne. Walter of Galmarden offered two holdings at Old Aingem to the church of Commerata; William and his brothers, together with their sister Bescela, gave one holding at Adelegem. Berta and her son Hilis gave their land at Berthem and a part of a mill. Gozoin, a nobleman of Veljeka, gave this church half a holding at Beiengem. Duke Godfrey the Younger freely granted two and a half holdings at Osselle with woodland; and his father offered to the aforesaid church [Col. 1210A] the site of a mill on the Strumbecca. Certainly, no one shall presume to exact tithes from you on the produce of lands which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or on the sustenance of your animals.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid place, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole, to serve in every way the use and benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the apostolic see and the canonical reverence due to the diocesan bishops. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly attempts rashly to act against [Col. 1210B] this page of our constitution, and, after a second or third admonition, does not make suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ; and let him be subject to strict vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve what is right for this place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good works and find with the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Given at Paris, on the seventh day before the Nones of May, in the year 1147 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the third year of our pontificate.

## CLXXIII. Privilege for the church of St Martin of Laon, of the Premonstratensian Order.

*(A.D. 1147, 6 May.)*

[LEPAIGE, *Premonstratensian Library*, 452.]

[Col. 1210C]

EUGENIUS, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons, the abbot and canons of the church of Blessed Martin situated in the suburb of Laon, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

Whenever something is requested from us which is known to accord with religion and uprightness, it is fitting that we grant it willingly and afford suitable assistance to the desires of petitioners. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions; following the example of our predecessors [Col. 1210D], Innocent and Lucius of happy memory, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid church in which you are dedicated to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions or goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, God being favourable, by grant of pontiffs, gift of kings or princes, offering of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors.

Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: namely, the allods of Diona, Coverchis, and Boelio; the mills of Fossa; the mill of Barrels; the allods of Taran, Planeto, Magniviler, Remicurte, and Floricurte; the mill of Maheriis with a part of the territory of that village; the mill of [Col. 1211A] Rouza with the fishery and adjoining meadow; the mill of Mount St Germanus; the mill called Cheternes; the lands which you have at Gisenicurte, with half the tithe; the mill of Alneto and Forkes; the land of Wahesual with its tithe; the land of Chalamonte; the vineyards on Mount Hunoldus; the vineyards which you have at Mailli; the tithe of Martiniac with its appurtenances; the entire territory of Salmoncei with woods, meadows, jurisdiction, and district, as granted to you by our venerable brother Stephen, bishop of Metz; the lands which you possess at Rokignicurte, Pierres, Pomereto, and Morolzis, with a mill; two portions of the tithe of Cilis, together with the tithe of cultivated lands; the lands of Avains with their tithe; the cultivated land of Monstrata; the lands which [Col. 1211B] you have at Verciniac, Burcis, and Makigni, with mill, oven, and meadows; the allod of Vorgia; two portions of the tithe of Mount Cavillus; the mill of Alneto; two portions of the tithe of Camulgia; the mill of Auvil; a part of the tithe of Pesullo, and the lands you have there and at Anthies; the mills of Anisi, Clari, Comportet, Destoueles, and Folia; the mill called Bekerellum; the mill of Chivi, as lawfully confirmed to you by our venerable brother Bartholomew, bishop of Laon; and the vineyards which you possess on Mount Laon, at Tirimac, Vorgia, Jovia, Brueria, Lirivallis, Mount Cavillus, Orgivallis, Camulgia, Capriniac, Mount Antelli, Trubercourt, Cryptae, Mons, and Fisains.

[Col. 1211C] Certainly, no one whatsoever shall exact tithes from you on the produce of lands which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or on the sustenance of your animals. In order that the integrity of the order may be observed inviolate both among your prelates and your subjects, we decree that, should any abbot belonging to your church depart from the order and custom of the monastery of St Martin of Laon, the abbot of that monastery shall admonish him regarding his correction a second and third time. If he proves incorrigible, the diocesan bishop, in the presence and on the testimony of the abbot of St Martin and two abbots of the same order, shall without any delay depose the transgressor against his order. The bishop shall return the deposed abbot to the church of Blessed Martin and immediately [Col. 1211D] appoint another suitable man by canonical election of the brethren.

We also grant that the burial-place of the same house shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who have decided to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict, without prejudice to the right of the parish churches.

Therefore no person may lawfully rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with presumptuous vexations; but all things shall be preserved whole, to serve in every way the use and benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the apostolic see and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular [Col. 1212A] person knowingly attempts rashly to act against this page of our constitution, and, after a second or third admonition, does not make suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let him be subject to strict vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve what is right for this place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good works and find with the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Given at Paris through the hand of Hugh, priest-cardinal, acting in place of Lord Guy, deacon-cardinal and chancellor of the holy [Col. 1212B] Roman Church, on the day before the Nones of May, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1147 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the third year of the pontificate of Pope Eugenius III.

## CLXXIV. He upholds for Adalbero, archbishop of Trier, the monastery of St Maximin and approves the agreement concluded between him and Henry, count of Namur, in the presence of Conrad, king of the Romans, through the work of Bernard, abbot of Clairvaux.

*(A.D. 1147, 7 May.)*

[HONTHEIM, *History of Trier*, I, 556.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother ADALBERO, archbishop of Trier, and to his successors to be canonically appointed, in perpetuity.

[Col. 1212C] Although, by the office of apostleship imposed upon us by God, we are indebted to all the children of Holy Church, we nevertheless wish to love and cherish with the closer arms of charity those fathers of ours—the bishops and rulers of God’s churches—whom we have known for a long time to have been especially devoted in fidelity and service to the Holy Roman Church, and to preserve their rightful claims in the churches in which they are known to serve the Lord. Therefore, venerable brother in Christ, Adalbero, Archbishop of Trier, considering your devotion toward blessed Peter, his holy Roman Church, and ourselves, we graciously assent to your just petitions; and, following the footsteps of our predecessor, Pope Innocent of blessed memory, [Col. 1212D] we apostolically confirm to you and your successors, and secure by the authority of this present document, that right which our most dear son Conrad, King of the Romans, or his predecessors are known to have held in the abbey of Saint Maximin, and which was conferred or restored to you, and through you to the Church of Trier, by that same Conrad, as is contained in the written instrument of that king concerning the restoration and confirmation.

We likewise decree that the peace and concord, or settlement, which was prudently made between you and the nobleman Henry, Count of Namur, in the presence of the aforesaid king through our most dear son Bernard, Abbot of Clairvaux, and the princes of that realm, and confirmed by the written instrument of the same king, shall remain valid and unshaken; and we strengthen it by the protection of this present document.
