CXCIII bis. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Martin of the Fields. (Year 1147, June 10.)

[DE MARRIER, *History of Saint-Martin-des-Champs*, p. 179.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ODO, prior of the monastery of Saint Martin of [Col. 1239B] the Fields, and his brothers, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

It is fitting readily to grant assent to religious desires, so that faithful devotion may obtain a swift result. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Prior Odo, assenting to your just petitions, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and fortify by the privilege of this present document, the monastery of Saint Martin, over which, by the Lord’s ordination, you preside under the institution of our venerable brother Peter, abbot of Cluny, just as we receive the other members of the Cluniac monastery. We enact that whatever possessions and goods the same monastery presently possesses justly and canonically, or may hereafter, through grants of popes, generosity of kings, benefactions of princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, by the Lord’s favor acquire, shall remain firm and undiminished to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names: in the district of Paris, the tithe of the aforesaid monastery of Saint Martin, the altar, and the tithe of Calloio. In the suburb of the city of Paris, the chapel of Saint James with its parish. Near the monastery of Saint Martin, the chapel of Saint Nicholas. Within the city, one prebend in the church of Saint Mary, the mother church of that city; the church of Saint Dionysius called “of the Prison,” with another prebend of the aforesaid mother church of the city. In the church of Saint Genevieve on the Mount, one prebend; the church of Saint Mary outside the castle of Gournay. Another church [Col. 1239D] within that same castle; the village of Nusiellum with church and churchyard; the village of Nusiacum with church and tithe; the church of Campiniacum with churchyard and one third of the tithe; Roissiacum with church, churchyard, and tithe; the church of Bercheriae with churchyard and tithe; the church of Pontolium with churchyard and tithe; the chapel in the castle called Cauda, with an oven; the chapel of Canolium; the church of Ororii with churchyard and tithe; one modius of grain from the tithe of Roissy; the church of Erigniacum; the village of Castaneum with church and tithe; the altar of Fontaneum; the church, churchyard, and tithe of Escuem; the church of Doomonte; the altar of Armenovilla; the church of Ceverenti with tithe; and the chapel of Luiriacum; Bonzeias with church; Penthinum with church; at Lecuras, [Col. 1240A] a church with churchyard and tithe; the church of Attenevilla with tithe; the church of Saint Opportuna of Montiacum; the church of Derenci with one third of the tithe; the church of Carrona with one third of the tithe; the church of blessed Martin outside the city; the church of Meru; two thirds of the tithe of Villari-Adam. Mairolas with church and tithes; the tithe of Grear; the church and tithe of Chivry; the tithe of Attilly; the village of Conflans with church; the church of Encra with tithe. At Clamart, a church yielding thirty solidi yearly with tithe. At Saint Cloud, half of the land called Anetum. Limogias, with church and tithe; Furcas with church and tithe. In the district of Noyon, the church of Capy; with the prebend of Saint Furseus of Péronne; the altar of Moeliens with one third of the tithe, formerly held by Milo, canon of Péronne; the altar of Eliescurte, formerly held by Gauterius, son of Walvodi of Nigella; the altar of Stripeium; the altar of Longeval; at the altar of Clari, the benefices of three feast-days, namely Good Friday, Easter Day, and the day of the Purification of Blessed Mary; half of the small tithe; two thirds of half the greater tithe; and half the churchyard; two thirds of the tithe of Barhes; the altar of Fontenis; the tithe of eels belonging to Girard of Capy; the altar of Revelon; the altar of Berencurt; the altar of Heldincurt; the church of Saint Hilary. In the district of Amiens, the church of Saint Modestus of Ligny; the altar of Vilerey; the church of Saint Mary [Col. 1240C] of Arenis; the church of Vaviller with tithe; the altar of Old Amiens; one third of the church of Morines; the tithe from the mill of Baldus; the church of Wainni; the church of Bonai with tithe. In the district of Arras, the church of Pas. In the district of Laon, half of the village called Disy, held by Luke, abbot of Quissiacum, and its church, which renders to your aforesaid monastery thirty solidi in Parisian currency yearly, according to the settlement of our venerable brothers Samson, archbishop of Reims, and Bartholomew, bishop of Laon. The allod of Briannia, held by the abbey of Saint Hubert of Ardennes, rendering to the same monastery two marks of silver yearly. In the district of Reims, the rent of Poelli, given by Gaulcher of Basoches. In [Col. 1240D] the district of Châlons, the church of Wailemont; the church of Frisivilla with chapel; the church of Virleu; the church of Curtis; the church of Old Dampetro. In the district of Soissons, the village of Saint Gemma with church; the church of Lergny with tithe, churchyard, male serfs, and female serfs; the church of Noa Saint Martin with churchyard and tithe. In the district of Beauvais, the church of Saint Leonorius of Bellomonte; the tithe of Mediana Curte; the altar of Saint Audomarus; the church of Cressonessart with tithe; the church of Wirma; the church of Frenci with half the tithe; the church of Blessed Mary of Insula; the church of Meru with churchyard, one third of the tithe, and the tithe of gardens; the church of Prateriae, yielding twenty Parisian solidi yearly with the small tithe; the church of Saint Remigius of [Col. 1241A] Noa with tithe; the church of Villa-Bernosa and five shares of the tithe; the church of Roveredo with churchyard, the small tithe, and half the greater tithe; two thirds of the tithe of Geals; one third of the tithe of Liencurt. In the district of Senlis, the church of Saint Nicholas with a prebend of the Blessed Mother Church of the city; the church of Oiri with the small tithe; the church of Sorvillers; the church of Coia with churchyard and the small tithe; half the altar of Brayo; half the small tithe of Fontanis and one ninth of the greater. In the district of Sens, the village of Fontanis with church and tithe; the church of Cona; the church of Dormella. In the church of Blessed Mary at Étampes, one prebend. In the district of Orléans, the church of Hienvilla with the parish of Puisat. In the district of Chartres, Ursonvilla [Col. 1241B] with church; Gouvellum with church and half the tithe; Roenvilla with church and tithe; the tithe of Bercheriae. At Crisperiae, a church and two thirds of the tithe; Saint Hilary with church. In the district of Meaux, Anetum with church and one third of the tithe; Choisiacum with church and tithe; the chapel of Meroliis; the tithe of Acy; the church of Saint Martin of Crécy, with parish, one third of the tithe, the chapel of Saint Mary, and the other appurtenances; the chapel of Marnoa; the chapel of Incy. In England, in the district of Exeter, the chapel of Saint James upon the water, close to the city itself, with its churchyard and the holding of Walter the knight; the church of Tinctona; the church of Saint Mary of Barnstaple; and the other things contained in the privileges of our predecessors of holy memory, Popes Urban, Paschal, Calixtus, Innocent, and Lucius. Moreover, following the footsteps of our predecessor Pope Urban of good memory, we enact that, with the bishops’ counsel, you shall place priests in the parish churches which you hold. If they are suitable, the bishops shall entrust them with the care of souls, so that such priests may render account to the bishops for the care of the people, while showing to you due subjection in temporal matters.

Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but let all things be preserved whole for the use and benefit in every respect of those for whose governance [Col. 1241D] and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical jurisdiction of the diocesan bishops. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing the tenor of this our constitution, should rashly act against it and, having been warned a second or third time, fails to correct that offense by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and honor; let that person know that he or she stands guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let that person be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and let that person be subject to severe vengeance at the last judgment. But may all who preserve their rights for that same place have the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good [Col. 1242A] action and find, before the strict judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

Given at Paris through the hand of Hugh, cardinal priest, acting in place of Lord Guy, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the sixth day before the Nones of June, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1147 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the third year of the pontificate of Pope Eugenius III.

CXCIV. Bull concerning the dedication of the church at Montmartre. (Year 1147, June 13.)

[MABILLON, *Benedictine Annals*, VI, 701, from the autograph.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to all the faithful of God: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1242B] The authority of our office urges us to love and support venerable places, together with the persons devoted to divine service therein, and to provide for their needs with paternal concern. Accordingly, considering the need of the nuns of Montmartre, at their request we visited that place in person on the Kalends of June, in the year 1147 from the Incarnation of the Lord; and there, after invoking the grace of the Holy Spirit, we consecrated, by the Lord’s authority, the high altar in honor of the blessed martyrs Dionysius, Rusticus, and Eleutherius. To those who then visited that place out of devotion and piety, or who shall hereafter visit it on the annual day of that consecration, and who have bestowed alms upon those nuns from the means [Col. 1242C] granted them by God, we remit seven hundred days of imposed penance, trusting in the merits of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul; and we have confirmed the same indulgence by the tenor of this document.

Given at Meaux, on the Ides of June.

On one side of the pendent seal: EUGENIUS POPE III.

CXCV. He confirms the agreement made by Gerald, bishop [of Limoges], between the monasteries of Uzerche and Meymac. (Year 1147, June 14.)

[BALUZE, *History of Tulle*, 885.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons BERNARD, abbot, and the other monks of the monastery of Uzerche [Col. 1242D]: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Whenever a request is made of us that is recognized to accord with religion and uprightness, it is fitting that we grant it willingly and give suitable assistance to the petitioners’ desires. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, moved by the prayers of our venerable brother Gerald, your bishop, we graciously assent to your just petitions; and, providing for your peace and tranquillity in the future, we confirm and decree to remain valid the agreement made between you and the monks of Meymac through the hand of that bishop for the sake of peace, and confirmed by his charter. Namely, the monastery of Meymac shall be subject in perpetual right to the monastery of Uzerche as a member to its head. [Col. 1243A] Upon the death of the abbot of the monastery of Meymac, the monks of that monastery shall freely elect from their own monastery a suitable person, with the counsel and consent of the abbot of Uzerche; provided, however, that either he shall have professed at the monastery of Uzerche before his election, or, if he has not professed there before, after election and before ascending the abbatial seat, he shall make profession to the monastery of Uzerche. If no suitable person to be elected abbot is found in the monastery of Meymac, the monks of Meymac shall elect and take as abbot a suitable person from the monastery of Uzerche, with the counsel and consent of the abbot of Uzerche. If anyone knowingly and rashly attempts to act against the tenor of this our confirmation, let that person incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Meaux, on the eighteenth day before the Kalends of July.

I, Peter, by the permission of divine mercy archbishop of the Church of Bourges, wish it to be committed to the memory of faithful people present and future that, at the command of Lord Pope Eugenius, Bernard, abbot of Uzerche, and Hugh, monk of Meymac, appeared before us to determine the controversy long disputed between them concerning the church of Meymac. Accordingly, when both parties had appeared before us on the appointed day, the abbot of Uzerche claimed back investiture of the church of Meymac, asserting that this church had long and peacefully been possessed by his predecessors as a priory: thus priors and the other monastic officers in that church were appointed by his predecessors, the abbots of Uzerche; an annual meal was supplied to the brothers of Uzerche by the prior of Meymac; and monks receiving the habit at Meymac were brought to the abbot of Uzerche, received blessing there, and made profession upon the altar at Uzerche according to monastic custom. When the opposing party denied this, the abbot of Uzerche produced witnesses, who, carefully examined by us and questioned individually, gave mutually consistent testimony concerning possession of the church of Meymac in accordance with the statements of the abbot of Uzerche. Therefore, after taking counsel with our brothers and receiving the witnesses’ oaths, we adjudged investiture to the monastery of Uzerche, saving the right of ownership; and we reinvested the abbot of Uzerche with the church of Meymac and all its appurtenances. We further command that Hugh himself and the other monks of Meymac shall obey the abbot of Uzerche. To ensure that this may be retained in memory, it is to be committed to the present document and confirmed by the impression of our seal.

Done at Vodolium, in the presence of our clerics Emeno the dean, Master Umbert, Stephen prior of Salis, Rainald prior of Malavalle, John our chaplain, and Absalon our chancellor, in the year 1146 of the Lord’s Incarnation, the eighth indiction, in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III, while Louis reigned as king of the Franks.

CXCVI. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Heribert at Deutz. (Year 1147, June 17.)

[LACOMBLET, *Charters*, I, 244.]

[Col. 1244A]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GERLAC, abbot of the monastery of Saint Heribert at Deutz, and his brothers, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

Since without true religious worship charity cannot endure, nor can service pleasing to God be rendered, it is expedient for apostolic authority to love religious persons [Col. 1244B] and, with God’s help, beneficially provide for their peace. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions; and we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and fortify by the privilege of this present document, the aforesaid monastery in which you are devoted to divine service. We enact that whatever possessions and goods the same monastery presently possesses justly and canonically, or may hereafter, through grants of popes, benefactions of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, by God’s favor acquire, shall remain firm and undiminished to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names: the castle of Deutz itself [Col. 1244C], with the church of Saint Urban, its tithes, and all its appurtenances and immunities. At Remagen, the tithe of fields and vineyards; at Windense, a church and manor with tithe. At Vene, a church with manor and tithe. At Disternich, a church with tithe. At Zudendorp, a church and manor with tithe. At Wadenhem, a manor. At Antwirle and Ewirle, a church and manor. At Westhone, a manor with chapel. At Houmere, a manor with chapel. At Herine, a manor with chapel. At Langela, a manor. At Belle, a manor. At Mursa, a manor with chapel. At Merehem, a manor. At Eltinge, a manor. At Vellepe, a manor; at Rinwich, a manor. At Wic, Werlinge, and Odnige, royal jurisdiction. At Settene, a church with tithe. At Gladbech, a church and manor. At Wermere, a manor. [Col. 1244D] At Hatneke, a church and manor. At Elipe, a manor. At Rodhe, a manor with chapel. At Heringe, a church and manor. At Pelechen, a manor with chapel. At Ardeia, a manor. At Quinem, a manor. At Wiesche, a manor with church. At Nona, a manor with church. At Bilha, a manor. At Wednerenghausen, a manor. At Walda, a church and manor. At Leichlingen, a church and manor; the castle of Burgele with manor and church. At Hozzela, a manor with chapel. At Hemlee, two and a half hides. At Oestheim, one hide. At Rathehe, vineyards. At Bulsen, vineyards; at Mulne, vineyards, fields, and a boat on the Rhine. At Heistre, vineyards and fields. At Rodhe, a church with tithe. At Unna, a church. At Boine, a church. At Burge, a church with tithe. At Birtine, a church with tithe. At Affeltelbeche [Col. 1245A], a church with tithe. At Derne, a church; at Datlen, a church. At Hirchhelle, a church. At Buron, a church. At Waldorp, a church. At Wattenscheid, a church. At Hirspe, a church. At Brunon, a church. At Heltnon, a church. At Winingen, a church.

Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but let all things be preserved whole for the use and benefit in every respect of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical jurisdiction of the diocesan bishops. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, [Col. 1245B] knowing the tenor of this our constitution, should rashly act against it and, having been warned a second or third time, fails to amend by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and honor; let that person know that he or she stands guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let that person be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let that person be subject to severe vengeance at the last judgment. But may all who preserve justice for that same place have the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Given at Meaux through the hand of Guy, cardinal and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of July, [Col. 1245C] in the tenth indiction, in the year 1147 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

CXCVII. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Quentin of the Mount. (Year 1147, June 19.)

[GUIBERT, *Works*, p. 619.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to HUGH, abbot of the monastery of Saint Quentin of the Mount, situated in the district of Vermandois, and to his brothers, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

[Col. 1245D] It befits the clemency of apostolic governance to cherish religious persons and to fortify their places with pious protection; for it is recognized as worthy and consonant with uprightness that we, who have been raised to the governance of the churches, should both defend them from the wickedness of evil men and foster them by the protection of the Apostolic See. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, following the footsteps of our predecessor Pope Paschal of happy memory, we graciously assent to your just petitions; and we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and fortify by the privilege of this present document, the aforesaid monastery in which you are devoted to divine service. We enact that whatever possessions and goods you presently possess justly and canonically, or may hereafter, through grants of popes, [Col. 1246A] generosity of kings, benefactions of princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, by the Lord’s favor acquire, shall remain firm and undiminished to you and your successors.

We have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names: the altar of Gresviller and that of Bresviller, with their appurtenances; the chapel of Hamelet with its appurtenances; the mill of Bellis Aisis with its appurtenances, and its milling-right from the Cross of Forensis as far as outside Britannum; the whole of Alania with its appurtenances, free from every exaction of secular persons—excepting the mills, the second tithing of the demesne fields, and the fiefs, which nevertheless shall be brought under the justice and jurisdiction of the aforesaid church; Heldincourt with its appurtenances, and the crossing of the river Hala. [Col. 1246B] We also grant that the burial-place of that same site shall be free, so that no one may obstruct the devotion and final wish of those who have determined to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict, while the right of the mother church is nevertheless preserved.

Upon the death of yourself, now abbot of the same place, or of any one of your successors, no one shall be set over it by any craft of intrigue or violence, except the person whom the brethren, by common consent, or the sounder part of their counsel, shall, in the fear of God and according to the Rule of blessed Benedict, determine ought to be chosen.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations whatsoever; but that all things be preserved whole [Col. 1246C] for the benefit in every respect of those uses for whose governance and support they were granted, with the authority of the Apostolic See and the justice of the diocesan bishop reserved.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, should not correct his offence by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let him be subject, at the last judgment, to strict vengeance.

[Col. 1246D] But upon all who preserve the rights of this place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Theodewinus, bishop of Saint Rufina. I, Albericus, bishop of Ostia. I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Chrysogonus. I, Hymboldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul. I, Gillibertus, unworthy priest of the title of Saint Mark. I, Hugh, priest of the title in Lucina. I, Odo, cardinal deacon of Saint George. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Angelo. [Col. 1247A] I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, Hyacinthus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin.

Given at Meaux, through the hand of Guido, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of July, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1147 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the third year of the pontificate of Pope Eugenius III.

## CXCVIII. Bull to Ivo, Abbot, and the Monks of Redon, confirming their privileges.

*(A.D. 1147, 24 June.)*

[Marten, *Thesaurus Anecdotorum*, I, 403, from a manuscript of Saint Michael in Peril of the Sea.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons [Col. 1247B] IVO, abbot of the monastery of Redon, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

A desire shown to pertain to the religious purpose and the salvation of souls ought, by God’s authorship, to be fulfilled without delay. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions; and, following in the footsteps of our predecessor Pope Gregory VII of blessed memory, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves, and strengthen by the privilege of this present writing, the aforesaid monastery of Redon, which belongs by right to the Holy Roman Church. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future [Col. 1247C] acquire, by concession of pontiffs, gift of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, God being favourable, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors.

Upon the death of yourself, now abbot of the same place, or of any one of your successors, no one shall be set over it through any craft of intrigue or violence, except the person whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren’s counsel, shall, in the fear of God and according to the Rule of blessed Benedict, determine ought to be elected from that same community. But if no person suitable for this governance can be found among you, then, with the counsel of the Roman pontiff, let them seek elsewhere for themselves a father and master.

Moreover, in the churches which you hold, we decree that you shall elect priests [Col. 1247D] and present them to the bishops. If they are suitable, the bishops shall commit to them the care of souls, so that such priests shall answer to the bishops for the care of the people, but shall render to you the due subjection in temporal matters. You shall receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or churches, and ordinations of monks or clerics to be promoted to sacred orders, from the diocesan bishops, provided that they possess the favour and communion of the Apostolic See and are willing to provide these things freely and without impropriety. Otherwise, you may receive the same sacraments from whichever Catholic bishops you prefer.

We also grant that the burial-place of that same site shall be free, so that no one may obstruct the devotion and [Col. 1248A] final wish of those who have determined to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict. *(The right of the mother church is nevertheless reserved.)* We further add by this present chapter that the monastery itself, its abbots, and its monks shall be secure from every harassment of secular service and removed from every burden of worldly oppression, diligent and undisturbed in the observance of holy religion; they shall be bound in no circumstance to be subject to any authority other than the Roman and Apostolic See, to which it belongs by right. As a token that their monastery belongs by right to blessed Peter and the Holy Roman Church, you shall pay three gold coins annually to our Lateran palace.

We therefore decree that absolutely no person may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its [Col. 1248B] possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but that all things be preserved whole for the benefit in every respect of those uses for whose governance they were granted, with the authority of the Apostolic See reserved. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, should not amend by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let him be subject, at the last judgment, to strict vengeance. But upon all [Col. 1248C] who preserve what is right for this place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Theodewinus, bishop of Saint Rufina, have subscribed. I, Albericus, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Chrysogonus, have subscribed. I, Gislebertus, unworthy priest of the title of Saint Martin, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Angelo, have subscribed. [Col. 1248D] I, Hyacinthus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin, have subscribed.

Given at Meaux, through the hand of Guido, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the eighth day before the Kalends of July, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1147 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

## CXCIX. To Stephen, King of the English—That he receive Robert, Bishop of London, into his favour.

*(A.D. 1147, 26 June.)*

[Mansi, *Concilia*, XXI, 648.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved [Col. 1249A] son in Christ STEPHEN, illustrious King of the English: greeting and apostolic blessing.

For this purpose heavenly providence ordained pontiffs in the Church: that the Christian people might receive from them the pastures of life, and that both secular princes and persons of lower station might show reverence to those pontiffs as Christ’s vicars. Our venerable brother Robert, bishop of London, being a wise and honourable man and a lover of religion, ought to be treated kindly by your nobility and more earnestly honoured because of the prudence granted him by God. Therefore, since, as we have learned truly, he cannot bind himself by the fidelity required of him without peril to his soul and his order, we desire and, from paternal affection, advise you [Col. 1249B] not to trouble our aforesaid brother in any way on this account; rather, for reverence toward blessed Peter and ourselves, receive him into your affection and favour. Since he cannot take that oath, let it suffice your discretion that he promise in a simple and truthful word that he will inflict no injury upon you or your land. Farewell.

Given at Meaux, on the seventh day before the Kalends of July.

## CC. To Matilda, Queen of the English—That she exhort her husband to affection for the aforesaid bishop.

*(A.D. 1147, 26 June.)*

[Mansi, *Concilia*, XXI, 649.]

[Col. 1249C]

EUGENIUS, etc.

As Solomon testifies, we have learned that a wise woman builds her house, but a foolish woman destroys with her hands what has been built. We rejoice on your account and commend in the Lord your zeal of devotion, because, as we have learned from the report of religious persons, keeping the fear of God before your eyes, you devote yourself to works of piety and both love and honour ecclesiastical persons.

Therefore, that you may, by the Lord’s inspiration, advance from good to better, we ask your nobility in the Lord and, by asking, admonish and exhort you in the Lord, that you may add better outcomes to your good beginnings and more attentively love and honour our venerable brother Robert, bishop of London, for the reverence of him who, though once rich [Col. 1249D], chose to become poor for our sake. Endeavour to bring it about with your husband, our beloved son Stephen, the renowned King of the English, that by your admonitions, exhortation, and counsel he may receive him into his favour and affection, and hold him more earnestly commended for reverence toward blessed Peter and ourselves. And because, as we observe on the testimony of truth, he cannot bind himself to our aforesaid son without peril to his salvation and order, we desire and advise both him and you with paternal affection that it suffice you to receive from him the promise, in a truthful and simple word, that he will inflict no injury or loss upon him or his land.

Given at Meaux, on the sixth day before the Kalends of July.

## CCI. To Theobald, Archbishop of Canterbury—Concerning the dispute between the Archbishop of Canterbury and Bernard, Bishop of Saint David’s, over metropolitan right. Both are ordered to appear before him “on the feast of blessed Luke in the following year.”

*(A.D. 1147, 29 June.)*

[Mansi, *Concilia*, XXI, 628.]

[Col. 1250A]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother THEOBALD, Archbishop of Canterbury: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Our venerable brother Bernard, bishop of Saint David’s, appearing before us, asserted orally that the Church of Saint David’s had once been a metropolitan see and requested that the same dignity be restored to him by us. [Col. 1250B] While he had remained in our court for a long time diligently pursuing this petition, you, brother archbishop, at last, in his presence, rose in opposition and lodged before us a complaint against him: namely, that he had withheld the obedience due to you as first metropolitan and had proved disobedient and rebellious toward you, although he had been consecrated by your predecessor as first metropolitan, had made a profession to the Church of Canterbury both orally and in writing, and afterwards had obeyed and attended you in many matters just as the other suffragans did.

He could not deny the consecration; but he wholly denied that he had made the profession or rendered obedience. Hearing this, you produced two witnesses, who testified [Col. 1250C] that after his consecration, in their sight and hearing, he had made a profession to the Church of Canterbury both orally and in writing. We therefore, having heard and carefully investigated the arguments of both parties, and having diligently examined your witnesses, and after taking counsel with our brethren, received their oaths and, as justice required, commanded that the bishop himself render you obedience and reverence as first metropolitan.

Accordingly, since we wish to preserve to every church and ecclesiastical person its own dignity and right, we have fixed a day for you and him on the feast of blessed Luke in the following year, so that, with the parties present, we may then ascertain the truth concerning the dignity and liberty [Col. 1250D] of the Church of Saint David’s, and thereafter, God being the author, determine what is just.

Given at Meaux, on the third day before the Kalends of July.

## CCII. Fragment of a privilege for the monastery of Saint Martin of the Fields.

*(A.D. 1147, 2 July.)*

[*Bibliotheca Cluniacensis*, 603.]

[lacuna] Therefore, beloved son Odo, prior, assenting to your just petitions, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves, and strengthen by the privilege of this present writing, the monastery of Saint Martin, over which, by God’s appointment, you preside through the institution of our venerable brother Peter, Abbot of Cluny, [Col. 1251A] just as the other members of the abbey of Cluny; etc.

Given at Paris through the hand of Hugh, cardinal priest acting in place of Lord Guido, cardinal of the Holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the sixth day before the Nones of July, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1147 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

## CCIII. To the priests of the churches of the monastery of Balmes—He relaxes the interdict by which he had justly punished churches belonging to the monastery of Balmes.

*(A.D. 1147, 14 July.)*

[Dom Bouquet, *Recueil*, XV, 445.]

[Col. 1251B] EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the priests and other clerics of the churches belonging to the monastery of Balmes, who remain in obedience to blessed Peter and ourselves: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Just as punishment is justly imposed upon those remaining in fault according to the character of their offence, so the gate of mercy is mercifully opened to those who repent. Therefore, from the customary clemency of the Apostolic See, we relax the interdict which had been imposed, by the rigour of justice, upon the churches in which you serve the Lord, because our beloved son Master Osbert had grievously offended in contempt of God and the Church. Now, since we have granted the aforesaid monastery, with all things belonging to it, to our beloved son Peter, abbot, and through him [Col. 1251C] to the monastery of Cluny, by this present writing we command and instruct you to obey him and ourselves in him reverently and humbly.

Given at Auxerre, on the nineteenth day before the Kalends of August.

## CCIV. He commands Henry, Bishop of Moravia, to exhort Conrad, King of the Romans, to apply himself to the union of the Church of Constantinople with the Roman Church.

*(A.D. 1147, 15 July.)*

[Boczek, *Codex diplomaticus Moraviae*, I, 257.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, Bishop of Moravia: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1251D] As your brotherhood knows, being solicitous with paternal affection for our dearest sons Conrad, King of the Romans, and Louis, most illustrious King of the Franks, and for the armies that are with them, we have sent from our side our venerable brethren Theodewinus, bishop of Saint Rufina, and Guido, cardinal priest of Saint Chrysogonus—men indeed prudent and honourable—that they may preserve them in concord and affection and, with the Lord as author, provide for their welfare both in spiritual and temporal matters.

Therefore we ask your brotherhood and, by asking, command you, for reverence toward blessed Peter and that same Roman Church, to love and honour them as persons sent from the bosom of your mother, the Roman Church, and to offer them counsel and aid in matters which you know concern the honour of God and of his Church. [Col. 1252A] And because we have the greatest confidence in your affection, and know that the king’s counsel largely rests in your prudence and direction, we direct your solicitude to strive in every way to exhort and admonish the king to devote himself to the honour and exaltation of his mother, the Holy Roman Church, and faithfully labour, according to the power granted him by God, to unite to her the Church of Constantinople, as it is known formerly to have been united. If, through your willing zeal and with the Lord’s aid, this comes to fruition, it will increase the favour and grace of the Apostolic See toward your person and confer an increase of honour upon your church.

Given at Auxerre, on the Ides of July.

## CCV. Privilege for the Church of Saint Saviour at Saragossa.

*(A.D. 1147, 16 July.)*

[Arruego, *Cátedra episcopal de Zaragoza*, 669.]

[Col. 1252B]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother BERNARD, Bishop of Saragossa, and to his successors canonically appointed: in perpetuity.

Placed, by the Lord’s ordering, on the lofty watchtower of the Apostolic See, we ought, from the office laid upon us, to love our brother bishops and preserve to the churches committed to them by God their rights. Therefore, venerable brother in Christ, Bishop Bernard, we graciously [Col. 1252C] assent to your just petitions; and we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and strengthen by the privilege of this present writing, the Church of Saint Saviour at Saragossa, over which you are known, by God’s agency, to preside. We decree that whatever possessions and goods you, brother bishop, now justly and canonically possess, or may in future acquire by concession of pontiffs, gift of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, God being favourable, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you, your successors, and through you to that same church. Among these, we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names: Teroham, with its forts and villages; Aranda; Siarcum; Arandagama, with the villages and castles contained in their watercourse; [Col. 1252D] Ricla; Capannas; Epila; Rota; Oreia; Turbena; Alagón, with all the villages and castles contained in the watercourse of the Exalón; Concrum; Aganción; Burota; Alberit; Magalón; Frascán; Mallén; Cortes; Novellas, with the villages and castles lying toward Saragossa in the watercourse of the Burguía; Gallur, with the villages and castles as far as the castle called Alagón; Gorreyam Salicem; Alcolea; Deuslibol; Alfaxarín; Pina; Villella; Michinentia, with the villages and castles lying toward Saragossa; Belchite; Orsa; and Sástago.

We also enact that, on the Saracen side, all the boundaries of that bishopric, as they are known lawfully to have been from antiquity, shall henceforth be preserved to you and your successors undisturbed and whole. We confirm by this page of the present writing the liberties [Col. 1253A] and immunities granted to that church in pious devotion by the illustrious King Alfonso and confirmed by his charter; and we decree that the same church shall be free from every secular yoke and dominion.

We therefore decree that absolutely no person may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but that all things be preserved whole, for the benefit in every respect of your uses and those of others for whose governance and support they were granted, with the authority of the Apostolic See reserved. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it and, having been warned a [Col. 1253B] second or third time, should not amend by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let him be subject, at the last judgment, to strict vengeance.

But upon all who preserve what is right for this place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Albericus, bishop of Ostia, etc.

Given at Auxerre, through the hand of Guido, [Col. 1253C] cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of August, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1147 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

## CCVI. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Mary of Lucelle.

*(A.D. 1147, 17 July.)*

[Schoepflin, *Alsatia diplomatica*, I, 233.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons CHRISTIAN, abbot of Saint Mary of Lucelle, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetual memory.

A desire known to pertain to the religious purpose and the salvation [Col. 1253D] of souls ought, by God’s authorship, to be fulfilled without any delay. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions; and we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and strengthen by the privilege of this present writing, the aforesaid place in which you are devoted to divine service. We decree that whatever possessions and goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may in future acquire by concession of pontiffs, gift of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, God being favourable, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors.

Among these, we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: namely, the place of Lucelle itself; the estates of Culmillis, Coronato, [Col. 1254A] Curtamaltru, Libunwilar, the spring of Alnulf, Muteresheim, Dornoso, Ytzvelden, Haldestatt, Sennheim, and Mosa, with all their appurtenances. Furthermore, no one whatsoever shall presume to exact tithes from you on the produce of the lands which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or from the sustenance of your animals.

We therefore decree that absolutely no person may rashly disturb the aforesaid place, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but that all things be preserved whole for the benefit in every respect of those uses for whose governance and support they were granted, with the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop reserved. If, therefore, in the future [Col. 1254B] any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it and, having been warned a second or third time, should not amend by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let him be subject, at the last judgment, to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve what is right for this place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. [Col. 1254C] I, Albericus, bishop of Ostia. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Laurence and Damasus. I, Julius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus. I, Hugh, cardinal priest in Lucina. I, Odo, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Octavianus, cardinal deacon of the title of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of the title of Saint Mary in Portico. I, Hyacinthus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Jordanus, cardinal priest of the title of Susanna.

[Col. 1254D] Given at Auxerre, through the hand of Guido, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of August, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1147 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

## CCVII. Privilege for the Church of Saint Mary of God’s Place.

*(A.D. 1147, 23 July.)*

[Hugo, *Annales Praemonstratenses*, I, preface, 503.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GARNER, abbot of the Church of Saint Mary of God’s Place, and his brethren, present and future, professing the canonical life: in perpetuity.

It is fitting readily to grant [Col. 1255A] assent to religious desires, so that faithful devotion may attain a swift effect. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions; and we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and strengthen by the privilege of this present writing, the aforesaid Church of Saint Mary, in which you devote yourselves to divine service. We decree that the canonical order known to have been instituted in your church according to the Rule of blessed Augustine shall be preserved there inviolate for all future time.

Furthermore, whatever possessions and goods the same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future acquire through the concession of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, the Lord providing, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you. [Col. 1255B] Among these, we have thought fit especially to note: the place itself in which that church is situated; the place called Fossa Mauri, with all its appurtenances; the place called Messiacus, with the territory called Thoriacum; the place called Malusrepatus; the place called Villapedes; the place called Aurea Vallis, with all their appurtenances; the mill of Fricambault, the mill of Salva Manu, and the mill which Lady Helia of Villamauri gave to your church, with all their appurtenances; likewise the right of use which Louis, King of the Franks of illustrious memory, gave you in his wood beside which that church is situated, [Col. 1255C] and which Henry, Archbishop of Sens of good memory, similarly granted in his own wood, so that you may take thence what is needed for all your uses and pasture your animals.

Furthermore, no one shall presume to exact tithes from you on the produce of the lands which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or from the sustenance of your animals. We also prohibit any of your brethren, after making profession, from leaving the cloister without the permission of the abbot and brethren; and no one shall dare to retain a departing brother without letters of commendation.

We therefore decree that absolutely no person may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it in any manner; but that all things be preserved whole [Col. 1255D] for the benefit in every respect of those uses for whose governance and support they were granted, with the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop reserved. If, in the future, any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it and, having been warned a second or third time, should not correct his offence by worthy satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of our Lord Jesus Christ; and let him be subject, at the last judgment, to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve what is right for this place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here [Col. 1256A] the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Albericus, bishop of Ostia. I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum. I, Humbaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul. I, Julius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus. I, Hugh, cardinal priest of the title in Lucina. I, Odo, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Octavianus, cardinal deacon of the title of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Angelo. [Col. 1256B] I, Hyacinthus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin.

Given at Auxerre through the hands of Guido, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the tenth day before the Kalends of August, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1147 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

## CCVIII. To the consuls of Lucca—On behalf of the brethren of the Church of Saint Frigidian.

*(A.D. 1147, 28 July.)*

[Baluze, *Miscellanea*, Lucan edition, IV, 594.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved [Col. 1256C] sons, the consuls of Lucca: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is our will diligently to apply ourselves to establishing religion and, once it has been established, to preserve it as the duty of our office requires. As we believe is known to your prudence, our predecessors, the Roman pontiffs of holy memory, wished to grant the Church of Saint Pantaleon to the brethren of the Church of Saint Frigidian, in order that through them the practice of religion might be restored there and, with God’s help, preserved.

Recently, however, as we have learned, when our venerable brother G., bishop, wished by our command to introduce the same brethren into the Church of Saint Pantaleon, Rodel. Pan. and others with him made an injurious assault upon them and, setting aside reverence for God and the Holy Roman Church, treated them [Col. 1256D] dishonourably. Your discernment, we believe, cannot be unaware with what severity and punishment this ought to be visited. Therefore, holding valid the sentence canonically pronounced by our aforesaid brother against those presumptuous persons, we command, admonish, and exhort your affection in the Lord not to inflict any vexation or molestation upon the aforesaid brethren in carrying out so praiseworthy a work; rather, that they may be able to possess the place itself in peace and serve the Lord there, provide them, according to the prudence bestowed upon you by God, with aid and counsel.

Given at Auxerre, on the fifth day before the Kalends of August.

## CCIX. To [Gregory], Bishop of Lucca—On the same matter.

*(A.D. 1147, July.)*

[Baluze, *Miscellanea*, Lucan edition, IV, 593.]

[Col. 1257A]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother G., Bishop of Lucca: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is known that the custom of the Holy and Apostolic See has been to establish religious communities and, with the Lord providing, to spread them through various places in the world. With this purpose in view, our predecessors, the Roman pontiffs of holy memory, entrusted the Church of Saint Pantaleon to the care of the brethren of blessed Frigidian, so that through their diligent efforts the religious observance of the canonical order [Col. 1257B] might be reformed there and, by God’s authorship, preserved henceforth.

But we have learned that, when you wished, in accordance with our command, to introduce the brethren of the aforesaid church into the said Church of Saint Pantaleon, Rodel. Pan. and certain others made an injurious assault upon you and the brethren of Saint Frigidian and treated you dishonourably; whereupon you pronounced sentences of excommunication against them. Therefore we, whose office it is to correct evil deeds and confirm good ones, hold valid the sentence canonically pronounced in this matter, because we are unwilling to fail the justice of the aforesaid brethren. Meanwhile, act manfully and prudently bring it about that the good undertaking may, through diligent care, reach completion [Col. 1257C] with a better outcome. Moreover, we wish you to know that if the priests Manfred and Lothair, Lambert, Cappellus, and Master William presume henceforth to resist the same brethren in this matter or to favour their persecutors, we shall not allow them to go unpunished as transgressors of your commands and of those of the Apostolic See.

## CCX. He receives under protection the Benedictine abbey of noble nuns at Messines, in the diocese of Ypres, and enumerates and confirms its possessions.

*(A.D. 1147, 28 July.)*

[Miraeus, *Opera diplomatica*, vol. III, p. 46, from the archives of the Abbey of Messines.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved [Col. 1257D] daughters in Christ, AELIDIS of the monastery of Messines (*Mecinense*, commonly *Messines*), and her sisters, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

The desire shown to concern the profession of religion and the salvation of souls ought, by God’s prompting, to be fulfilled without any delay. Therefore, beloved daughters in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions, and receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid convent of Messines, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. First, indeed, we decree that the monastic order, according to the Rule of Blessed Benedict and the institution of the Cluniac brethren, shall be preserved there inviolate for all time [Col. 1258A]. Moreover, we decree that whatever possessions and goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may hereafter, God willing, acquire by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and for those who shall succeed you. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names: the place itself in which the church is situated, with the tithe and the annual market, which Count Robert granted to your church; at Lampernessa, ten *berqueriae* and one quarter of one; at Alvergem, seven *mansi* of land; at Ekes, seven *mansi* of land; at Wideschat, twenty-eight *mansi* of land; the altar of Warnestun and half the toll of Duvia. At Ferlinghem, half a cattle-farm [*vaccaria*]. At the Double Mountains, a manor and two mills, and twelve *mansi* of land, and a share in the water. The tithe of Merengies and of Martini Campus; the village of Scotis. At Ypres, ten pounds of rent, Alcher’s dwelling-place, and the dwelling-places which Hugh granted to that same church; the village of Croisette with its appurtenances; one *mansus* at Martini Campus. At Douai, land divided into twelve shares. At Alawange, a *mansus* of land; the tithe of Saint Richarius. At Commines, the meadow and land called Ploitt, with its tenants, which Iwanus granted to the same church. At Chemlam, eight solidi of pennies; the chapel of Merkem, with its revenues and adjoining lands.

Upon the death of you, the present abbess of that place [Col. 1258C], or of any woman who shall succeed you, let no one be set over it by any artifice of deceit or violence, except the one whom the sisters, by common consent and according to the fear of God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict, shall provide to be elected.

Therefore we decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid convent, or to take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but let all things be preserved whole for the full benefit of those for whose governance and support they have been granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowing this page of our constitution [Col. 1258D], should rashly attempt to act against it, then, having been warned a second or third time, unless he makes suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ; and at the last judgment let him be subject to severe vengeance. But for all who preserve the rights of that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action, and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Albert, bishop of Ostia. I, Hugh, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina. [Col. 1259A] I, Hyacinth, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Guy, cardinal priest of the title of the Shepherd.

Given at Auxerre, by the hand of Guy, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Roman Church, on the fifth day before the Kalends of August, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1147 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the third year of the pontificate of Pope Eugenius III.

## CCXI. Privilege for the monastery of Tronchiennes. (1147, July 29.)

[HUGO, *Annals of Prémontré*, II, Preface, p. 611.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GOZWIN, abbot of the Church of Tronchiennes, [Col. 1259B] and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

Since without the true worship of religion neither can the Church securely endure nor service pleasing to God be offered, it is fitting that wherever we can, we establish the sacred observance of religion and, once established, preserve it with exact diligence. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions, and receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and of ourselves the church of Saint Mary, Mother of God, at Tronchiennes, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it with the protection of this present writing. Moreover, whatever possessions and goods that same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter [Col. 1259C], God willing, acquire by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names: the altar of Nivelle; the altar of Hansbeke; the altar of Landegem; the altar of Vorselaar; the altar of Petegem; the altar of Astene; the altar of Verrebruc; the altar of Cerscamp; also the two estates of Burst and Spinohtt; and two parts of the tithe of Ursle. Certainly, let no one presume to exact tithes from you on the produce which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or on the increase of your animals. Moreover, when the parish of Tournai lies under a general interdict [Col. 1259D], you may, with closed doors and with excommunicated and interdicted persons excluded, celebrate the divine offices in a low voice, unless there has been manifest fault on the part of the abbot and brethren of that place.

Therefore we decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any other vexations; but let all things be preserved whole for the full benefit of those for whose governance and support they have been granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, having been warned a second or third time [Col. 1260A], unless he makes suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ our Redeemer; and at the last judgment let him be subject to severe vengeance. But for all who preserve what is right for that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action, and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia. I, Imar, bishop of Tusculum. I, Humbald, cardinal priest of the title of Saints [Col. 1260B] John and Paul. I, Hugh, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus. I, Guy, cardinal priest of the title of the Shepherd. I, Jordan, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. I, Hyacinth, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin.

Given at Auxerre, by the hand of Guy, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the fourth day before the Kalends of August, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1147 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the third year of the pontificate of Pope Eugenius III.

## CCXII. He grants a bull to Nicholas, abbot of Corbie, “given at Auxerre by the hand of Guy, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the third day before the Kalends of August [July 30], in the tenth indiction, in the year 1147.” (1147, July 30.) [Col. 1260C]

[MABILLON, *Benedictine Annals*, VI, 423.]

## CCXIII. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Mary of Vallis-Christiana. (1147, July 31.)

[HUGO, *Annals of Prémontré*, II, Preface, 629.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons MAURICE, abbot of the Church of Blessed Mary of Vallis-Christiana, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

For this purpose the care of the universal Church has been entrusted to us by God, the provider [Col. 1260D] of all good things: that we may cherish religious persons and endeavour by every means to advance religion pleasing to God. For no service is ever rendered to God in a manner burdensome to him, unless, proceeding from the root of charity, it is maintained in the purity of religion. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions, receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid church in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. First, indeed, we decree that the canonical order which you have professed, according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine and the institution of the brethren of Prémontré, shall be preserved inviolate in your church for all time. Moreover, we decree [Col. 1261A] that whatever possessions and goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may hereafter, God willing, acquire by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names: the land of Rheincurt (Reincourt) at Bruyères; the land of Renaud the provost; the land of Theodoric; the land of the Hunters; one third of the tithe of the same place at Crameria; the tithe of the vegetable gardens [*olcae*] and land which you possess there by right; the whole of Currexxicui; the oven of that village; and a certain part of arable land; the whole tithe of Plaissiet; the whole tithe of Brutuel, except for a small portion; two thirds of the tithe of Noeroit (Noroy); one quarter of the tithe of Nuely; one *modius* of grain at the mill of Berny; at Holy Cross, three ploughlands [*carrucatae*] with their appurtenances; the manor of Martinpel, with its dependencies and appurtenances; one half of Bucylebarat, in woods and pastures alike, in cultivated and uncultivated land, in the whole tithe-assessment and in all jurisdiction; one third of the greater tithe of Long at Beilou; the tithe of the land of Malote; and one sixth of the tithe of Fara.

Certainly, let no one presume to exact tithes from you on the produce which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or on the increase of your animals [Col. 1261C]. Nor, after making profession there, may anyone, through the prompting of fickleness or under pretext of a stricter religious life, lawfully transfer to other places without the permission of the abbot and of the entire congregation; and if he does so, let no one whatsoever receive him without a common guarantee by letters.

Therefore we decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid place, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but let all things be preserved whole for the full benefit of those for whose governance and support they have been granted, saving in all things the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in future [Col. 1261D], knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, having been warned a second or third time, unless he makes suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ our Redeemer; and at the last judgment let him be subject to severe vengeance. But for all who preserve what is right for that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action, and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

[Col. 1262A] Given at Auxerre, by the hand of Guy, cardinal deacon and canon of the holy Roman Church, on the second day before the Kalends of August, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1147 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the third year of the pontificate of Pope Eugenius III.

## CCXIV. To Henry, bishop of Moravia.—He states that it would have pleased him more had Henry proceeded to the Holy Land rather than against the Slavs in Pomerania. (1147.)

[BOCZEK, *Moravian Diplomatic Codex*, I, 258.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, bishop of Moravia: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Your design, together with the Moravian dukes Otto, Zuatopluk, and Wratislaw [Col. 1262B], of proceeding against the Slavs and other pagans dwelling toward the north and of subjecting them to the Christian religion, was no less pleasing and welcome to us than your undertaking, dear brother, by which you have, God willing, inspired the illustrious duke of the Bohemians together with his brethren to take up the cross and set out on an expedition to the Holy Land. Indeed, I should have been pricked by a keener spur of joy when I heard from your messenger that the prudence of your person and your penetrating intelligence would sow in the heart of the king of the Romans the seed from which the union of the Church of Constantinople might grow up as a most fruitful harvest for me and for the Roman Church, mother of all. But after I learned that you had withdrawn from the king’s side, I have lost all confidence [Col. 1262C] in the successful prosecution of such an enterprise. Yet the matter was certainly difficult; and I cannot but praise the plan which you arranged with the greatest wisdom. Go forth, therefore, with the blessing of Christ and of the Apostolic See; and know that the welfare of your brotherhood is included in my daily prayer. Do not fail to inform me fully of the progress of such an expedition. Farewell in Christ.

## CCXV. He receives the monastery of Saint Mary of Neuburg into the protection of the Apostolic See. (1147, August 3.)

[SCHOEPFLIN, *Alsatian Diplomatic Records*, I, 234, from the cartulary of the monastery of Neuburg.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ULDARIC, abbot of Saint Mary of Neuburg, [Col. 1262D] and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

It is fitting readily to give assent to religious desires, so that faithful devotion may attain a swift effect. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions and receive the aforesaid church under the protection of Blessed Peter and of ourselves, strengthening it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, God willing, acquire by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors [Col. 1263A]. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names: namely, the place itself in which the abbey is founded; the grange of Harthusen; the grange of Lobach; the grange of Hohenscheit; the grange of Wilinbach; the grange of Suvelnheim; the grange of Gerute; the grange of Buttenheim; the grange of Atmonsvillere; and the grange of Hechenheim. Certainly, let no one presume to exact tithes from you on the produce which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or on the increase of your animals.

Therefore we decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any annoyances; but let all things be preserved whole [Col. 1263B] for the full benefit of those for whose governance and support they have been granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, having been warned a second or third time, unless he makes suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ; and at the last judgment let him be subject to severe vengeance. But for all who preserve what is right for that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that [Col. 1263C] here they may receive the fruit of good action, and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia. I, Humbald, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul. I, Julius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus. I, Hugh, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina. I, Jordan, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna. I, Odo, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of the title of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. I, Guy, cardinal deacon of the title of Saint Mary in Portico. I, Hyacinth, cardinal deacon of the title of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. [Col. 1263D] I, John Paparo, cardinal deacon of the title of Saint Adrian.

Given at Auxerre, by the hand of Guy, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the third day before the Nones of August, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1147 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the third year of the pontificate of Pope Eugenius.

## CCXVI. Bull confirming the Church of Ilbenstadt. (1147, August 8.)

[HUGO, *Annals of Prémontré*, I, Preface, 665.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ANTHONY, provost of Blessed Mary of Ilbenstadt, and his brethren, present and future, [Col. 1264A] professing the canonical life, in perpetuity.

Whenever something is requested of us which is recognized as befitting religion and honour, it is proper for us to grant it with willing mind and give fitting support to the desires of the petitioners. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions, and receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid church of Saint Mary, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. First, indeed, we decree that the canonical order established there, as is known, according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine and the institution of the brethren of Prémontré, shall be preserved there inviolate for all future time. Likewise, whatever possessions and goods you now [Col. 1264B] justly and canonically possess, or may hereafter, God willing, acquire by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by name: the allod of Dorcheim; the tithe and allod of Wlucrsheim; the rent and every due from one and a half *mansi* of vineyards which you possess at Everbach and at Alta Villa—rent and due which our venerable brother Henry, archbishop of Mainz, granted you and confirmed in writing. We likewise confirm for you the liberty granted to your church by Albert, archbishop of Mainz, of blessed memory, and confirmed by his writing: namely, that you are to answer to no archdeacons or clerics of the diocese of Mainz, but only to the archbishop himself [Col. 1264C]. Moreover, we prohibit the appointment in future of any advocate over you except with your common consent; rather, as it is known to have been hitherto, let your church remain free and undisturbed, without interference from any advocate.

Therefore we decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any annoyances; but let all things be preserved whole for the full benefit of those for whose governance and support they have been granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the archbishop of Mainz [Col. 1264D]. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, having been warned a second or third time, unless he makes suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ; and at the last judgment let him be subject to severe vengeance. But for all who preserve what is right for that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action, and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen. Amen, amen.

[Col. 1265A] I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia. I, Odo, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Imar, bishop of Tusculum. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. I, Humbald, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul. I, Gilbert, unworthy priest of the title of Saint Mark. I, Guy, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Lawrence and Damasus. I, Servatius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus. I, [unnamed] cardinal priest of the title in Lucina.

Given at Auxerre, by the hand of Guy, [Col. 1265B] cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the sixth day before the Ides of August, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1147 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the third year of the pontificate of Pope Eugenius III.

## CCXVII. He receives the Cistercian monastery of Saint Mary of Aldersbach under the protection of the Apostolic See. (1147, August 13.)

[HUNDIUS, *Metropolis of Salzburg*, II, 27.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son SIGFRID, abbot of Saint Mary of Aldersbach, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

[Col. 1265C] It is fitting readily to give assent to religious desires. Therefore, beloved son Sigfrid, abbot in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions and receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and of ourselves the monastery of Blessed Mary, over which, by God’s authority, you are known to preside; and we strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing.
