A modius of wheat granted to you each year by the illustrious Count Theobald, [Col. 1292A] and all fishing rights in his mills at Pontes; the vineyard given you by Berfridus of Calestra; twelve denarii of rent at Saint-Ferreol; a vineyard at Calestra; a rent of five solidi in the same place; at Mont Portarum, a rent of three solidi; the land of Croisum; all the land which Rainald, Milo’s son, held at Murgeoris; rights of use in the woods of Gurgiuolt and Poiseo, of Maceilliac, Charmeio, and in all the woods of Ansel of Triagnel, both for pasturing livestock and for building or other necessities. A rent of five solidi at the bridge of Baldiment (Pont-de-Baudement), six solidi at the mill of Canturanae, and five solidi at Oscha Theold, [Col. 1292B] at Gurgiuolt; the vineyard of Fonte Beton; and whatever William held in the meadow of Gandeleu; the vineyard of Saldon. From the gift of Gautier of Curtemaim, two sextarii of rye annually; the land of Tilliac; whatever you lawfully possess from the gift of Hervulf of Insula at Villeneuve and Tranqueil (Tranquaut); the land of Spinetum; land at Gumeri, at Summum-Fontem (Somme-Fontaine), and at Tremblei; the mill of Barsam; half the mill at the spring of Amau; a share in the mill of the pagan of Frou; whatever you possess at Planteiz; a rent of six denarii from Ubert of Tranqueil; whatever Thehelin held in the same place, except the people; the land of Amicus, knight of Somme-Fontaine; whatever Ermengardius Postellus held in the canons’ mills [Col. 1292C] of Villa Maurorum (Villemar), and in the gardens beyond the bridge of the Vanne; a share in the fishing rights which Felix held in the water of Bucennai, a share which he held in the land of Scrobium, and a rent of two solidi from the same man; the land on which your grange stands, and an *oscha* in the same place; the land given by Amaldricus and Hilduimus; the meadows of Vergeron; the lands which you possess at Quincey; a fourth of the meadow of Orella; four arpents of meadow at Tilley; half the mill of Quincey; all Geoffrey’s holding; half an arpent of vineyard at Ponstingiatum; from the gift of Hugh Capri, the vineyard of Montearpon, the house in which he himself lived, and the cellar; Guarin’s holding at Sancey.

[Col. 1292D] A vineyard at Sesana; land between Pisiacum (Pisy and Aisy) and Aizium; the mill of Bretigniac; a mill, land, and meadow at Marcilliac; an eighth share of the wood of Pisiac, and another share in the same wood. From the gift of Walter Rungifer, four arpents of meadow and forty solidi of rent; from the gift of Heloise of Villari, land, vineyard, and house; whatever Rodulf Gaius held in the wood of Fraxinetum, by gift of the aforesaid Count Theobald; sixteen sextarii of grain at the mill of Stagno; the mill of Changei; fifteen sextarii of grain at the mill of Planca; the mill of Justigniac (Jutigny); half the mill of Crevecuer and a vineyard; half the oven of the Vicomtesse.

[Col. 1293A] Half the meadow below the church of Saint Nicholas; the vineyards of Paula and Emmellina; Peter of Valle’s holding; and three denarii of rent from Ponne; the vineyards of Galcherius Cementarius; an arpent of vineyard and fourteen denarii of rent from Frodemund Peregrinus; Hugh Butarius’s vineyard; Rahaldis’s vineyard; seven jugera of land from Peter of Ponne; four jugera from Alburge of Ponne; two jugera and a building plot from the aforesaid Galcherius; seven jugera from Ada of Altomuro; an arpent and a half of meadow, and half a house, from Emmelina Rebursata; an arpent and a half of meadow from Bonade of Provins; Theodoric’s meadow; Ascrana’s house and lane; the houses of Richeldis, Paula, Hugh Butarius, Loberius, Adan, John Tyrannus, and half of Sunbard’s house; the house [Col. 1293B] of Bonellus Uvaura, and half of another house; three chambers and the vineyard of the same man; a modius of oats and twenty hens from Margaret, vicomtesse of Marrolis; the mill of Roscha; a fourth share of a house from Andrew; six jugera of land in Campo Levato and eighteen jugera above Mount Hanepon; a fourth of the land of Villa Cren; half the plantation of Fuliniac; from Evrard, a vineyard and twelve denarii of rent; the holding of the wife of Paganus the saddler, three solidi of rent at Lisinas, and the said Paganus’s house at Provins; the land of Radulf the canon at Lizinnia (Lisinec); half a house in the courtyard of Saint Nicholas; seven solidi of rent at Calestra; twenty solidi at Provins; twenty solidi at Lisinnias; seven and a half [solidi] from Tescia Majorissa; seventeen [solidi] from Mount Henepon; four solidi and two denarii from Buath; two solidi from Godfrey the Moneyer; twenty solidi from the lands of Coulet; the land of Greviars.

Moreover, from the gift of Hato, bishop of Troyes: half of all the tithe of Saint-Albin, and half the candles at the Purification of Saint Mary; the whole tithe of Aneuz; whatever Peter Sanctus held in the offering of the church of Tranqueil, and a share of the tithe of the same place; a third of the aforesaid offering, the rent of the courtyard, and the greater part of the tithe of Parigniac; whatever you possess in tithes at Balbusia, and at Saint-Parres in the tithes of Quincey, and at Ulmellos two parts of the tithe of [Col. 1293D] Gurgiuolt; whatever you possess in the tithe of Villagruis; a third of the tithe of Nogent; the tithe which you possess at Aurigniac, at Occe (Osse and Maupigny), at Malpigniac, and at Saint-Flavit; whatever you possess at Marigniac in tithes and offerings, and at each of the churches of Bocennay, at Ferroum, at Capella, at Codes, at Calestra, at Maferial (Maferey), and at Bernerias; likewise, whatever Peter, priest of Parigniac, gave you in houses, vineyards, or other things. From the gift of Henry, archbishop of Sens: the tithe of Lisignis and a share of the tithe of Cuchermey.

Furthermore, we apostolically confirm to you the places of Triagnel and Pomarium, as they have reasonably been granted to you, with all their appurtenances; and we decree that they are to remain subject to you, and that their prioresses are to be appointed and removed according to the decision of the abbess of the Paraclete and her sisters. [Col. 1294A]

We decree, moreover, that you shall not be compelled to leave the monastery in order to receive consecration or blessing, nor shall a bishop or anyone else inflict burden or annoyance upon you on account of the election of an abbess or for any other reason. No one shall exact tithes from you on account of your labours or annual produce. As a token of this liberty received from the Roman Church, you shall pay one gold obol each year to us and to our successors. Therefore let no person whatsoever rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain possessions taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; rather, let all things be preserved whole for the beneficial use of those for whose support and governance they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See. If anyone therefore, etc. [Col. 1294B]

Given at Châlons, through the hand of Guy, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the Kalends of November, in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1147 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

## CCXXXIX. To the abbot of Cluny.—He establishes that henceforth the abbot of Saint-Germain of Auxerre shall be elected with the counsel of the abbot of Cluny, and that the person elected shall receive blessing from the bishop of Auxerre. (3 November 1147.)

[D. Bouquet, *Recueil*, XV, 447.]

[Col. 1294C]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son PETER, abbot of Cluny, and to his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.

Recognizing that it is not fitting for servants of God to litigate, we are bound by the office entrusted to us to remove disputes and scandals from their midst and to provide, with watchful diligence, for the peace and tranquillity of the Churches. Therefore we order that the following judgment concerning the controversy which was being conducted over the monastery of Saint-Germain between you and our venerable brother Hugh, bishop of Auxerre, and between you and [Col. 1294D] the monks of Saint-Germain, be recorded in the series of this letter, lest it be withheld from the memory of future generations.

Having deliberated at length with our brethren upon this matter, and since there was no doubt that you and your brethren had possessed both the reception and correction of the order, and that after the death of Abbot Gervasius you had been deprived of all these things, we judged that you ought before all others to be restored.

[Note: [Col. 1293D] See the letters of Pope Urban II.]

[Note: [Col. 1293] Gervasius died in 1147, on the fourth Nones of August, according to the *Deeds of the Abbots of Saint-Germain*.]

Further, following in the footsteps of our predecessors and renewing what had been established by us, we command that no abbot whatsoever be elected in the abbacy of Saint-Germain without the counsel of you and your successors. [Col. 1295A] The bishop of Auxerre shall have full liberty canonically to approve or reject the person elected and, if he is worthy, to bless him as abbot. Once blessed, he shall promise obedience to the bishop. His deposition, should he prove such a man—which God forbid—shall likewise be carried out by judicial procedure; and the canonical correction both of the abbot and of the monks shall pertain to that same bishop. The abbot and monks of Saint-Germain shall receive from the bishop of Auxerre, as their diocesan, chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or churches, and the ordinations of monks or clerics who are to be promoted to holy orders, until he shall have incurred the favour of the Apostolic See.

If anyone knowingly attempts rashly to contravene this decree of ours, [Note: [Col. 1295D] Eugenius himself retracted this definition not long afterwards, as will be stated below.] [Col. 1295B] let him suffer the loss of his rank and office or be punished by the penalty of excommunication, unless he corrects his presumption by fitting satisfaction.

Given at Châlons, on the third Nones of November.

## CCXL. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Augustine at Thérouanne. (22 November 1147.)

[Hugo, *Annales Praemonstratenses*, I, Preface, p. 131.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ALELM, abbot of the church of Blessed Augustine, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

A desire shown to pertain to the purpose of religion and the salvation of souls must, by God’s authorship, be fulfilled without delay. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests; we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid church, in which you are devoted to divine service; and we strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions or goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future acquire, God favouring it, through grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and undiminished for you and your successors. We have considered the following to be specified by their proper names: the altars of Nielles, Quaquella, Beinghem, [Col. 1295D] Haringes, and Rincy, which our venerable brother Milo, bishop of Thérouanne, granted to your church and confirmed by his own written instrument; the land on which the courtyard stands, which Robert of Corbie and his sons, and Hugh of Sobrois, granted to your church; from the gift of the knight Elias, Robert’s son, a meadow; the land of Saint Philibert, which Amalric granted you for an annual rent of half a modius of wheat and half a modius of oats; the land of Robert of Corbie’s wife in Arnold’s valley; the land of Licendis, the miller-woman, in the parish of Nielles; the land of Laris, as granted to you by the monastery of Corbie for an annual payment of ten solidi; [Col. 1296A] all the land which Hugh of Chertucia held in the territory of Alceris, as he granted it to you for an annual rent of one mark of silver.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain possessions taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but let all things be preserved whole for the beneficial use of those for whose support and governance they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If, in future, any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly attempts rashly to contravene this charter of our constitution, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not make amendment by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour; let them know themselves guilty before the divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let them be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, Redeemer; and at the last judgment let them be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve what is right for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good works and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Alberic, bishop of Ostia. I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum. I, Hubald, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul. [Col. 1296C] I, Wilbert, unworthy priest of the title of Saint Mark. I, Aribert, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia. I, Hugh, cardinal priest of the title in Lucina.

Given at Lyons [Note: [Col. 1295D] Read Verdun. Jaffé.] through the hand [Note: [Col. 1295D] I think that “Guy” should be read: the same person who subscribed the privilege of this pontiff granted at Reims in favour of the monastery of Saint-Theodoric, on the fourteenth Kalends of May, 1148.] of Willo, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the tenth Kalends of December, in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1148, and in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

## CCXLI. He releases Henry, bishop of Moravia, from the summons to the council at Trier. (18 December 1147.)

[Boczek, *Codex diplomaticus Moraviae*, I, 259.]

[Col. 1296D]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, bishop of Moravia, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have long since learned, through the manifestation of past acts, how great is your affection of charity toward us and the holy Roman Church. Therefore we love your person with true charity in the Lord, and, insofar as we can according to God, desire to honour you as a lover of religion. Moreover, our beloved son Daniel, provost of Prague, has humbly asked us on your behalf that, because of the many pressing matters confronting you, we might graciously release you from the summons to the council which, God willing, we shall celebrate in the middle of Lent. Although we desire your presence, we nevertheless wish, in accordance with the customary kindness of the Apostolic See, graciously to accede to your requests. We therefore release your brotherhood from the summons to the aforesaid council.

Furthermore, because we have need of your discernment, it pleases us that you present your welcome presence to us as soon as it may be expedient for you, so that we may enjoy one another’s mutual and sweet conversation. We also ask that you remember us in your prayers, as indeed you do, and that we thus assist one another before God by mutual intercessions, so that the charity joined here in Christ may prepare for us, through his grant, one common dwelling and joy in the kingdom of our Father. [Col. 1297B]

Given at Trier, on the fifteenth Kalends of January.

## CCXLII. He receives the church of Saint Alban at Basle into his protection and confirms each of its possessions by name. (20 December 1147.)

[Schoepflin, *Alsatian Diplomata*, I, 231, from the paper cartulary of the monastery of Saint Alban at Basle, preserved in the Huber Library at Moutier.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons HESSON, prior of Saint Alban at Basle, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular [Col. 1297C] life, in perpetuity.

Just as no effect is to be granted to those asking for unjust things, so the petition of those asking what is lawful and just ought not to be delayed. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests; we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid church, in which you are devoted to divine service; and we strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions or goods the same church now justly and canonically possesses—especially those which Burchard, bishop of Basle of good memory, granted to your church and confirmed by his writing—or may in the future acquire, God favouring it, through grants of popes, gifts of kings [Col. 1297D] or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and undiminished for you and your successors. We have considered the following to be specified by their proper names: in the city itself, the parish churches of Saint Alban and Saint Martin, as bounded by the river Persicus; the church of Buozsensheim with its appurtenances; in the settlement called Lower Basle, the church with its appurtenances; your right in the church of the settlement called Hemps, and half of that settlement with its appurtenances; the church of Haegendorf; the church and villages of Appenwillare with their appurtenances; Loerrach, with its church and all [Col. 1298A] its appurtenances, in vineyards, fields, meadows, and woods; the church of Howingen; the church of Candro; the church of Enschossingen with all their appurtenances; the wood situated beside Saint Alban; mills on the bank of the Birs with adjoining meadows; tithes in the settlements called Huningen, Rinwilr, Amparingen, Lechdencoven, Rabchensheim, Gueswibre, and Sierentze; in the settlement called Westhalda, one manor with vineyards; Morswilr, Usheim, Ramspach, Michelnbach, Oberwilrr, Bratella, Gelterchingen, Dürnen, Hoeltein, Meten, Bladoltzeim, Biningen, Machstatt, and Vettingen, with all their appurtenances.

[Note: [Col. 1297] Today Blozheim. The remaining places, situated around Basle in Sundgau, Breisgau, and Augstgau, have in part been destroyed.]

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain possessions taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations. Rather, let all things be preserved whole for the beneficial use of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If, in future, any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly attempts rashly to contravene this charter of our constitution, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not make amendment by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour; let them know themselves guilty before the divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let them be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus [Col. 1298C] Christ, Redeemer; and at the last judgment let them be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve what is right for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good works and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

Given at Trier, through the hand of Guy, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the thirteenth Kalends of January, in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1147 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Eugenius III.

## CCXLIII. He rebukes T[heobald], bishop of Verona, because, without restoring the canons’ possessions, he had lifted the interdict from the city. He commands him to ensure their restoration. (22 December 1147.)

[Ughelli, *Italia sacra*, V, 786.]

[Col. 1298D]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother T., bishop of Verona, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We remember having often instructed you by other letters to administer canonical justice against those invaders who violently and unlawfully hold the goods and possessions of our sons, the canons of the Church of Verona. As their repeated complaint indicates, this has not yet been carried into effect; hence we are greatly astonished and deeply grieved. For you yourself had prohibited the celebration of divine offices in the city of Verona because of the offences of certain of your parishioners, but, contrary to our command—which we had sent you on this subject, namely, that you were firmly to keep this same interdict in force until fitting satisfaction had been rendered—you lifted it although no satisfaction had been made. [Col. 1299A]

Since we cannot and ought not fail the aforesaid canons in their justice, we command and enjoin you by repeated letters that you strictly admonish E., P. and his son, Ald., Recl., Anf., Reg., Odel., and Saccetus to restore in full the goods of the aforesaid church and henceforth desist from molesting it. If they refuse to do so within thirty days after receiving this letter, restrain them by canonical censure, setting aside every pretext, and do not release them from the sentence which you have canonically pronounced against them until they have made satisfaction. [Col. 1299B]

Given at Trier, on the eleventh Kalends of January.

## CCXLIV. To P[eregrinus], patriarch of Aquileia.—He writes that he is astonished that the patriarch absolved certain knights excommunicated for occupying possessions of the Church of Verona. He commands him to compel them to restore what they took. (22 December 1147.)

[Ughelli, *Italia sacra*, VI, 786.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother P., patriarch of Aquileia, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We are called by the duty of our office to provide, with the care of paternal solicitude, for Churches situated near and far. It has been reported to us that you have absolved G. C., his son A., and A.’s brother—men who had been bound by the bond of excommunication because they had long dared to possess unjustly and violently the goods of our sons, the canons of the Church of Verona—without satisfaction having been rendered. We greatly marvel at this. We do not believe that your prudence is ignorant how grave this is and how worthy of correction. Although we could with justice restore them to the same sentence, we have nevertheless decided for the present to defer this, wishing to show deference to you.

But because we do not wish the aforesaid church to be defrauded of its justice, we command you by the authority of this letter strictly to admonish the knights named above to leave in free and peaceful possession to the aforesaid canons the goods of the Church of Verona which they unjustly hold. [Col. 1299D] If they prove contemptuous within thirty days after you receive this letter, restore them to the same sentence; nor are they to be absolved until they restore to the Church of Verona all that they have taken away.

Given at Trier, on the eleventh Kalends of January.

## CCXLV. To Henry the Younger, king of the Romans.—He commends his zeal for the Church and wishes him every prosperity. (1147.)

[Martène, *Amplissima Collectio*, II, 231.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son in Christ HENRY the Younger, king of the Romans, [Col. 1300A] son of the illustrious King Conrad, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Considering your father’s devotion toward blessed Peter and the holy Roman Church, and keeping before the eyes of our heart the fact that, pierced by divine inspiration, he has taken up the sign of life and has courageously and powerfully girded himself to subdue the enemies of the faith and enlarge the Catholic Church, we embrace you, as it were our own bowels, with special affection; and in your father’s absence we are in some measure consoled as we behold his image in you. Therefore we have received your envoys and letter with paternal kindness, and we have been, and are, pleased that, though still in tender years, you have declared in your letter that you stand ready to render obedience to the Roman Church and to us. [Col. 1300B] We hope that, as your age increases, the steadfast sincerity of your devotion and service toward the Apostolic See will grow yet more earnestly.

Therefore we pray the supreme mercy of almighty God that in his ineffable goodness he may advance your days and deeds from good to better, and, by a continual increase of well-being, may make your person happily prosper. For our part, in whatever we can do without detriment to God’s honour and that of his Church, we shall endeavour to provide you, as a most beloved son, with aid and counsel.

## CCXLVI. To Anselm, bishop of Havelberg.—That he should ensure the restoration of estates of Corvey which his people had usurped. (About 1147.)

[Martène, *Amplissima Collectio*, II, 211.]

[Col. 1300C]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother A., bishop of Havelberg, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Our beloved son Abbot Wibald and the monks of Corvey have complained to us that Poppo of Blanchenburg, his son C., and your canon R. have violently taken from them and unjustly retain all the revenues which they possessed at Cropensteden and Gruningue. Therefore, since by the duty of our office we neither wish nor ought to fail them in their justice, we command and enjoin you by apostolic letters that, if their complaint rests on truth, you strictly admonish those invaders to restore in full what they have taken. Otherwise, within two months [Col. 1300D] after receiving this letter, administer canonical justice against them.

## CCXLVII. To Reinher, canon of Havelberg.—That he should restore twenty holdings which he had taken from the monastery of Corvey. (About 1147.)

[Ibid., 212.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to REINHER, canon of Havelberg, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have received the complaint of our beloved sons Wibald and the monks of Corvey that at the village of Cropensteden you have unjustly and violently taken twenty *mansi* from them. Since we do not believe you are ignorant how severely those who despoil ecclesiastical goods must be punished, we command and enjoin you by apostolic letters to restore in full both the aforesaid *mansi* which you seized and the other goods taken therefrom. If you prove contemptuous, we wish you to know that we shall not let the matter pass without severe punishment if a repeated outcry concerning the aforesaid injury reaches us. [Col. 1301A]

## CCXLVIII. Privilege for the monastery of Laach. (20 January 1148.)

[Gunther, *Codex diplomaticus Rheno-Mosellanus*, I, 303.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GISLEBERT, abbot of the monastery of Laach, situated in the diocese of Trier, and his brethren, [Col. 1301B] present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

A pious request must be fulfilled by a corresponding act of will, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth worthily and the benefit sought may undoubtedly acquire strength. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests; we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service; and we strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing.

First, indeed, we decree that the monastic order in that place shall be inviolably observed for all future time according to the Rule of blessed Benedict and the norm of the monastery of Cluny. [Col. 1301C] We also decree that whatever possessions or goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future acquire, the Lord granting it, through grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and undiminished for you and your successors. We have considered the following to be specified by their proper names: the place itself called Laach, in which the said monastery is known to have been founded especially by the nobleman Henry, Count Palatine, and his wife Adelaide, free from every yoke and secular authority; the church of Saint Dionysius at Croth; moreover, the villages called Bella, Reida, Alchena, Willeberge, Croht, and Beytendorp with all their appurtenances, bestowed upon you by the aforesaid Henry. That estate of Beitendorp, namely, having been wrongfully removed from the church’s right by the plunder of certain persons, our beloved son Conrad, king of the Romans, in the first year of his reign, by the just judgment of his princes, restored to your church and confirmed in perpetuity by his privilege and by the ban of our venerable brethren Theodowin, bishop of Santa Rufina, Albero, archbishop of Trier, Arnold, archbishop of Cologne, and others present. [Col. 1301D] The Salic tithe of Metschet, which Rembald of Isenburg wholly surrendered to you in our presence; four *mansi* at Croth and Meilen, at Braant, from the gift of Count Palatine Sigefrid; one *mansus* at Croth, granted to you by the nobleman William, Count Palatine, and his mother Gertrude, with the consent of the knight Robert, who held it from them in fief; the allod at Masella called Neuin, with its appurtenances, which Bertram, abbot of Saint-Arnulf at Metz, with the consent of our venerable brother Stephen, bishop of that city, and of his chapter, sold to your monastery for a suitable price.

The allod at Evernac, given to you by the knight John and his wife Matilda; vineyards at Winengen and Leia, given to you by Pugner and other faithful persons; vineyards at Andernac, Ludestorp, and Amerstein, given to you by Frederick, archbishop of Cologne, of revered memory; an estate at Wadenheim, given by Enbrico; the manor of Budenarde, given by Henry and his brothers, and by Garner and his brothers; fields and vineyards in Luzinc and Lower Menedich; fields in Upper Menedich given by Theoderic and his brother; [Col. 1302B] the manor at Chella, conveyed by Drudewin and partly redeemed by payment; the allod at Pumero, given by the knight Robert and Hermann; the manor of Hadenhaga, with serfs and forests, given by Meimgot, Ernest, and Erluin; a *mansus* at Aldendorp, given by Albert; the allod at Loe from the alms of the knight Emicho; likewise the allod at Glensa from the alms of Folcold; at Gerchenrodee, two *mansi* from the alms of Count Hermann; vineyards at Cuchemo and a *mansus* at Wilre from the gift of Theoderic; vineyards at Clotena from the gift of Hermann and Hartmud; vineyards at Mudena; a *mansus* given by the knight Rodulf; two *mansi* granted for the soul of Demodis, likewise two given for the soul of Sibevuir; the allod at Caldine, given by Frederick; half a *mansus* and half a share of a lake, given by Count Gerard; the allod at Nederusen, the allod at Mesenhim, and at Bleida, given by Folcnand, Richin, Radulf, and Frowin; the allod at Diffindale, the allod at Franchen, and the allod at Staphela. Nor shall anyone have power, etc., and to appoint another. We therefore decree, etc. Amen, amen, amen. [Col. 1302C]

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. I, Herubald, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul. I, Hugh, cardinal priest of the title in Lucina.

Given at Trier, through the hand of Guy, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the thirteenth Kalends of February, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1147 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III. [Col. 1302D]

## CCXLIX. He receives the monastery of Saint Peter in the Black Forest into protection and confirms its goods. (27 January 1148—at Trier.)

[Dumgé, *Regesta Badensia*, 1137.]

## CCL. He receives the monastery of Heilsbronn into protection and confirms its possessions. (28 January 1148—at Trier.)

[Hocker, *Supplement to the Heilsbronn Antiquities*, II, 74.]

[Col. 1303A]

## CCLI. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Eucharius at Trier. (6 February 1148.)

[Gunther, *Codex diplomaticus Rheno-Mosellanus*, I, 308.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons BERTULF, abbot of the monastery of Saint Eucharius, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

The care of the universal Church has been entrusted to us by God, the provider of all good things, in order that we may love religious persons and strive by every means to promote the form of religious life pleasing to God. For no service is ever rendered acceptably to God unless it proceeds from the root of charity and is preserved by the purity of religious life. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously grant your just requests; and we receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by God’s favor, acquire through grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors.

Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: the cell of Blessed Mary at Boppard; the estate of Wilmar with its appurtenances; the churches of Greater and Lesser Wilmar and of Vilre, Upper Brichen, and Armvurt, with their tithes; the estate of Benizenrode with its appurtenances; the church of Niederberg with its tithes and appurtenances; the estate of Pulch with its appurtenances; the estate of Cobesa with its appurtenances; the estate of Trittenheim with its church, tithes, and appurtenances; the estate of Uren with its appurtenances; Longasura and the church of the same village with its tithes and appurtenances; the estate of Cretenach with its church, tithes, and appurtenances; the estate of Pelling with its church and appurtenances; the estate of Hemetre with its church and appurtenances; the estate of Lampaide with its church, fishing rights, and appurtenances; the village of Mamon with its church; the village of Halesfeld with its church; the village of Palzela with its church and tithes; Nannicho with its church and tithes; Sencicho with its church and tithes and all their appurtenances; the church of Saint Gervasius within the city wall, with its tithes; the village of Saint Eucharius with its church and all the jurisdiction of that village, except the toll on the feast-day of Saint Eucharius.

Moreover, we likewise confirm for you the liberties or immunities granted to your monastery by the decision of bishops and kings and established by their written instruments. We also forbid anyone who has fled within the precincts of your monastery to be seized, or for anyone to dare lay hands upon him. When you, the present abbot of that place, or any one of your successors dies, no one shall be placed over it by any craft of deception or violence, except one whom the brothers, by common consent or by the sounder part of the brothers’ counsel, shall provide to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict. We therefore decree, etc.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Herumbald, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul. I, Hugh, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina. I, Giselbert, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Mark. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Lawrence and Damasus. I, Heribert, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia. I, Julius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus. I, Wiclodent, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Pudentiana. I, Oddo, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. I, John, cardinal of the title of Saint Mary the New. [Col. 1304C] I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Angelus. I, Hyacinth, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin.

Given at Trier through the hand of Guido, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the eighth day before the Ides of February, in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1146 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius.

CCLII. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Mary at Lonnich. (A.D. 1148, February 13.)

[Ibid., p. 306.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons FOLMAR, abbot of the church of Saint Mary at Lonnechin, [Col. 1304D] and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

Since without the observance of true religion neither the unity of charity can endure nor service acceptable to God be offered, it is fitting for apostolic authority to love religious persons and fortify their places with pious protection. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously grant your just requests; and, following in the footsteps of our predecessor Pope Innocent of blessed memory, we receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and of ourselves the church of Blessed Mary at Lonnechin, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present document.

First, indeed, we decree that the canonical order established in your church according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine shall be observed there inviolably for all time. Further, whatever possessions or goods the same place now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by God’s favor, acquire through grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: namely, the court at Mendich with its appurtenances; the estate at Minchelue with its chapel and appurtenances.

We further forbid your church to have any advocate other than the Archbishop of Trier for the time being. We likewise confirm whatever of his own right the aforesaid archbishop has granted to your church in the estates of Valendra and Adenroda. When you, the present abbot of that place, or any of your successors dies, no one shall be placed over it by any craft of deception or violence, except one whom the brothers, by the common counsel of religious men of the same order or by the sounder part of the counsel, shall provide to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of Blessed Augustine.

No brother, after having made his profession there, may leave that cloister without the consent of the abbot and the whole community; and no one may dare retain a departing brother without common letters of authorization. From the produce which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or from the feed of your animals, no one may presume to exact tithes from you. We therefore decree, etc.

[Col. 1305C] Given at Trier through the hand of Guido, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the Ides of February, in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1147 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

CCLIII. To the priests, clerics, and laypersons established throughout the parishes of Ahr and Zülpich. (A.D. 1148, February 13.)

[GUNTHER, *Codex diplomaticus Rheno-Mosellanus*, I, p. 339.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the priests and others, both clerics and laypersons, established throughout the parishes of Ahr and Zülpich: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1305D] The dispute which was being litigated between our beloved sons G., provost of Bonn, and Fred., provost of Saint George, concerning the visitation of the deanery, we have concluded by judicial sentence, after hearing and diligently examining the arguments of both parties and sufficiently inspecting their documentary proofs, with the counsel of our brethren. Since, therefore, we are bound by the office entrusted to us to preserve each person’s right, by these present letters we command you, and in commanding enjoin you, to receive the aforesaid G. honorably and to render him obedience and reverence as your archdeacon. For, in accordance with the general custom of the Church, we have granted him full power, by right of archdeaconry, to visit and make circuits through your parishes belonging to him by right.

Given at Trier, on the Ides of February.

CCLIV. To the monks of Corvey.—He exhorts them to show humble reverence to Abbot Wibald. (A.D. 1148.)

[MARTÈNE, *Amplissima Collectio*, II, 229.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved monks of Corvey: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We remember that in other letters we commanded you to obey our beloved son Wibald with due humility as your abbot. When he recently came to us, we received him with paternal kindness; and we carefully urged him in those matters which pertain to restoring religious observance in your monastery [Col. 1306B] and preserving it. Therefore, as we send him back to you with the favor of the Apostolic See and the support of our letters, we command, admonish, and exhort your whole community in the Lord to love and honor him as good and humble sons, to render him the fitting reverence due to your shepherd, and to assist him manfully and faithfully in recovering and retaining the possessions and goods of Corvey monastery. For we love this same abbot with paternal affection and are willing, in matters in which we can act according to God, to hear him favorably.

CCLV. To Henry, bishop of Liège.—That he restrain those who plunder the goods of Stavelot monastery. (A.D. 1148.)

[Ibid.]

[Col. 1306C]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, bishop of Liège: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We do not believe that your prudence is unaware with what severity those who seize ecclesiastical goods ought to be punished. A complaint of the brethren of the church of Stavelot has reached us: Eustace, one of your parishioners, has violently taken their goods on the estate of Turnines and by no means ceases from harassing them. Macharius of Suingeis also, together with certain other arsonists and robbers assisting him, does not fear to afflict the same church by plunder [Col. 1306D] and other means. Since the reckless audacity of robbers must be more forcibly resisted with the spiritual sword, by the authority of these present letters we command you strictly to compel both the aforesaid Eustace and the other robbers to restore what they have taken and henceforth cease from harassing them. If they prove contemptuous, then within forty days after you have received these present letters, setting aside any dilatory evasion, you shall administer canonical justice upon them.

CCLVI. To the abbot and brethren of Saint Benedict beyond the Po.—He commands them to render obedience and reverence to the Abbot of Cluny, and that they may not elect an abbot for themselves without his authority, command, counsel, and consent. (A.D. 1148, February 15.)

[*Bullarium Cluniacense*, 61.]

[Col. 1307A]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons W., abbot of Saint Benedict, and his brethren: greeting and apostolic blessing.

After we had repeatedly received the complaint of our beloved son Peter, abbot of Cluny, and his brethren, that you had withheld from them those rights granted to them in the monastery of Saint Benedict by our predecessors, both concerning the election of the abbot and other matters, and confirmed in their writings; and that, contrary to the tenor of the privileges of the Apostolic See, you had elected an abbot, we summoned both parties before us. We carefully heard the arguments and allegations on both sides, studied the documents attentively, and deliberated long concerning them with our brethren. From these we learned that the care of the Church of Cluny, by the favor of divine clemency, has brought great increase to the monastery of Saint Benedict in both temporal and spiritual matters.

Accordingly, wishing to preserve unimpaired the privileges of the Church of Cluny, we command that you, Abbot William, before the first feast of the blessed Apostles Peter and Paul, visit the monastery of Cluny with honorable and prudent persons from among your brethren, as was commanded by our predecessors Innocent and Lucius of blessed memory, and humbly render honor and reverence to our beloved son Peter, abbot of Cluny. [Col. 1307C] If, burdened by illness, you cannot accomplish this yourself, you shall accomplish it through the better persons of that monastery.

When the abbot of that place dies, the brethren of Saint Benedict shall approach the Abbot of Cluny, announce to him the death of their abbot, and with due humility seek from him authority, command, counsel, and consent concerning the election of an abbot from their own community, if a suitable man is found, or from the Cluniac congregation. When this has been done, they shall canonically elect an abbot for themselves; and the person elected shall be presented to the Abbot of Cluny and promise him obedience. Whenever the Abbot of Cluny wishes to come in person, or through his vicar, to the aforesaid monastery of Saint Benedict, he shall be received and treated reverently by you; [Col. 1307D] he shall diligently attend to the observance of religious life and freely and regularly correct whatever he finds among them requiring correction.

Given at Sarranium, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of March.

CCLVII. He receives the monastery of Saint Disibod under protection and confirms its goods and privileges. (A.D. 1148, February 18—Metz.)

[JOANN., *Tabularium spicilegium*, 127.]

CCLVIII. Privilege for the monastery of Bonifagetensis (Bonfail). (A.D. 1148, February 22.)

[HUGO, *Annals of Prémontré*, I, Preface, p. 309.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved [Col. 1308A] sons GUNTHER, abbot of Bonfail, and his brethren, present and future: in perpetuity.

It is fitting readily to grant consent to religious desires, so that faithful devotion may obtain a swift effect. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously grant your just requests; and we receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid place in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the same place now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by God’s favor, acquire through grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors.

Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: whatever right you have in Bonfail, namely in fields and meadows, woods and waters, with mills; the land of Bainvilli, as Hugh held it. Furthermore, from the produce which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or from the feed of your animals, no one may presume to exact tithes from you.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid place, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or wear it down by any vexations; but that all things be preserved intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop being preserved. If any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowingly attempting rashly to act against this page of our constitution, after a second or third warning fails to make amends by fitting satisfaction, he shall be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; he shall know himself guilty before righteous judgment of the wrong perpetrated; he shall be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and at the final judgment shall be subject to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

[Col. 1308D] I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Oddo, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Veil. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Prison. I, Humbald, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Lawrence and Damasus. I, Hugh, cardinal priest of the title in Lucina. I, Jordan, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna.

Given at Verdun through the hand of Guido, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the eighth day before the Kalends of March, in the year 1147 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

CCLIX. Bull to the captains, vassals of Nonantola monastery.—That they defend the monastery against its enemies. (A.D. 1148, February 26.)

[TIRABOSCHI, *History of the Abbey of Nonantola*, II, 263; copy in the Roman codex—Nonantola.]

[Col. 1309A]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, all captains who are vassals of the monastery: greeting and apostolic blessing.

How greatly the monastery of Nonantola has flourished in spiritual as well as temporal matters is sufficiently well known throughout all regions of Lombardy. But, as sins have demanded, it has been diminished in both respects by the persecution of wicked men. Since you are bound to be faithful to that monastery on account of the goods of the same monastery which you enjoy, you are to help it against the vexations of evil men [Col. 1309B] and defend it against the persecutions of its enemies by whom it is oppressed.

Given at Verdun, on the fourth day before the Kalends of March.

CCLX. Privilege for the church of the Holy Apostles on Mont Cornillon at Liège. (A.D. 1148, March 16.)

[HUGO, *Annals of Prémontré*, I, Proofs, p. 275.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons LUKE, abbot of the church of the Holy Apostles situated on Mont Cornillon near Liège, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

[Col. 1309C] Whenever that is requested of us which is recognized as befitting religion and uprightness, it is fitting that we grant it with willing mind and offer suitable support to the desires of petitioners. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, following in the footsteps of our predecessor Pope Innocent of blessed memory, we graciously grant your just requests; and we receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid church of the Holy Apostles, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the patronage of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions or goods the same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by God’s favor, acquire through grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors.

Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: in the city of Liège, twenty-five solidi which Obert, bishop of Liège of good memory, granted to be paid to you yearly from his toll; the house which Lambert of the Meuse gave you, with its granary beside the market of Liège; the house of Mary of Coir in the same market; seven stalls of sellers of both bread and *subterales* [a kind of baked good, uncertain]; a house outside the castle; the vineyard of Ralph near the bishop’s village; the land of Udelin, chamberlain of the aforesaid bishop; the land of Giselbert; the land of Illin with houses, gardens, and meadows; the land of Bovo the priest; the land of Frederick; [Col. 1310A] the land of John, his son; the land of John, son-in-law of the same Frederick; the land of the knight Godfrey in the village called Latin; the land which the aforesaid Lambert of the Meuse gave you; the land of Frederick the reeve and his wife Mabilia in the village called Holonia on the Jeker; and, in the village called Hastaples, the lands which Giselbert of the Island and his wife gave you; and what you possess in the village called Richen—in the church, in money-rents, arable land, woods, meadows, cultivated and uncultivated land; likewise, whatever you possess in the village called Mecheroul and in the cleared land called Roliers, in the place called Heis, or the court of Aufrid; the mill with the land that you hold there in the village called Guntheries, namely in the church of Blessed Peter [Col. 1310B] and Saint George, in tithe, money-rent, arable land, woods, meadows, pastures, cultivated and uncultivated land; in the village called Radenchen, a hospital house with its appurtenances, which Giselbert the knight granted to you; likewise daily use in the wood called Brues, or in another wood belonging to the court of Jupille, which our venerable brother Albero, bishop of Verdun, with the consent of his church granted you and confirmed by his document; the whole allod called Bofoith, in woods as well as meadows, pastures, cultivated and uncultivated lands, with the church situated in that allod, its tithe, and the endowment belonging to that church; the land which you hold in the village called Borsoith; one *mansus* of land which you possess between Hesbines and Halincurth, with its dependent household; the land of Walter, knight of Bassines, with its dependent household.

Furthermore, no one may dare alter your canonical rule and purpose of life according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine and the institution of the Church of Prémontré, or impose upon you the order of another profession. Nor may any of your brethren, after making profession there, leave that cloister without the permission of the abbot and his chapter; and no one may dare retain a departing brother. You shall receive the oil for the sick, consecrations of altars or churches, and ordinations of clerics from the diocesan bishop, if he enjoys the favor of the Apostolic See and is willing to provide these to you freely and without any exaction; [Col. 1310D] otherwise, you shall receive them from any Catholic bishop who, supported by our authority, grants what is requested. Moreover, we confirm for you by apostolic authority the freedom of your church, defined and established by privilege by Bishops Obert and Albero with the assent of the Church of Liège. We therefore decree, etc.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given at Reims through the hand of Guido, cardinal deacon and librarian of the holy Roman Church, on the fourth day before the Nones of May, in the sixth indiction, in the year 1147 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the third year of the episcopate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

CCLX. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Mary of Longpont. (A.D. 1148, March 17.)

[MULDRAC., *Chronicle of the Abbey of Longpont*, p. 26.]

[Col. 1311A]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons BALDWIN, abbot of the church of Saint Mary of Longpont, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetual memory.

Whenever that is requested of us which is recognized as befitting religion and uprightness, it is fitting that we grant it with willing mind and offer suitable support to the desires of petitioners. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously grant your just requests; [Col. 1311B] and we receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid monastery of Saint Mary, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions or goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by God’s favor, acquire through grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors.

Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: namely, the place itself called Longuspons, with all matters belonging to the altar-right of that place; and the entire holding of Gerard of Chrisiac, which he held at that same place in his own demesne, or another held from him in fee—except the wood called Caisnetus, in which he also granted a portion separated from the rest by established boundaries; and free rights of use in the remaining portion of the land called Maisniliorum. Also, whatever Adam Broslart, John of Colomella, Robert of Musy, and Gillebert Wacca are known to have held from that same Gerard; the land which you possess beside the grange of Longpont and beyond the stream of Saveria; the lands, woods, and pastures extending to the crest of the hill which you hold from the church of Saint John in vineyards near the city of Soissons, at the place called Pratella; the court and wine-cellar with their vineyards and appurtenances.

At Mount Rambaud: the grange and lands, [Col. 1311D] on the hill, and other sloping lands which they call *latera* (“slopes”), from the fishpond of Contris and the territory of Parrechi as far as the fishpond of the valley and the wood of Virgiac; and in the same wood, free rights of use; and all the other lands which you possess in the territory of Parrechi. At Dementart: the entire holding of Peter of Brana, granted to you free of him, his wife, and his sons through the hand of our venerable brother Goslen, bishop of Soissons. At Montegnetum: your court and grange with vineyards, lands, and their other appurtenances; the vineyard of Campellis which, through Peter, prior of Charity, you received in exchange from Walter, prior of Montineto. At Fontaine-Morte: the land given you by Roger Salvagius, namely thirteen *modiata* of free allod. In the district [Col. 1312A] of Noyon: the grange of Elenvalle; likewise the lands and woods which you possess with the land of Geoffrey Martel, and the meadows and pastures granted to you both by the same Geoffrey and by Hugh Furnarius and his wife; beside those same meadows, a court on the land of Hugh Furnarius, free from every exaction, and dwellings in that court for enclosing and keeping your animals. In the district of Vermandois, near Saint-Quentin: the grange of Murimont with the woods, holdings, and lands which you possess there; the fishery in the river Somme; likewise freedom throughout the land of the Count of Vermandois and the land of Enguerrand of Coucy, as it was granted to you by them.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or wear it down with any vexations; but that all things be preserved intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted. If any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter knowingly attempts rashly to act against this page of our constitution and, after a second or third warning, fails to make amends by fitting satisfaction, he shall be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; he shall know himself guilty before divine judgment of the wrong perpetrated; he shall be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and at the final judgment shall be subject to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place [Col. 1312C] may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum. I, Hubald, cardinal priest of Saint Praxedes. I, Oddo, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Lawrence and Damasus. I, Hugh, cardinal priest of the title in Lucina. I, Julius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus. [Col. 1312D] I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Angelus. I, John, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary. I, Hyacinth, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin.

Given at Reims through the hand of Hugh, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the tenth day before the Kalends of April, in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1148 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

CCLXII. He confirms the goods and privileges of the monastery of Benediktbeuern. (A.D. 1148, March 28.)

[*Monumenta Boica*, VII, 102.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GUALTER, abbot of Saint Benedict at Burin, [Col. 1313A] and his brethren: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We receive pastoral care in the governance of the Apostolic See from the supreme shepherd of all, in order that with paternal affection we may provide for the salvation of those subject to us and defend them from the oppression of aggressors by the protection of the Apostolic See. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, granting favorable consent to your petitions, we receive the aforesaid monastery of Saint Benedict under the protection of Blessed Peter and of ourselves, and strengthen it by the patronage of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions and goods your church now possesses through grants of popes, gifts of kings, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, [Col. 1313B] or may hereafter justly and canonically, by God’s favor, acquire, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors.

And because that monastery, formerly enriched with many possessions and riches, was despoiled by the needs and pressing affairs of the realm, as we have seen from the rescript of the letters of Lothair, Roman Emperor of illustrious memory, it pleased that emperor to grant it freedom and establish it immune from every injury or exaction. We therefore confirm that same freedom by apostolic authority and decree that it shall remain inviolate in perpetuity. Likewise, as that emperor decreed, no advocate shall be appointed there except one whom the abbot of that place chooses with the counsel of the brethren. If he extends his hand beyond his right to the goods of the Church contrary to the will of the abbot, then, in accordance with the tenor of the letters of the aforesaid emperor, the abbot shall have power to reject him. When you, the present abbot of that place, or any of your successors dies, no one shall be placed over it by any craft of deception or violence, except one whom the brothers, by common consent or by the sounder part of the brothers’ counsel, shall provide to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict.

No cleric or layperson, therefore, may lawfully rashly disturb that monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or burden it with any molestations; but all things shall be preserved intact for the benefit of those for whose governance [Col. 1313D] and support they were granted, the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop being preserved. If anyone hereafter knowingly attempts to act against the page of this our document and, having been warned, scorns to amend his presumption, he shall know himself guilty before the judgment to come of the wrong perpetrated and shall be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ. But may divine grace preserve those who observe it and make them sharers in His blessing.

Given at Reims through the hand of Guido, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the fifth day before the Kalends of April, in the eleventh indiction, in the year [Col. 1314A] 1148 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

CCLXIII. He confirms a judgment delivered by certain bishops between Henry, abbot of Hersfeld, and Otto, bishop of Halberstadt, concerning tithes. (A.D. 1148, March 29—Reims.)

[WENCK, *Hessian Territorial History*, charter 69.]

CCLXIV. To Moses, Archbishop of Ravenna.—Concerning his right with respect to confirmation of the election of the bishop of Piacenza. (A.D. 1148, March 29.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 665.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother MOSES, Archbishop of Ravenna: greeting [Col. 1314B] and apostolic blessing.

Because we trust in the devotion of your brotherhood, we have thought our circumstances should be communicated to you. For we and our brethren are safe by divine mercy; and after, with the Lord’s help, we celebrated a council concerning the Cisalpine provinces, corrected many abuses by apostolic grace, and established in that same council what had to be ordained for the honor of God, we intend to return to Italy.

Moreover, we neither deem it burdensome to your affection nor wish it to be unknown to you that, without prejudice to your right, we have confirmed by apostolic authority the election of the Church of Piacenza. We had already thought fit to warn you of this by our letters; and by these present letters we command you to appear before us at the next feast of Blessed Luke, with your records and arguments, so that we may examine that controversy more fully. The people of Piacenza, indeed, as they promised us, will come at the appointed time, prepared to obey our commands. For they asserted that, so long as Piacenza was deprived of a shepherd, there was no one who could act for that church in litigation. Moreover, both the church itself and the whole city were suffering innumerable losses.

Given at Reims, on the fourth day before the Kalends of April.

CCLXV. Privilege for the monastery of Lorsch. (A.D. 1148, March 29.)

[*Codex diplomaticus Laureshamensis*, I, 247.]

[Col. 1314D] EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons FOLINAND, abbot of Lorsch monastery, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

By the authority of the Apostolic See, over which by divine grace we preside, and by our duty, we are compelled to concern ourselves for the condition of all Churches and, that religious men may be able more freely to devote themselves to God’s service, to make salutary provision for their peace. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we mercifully grant your just petitions, receive the aforesaid monastery of Lorsch under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing; decreeing that whatsoever possessions, whatsoever goods, in cultivated or uncultivated lands, vineyards, meadows, woods, pastures, waters, mills, castles, villages, tenants, tithes, or other things, that same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, God being propitious, acquire by grant of pontiffs, bounty of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors.

[Col. 1315A] Moreover, we forbid that any ecclesiastical or secular person henceforth presume to demand, or in any way to harass the abbot of the same monastery concerning, the service of one hundred marks which your monastery had customarily paid every year to the king or emperor, and which our dearest son Conrad, King of the Romans, granted to that monastery and confirmed by the record of his own charter. Rather, as established by that king himself, the aforesaid monastery shall remain forever free and exempt from that service.

Upon the death of you, the present abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be placed over it by any artifice of fraud or violence, except one whom the brothers of the same monastery, by common consent, or the sounder part of the brothers, shall have judged fit to elect according to the fear of God and the Rule of Saint Benedict. You shall receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or churches, ordinations of clerics or monks, and the blessing of the abbot from the diocesan bishop, provided that he is Catholic, enjoys the favour of the Apostolic See, and is willing to confer these things freely and without any impropriety. [Col. 1315B] Otherwise, you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer, who, supported by our authority, may grant what is requested.

Therefore let no person whatsoever be permitted rashly to disturb the aforesaid monastery, remove its possessions, retain possessions removed, diminish them, or harass it with any molestations; but let all things be preserved intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose support and governance they were granted. If anyone hereafter, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, having been warned a second and third time, unless he correct his presumption by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; and let him know that he is answerable before the divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed, [Col. 1315D] that he is cut off from the most holy body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, and that at the last judgment he is subject to severe vengeance.

But let all who preserve what is right for that place have the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good conduct and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

SAINT PETER. SAINT PAUL. POPE EUGENIUS III. FARE WELL.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Octavianus, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in Carcere, have subscribed. [Col. 1316A] I, John, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary the New, have subscribed.

Given at Reims through the hand of Guy, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the fourth day before the Kalends of April, in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1148 of the Incarnation of the Lord, and in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### CCLXVI. Mandate to archbishops, bishops, etc., concerning restitution to be made to the monastery of Lorsch. (A.D. 1148, March 29.)

*[Codex diplomaticus Laureshamensis, I, 249.]*

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brothers, archbishops and bishops, in whose dioceses the properties of the monastery of Lorsch are situated: [Col. 1316B] greetings and apostolic blessing.

Your brotherhood is not unaware with how many possessions the monastery of Lorsch was once endowed, nor how richly it abounded through the donations of emperors; but, because sins have required it, it has been greatly diminished through many disturbances and the necessities of the realm. It therefore has great need of your aid, both that you may help maintain its possessions and defend them from the injuries of assailants. By these present letters, therefore, we command you strictly to admonish your parishioners who unjustly hold goods of the same monastery to restore them; and, should they refuse to do so, to administer canonical justice upon them.

Given at Reims, on the fourth day before the Kalends of April.

### CCLXVII. He confirms the privileges and possessions of the monastery of Maulbronn. (A.D. 1148, March 29.)

*[PETRI, Suevia ecclesiastica, p. 572.]*

[Col. 1316C]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons DIETHER, abbot of Maulbronn, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

A desire shown to concern the religious calling and the salvation of souls ought, God being its author, to be fulfilled without any delay. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we mercifully grant your just petitions; and we receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves, and fortify by the privilege of this present writing, the aforesaid place granted to you by our venerable brother Gunther, bishop of Speyer, together with [Col. 1316D] the adjoining fields, in which your monastery is situated. We decree that whatsoever possessions and goods that place now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, God being propitious, acquire by grants of pontiffs, bounty of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors. Furthermore, no one shall demand tithes from you upon the produce of your labour which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or upon the increase of your animals.

Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb [Col. 1317A] the aforesaid place, remove its possessions, retain possessions removed, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but that all things be preserved whole for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter violates this page of our constitution, or knowingly rashly attempts to act against it, then, having been warned a second and third time, unless he makes amends by fitting satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity he has committed; and let him be cut off from the most holy body and blood of God and our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer [Col. 1317B] and be subject, at the last judgment, to severe vengeance. But let all who preserve what is right for that place have the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good conduct and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Given at Reims through the hand of Guy, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the fourth day before the Kalends of April, in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1148 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### CCLXVIII. Privilege for the monastery of Helmesward [Helmershausen]. (A.D. 1148, March 30.)

*[SCHATEN, Annales Paderbornenses, I, 778.]*

[Col. 1317C]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved lovers: blessing and mercy in the true faith from God their Saviour.

As it is fitting and just that we should, by apostolic authority, provide for the community of the faithful with regard to the condition of temporal things and the hope of future things, so it is still more fully and perfectly equitable and salutary that we lend the ears of our kindness to the vows of the humble and the prayers of the meek. Therefore we make known, both to the present Church and to the generation to come, that while we presided over the general council at Reims and arranged matters concerning the peace of the Churches, the venerable abbot of the monastery of Helmesward, Conrad by name, [Col. 1317D] approached us with reverent devotion. He set forth to us briefly, as time permitted, matters concerning the condition, right, and liberty of his Church, and urgently and devoutly requested that we endorse upon the decrees of our predecessors the authority of our own privilege regarding these matters.

Accordingly, after deliberation, moved both by the generous liberality of the assembled Apostolic See and by the gracious intervention of our bishops—namely Henry of Mainz, [Minden?], Theobald of Bremen, [Thetmar of Verden?], Bernard of Hildesheim, likewise Bernard of Paderborn, and Wibald, prelate of the monastery of Stavelot—we mercifully grant these just petitions and receive the aforesaid Church, henceforth and forever, under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves.

[Col. 1318A] Therefore we establish and decree that no person whatsoever, of whatever order or rank, may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, remove its possessions, retain possessions removed, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but that whatever possessions and goods, whether in estates, revenues, or other things, it now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, God being propitious, acquire by the grant of pontiffs, bounty of kings, or offerings of the faithful, shall remain whole and unimpaired for those who serve God there and live according to rule. Let the brethren also have free power to choose an advocate useful to the affairs [lacuna]. Let that same monastery likewise, according to the ordinance of the Roman pontiffs, enjoy Roman liberty [lacuna], namely [the liberty] of Saint Benedict, free from every jurisdiction of the bishop in [Col. 1318B] whose diocese [lacuna], save only for holy orders or consecrations graciously [lacuna]. If any ecclesiastical or secular power should attempt to act against this page of our privilege, let it acknowledge itself guilty before divine judgment of [lacuna] fault; and unless it repent through satisfaction, let it be subject, under the bond of anathema, to severe vengeance. But whoever shall be guardian and observer of this our privilege shall not be harmed by the second death, but shall enjoy perpetual blessing and thanksgiving with God and the Lamb in the heavenly Jerusalem. Amen.

Given at Reims through the hand of Guy, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the third day before the Kalends of April, in the eleventh indiction.

### CCLXIX. Privilege confirming all the goods of the monastery of Altaich, or Lower Altaich, in the diocese of Salzburg. (A.D. 1148, March 30.)

*[HUND, Metropolis Salisburgensis, II, 27.]*

[Col. 1318C]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons CONRAD, abbot of the monastery of Saint Maurice at Altaich, and his brethren, present and future, professing the monastic life: in perpetuity.

Whenever a request is made to us which is recognized as consonant with reason and honour, it befits us to grant it with a willing spirit and to afford suitable assistance to the desires of the petitioners. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we mercifully grant your just petitions [Col. 1318D] and receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves, and fortify by the safeguard of this present writing, the aforesaid monastery in which you are devoted to divine service. We decree that whatever possessions and goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may hereafter, God being propitious, acquire by grants of pontiffs, bounty of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these, we have thought fit to specify in their own terms:
