namely, the churches of Zaja, Abbatisdorff, Grie, Chunezen, Cassen, Mynchendorff, Itrehoven, Puchoven, Wialtorf, Erlbac, Sinichengen, Munterte, Ingen, Ingoltestat, Otelingen, [Col. 1319A] Wilbac, Peringen, Usterlingen, Peirbach, Metmenhusen, Ibach, Suarza, Pfolingen, Palkingen, Suarza, Rorbach, Urbac, Loting, Tundorf, Aicha, Winchilgen, Regen, Mount Saint Godhard, Naszelbach, Heidofingen, Cella; Mount Saint Mary of Scoliunge; Runichenae, Tagmanpach, Winchingen, Hohenoe, Aespach with vineyards and a harbour; vineyards at Spizze, Scongerinen, Otheneshaim, Gerlochesperch, Willensingen, Mannendorf, Hofdorf, Ranvenstetten, Ranthingen, Casebalchesteinden, Kadingen, Adelboldingen, Asingen, Jallingen, Teuvelsperch; and whatever right you possess in Halla. Furthermore, we likewise confirm to you whatever goods you justly and canonically possess both in tithes and in dependants.

[Col. 1319B] Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, remove its possessions, retain possessions removed, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but that all things be preserved whole for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical reverence due to diocesan bishops. If any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter knowingly attempts to act against this page of our constitution, then, having been warned a second and third time, unless he makes amends by fitting satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; [Col. 1319C] let him know himself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity he has committed; and let him be cut off from the most holy body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, and be subject, at the last judgment, to severe vengeance. But let all who preserve what is right for that place have the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good conduct and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Octavianus, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in Carcere Tulliano, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Angelo, have subscribed. I, Hyacinth, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in [Col. 1319D] Cosmedin, have subscribed.

Given at Reims through the hand of Guy, cardinal of the Holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the third day before the Kalends of April, in the twelfth indiction, in the year 1149 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the fifth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### CCLXX. He commands [Peregrinus], patriarch of Aquileia, to order certain counts to pay the three hundred pounds owed to T[heobald], bishop of Verona, and to restore estates taken from the canons of Verona. (A.D. 1148, April–May.)

*[UGHELLI, Italia sacra, V, 786.]*

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother P., patriarch of Aquileia: greetings and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1320A] It has been reported to us that our venerable brother T., bishop of Verona, on account of the dispute being conducted between the counts of Runcho—namely Girard Graffus, Albert Surdus, and the son of Count Maleregolatus—and the canons of Verona, paid three hundred pounds in Veronese money to those canons on behalf of the counts. Yet those same counts, on whose behalf he paid, remain liable to those canons for certain estates which they despoiled from them. Since, therefore, by the Lord’s disposition we have been placed in the seat of justice in order that every person’s rights may be preserved through us, we command you by apostolic letters and under injunction that, by the oath through which they are bound to you, you firmly order the aforesaid counts to pay three hundred pounds to our aforesaid brother, the bishop of Verona, and to restore the estates [Col. 1320B] in their entirety to the canons. If they despise this command, restore them without delay to the same sentence of excommunication by which they were previously bound.

Given at Reims.

### CCLXXI. To Henry the Younger, King of the Romans.—He promises to provide for his aunt, the duchess of Poland. (A.D. 1148, April 1.)

*[MARTENE, Amplissima Collectio, II, 239.]*

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son in Christ HENRY the Younger, illustrious King of the Romans, son of Emperor Conrad: greetings and apostolic blessing.

We have received your letters and messengers with due kindness, and have carefully considered their prayers. For we love your person with true charity in the Lord and, mindful of our fatherly devotion, desire to honour you in those matters in which we are able to do so according to God. Therefore, concerning your aunt, for whom you have asked, we shall take care, God being the author, to make provision, so far as we can do so consistently with our honour, through our messenger whom we intend to send to those regions, with the clemency customarily shown by the Apostolic See. [Col. 1320C] But while you are still of boyish age, strive to apply yourself to good and honourable actions, so that your mother, the Holy Roman Church, may rejoice in your successes.

Given at Reims, on the Kalends of April.

### CCLXXII. To the German prelates.—That they should support the younger King Henry and assist him with their counsel and deeds. (A.D. 1148, April 1.)

*[Ibid.]*

[Col. 1320D]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brothers, archbishops and bishops, and beloved sons, abbots established throughout the German kingdom: greetings and apostolic blessing.

As your prudence plainly recognizes, our dearest son Conrad, King of the Romans, stirred by the ardours of divine love, has received the sign of the life-giving Cross and has girded himself manfully and mightily to overthrow the madness of idolaters and to extend the worship of the Christian name. Since we are debtors to all by virtue of our office, we ought nevertheless to be more especially and more earnestly solicitous for him. Therefore, by these present letters we exhort your brotherhood and, in exhorting, command you diligently and faithfully to support our dearest son Henry the Younger, [Col. 1321A] king, son of the illustrious Conrad, King of the Romans. In matters known to concern the honour of his father and the condition of the kingdom, so that peace may by the grace of almighty God be preserved entire among the peoples subject to him, give him aid and counsel whenever he seeks your assistance. For we do not wish him, under the protection of Blessed Peter during his father’s absence, to suffer in any way a loss or deficiency of his honour.

Given at Reims, on the Kalends of April.

### CCLXXIII. Privilege for the Church of Saint Mary of Cambrai. (A.D. 1148, April 1.)

*[LEGLAY, Glossaire du Cambrésis, cathedral collection, copy.]*

[Col. 1321B]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons HUGH, dean of the Church of Cambrai, and his brethren, present and future, to be canonically appointed: in perpetuity.

The principle of equity and justice persuades us to confer upon churches lasting security for their affairs and protections of unshaken strength. For it is not fitting that clerics called to the Lord’s portion should be troubled by the hostile vexations of evil men or wearied by the reckless assaults of anyone whatsoever. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we mercifully grant your just petitions, receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves the church of Saint Mary, Mother of God and Virgin, [Col. 1321C] in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatsoever possessions and goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, God being propitious, acquire by grants of pontiffs, generosity of kings, bounty of princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these, we have thought fit to specify in their own terms:

namely, Vileirs with its altar; three parts of Maerech with its altar; Unaing with its altar; the altar of Genlaing; the altar of Lissinis; and the freehold which Bishop Lietbert held in that same village; [Col. 1321D] the altar of Ogi and whatever the same bishop held in that [Col. 1322A] village; the altar of Yser; Risbercurt; Hahiercurt; Elneus; Fontanis; the altar of Sanctis; the altar of Burlun; the altar of Harmies; the altar of Ramincurt; the altar of Riolcurt; the altar of Hauraincurt; the altar of Felchires; the altar of Saint Brice, situated in the city of Tournai; the altar of Morceis; the altar of Hualdre; the altar of Chiuvrain; the altar of Dangre; the altar of Muntenni; the altar of Lestinis; the altar of Anderlert; the altar of Caing; and the altar of Maslines, with all their appurtenances.

> **Note:** [Col. 1321D] Vileirs: Villers-Pol; Maerech: Maresches; Unaing: Onnaing; Genlaing: Jenlain, on the little Rhonelle, arrondissement of Avesnes, canton of Le Quesnoy; Lissinis: Lessines in Belgium; Risbercurth: Ribécourt; Hahiercurt: Gualtercurth, a destroyed village; Elneus: Anneux; Fontanis: Fontaine-Notre-Dame; Sanctis: Sains-lez-Marquion; Burlun: Bourlon, canton of Marquion, Artois, but possessing a lordship dependent on the Cambraisis; Harmies: Hermies, Pas-de-Calais, canton of Bertincourt, Artois, with an enclave of the Cambraisis; Ramincurt: Rumaucourt, canton of Marquion; Riolcurt: Ruyaulcourt, canton of Bertincourt; Hauraincurt: Havrincourt, canton of Bertincourt; Felchires: Flesquières, arrondissement of Cambrai, canton of Marcoing; Morceis: Morchies, canton of Bertincourt, Pas-de-Calais; Hualdre: [Col. 1322D] name unknown; Chiuvrain: Quiévrain, now in the province of Hainaut, Belgium, formerly in the deanery of Bavai; Dangre: Angre; Muntenni: Montigny in the Cambraisis or Montigni-sur-Roc, Belgium, province of Hainaut, formerly in the deanery of Bavai; Lestinis: Estines, now in Belgium, province of Hainaut, a place celebrated for the two councils held there in the eighth century; Anderlert: Anderlecht, Belgium, province of Brabant; Caing, called Caym in other charters, is Chin, now a hamlet belonging to Ramegnies-Chin near Tournai, or else the neighbouring village of Kain. In a repertory of charters of the Church of Cambrai one reads: “Caym is a village near Tournai”; Maslines: Malines, now the seat of an archbishopric in Belgium.

Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, remove its possessions, retain possessions removed, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but that all things be preserved whole for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance [Col. 1322B] and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical justice of diocesan bishops. If any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowingly, rashly attempts to act against this page of our constitution, then, having been warned a second and third time, unless he makes amends by fitting satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty in judgment of the iniquity he has committed; and let him be cut off from the most holy body and blood of God and our Lord Jesus Christ. But let all who preserve what is right for that place have the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good conduct and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, [Col. 1322C] amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum. I, Ubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes. I, Gislebert, unworthy priest of the title of Saint Mark. I, Gindopsir, cardinal of the title of Saints Lawrence and Damasus. I, Hugh, cardinal priest of the title in Lucina Matrona. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Octavianus, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in [Col. 1322D] Carcere Tulliano. [Col. 1323A] I, G., cardinal deacon of Saint Angelo. I, John Paparo, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian. I, Hyacinth, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin.

Given at Reims through the hand of Guy, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the Kalends of April, in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1148 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Eugenius III.

### CCLXXIV. To Odo, duke of Burgundy.—He rebukes him for hostility to the Church of Vézelay. (A.D. 1148, April 3.)

*[MANSI, Councils, XXI, 657.]*

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved [Col. 1323B] son O., duke of Burgundy: greetings and apostolic blessing.

Since all authority comes from the Lord God, earthly princes and rulers of worldly peoples ought more earnestly to pursue what they recognize concerns God’s honour. Yet we have received a complaint against your person to the contrary. For it has been reported to us that you repeatedly trouble and harass the church of Saint Mary Magdalene and its people. We bear this all the more grievously because we love your person with more earnest charity and desire your salvation with due affection. Therefore, by these present letters, we command you not henceforth to presume to harass the said church and its people, lest a repeated outcry reach our ears. [Col. 1323C]

Given at Reims, on the third day before the Nones of April.

### CCLXXV. To Countess I. of Nevers.—He rebukes her for harassing those travelling to Vézelay. (A.D. 1148, April 3.)

*[MANSI, Councils, XXI, 662.]*

William, count of blessed memory, is said to have promised, in the presence of our venerable brother Hugh of Auxerre and our beloved son Bernard, abbot of Clairvaux, that neither he nor the people of his land would prevent merchants and others wishing to go to Vézelay from doing so. But now, as we have learned from the report of our beloved son Pons, abbot of Vézelay, you and your men prevent and harass those wishing to go there. [Col. 1323D] Therefore, by these present letters, we command your nobility not henceforth to presume to commit this inhumanity. If you do presume to do so, you should fear lest, through the prayers of blessed Mary, who loved the Lord greatly, you incur the indignation of almighty God.

Given at Reims, on the third day before the Nones of April.

### CCLXXVI. Privilege for the monastery of Affligem, diocese of Cambrai. (A.D. 1148, April 3.)

*[MIRAEUS, Diplomatic Works, I, 534.]*

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son GODESCALC, abbot of the monastery of Affligem, [Col. 1324A] and to his successors regularly appointed: in perpetuity.

A desire recognized as concerning the religious calling and the salvation of souls ought, God being its author, to be fulfilled without any delay. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Godescalc, we mercifully grant your just petitions. Following the example of our predecessors of holy memory, Paschal and Calixtus, Roman pontiffs, we receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves, and fortify by the privilege of this present writing, the monastery of Blessed Peter at Affligem, over which, God being the author, you are recognized to preside. We decree that whatsoever possessions and goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter [Col. 1324B] acquire, God being propitious, by grants of pontiffs, bounty of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these, we have thought fit to specify in their own terms:

the church of Ascha, free and exempt from the *personatus* and episcopal procuration; and whatever Count Henry of blessed memory, with the consent of his brother Godfrey, is known to have granted to the aforesaid monastery from his freehold of his own right; the church of Saint Peter at Trasna; the cell and church of Saint Andrew near Bruges; the cell and church of Saint Mary at Warvria; the cell and church of Saint Mary at Bornhem; the cell of Saint Mary at Uliederbecka with the churches of Lindenaet and Villebrinca; the church at Genappa, by gift of Countess Ida of Boulogne; [Col. 1324C] a freehold with lands and woods in the village of Genapha itself; the land which the aforesaid monastery holds at an annual rent from the church of Nivelles, and at Lanso and Anselo; the monasteries of nuns at Forest and Bigard; also the churches of Eschen, Hekelgem, Wiese, Herdinghem, Erembodenghem, Merchtene, Lenendecke, Meerbecka, Ossensele, Londersele, Lisele, Puersche, and Baesrode, with all their appurtenances, free from the *personatus*, saving only episcopal procurations; lands in England at Iderswerda, given by Aleidis, widow of Henry, king of the English; and gifts at Westernere, Uremdick, Frondic, and Pakenge; Beckarias [lacuna], by gift of Count Theoderic of Flanders and of Countess Clementia, wife of Count Robert; and the freeholds at [Col. 1324D] Zellecka, Cabbegem, and Getza.

Moreover, whatever exemption and liberty have been justly granted to that monastery by the bishops of Cambrai—Gerard, Odo, Burchard, and Nicholas—we likewise confirm to you. You shall receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or churches, and the ordination of monks to be advanced to holy orders, from the diocesan [lacuna] bishop, provided that he has the favour and communion of the Apostolic See and is willing to confer these things freely. Otherwise, you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer, who, indeed, supported by our authority, may grant what is requested.

Upon the death of you, now abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be placed over it by any artifice of fraud or violence, except one whom the brothers, by common consent, or the sounder part of the brothers, according to the fear of God and the Rule of Saint Benedict, elect either from their own community or, if necessary, from another. [Col. 1325A] We add also that the advocates of your monastery or of your churches shall not have power to substitute another person in their place in the advocacy, through whom the goods of that monastery or its churches may be dissipated.

Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, remove its possessions, retain possessions removed, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but that all things be preserved whole for the benefit in every way [Col. 1325B] of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical justice of diocesan bishops. If any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter knowingly attempts to act against this page of our constitution, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most holy body and blood of God and our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer; and let him be subject, at the last judgment, to severe vengeance. But let all who preserve what is right for that place have the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good conduct and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

[Col. 1325C] I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have signed.

Given at Reims through the hand of Guy, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the third day before the Nones of April, in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1148 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### CCLXXVII. He confirms the altars, possessions, and privileges of the abbey of Eename, of the Order of Saint Benedict, in the diocese of Mechelen. (A.D. 1148, April 3.)

*[MIRAEUS, Diplomatic Works, IV, 17.]*

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved [Col. 1326A] sons SNELLARD, venerable abbot of Eename, and his successors regularly appointed: in perpetuity.

Whenever a request is made of us which is recognized as befitting religion and uprightness, it is proper for us to grant it with willing mind and to afford suitable support to the desires of those who ask. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Snellard, abbot, we graciously assent to your just petitions; and, following in the footsteps of our predecessors Alexander and Paschal, popes of Rome of blessed memory, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the monastery of Saint Saviour, over which, by God’s agency, you preside, together with the village adjoining it and all else belonging to it, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. [Col. 1326B] We decree that whatever possessions and goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, God favouring it, by grants of popes, gifts of princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have judged the following to be specified by their proper names:

In the diocese of Cambrai: the church of Saint Lawrence and Saint Vedastus [Note: [Col. 1325D] The church of Saint Lawrence is in Upper Eename, where the abbey is situated. The church of Saint Vedastus is in Lower Eename.]; the pasture of the hill adjoining those churches. In the new borough near Oudenaarde, the cell of Saint Mary, with its free parish and the churches belonging to it, namely Edelar [Note: [Col. 1325D] Today Edelaer, Leupeghem, Volckegen, and Horenbeca of Saint Mary are villages of the diocese of Mechelen in the neighbourhood of Oudenaarde.], Lupeghem, Folkenghem with the church of Saint Mary of [Col. 1326C] Upper Horenbeka; the church of Cervia [Note: [Col. 1325D] Cervia, Chievre, an ancient barony and small town of Hainaut, one mile from Ath, renowned for the chapel of the Virgin and for miracles.] with the male and female serfs belonging to it; the entire village of Helbeka [Note: [Col. 1325D] Helbeka, today Helbeque, a village between the towns of Ath and Enghien in Hainaut.] with its church and all its appurtenances; the church of Upper Bracla [Note: [Col. 1325D] Upper Bracla, in the vernacular Opbrakel, a village in the county of Aalst, on the border of Hainaut, in the deanery of Geraardsbergen.]; the church of Wenlines [Note: [Col. 1325D] Wenlides, today Weldene on the River Scheldt, in the deanery of Ronse.]; the church of Cimbersaca [Note: [Col. 1325D] Cimbersaca, today Semmersake on the River Scheldt [Col. 1326D], near Gavere.]; the church of Melcines [Note: [Col. 1326D] Melcines, Melsene on the River Scheldt, subject to the diocese of Ghent.]; the church of Morttella [Note: [Col. 1326D] Morttela, Moortzele, a village in the deanery of Oordegem.] with its dependencies; the church of Boucla of Saint Bavo [Note: [Col. 1326D] Boucla of Saint Bavo, today Boucla of Saint Blaise, in the deanery of Ronse.]; the church of Saint Mary at Tongra [Note: [Col. 1326D] Tongra of Saint Mary in Hainaut, near Chievre, a place distinguished by miracles of the Mother of God; nearby is Tongra of Saint Martin. Both are in the archdiocese of Cambrai.]; the right which it has in Saint Martin’s of Tongra; the church of Bassilgi and half of that same village.

In the diocese of Tournai: the church of Harrizam [Note: [Col. 1326D] Harrizam is cited incorrectly; it is Handsaeme, a parish of the diocese of Bruges under the deanery of Thorout, where the abbot of Eename to this day enjoys the right of patronage and the tithes, as also in the following village.]; the church of Merch [Note: [Col. 1326D] Merch is incorrect; it is Cortemarcke, in the diocese of Bruges, deanery of Thorout.].

In the diocese of Arras: two parts of the tithe [Col. 1327A] of the harvests of Assilogiae, Wlpra, and Willerval; in Flanders, four sheep-runs [Note: [Col. 1327C] *Bercaria*: a place suitable for keeping sheep, though distinct from a sheepfold; also a kind of estate with a fixed quantity of land. See Du Cange, *Glossary of Latin*.] at the place called Paradise; two parts of the freehold of Bossunt above the River Scheldt; the manor of Buri with its freehold; the manor of Geron with the land of Gerard the chamberlain; the manor of Astruis; and the freehold of Rugis.

Moreover, whatever liberty and immunity has reasonably been bestowed upon that monastery by bishops or princes, we likewise confirm to you. Upon your death, now abbot of that place, or that of any of your successors, no one shall be set over it through any device of fraud or force, except one whom the brethren, by common consent, or by the sounder counsel of the brethren, in accordance with the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Benedict, have elected from their own community or, if necessary, from another. [Col. 1327B] We also add that the advocate of your monastery shall have no power to substitute another person in his place in the advocacy, through whom the goods of the aforesaid monastery may be dissipated. We also decree that burial in that place shall be free, so that no one may obstruct the devotion of those who have resolved to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict, while the right of the mother church is preserved. If, however, the see of Cambrai is vacant, or—God forbid—does not have a Catholic bishop, you may receive the sacraments of consecration from any Catholic bishop.

If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not make amends by suitable satisfaction, [Col. 1327C] let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and honour, recognize himself or herself as guilty before divine judgment for the wrong committed, be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and our Lord Jesus Christ, and be subject to strict vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who uphold what is just for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good works and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Given at Reims, through the hand of Guy, cardinal-deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the third day before the Nones of April, in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1148 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

CCLXXVIII. He receives the Church of Włocławek into his faith and protection, and confirms the boundaries of the bishopric and diocese of Włocławek established by Aegidius, bishop of Tusculum, and Bolesław, duke of Poland. [Note: [Col. 1327C] Copied from a parchment original preserved in a private archive in the kingdom of Galicia. The original itself is written on parchment; the seal, commonly called the Fisherman’s Ring, has been broken off. This bull was printed in Damalewicz’s work, *Lives of the Bishops of Włocławek*, p. 32, and was then reprinted in Hartknoch’s work, *Preussische Kirchengeschichte*, p. 175, no. 17. Yet it was always, as is now evident, copied from a faulty exemplar; consequently some historians cast doubts upon its authenticity. The very learned editor of *Preussische Sammlung* was thereby given an opportunity to conjecture most ingeniously concerning the bull itself—for that man’s conjectures are confirmed by the discovery of the original bull. All this may be gathered from the following notes.] (Year 1148, April 4.)

[Leon Rzyszczewski, *Codex Diplomaticus Poloniae*, II, I, 1.]

[Col. 1328B]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother WARNER [Note: [Col. 1327D] In the list of bishops of Cuiavia for the year 1148 we find no Bishop Warner—incorrectly called Werner by all historians—but only Świdger, the distinguished Grzymała. This register caused Damalewicz some difficulty, which, lacking critical skill, he did not resolve. He therefore repeats the error he found; and, conjecturing that the date when the bull was written had been falsely assigned, follows Długosz in assigning Bishop Warner the twelfth place in the chronological series under the year 1171. For he states on p. 131: “Rudger was followed by Verner, according to Długosz, in the year 1171”; but since the name of Verner is expressly found in the privilege of the Church of Włocławek in 1148, his episcopate must be referred altogether to earlier times. The most learned author of *Preussische Sammlung* nearly resolves this knot in these words: “If the document is correct, Werner would have become bishop in the year 1148 or 1147.” Since, in our view, the authenticity of this bull is beyond doubt, we can therefore state with certainty that Warner was the ninth bishop in order and acquired that dignity in 1147, not in 1171. Other sources will show that errors have also been made in reckoning other bishops.] bishop of Włocławek [Note: [Col. 1328D] Vlatizlavia, Wladislavia—Włocławek, Władysławów, Leslau—a city founded by Władysław II between 1139 and 1148. The see of the bishops of Kruszwica was transferred here about 1159; from that time the bishopric of Kruszwica began to be called that of Włocławek, or Cuiavia.], and to his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.

Whenever a request is made of us which is recognized as consonant with reason and uprightness, it is proper for us to grant it with willing mind and to afford suitable support to the desires of those who ask. Therefore, venerable brother, we graciously assent to your just petitions, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the Church of Włocławek, over which, by God’s agency, you are known to preside, and fortify it with the privilege of this present writing. [Col. 1328C] We decree that you and your successors shall possess forever, without any diminution, the boundaries of your bishopric, as they were established by Aegidius, bishop of Tusculum, of blessed memory, then legate of the Apostolic See, and by Bolesław, noble duke of the same land [Note: [Col. 1328D] On Aegidius, cardinal and legate, see Lelewel’s discussion in his notes on the charter of 1105 (1224), in the work *Początkowe Prawodawstwo Polskie*, given by that same Aegidius to the bishopric of Cracow. Yet that charter makes no mention either of the Church of Cuiavia or of that of Kruszwica. Another enactment concerning that same Church of Włocławek must therefore have been made and completed by the same legate, since the pope asserts this so explicitly. The same appears from the bull of Innocent II of the year 1133, printed in the new *Codex of Pomerania*, p. 25, no. 12. In that bull, subjecting the bishopric of Włocławek to the authority of the archbishop of Magdeburg, the pope also mentions, among other things, the ancient ordinances of his predecessors promulgated in this matter.].

Whatever possessions and goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, God favouring it, through grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have judged the following to be specified in particular: the castle of Woibor [Note: [Col. 1329C] Wolbórz, a town and castle in the Piotrków region.] with all its dependencies; the church of Saint Mary at Zawichost [Note: [Col. 1329C] Zawichost, a town in the Sandomierz region.] with the castle of Łagów [Note: [Col. 1329C] Łagów, a castle and town in the Sandomierz palatinate, Opatów region. Długosz relates that, at the request of his wife Judith, Władysław Herman gave the castellany of Łagów with its district to the Church of Cuiavia in 1085. By a privilege of 1375, Elizabeth, queen of Poland and Hungary, converted the village of Łagów into a town.] and its tithe and other dependencies; the ninth penny from everything paid to the church of Saint Mary of Sandomierz [Note: [Col. 1329D] Sandomierz (*Sandomiria*), capital city of the province of the same name.] according to Polish law; the provostship of Saint Michael at Cracow with all belonging to it; the castle of Gdańsk [Note: [Col. 1329D] Gdańsk (*Gedanum*), in German Danzig.] in Pomerania, with a tithe both of grain [Col. 1329B] and of all payments made from ships; and a tenth part of the revenue from coinage and judicial proceedings throughout the whole bishopric.

Therefore, let no person be permitted rashly to disturb the aforesaid Church of Włocławek, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; rather, let all things be preserved whole, for the benefit in every way of those for whose support and governance they were granted. If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, rashly attempts to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not correct that person’s presumption by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and honour; let him or her recognize [Col. 1329C] himself or herself as guilty before divine judgment for the wrong committed; let him or her be excluded from the most sacred body and blood [Col. 1330A] of our Lord Jesus Christ; and let him or her be subject to strict vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good works and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

**Show me a sign of favor, O Lord.**

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. (*Fare well* in the monogram.) I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum [Note: [Col. 1329D] In Damalewicz and in *Preussische Sammlung*, it appears as Linarus. Muratori incorrectly calls him Jomarus. In Hardouin, vol. IV, tome VI of the *Councils*, cols. 1241 ff., in two charters of the same period, he is called, as in our charter, Ymarus.]. I, Ubaldus, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Praxedis. I, Aribertus, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Anastasia [Note: [Col. 1329D] Rymer, in his *Foedera* (vol. I), citing a bull of the same pope from 1147 in which almost all the cardinals listed here occur, reads Ariticus; this reading, however, seems to us to deserve acceptance.]. [Col. 1330B] I, Julius, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Marcellus. I, Bernardus, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Clement. I, Jordanus, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Susanna. I, Oddo, cardinal-deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Octavianus, cardinal-deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. I, Gregorius, cardinal-deacon of Saint Angelo. I, Guido, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, Jacintus, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin.

Given at Reims [Note: [Col. 1329D] In Damalewicz and the other authors who followed him in printing this bull, “at Rome” is read. This very serious error contributed greatly to doubts concerning the authenticity of the bull. Baronius, in the *Ecclesiastical Annals*, vol. XII, p. 429, states that Pope Eugenius convened a council at Reims in Gaul in 1148; that it began on 21 March, the eleventh day before the Kalends of April; that it continued until Easter, 11 April; and that the pope was continuously present there. How, then, could “at Rome” have been appended to this bull, issued on 3 April? The author of *Preussische Sammlung* did not overlook this point. He therefore conjectures that some error was made through the carelessness of a copyist who, puzzled by the word *Remis*, perhaps unable to resolve it, inserted *Romae*, a word more familiar to him. The original now discovered removes every doubt and proves that Reims, the city of Gaul and seat of an archbishop, is meant here. There can be no doubt that matters concerning Poland were discussed at the council held there, especially since bishops from different peoples had been summoned there. Baronius himself says, p. 431, no. 7: “There came to the aforesaid council, with a golden bull, envoys of Henry, younger king of the Romans, notifying the Roman pontiff both of his elevation to the empire, and lodging a complaint concerning the three brothers of the duchy of Poland, who, having expelled the fourth and eldest, had divided the duchy among themselves, and concerning the bishops of that province, who had sworn an oath to their father in this matter.” Who would dare deny that Bishop Warner himself was present there?—Whatever the case, this bull is of all the greater importance because it was promulgated at the time the council was held; and its authenticity is especially confirmed by the witnesses who were present at that council and are appended to all other contemporary charters.], through the hand of Guy, cardinal-deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the Nones of April [Note: [Col. 1330D] Damalewicz and others read “Nones of April”; in the original, “the second day before the Nones of April,” that is, 4 April. We have therefore supplied this date, not 9 April as in *Preussische Sammlung*. We have not thought it worthwhile to set out here the variant readings of the charter printed by Damalewicz, since that text teems with errors caused by the copyist’s carelessness.], in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1148 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III [Col. 1330C].

CCLXXIX. He confirms for Saint Martin a perpetual prebend in the church of Amiens. (Year 1148, April 5.)

[*Gallia Christiana nova*, X, Documents, 314.]

[Col. 1331A]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons THEOBALD, abbot of the church of Saint Martin of Amiens, and his brethren: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The force of equity and the order of reason require that just petitioners be granted their requests, especially when piety supports their will and truth does not fail it. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, granting assent to your just petitions, we confirm by the authority of the Apostolic See the grant concerning the prebend which, in the mother church of Amiens, [Col. 1331B] with the consent of the chapter of that church and at the request of our beloved son Bernard, abbot of Clairvaux, our venerable brother Theoderic, bishop of Amiens, is known to have reasonably granted to you and your successors; and we decree that it shall remain in the right and power of your church in future times. Should anyone knowingly presume rashly to act against this page of our confirmation, let that person know that he or she will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Reims, on the Nones of April, in the eleventh indiction.

CCLXXX. To A., archbishop of Bremen; H., bishop of Minden; and T., bishop of Verden.—That they are to ensure the restoration of the estates of the monastery of Kemnade, usurped by various persons. (Year 1148, April 5.)

[Marten, *Amplissima Collectio*, II, 240.]

[Col. 1331C]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brothers A. [Note: [Col. 1332D] Adalberon.], archbishop of Bremen; HE. [Note: [Col. 1332D] Henry.], bishop of Minden; and T. [Note: [Col. 1332D] Thiethmar.], bishop of Verden: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The possessions of churches are known to be the patrimony of the poor and the price of sinners; therefore, whoever presumes to retain them against justice certainly commits sacrilege. It has been reported to us that your parishioners, brother archbishop—Odico, Riembertus, Thederinus, Rainerus, Hermannus, and certain others—presumed to receive possessions of the Church of Kemnade from the hand of Judith, formerly abbess, after she had been deposed, [Col. 1331D] and, forgetful of their salvation, refuse to restore them to that monastery. Hugoldus, Waltardus, Gerardus, and certain other parishioners of yours, brother bishop of Verden, likewise received certain benefices, as has been represented to us, from the hand of that same woman after she had been deposed. Since, therefore, after the aforesaid Judith had been deposed from the government of the Church of Kemnade by the judgment of our venerable brother Thomas, cardinal-priest of blessed memory, then legate of the Apostolic See, [Col. 1332A] she had no authority to alienate or pledge the goods of that church, we command you by this present writing strictly to admonish them to restore in their entirety to the aforesaid church the goods which they presume to retain to the peril of their souls, and to cease harassing it. If they scorn to do so within forty days after being warned by you, administer canonical justice against them. Likewise, brother bishop of Minden, by the authority of this present writing we command you strictly to admonish Walderus, who, disregarding the requirements of his clerical office, is said to have received estates of that same monastery from the woman who had no power to give them, to restore what he wrongly acquired and permit [Col. 1332B] that church to possess them in peace. If he refuses to do so, restrain him by canonical censure.

Given at Reims, on the Nones of April.

CCLXXXI. To the monks of Corvey.—He confirms the deposition of Abbot Henry. (Year 1148, April 5.)

[Same source, 241.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the monks, free persons, and ministeriales of Corvey: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The office which we exercised in governing an abbey before our elevation informs us how necessary it is to provide for the peace of monasteries [Col. 1332C] and to think carefully of their welfare. Therefore, providing for the peace and tranquillity of the Church of Corvey, we confirm the sentence which our venerable brother Thomas, cardinal-priest of blessed memory and legate of the Apostolic See, pronounced against Henry, formerly abbot of that monastery; and we decree that if the same Henry presumes to disturb the peace of the monastery of Corvey and, after being warned twice or three times, does not come to his senses, he shall not only hold no further office of prelate there, but we forbid him thereafter even to remain there among the subjects.

Given at Reims, on the Nones of April.

CCLXXXII. He receives under protection the monastery of Saints Facundus and Primitivus at Sahagún, and confirms its possessions and privileges. (Year 1148, April 7.) [Col. 1332D]

[Escalona, *History of Sahagún*, 529.]

CCLXXXIII. Bull for the abbey of Saint Mary of Flavigny-Mont. (Year 1148, April 8.)

[Hugo, *Annals of Prémontré*, I, Preface, p. 547.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved [Col. 1333A] sons STEPHEN, abbot of Saint Mary of Flabonis-mont, and his brethren, both present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

By the authority and duty of the Apostolic See we are compelled to labour for the condition of all churches and, with the Lord’s help, to provide for their peace. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the church of Flabonis-mont, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it with the patronage of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods, in cultivated or uncultivated lands, meadows, woods, pastures, mills, tithes, or otherwise, that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter [Col. 1333B] acquire by grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, the Lord granting it, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have judged the following to be specified by their proper names:

The church of Saint Mary of Flabonis-mont itself, with that place and all its dependencies; the tithe which Genoldus and his heirs had in the aforesaid place; the freehold of Lielencourt with its mill, granted to you by the same Genoldus and Horrico with their heirs; whatever the church of Ronengis possessed there; two mills and the usufruct of the territory of Baigneval; the land which the abbot of Luxeuil possessed within your precinct; the place called Bertini’s Stream, given by Count Hugh to the aforesaid church for the remedy of his soul; and whatever was granted to you in the same place by Duke Simon. The liberty which you received from the aforesaid count: that whoever wished to bestow upon your church property from his freehold or fief belonging to that count might lawfully give it, and you might lawfully receive it; the estate of Dura-aqua with the mill called Munel and all its dependencies; the tithes granted to you by the church of Saint Vincent of Besançon, and whatever cultivated land you bring under cultivation; also that which Leobaldus and his heirs granted you from the aforesaid tithes; the land called Cold Spring, with the right of pasture at Hagevilla. Moreover, we likewise confirm the tithe which Albericus of Tillut gave you.

[Col. 1333D] We therefore decree that no one at all may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or afflict it by any harassments. Rather, let all things be preserved whole, for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan. If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not make amends by suitable satisfaction, [Col. 1334A] let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and honour, recognize himself or herself as guilty before divine judgment for the wrong committed, be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, and be subject to strict vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who uphold what is just for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good works and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, etc.

Given at Reims, through the hand [of Guy], etc., on the sixth day before the Ides of April, in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1148, in the fourth year of Pope Eugenius III.

CCLXXXIV. To the people of Fulda.—He declares void an election made by them contrary to his command, and orders them, in the presence of certain abbots whom he names, to elect an abbot from another monastery. (Year 1148, April 8.)

[Marten, *Amplissima Collectio*, II, 241.]

[Col. 1334B]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the monks, free persons, and ministeriales of the monastery of Fulda: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Unless the discerning attention of the head is directed toward the reasonable governance of its members, the frame of the body, dissolved, will totter. After the Church of Fulda was first deprived of its shepherd, we took care to command orally the brethren [Col. 1334C] who were present to elect, unanimously, from another monastery an abbot to be set over them—one through whom the cultivation of true religion, pleasing to God, might, with the Lord’s help, be restored in the monastery of Fulda, which through the shepherd’s negligence had been diminished in spiritual as well as temporal matters. You, however, contrary to the form of our command, presumed to elect an abbot from your own monastery, although because of bodily deformity he could not be advanced to the priesthood. We therefore nullify by apostolic authority what was done concerning his election, and absolve the clerical monks from the obedience and the laymen from the fealty which they are known to have rendered him. Accordingly, by this present writing [Col. 1334D] we command and direct you, by the counsel of our beloved sons the abbots of Ebrach, Eberbach, Hersfeld, and Corvey, to elect from another monastery, divine grace having been invoked, a religious, discerning, learned person as your abbot, through whom the fervour of religion in your monastery—which is known to have grown lukewarm there as sins demanded—may be restored and may in future be maintained by his word and the example of his good conduct.

[Note: [Col. 1333D] This is Adam, who passed from being a monk of Marmoutier to the Cistercians, professed a stricter discipline at the monastery of Morimond, and was thence chosen to govern the abbey of Ebrach. Saint Bernard’s Letter 7 to him survives.]

Given at Reims, on the sixth day before the Ides of April.

CCLXXXV. To the abbots of Ebrach, Eberbach, Hersfeld, and Corvey.—That, on going to Fulda, they are to ensure the election of an abbot from another monastery. (Year 1148, April 8.)

[Marten, *Amplissima Collectio*, II, 242.]

[Col. 1335A]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the abbots of Ebrach, Eberbach, Hersfeld, and Corvey: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Placed, by God’s ordering, upon the watchtower of the Apostolic See, we are compelled to provide with diligent care for all churches of the world, whether near or far. Since the brethren of the monastery of Fulda, contrary to our prohibition, [Col. 1335B] elected a person from their own monastery, who, hindered by bodily deformity, ought not to have advanced to the priesthood, we have nullified what was done concerning him. Therefore, lest that church suffer serious losses in spiritual as well as temporal matters through the absence of a shepherd, by this present writing we command you to go to the aforesaid church, so that the brethren of that place may, by your counsel and with the Lord’s help, elect from another monastery such a shepherd for themselves as may restore the cultivation of true religion pleasing to God, which is known to have perished there.

Given at Reims, on the sixth day before the Ides of April.

CCLXXXVI. Privilege for the nunnery of Saint Andrew at Göss. (Year 1148, April 13.)

[Pusch and Froehlich, *Diplomata sacra of the Duchy of Styria*, I, 123.]

[Col. 1335C]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ, ADOLESSA, abbess of the monastery of Saint Andrew at Göss, and her sisters, both present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

Whenever a request is made of us which is recognized as consonant with reason and uprightness, it is proper for us to grant it with willing mind and to afford suitable support to the desires of those who ask. Therefore, beloved daughters in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it with the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods it now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, God favouring it, by grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and those who succeed you in the same place. Among these we have judged the following to be specified by their proper names: the place of Göss itself; the church of Saint Nicholas at Michlindorf; the church of Saint Martin at Wenchilen; the church of Saint Lambert at Sclatetiz; the church of Saint Martin at Soriche; Lominich, Tragisse, Lebena, Poumgartten, Englobortisdorf, Minoz, Sirisperich, Rottenstein, Domelache, Waltenpach, [Col. 1336A] Pulzeisdorf, Chuntur, Chruglache, Zeittes, Zemoze, Viringen, Walensdorf, Arbenorf, and Emanue, with all the appurtenances of everything aforesaid.

As a token of the protection received from the Roman Church, you shall pay one gold piece each year to us and to our successors. We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations. Rather, let all things be preserved whole, for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and, in the churches subject to the aforesaid monastery, the canonical right of the diocesan bishops. If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical [Col. 1336B] or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not make amends by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and honour; let him or her recognize himself or herself as guilty before divine judgment for the wrong committed; let him or her be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and our Lord Jesus Christ; and let him or her be subject to strict vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who uphold what is just for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good works and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum, have subscribed. [Col. 1336C] I, Hubaldus, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Praxedis, have subscribed. I, Hubaldus, cardinal-priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Aribertus, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Anastasia, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal-priest of the title of the Shepherd, have subscribed. I, Oddo, cardinal-deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Octavianus, cardinal-deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed. I, John Paparo, cardinal-deacon of Saint Adrian, have subscribed. I, Gregorius, cardinal-deacon of Saint Angelo, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed. I, Jacintus, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin.

[Col. 1336D] Given at Reims, through the hands of Guy, cardinal-deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the Ides of April, in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1148 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

CCLXXXVII. He took the monastery of Saint Giles of Canawella under his protection. (Year 1148, April 13.)

[Rymer, *Foedera*, I, 15.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons WILLIAM, prior of the monastery of Saint Giles of Canawella, and his brethren, both present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

It is fitting to grant ready assent to religious desires, so that faithful devotion may obtain a swift result. [Col. 1337A] Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests: we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. First, indeed, we decree that the monastic order established in your church according to the Rule of blessed Benedict shall there be preserved inviolate in times to come. Moreover, whatever possessions or goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses—in cultivated or uncultivated lands, meadows, woods, pastures, mills, tithes, or other things—or may hereafter acquire, God being favourable, through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. [Col. 1337B] Among these, we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: namely, the place itself, Canawella, with the aforesaid church of Saint Giles; by the gift of Geva, daughter of Hugh, count of Chester, in whose lordship the aforesaid church is situated, the land called Stichesleia; one dwelling in Draitona; in Duntona, one mill, which is on the Corre, and four virgates of land in the same vill with the adjoining meadow at Ellefordia, by the gift of Robert of Weffordia; sixty acres of land in his wood at Witemora, besides the plain at Sticelleia.

We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid monastery, or to take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, [Col. 1337C] or harass it by any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole for the use, and to every benefit, of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishops. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this text of our constitution, shall rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second and third time, shall not make amends by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour, know himself or herself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, and be subject at the last judgment to severe vengeance. [Col. 1337D] But upon all who preserve what is right for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

### CCLXXXVIII. Letter to the Gallican bishops, defining the rights of Marmoutier in the parishes subject to it. (1148, 14 April)

[MABILLON, *Annales Benedictini*, VI, 708.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brethren P. [Peter], archbishop of Bourges; S. [Samson], archbishop of Reims; EN. [Engelbaud], archbishop of Tours; G. [Geoffrey], archbishop of Bordeaux; HU. [Hugh], archbishop of Rouen; [Col. 1339A] [Col. 1338A] G. [Geoffrey], bishop of Chartres; M. [Manasses], bishop of Orléans; G. [Gilbert], bishop of Poitiers; G. [William], bishop of Le Mans; U. [Ulger], bishop of Angers; A. [Alan], bishop of Rennes; J. [John], bishop of Aleth; B. [Bernard], bishop of Nantes; T. [Theobald], bishop of Paris; M. [Manasses], bishop of Meaux; G. [Goslin], bishop of Soissons; H. [Henry], bishop of Troyes; G. [Gerard], bishop of Séez; A. [Algar], bishop of Coutances; R. [Richard], bishop of Avranches; R. [Rotrou], bishop of Évreux; M. [Milo], bishop of Thérouanne; B. [Bartholomew], bishop of Laon; T. [Theodoric], bishop of Amiens; and O. [Odo], bishop of Beauvais: greeting and the apostolic blessing.

It is known to have been decreed in general councils that priests residing in churches belonging to monasteries shall answer to the diocesan bishop concerning the care of souls, [Col. 1338B] but shall render due subjection to the abbot and his brethren in temporal affairs. To the contrary, we have received the complaint of our beloved sons G., abbot of Marmoutier, and his brethren: namely, that the priests of churches belonging to them and situated in your parishes withhold their due subjection from them, and, through malicious intent adhering to the archdeacons, answer that they owe them nothing. Since we wish no one to be deprived of his right, we command you by apostolic letters strictly to admonish those priests concerning whom the said abbot or his brethren complain to you, that they render them due reverence and subjection, and that on no pretext they presume to diminish [Col. 1338C] or withhold from them anything known to be theirs by right. Otherwise, we grant our aforesaid son the abbot and his brethren free authority to exact due redress from the aforesaid priests concerning those matters which belong to them.

Given at Reims, 18 Kalends of May [14 April].

### CCLXXXIX. He commands the deans established throughout the archdeaconry of the Church of Bonn to obey Provost G. (1148, 18 April)

[GUNTHER, *Codex diplomaticus Rheno-Mosellanus*, I, 340.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the deans established throughout the archdeaconry of the Church of Bonn: greeting and the apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1338D] As obedient sons, through obedience, maintain the safeguard of virtues, so the disobedient, through disobedience, introduce a heap of sins. For to resist is as the sin of divination, and to refuse assent is like the crime of idolatry. Therefore we command you by these present letters that, rendering obedience and reverence to our beloved son G., provost of Bonn, you humbly obey his just admonitions and commands.

Given at Reims, 14 Kalends of May [18 April].

### CCLXXXIX bis. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Theoderic at Reims. (1148, 18 April)

[D. MARLOT, *Metropolis Remensis*, II, 358.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son in Christ ALDRIC, abbot of Saint Theoderic, and to his successors to be regularly appointed.

A pious petition ought to be fulfilled by a corresponding result, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth worthily and the advantage sought may assuredly gain strength. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Aldric, granting favourable assent to your just requests, we receive under the guardianship of blessed Peter and our protection the monastery of Saint Theoderic, over which, by the Lord’s authorship, you are known to preside.

Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. Given at Reims, through the hand of Guido, cardinal-deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, 14 Kalends of May [18 April], indiction II, in the year 1148 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the third year of the pontificate of Eugenius [Col. 1339B] III. Hulbaldus, cardinal-priest of Saint Praxedes. Imarus, bishop of Tusculum; Odo, cardinal-deacon of Saint George at the Velum Aureum. Hulbaldus, cardinal-priest of Saints John and Paul. Guido, cardinal-priest of Saint Lawrence in Damaso. Aribertus, cardinal-priest of Saint Anastasia. John, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary the New. Guido, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Portico.

### CCXC. Privilege for the abbot of Saint-Denis at Paris. (1148, 20 April)

[DOUBLET, *Histoire de l’abbaye de Saint-Denis*, p. 494.]

[Col. 1339C]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son in Christ SUGER, abbot of the venerable monastery situated at Paris in honour of blessed Denis the martyr, and to his successors to be regularly appointed, in perpetuity.

By the office of apostolate laid upon us by God, we consider ourselves debtors to all churches and ecclesiastical persons; yet it is fitting that we provide with a more devoted concern of charity for those known to be more closely attached to blessed Peter [Col. 1339D] and the Holy Roman Church. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord Suger, whose fidelity and devotion to blessed Peter and the Holy Roman Church we have experienced through certain proofs, and through whose industry and solicitude we have learned that a form of religion pleasing to God has been reformed in the aforesaid monastery of Saint Denis, we grant favourable assent to your reasonable requests. We decree, therefore, that whatever dignity has been granted to that place by the authentic privileges of our predecessors Zachary, Stephen, Leo, Alexander, Paschal, and Calixtus, Roman pontiffs; whatever goods are known to belong to the same monastery through the lawful offerings of Catholic kings or other faithful persons; and whatever it may hereafter acquire through grants of pontiffs, the liberality of princes, or other just means, by the Lord’s bounty, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. [Col. 1340A] Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: in the district of Metz, the new cell, with all its appurtenances, namely Hulspere, Ausminge, Eumelingas, the church of Fulcreia, saltworks and salt-pans at Marsalcia; the monastery of Argenteuil, situated in the district of Paris on the River Seine, with its appurtenances; in the diocese of Orléans, the field of Mainerius, Villare, Vendrous, Villammeium, Feienis, Liuns. In addition, we confirm to you and your successors the county of Vexin, which belongs by right to Saint Denis and which our dearest son Louis, king of the Franks, is known through you to have received from blessed Denis in benefice and fief—for he possesses it in whose name it is possessed. [Col. 1340B] We likewise strengthen for you the vicariate, every kind of jurisdiction, and full liberty around the vill of Saint-Denis, as distinguished by the following boundaries: namely, from the River Seine, from the mill commonly called Bayard, as far as the upper end of the vill called Halbervillaro, which the aforesaid king, acknowledging that it belonged by right to blessed Denis, restored to blessed Denis; we nevertheless confirm this to you.

Moreover, in the diocese of Laon: the altar-right of Caadursa; the altar-right of Saint Gobert; the altar-right of Piloris; the altar-right of Sairiacum, with the chapel of Saint Denis at Ribomont; in the valley of Visana, the altar-rights of Sorbais, Altrepia, Rochiniis, Rosbais, [Col. 1340C] and Serenis Fontibus. In the diocese of Cambrai: the altar-right of Solesmes and that of Vertiniolum, with their tithes and all appurtenances. In the diocese of Rouen: the church of Calvomonte with its appurtenances, which our venerable brother Hugh, archbishop of Rouen, with the consent of our dearest son Louis, king of the Franks, gave you. In the diocese of Paris: the cell of Blessed Mary situated near Corbeil on the River Essonne, with its appurtenances. By gift of the aforesaid king: whatever he had in the vill of Trappes, except annual hospitality when he should lodge there; and the tallage which he gave you at Cergiacum in Vexin and at Cormelias. By gift of Geoffrey, bishop of Chartres, of good memory: [Col. 1340D] the altar-rights of Monarvilla and Rubridum. By gift of Aluis, bishop of Arras: the altar-right of Anechin. By gift of the illustrious kings Edward and William of England: Derhestia, situated on the River Severn, Taunton, and More.

We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid monastery, or take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with rash vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole for the use, and to every benefit, of those for whose support and governance they were granted. Upon your death, as present abbot of that place, no one shall be set over it by any cunning contrivance or force, except one whom the brethren, by common consent or by the sounder part of the council, elect according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Benedict. [Col. 1341A] The person elected shall be consecrated either by the Roman pontiff or by whatever Catholic bishop he may prefer. You shall receive chrism, holy oil, the consecration of altars or churches, and the ordination of monks or clerics belonging to that monastery from Catholic bishops, as has been established by the privileges of our predecessors in canonical equity. We prohibit public masses from being celebrated or a station being held in the same monastery without the abbot’s consent; nor do we permit bishops or the ministers of bishops to interdict, excommunicate, summon to synod, or otherwise exercise such power over either the abbot or the monks of that place. Furthermore, we grant both you [Col. 1341B] and your successors leave to appeal to the Apostolic See in more serious matters; nor shall any harm befall those making an appeal before the matter is concluded, so that, by God’s authorship, you may remain peaceful and diligent in the pursuits of holy religion.

If anyone in the future, knowing this text of our constitution, shall attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second and third time, shall not amend by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour, know himself or herself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ, and be subject at the last judgment to severe vengeance. [Col. 1341C] But upon all who observe these provisions for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum, have subscribed. I, Hubaldus, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Praxedes, have subscribed. I, Julius, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Marcellus, have subscribed. I, Bernardus, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Clement, have subscribed. I, Odo, cardinal-deacon of the Holy Roman Church, of the title of Saint George at the Velum Aureum, have subscribed. [Col. 1341D] I, Octavianus, cardinal-deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed. I, John, cardinal-deacon of Saint Adrian, have subscribed. I, Jacinthus, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin, have subscribed.

Given at Châlons, through the hand of Guido, cardinal-deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, 12 Kalends of May [20 April], indiction XI, in the year 1148 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### CCXCI. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Remigius at Reims. (1148, 20 April)

[MARLOT, *Metropolis Remensis*, II, 359.]

[Col. 1342A]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ODON, abbot of the monastery of Saint Remigius, and his brethren, both present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

The authority of our office exhorts us to labour for the condition of the churches and, with the Lord’s aid, beneficially to provide for their peace and advantage, etc. For it is known to be fitting and consonant with honour that we, who have been taken up for the governance of churches, should defend them against the wickedness of evil men and fortify them with the patronage of blessed Peter and the Apostolic See. [Col. 1342B] Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests, receive the aforesaid monastery under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing, etc. If any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this text of our constitution, shall attempt to act against it [lacuna] let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour, etc.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum. I, Odo, cardinal-deacon of Saint Gregory at the Velum Aureum. I, Octavianus, cardinal-deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. [Col. 1342C] I, John Paparo, cardinal-deacon of Saint Adrian. I, Hebaldus, cardinal-priest of Saint Praxedes. I, Humbaldus, cardinal-priest of the title of Saints John and Paul. I, Gillebertus, unworthy priest of the title of Saint Marius. I, Julius, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Marcellus.

Given at Châlons, through the hand of Guido, cardinal-deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, 12 Kalends of May [20 April], indiction II, in the year 1148 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### CCXCII. To the abbess and nuns of Saint Peter at Reims.—Instrument securing the abbess and nuns of Saint Peter at Reims against the abbot and monks of Saint Nicasius, concerning the causeway of Thour. (1148, 23 April)

[MARTÈNE, *Anecdota*, 627.]

[Col. 1342D]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ, the abbess of Saint Peter and her sisters S. and A. B.

Settlements of lawsuits and agreements resolving disputes are committed to written records so that they may not be withdrawn from the memory of posterity. The controversy between you and the abbot [Note: [Col. 1341] The abbey of Saint Nicasius at Reims, of the order of Saint Benedict, founded by Archbishop Gervasius in 1066, remains to this day under the Congregation of Saint Maur.] of Saint Nicasius has been settled in our presence by agreement in the following manner. The entire causeway beside the castle of Thour shall belong by parochial right to the church of Saint Nicasius, and all inhabitants of that causeway shall pay it all parochial dues in full. But all those living in houses outside the gate of that causeway, and all who hereafter live within those houses and the church of Blessed Peter at Jardincurte, shall be parishioners of Saint Peter. On the other side of the houses, however, all who dwell between those houses and the church of Saint Simeon shall be parishioners of the church of Saint Nicasius. Whatever the inhabitants of the causeway paid you, whether from gardens, houses on the causeway, or other sources, they shall nevertheless continue to pay you. Because you, the abbess, renounced in the hand of the abbot of Saint Nicasius the lawsuit concerning the causeway and parochial right, [Col. 1343B] the abbot remitted to you nine sextaries of grain: six of these the church of Saint Peter had paid each year to the church of Saint Nicasius for mills, and three for a certain cultivated holding. We therefore confirm this agreement as stated and decree that it shall remain ratified. We likewise confirm to you, during her lifetime, the forty Châlons solidi which are owed to your church by the church [Note: [Col. 1343] Bucilium: a monastery of the Premonstratensian order in the diocese of Laon, founded by the count of Vermandois.] of Buciliensium, on behalf of the abbess of that place, under an agreement between her and the abbot of Buciliensium. If anyone, knowing this text of our confirmation, shall rashly attempt to act against it, let that person know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of his apostles Peter and Paul, [Col. 1343C] and that at the last judgment he will render an account to the Lord for the guilt committed.

Given in the territory of Troyes, at Brenne, 9 Kalends of May [23 April].

### CCXCIII. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Mary of Basse-Fontaine. (1148, 24 April)

[HUGO, *Annales Praemonstratenses*, I, 151.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons BALDWIN, abbot of Basse-Fontaine, and his brethren, both present and future, in perpetuity.

Whenever a request is made to us which is recognized to accord with reason and propriety, it is fitting that we grant it with willing mind and give suitable support to the petitioners’ desires. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, [Col. 1343D] we graciously assent to your just requests, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the church of Saint Mary of Basse-Fontaine, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. First, indeed, we decree that the canonical order, according to the Rule of Saint Augustine and the institution of the Premonstratensian brethren, shall be preserved inviolate in your church for all future time. Moreover, whatever possessions or goods the same church now justly and canonically possesses—in fields, vineyards, meadows, woods, pastures, cultivated or uncultivated lands, tithes, or other things—or may hereafter acquire, God being favourable, through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. [Col. 1344A] Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: the place itself of Basse-Fontaine; the place of Magnissilium (Mesnil), with its mills; the grange of Verpelleria (Verpillière), with all their appurtenances; whatever has been given to you by Walter, count of Brienne, and confirmed by the seal of the bishop of Troyes; the tithes of Bleincurtis, Neuville, Vitry, Cepeoii (Spois), Convenii (Couvignon), and Froevallis (Froeval); likewise, one eighth of the tithe of New and Old Brenne, with the tithes of Calderii (Cheidray), Saint Navortius [Col. 1344B] (Saint Nabor), and Pressei (Pressy); likewise, one eighth of all the land and water adjoining the land of Albertus Monilis (Mainil-Aubert). Furthermore, no one shall presume to exact tithes from you upon the produce of your labours which you cultivate in newly cleared land by your own hands or at your own expense, or upon the sustenance of your animals.

We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or vex it with any harassments.

Given at Clairvaux, through the hand of Guido, cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, 8 Kalends of May [24 April], indiction XI, in the year 1148 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord [Col. 1344C] Pope Eugenius III.

### CCXCIV. Bull confirming the substitution of Premonstratensians at Bucilium. (1148, 26 April)

[HUGO, *Annales Praemonstratenses*, I, preface, p. 336.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons PERSICUS, abbot of the Church of Bucilium, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

The affection of a pious will ought to be fulfilled by a corresponding result, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth worthily and the benefit sought may assuredly gain strength. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just [Col. 1344D] requests; we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the church of Saint Peter of Bucilium, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. First, indeed, we decree that the canonical order according to the Rule of blessed Augustine and the institution of the Premonstratensian brethren shall be preserved inviolate in your church for all future time. Moreover, whatever possessions or goods it now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, God being favourable, through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, [Col. 1345A] or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever shall have the right rashly to disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any other vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole for the use, and to every benefit, of those for whose governance and support they were granted. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this text of our constitution, shall rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second and third time, shall not correct his or her offence by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour, know himself or herself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed, [Col. 1345B] be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ, and be subject at the last judgment to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve what is right for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.
