I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum. I, Hubaldus, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Praxedes. I, Hugh, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Marcellus. I, Guido, cardinal-priest of the title of Pastor. I, Bernardus, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Clement. [Col. 1345C] I, Oddo, cardinal-deacon, scribe. I, Octavianus, cardinal-deacon of the title of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. I, John Paparo, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary the New. I, Jacinthus, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin.

Given at Clairvaux, through the hand of Guido, cardinal-deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, 6 Kalends of May [26 April], indiction I, in the year 1148 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### CCXCV. He receives the monastery of Theloniensis under protection and confirms its Premonstratensian discipline and possessions. (1148, April, at Clairvaux) [Col. 1345D]

[HUGO, *Vie de S. Norbert*, 134, as reported by BRÉQUIGNY, *Table chronologique*, III, 145.]

### CCXCVI. To A. [Alfonso], king of the Spains.—He confirms the primacy of Toledo. (1148, 27 April)

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XXI, 672.]

Set by the Lord’s disposition upon the watchtower of shepherds, we ought with fatherly affection to love Catholic princes and kings of the lands, especially those known faithfully to adhere to blessed Peter and his Holy Roman Church; and by the office laid upon us, we ought to preserve their rights for them. Never, most reverend son in the Lord, was it our intention concerning you that we should in any respect diminish your honour, dignity, or the right of the kingdom entrusted to you by the Lord—especially since we know that, both in the time of our predecessors and in ours, you have been obedient and devoted to the Apostolic See. [Col. 1346A] Having regard to this, we willingly received your requests concerning an expedition to be made against the tyranny of the unbelievers; and, for the Lord’s honour, we are bound by the duty of paternal charity to be ready to do this in future as well. It is therefore fitting henceforth that you cease your complaint—namely, that, led by persuasions unknown to us, you have supposed we received something from the duke of the Portuguese, or even granted something to him, whereby the rights of your kingdom ought to be diminished, taken away, or permanently subjected to injury.

For our part, setting before our eyes the love and devotion towards the Roman Church of your grandfather Alfonso, of revered memory, then the most renowned king in the regions of Spain, and greatly rejoicing in the Lord over the victory mercifully granted you by the Lord God of Hosts against the enemies of the Christian faith, [Col. 1346B] we are bound to you by a spiritual sincerity of affection, and are all the more disposed to provide, as we can in the Lord, for your royal serenity and your heirs. Furthermore, that the bishop of Braga and his suffragans should obey the archbishop of Toledo as their primate was rightly commanded by our predecessors; and we too have commanded it by our writings and desire it to be observed. The bishop of Braga is indeed bound by a sentence of suspension because he does not render this obedience to the archbishop of Toledo. It is therefore your concern to persist in the service and devotion of blessed Peter, and with the Lord’s help labour to subdue barbarian nations, while likewise revering and loving churches and ecclesiastical persons; so that in your actions he through whom kings reign may be more abundantly honoured, and your mother, the Holy Roman Church, may rejoice and exult more greatly in so great a son and so Catholic a prince. [Col. 1346C]

In addition, we wish it to be known to your nobility that we have thought it necessary to retain with us the bishop of Coria: first, because, as we have learned, he was burdened by grave poverty in the church entrusted to him and could not there usefully exercise his office; secondly, because we trust that your munificence ought more honourably to provide for his necessities. As a sign of our good will and favour toward you, we have arranged to send to your serenity, through our venerable brother B., bishop of Segovia, the golden rose which, as a sign of the passion and resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Roman pontiff customarily bears every year on the Sunday when *Laetare Jerusalem* is sung. [Col. 1346D] Stirred by the remembrance of that rose, strive, with the Lord’s help, to complete in your body those things lacking of Christ’s sufferings, and, aided by his mercy, to attain the glory of the resurrection. Since, moreover, as a devoted and humble son, you wished the bishops and abbots of your kingdom to attend the Council of Reims at our summons, we give thanks for your good will and, overcome by consideration of your prayers, release from the sentence of suspension those who did not come.

Given in the territory of Langres, 5 Kalends of May [27 April].

### CCXCVII. To Abbot Suger.—Concerning monks to be established in the church of Saint Geneviève. (1148, 29 April)

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XXI, 637.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son SUGER, abbot of Saint-Denis: greeting and the apostolic blessing.

The authority of our office exhorts us diligently to apply ourselves to the establishment of religious life and, once it has been established, to preserve it with exact care. Hence it is, as your affection knows, [Col. 1347B] that we conferred with our dearest son Louis, illustrious king of the Franks, concerning placing religious brethren in the church of Saint Geneviève for God’s service. Since lack of time prevented us, we were unable to bring this to effect according to his purpose and ours. But because you are known to exercise royal functions in the regions of Gaul, and because we have the greatest confidence in your discernment, we command you by these present letters to establish there, as free and independent abbot, the prior of Abbeville, and to endeavour to assign to his community eight brethren of the church of Saint-Martin-des-Champs, so that, by the example of their good manner of life, those whose inclinations are less honourable may be summoned to the divine office. We have, moreover, commanded the prior of Saint-Martin-des-Champs by apostolic letters, [Col. 1347C] whenever it pleases you, to furnish and allow the aforesaid number of brethren. For their support, by apostolic authority, we assign the benefice of the deanery and the prebends of our venerable brother, the bishop of Senlis, and of our sons Gregory, cardinal-deacon, and the treasurer of Auxerre. We also will and command that all benefices of deceased canons be assigned to their use.

Given at Langres, 3 Kalends of May [29 April].

### CCXCVIII. To the canons of Saint Geneviève.—That they receive honourably the monks whom he is to send to their monastery. (1148, 29 April)

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XXI, 637.]

[Col. 1347D]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the canons of Saint Geneviève: greeting and the apostolic blessing.

Whoever is known to hold the truth of the Catholic faith and the charity of true religion does not doubt, but affirms, that the Holy Roman Church is the head of all churches, and venerates it as a devoted son. Since, therefore, by God’s disposition, we are set upon it as if on a watchtower, we are compelled to provide with fatherly solicitude for all the churches of the world; and in churches which belong by right to blessed Peter we desire and wish to establish religious life. Hence it is that, wishing to establish in your church a cultivation of true religion pleasing to God, [Col. 1348A] we commanded our beloved son, the abbot of Saint-Denis, by apostolic letters to institute and plant it in the said church through our beloved son, the prior of Abbeville, whom we wish to be appointed there, and through the brethren of Saint-Martin-des-Champs, whom we wish to be assigned to his community. We therefore command your whole body by these present letters to receive them honourably and, without prejudice to your prebends, to inflict no harassment or injury upon them. If you presume to do otherwise, the sentence which our aforesaid son, the abbot of Saint-Denis, shall pronounce against you in this matter we shall, by God’s authority, hold ratified. For the support of him and the aforesaid brethren, we assign by apostolic authority the benefice of the deanery and the prebends of our venerable brother, the bishop of Senlis, and of our sons Gregory, cardinal-deacon, [Col. 1348B] and the treasurer of Auxerre. We also will and command that all benefices of deceased canons be assigned to their use.

Given at Langres, 3 Kalends of May [29 April].

### CCXCIX. Brief to Hugh, bishop of Auxerre. (1148, 7 May)

[*Gallia Christiana nova*, XII, 122.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother HUGH, bishop of Auxerre: greeting and the apostolic blessing.

After the controversy between you and our beloved son P., abbot of Cluny, concerning the monastery [Col. 1348C] of Saint German was settled in our presence, and the said lord, our son the abbot, invested by staff the abbot who presides over the brethren serving God there, a dispute has arisen between you—at which we grieve through the duty of paternal love—because in this matter the dignity of your church appears to be obscured and suppressed. Since we are compelled to provide with attentive solicitude for the peace and tranquillity of churches, by the authority of this writing we decree that what he has done shall hereafter cause no prejudice or loss to you or your church. Moreover, we forbid the abbot of Saint German henceforth to receive investiture by staff from the abbot of Cluny.

Given at Besançon, on the Nones of May [7 May].

### CCC. Privilege for the Church of the Holy Sepulchre at Jerusalem. (1148, 7 May)

[Eug. de ROZIÈRE, *Cartulaire du Saint-Sépulcre*, 42.]

[Col. 1348D]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons PETER, prior of the church of the Holy Sepulchre, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

The incomprehensible and ineffable mercy of the divine power has placed us, by this dispensation of providence, in the governance of the apostolic see, so that we ought to exercise paternal solicitude for all churches, whether near at hand or far removed. For the holy Roman [Col. 1349A] Church, which holds from God the primacy granted to it over all churches, ought, like a loving mother, to provide with vigilant care for each individual church, and especially for that of Jerusalem, in which the Redeemer of the world willed to accomplish our salvation. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions; and, following in the footsteps of our predecessors of happy memory, Honorius, Innocent, Celestine, and Lucius, Roman pontiffs, we take under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the church of the Holy Sepulchre, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions and goods have been secured to you by authentic writings of our venerable brethren, the patriarchs of the Church of Jerusalem [Col. 1349B], as well as whatever that Church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by grant of pontiffs, generosity of kings, benefactions of princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, obtain through the Lord’s favour, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors.

Among these we have considered it proper to specify by name: namely, one half of all offerings made at the Lord’s Sepulchre; the offerings of the Cross, except only on the day of Holy Parasceve [Good Friday], and when the patriarch carries it with him for some necessity; the tithes of the city of Jerusalem and of the neighbouring places, excepting the tithes of the fundae (estates); the church of St. Peter at Joppa, with [Col. 1349C] the entirety of its honour and dignity. We further ordain that no person whatsoever may alter in your church the order of canonical life which you have professed. Moreover, if you believe yourselves oppressed by anyone, you may freely appeal to the apostolic see. For we decree that you, Peter, prior, and your successors for the time being, shall have full authority, after taking counsel with your brethren, to dispose, for the honour of God and the benefit of your church, of the possessions and goods which are properly within your jurisdiction.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but that all things be preserved whole [Col. 1349D] for the use and in every respect for the benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted, without prejudice to the authority of the apostolic see and to the canonical right and reverence due to the patriarch of Jerusalem. If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly presume to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to make proper satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour, acknowledge himself or herself answerable before divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God our Redeemer Jesus Christ, and be subject at the last judgment to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve justice for the same place may there be the peace of our Lord [Col. 1350A] Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the severe Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum, have subscribed. I, Hubaldus, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Praxedes, have subscribed. I, Humbaldus, cardinal-priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Gillibertus, unworthy priest of the title of Saint Mark, have subscribed. I, Aribertus, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Anastasia, have subscribed. I, Julius, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Marcellus, [Col. 1350B] have subscribed. I, Hugo, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal-priest of the title of Pastor, have subscribed. I, Bernardus, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Clement, have subscribed. I, Jordanus, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Susanna, have subscribed. I, Oddo, cardinal-deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Octavianus, cardinal-deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed. I, John Paparo, cardinal-deacon of Saint [Col. 1350C] Adrian, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal-deacon of Saint Angelo, have subscribed. I, John, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary the New, have subscribed. I, Jacinctus, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin, have subscribed.

Given at Besançon, through the hand of Guido, cardinal-deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the Nones of May, in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1148 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the fourth year of the pontificate of our lord Pope Eugenius III.

### CCCI. Privilege for the church called the Parish of the Martyrs (at Ulx).

*(A.D. 1148, May 14.)*

*[Hist. patriae Monum. Script. 398.]*

[Col. 1350D]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons PETER, provost of the church called the Parish of the Martyrs, and his brethren, present and future, professing the canonical life, in perpetuity.

A pious request ought to be fulfilled by the effect which follows the will, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth praiseworthily and the benefit sought may undoubtedly acquire force. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions; and, following in the footsteps of our predecessor of happy memory, Pope Calixtus, we take the aforesaid Church, in which you are devoted to divine service, under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves [Col. 1351A], and strengthen it by the privilege of this present document. We decree that the canonical order known to have been established in that Church according to the Rule of blessed Augustine shall there be observed inviolate in future times; and that whatever possessions and goods in cultivated or uncultivated lands, vineyards, pastures, tithes, or other things that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, through grants of pontiffs, benefactions of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, obtain through God’s favour, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors.

Among these we have considered it proper to specify by name:

In the diocese of Turin, in the village of Ulx, the church of Saint Mary; [Col. 1351B] in the village of Beaulard, the church of St. Michael; the churches of St. Mary and St. Hippolytus of Bardonecchia, of St. John of Salbertrand, and of St. Mary of Chaumont; in the village of Lesana, the church of St. John; the churches in the valley of Cluson, namely those of Pragelato, (70) Fenestrelle, and Mentoulles; the church of Montebracco; the churches of Bagnolo; the church of Blessed Mary of Revello, with its chapels; the church of Blessed John of the parish, with its dependent churches; the church of Pietra Alba; the church of St. Christina; the church of the Holy Saviour; the church of Villarotto; the church of Almese; the churches of Villar Focchiardo; and the church of St. Mary of Susa, with all its appurtenances.

In the diocese of Alba, the church of St. Stephen, with the chapels belonging to it; in that of Acqui, the [Col. 1351C] churches of Ripalta, the churches of Canelli, and the church of St. George of Monte. In the diocese of Savona, the church of St. John of Vado, with the chapels and dependent churches belonging to it. In the diocese of Embrun, the church of St. Mary of Briançon, the church of St. Theofredus, the church of St. Marcellinus of Salta, the church of St. Pelagius of Nevasia, the church of Serveria, the church of St. Pancras, the church of Puy, the church of St. Martin of Cayreria with its chapels; the churches of the valley of Jarentona; and the church of St. Mary of Calme. In the parish village called Monasterium, one half of the whole tithe. In the diocese of Gap, the church of St. Areigius, the church of St. Lawrence of Bellomonte, with its chapel and the parish churches belonging to it. In Camposauro, [Col. 1351D] one third of the whole tithe between the two Severiascas. In the diocese of Grenoble, the church of St. John in the valley of Navigii; the churches of Cornerio: St. Mary, St. Peter, St. George, St. Agnes of Gardenco; the church of St. Peter of Avellanth; and the whole tithe of the castle called Muta; the church of Albino, the church of Osso, and the church of the face of Ganua. Also, all the churches from Lake Orsinacii as far as the hill called Altariolum; and the church of St. Christopher of Pascherio, with its chapels. In the diocese of Die, the church of St. Mary of Synard, the church of Clermont, the church of Avignon, the church of St. Paul, the church of St. William with the chapel of the castle called Toscona, and the whole tithe of that valley. In the archdiocese of Vienne, [Col. 1352A] the church of Saint Donatus with all its appurtenances, etc.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Ubaldus, cardinal of St. Praxedes. I, Ubaldus, cardinal-priest of Saints John and Paul. I, Gilibertus, unworthy priest, of the title of St. Mark. I, Aubertus, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Anastasia. I, Ingo, cardinal-priest of the title in Lucina. I, Julius, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Marcellus. I, Hugo, cardinal-priest of the title of Pastor. I, Bernardus, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Clement. I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum. [Col. 1352B] I, Odo, cardinal-deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil. I, Octavianus, cardinal-deacon of St. Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. I, John Paparo, cardinal-deacon of St. Adrian. I, Gregory, cardinal-deacon of St. Angelo. I, John, cardinal-deacon of St. Mary the New. I, Jacynthus, cardinal-deacon of St. Mary in Cosmedin.

Given at Lausanne, through the hand of Guido, cardinal-deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the second day before the Ides of May, in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1148 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the fourth year of the pontificate of our lord Pope Eugenius III.

### CCCII. Privilege for the monastery of Bellelay.

*(A.D. 1148, May 17.)*

*[HUGO, Annal. Praem., I, Pr., p. 217.]*

[Col. 1352C]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GEROLD, abbot of the monastery of Bellelay, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

It is fitting that we make suitable provision for those choosing the religious life, lest any occasion of need make them negligent or—far be it!—weaken the strength of their manner of life. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously [Col. 1352D] assent to your just petitions and take the aforesaid place, in which you are devoted to divine service, under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves, and strengthen it by the patronage of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, through grants of pontiffs, benefactions of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, obtain through the Lord’s favour, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have considered it proper to specify by name: the church of Boccourt with all its appurtenances; the church of Tharvenna with its appurtenances, as our venerable brother Ordibus (Orttiebus), bishop of Basel, reasonably granted and confirmed to you by his document; the church of St. Ursicinus of Nugerol; vineyards at Bielno; and an estate at Boescorth.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid place, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but that all things be preserved whole [Col. 1353A] for the use and in every respect for the benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted, without prejudice to the authority of the apostolic see and to the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly presume to act against it and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to make proper satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour, acknowledge himself or herself answerable before divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and our Lord, Redeemer Jesus Christ, and be subject at the last judgment to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve justice for the same place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the severe Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given at Lausanne through the hand of Guido, cardinal-deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of June, in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1148 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the fourth year of the pontificate of our lord [Col. 1353C] Pope Eugenius III.

### CCCIII. To Humbert, archbishop of Besançon, etc.—That they should fittingly punish contempt of the Roman Church in the priest who had transgressed an excommunication pronounced by him and had stolen the revenues of the monastery of Baume from the Cluniacs.

*(A.D. 1148, May 20.)*

*[BOUQUET, XV, 451.]*

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons H[UMBERT], archbishop of Besançon, P., dean, and the whole chapter of St. Stephen, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have received a complaint from the Cluniac brethren that the priest Aimo, in the church of Biliaco, [Col. 1353D] which the church of Baume possessed uninterruptedly for thirty years and more, sang for a long time while under our excommunication, and has retained for himself, partly by violence and partly by theft, the revenues of the church due to Baume. But because we neither can nor ought to fail the Cluniac brethren in the justice due to them, especially in matters pertaining to the monastery of Baume—which monastery, with all its appurtenances with which it was invested in the time of Abbot Alberic and afterwards, we bestowed upon them—we command and enjoin you by this present writing to punish fittingly and sufficiently in the aforesaid priest the transgression of our sentence and the contempt of the holy Roman Church; and to ensure that the revenues which he stole from the church of Baume are restored in full, [Col. 1354A] so that no renewed cry may reach our ears and the priest may no longer boast in the church in which for so long he despised excommunication and remained disobedient to us.

Given at Lausanne, on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of June.

### CCCIV. He takes the monastery of Rüeggisberg under protection and confirms its possessions.

*(A.D. 1148, May 27.)*

*[SOLOTHURNER, Wochenblatt, 1829, p. 555, as cited by Stettler, Regesten der Klöster von Bern, p. 11.]*

### CCCV. To Abbot Suger.—Having changed his mind, he no longer wishes monks to be sent to the church of St. Geneviève, but regular canons.

*(A.D. 1148, June 16.)*

*[MANSI, Concil., XXI, 638.]*

[Col. 1354B]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son SUGER, abbot of St. Denis, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since our Lord and Redeemer is known to be peace and truth, when he was about to ascend to the right hand of the Father he left peace to his disciples, as though by testament, commanding them to possess it in themselves and preach it to others. Hence, he is believed to be loved by Christ and reckoned among his disciples who both loves peace and strives to preserve it among those subject to him. Therefore, since we have been placed by the Lord upon the watchtower of the apostolic see and are successors of blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, we alter for the sake of peace the command which we remember having issued concerning monastic religious life in the church [Col. 1354C] of Saint Geneviève, provided that the canons of that church receive regular canons while preserving their prebends. We command that the benefices which we considered should be assigned to monks, if they had been received in the aforesaid church, be assigned by you to those canons under apostolic authority. But if they are unwilling to do this, we command that the instruction concerning the establishment of monks there be observed inviolate.

Given at Vercelli, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of July.

### CCCVI. He confirms the possessions of the Milanese monastery of Clairvaux.

*(A.D. 1148, June 23.)*

*[GIULINI, Mem. di Milan., V, 478–79.]*

### CCCVII. He commands Albero, archbishop of Trier, Albero, bishop of Verdun, and the archdeacons of the Churches of Metz and Toul, under pain of excommunication to admonish Duke Matthew to demolish a castle built near Toul.

*(A.D. 1148, June 30.)*

*[D. CALMET, Hist. de Lorraine, II, Pr., p. CCCXXXIV.]*

[Col. 1354D]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brethren A. [ADALBERO], bishop of Trier, [ALBERO], bishop of Verdun, and his beloved sons the archdeacons of the Churches of Metz and Toul, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Just as the holy Church ought in spiritual matters to shine continually in the splendour of unity, without wrinkle, stain, or schism, so in temporal matters [Col. 1355A] it ought to suffer no burdens, be disturbed by no exactions, and endure nothing extraordinary. For it is expedient that every Church, remaining immovably in the prerogative of its own status, remain free and exempt from vexation of this kind. It has been reported to us that Duke Matthew, although he promised under the kiss of peace to our venerable brother Henry, bishop of Toul, and to the men of the city of Toul who set out with him for Jerusalem, that he would provide the aid of his protection both to the church and to the city, nevertheless, setting aside consideration of the fear of God, has presumed to build near the city of Toul, contrary to the oath made by his father and to the ancient liberty of the aforesaid city and Church, a certain castle at a distance of half a mile from the city. From this construction the Church of Toul, it is said, will suffer many losses and injuries. Wishing to oppose these things in accordance with the duty of our office, we command you by this present writing [Col. 1355B] strictly to admonish him to destroy what he has presumed to build and to desist from molesting that church. If he should scorn to do so, pronounce against him also on this account a sentence of excommunication, and ensure that it is likewise observed.

Given at Pavia, on the second day before the Kalends of July.

### CCCVIII. He commands the churches of the diocese of Cremona to obey Bishop Oberto.

*(A.D. 1148, July 7.)*

*[UGHELLI, Italia sacra, IV, 604.]*

[Col. 1355C]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother OBERTO, bishop of Cremona, and to his successors canonically appointed, in perpetuity.

The holy Fathers willed that there should be diverse ranks and orders in the Church of God, so that, while inferiors render obedience and reverence to their superiors, there may arise from diversity a single harmonious connection and the administration of individual offices may be rightly conducted. With this purpose in view, venerable brother Oberto, bishop, we graciously assent to your just petitions and wish by the authority of our office to ensure that the Church of Cremona is not defrauded of its right. When we were at Cremona with our brethren, you brought before us a complaint that certain churches of Cremona [Col. 1355D] which are subject to your bishopric showed you no due reverence. Since we desire each Church to retain its own right, we decree that the churches of Cremona known to belong to you by parish right, and that part of the clergy of the church of St. Mary which ought by the same right to be subject to you, shall henceforth be subject and obedient to you and your successors, and shall render due reverence and honour to you as their own pastors and bishops of their souls. We forbid any cleric to be received into those churches by laymen, and any provost to be established without the counsel and assent of the bishop of Cremona, or of the Church if there is no bishop. We also add that the bishop of Cremona shall be received and honoured as the proper pastor in the aforesaid churches, and that due reverence and obedience in spiritual as well as temporal matters shall be rendered to him by the clerics and laity of that place. If the bishop of Cremona, or the Church, has canonically pronounced a sentence of excommunication or interdict against any of its parishioners, it shall be observed both by those belonging to the diocese of Piacenza and by those belonging to that of Cremona. But if anyone knowingly presumes rashly to contravene the page of this our decree, a cleric shall incur loss of his dignity and office, while a layman shall be deprived of ecclesiastical communion.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given at Cremona through the hand of Guido, cardinal-deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the Nones of July, [Col. 1356B] in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1148 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the fourth year of the pontificate of our lord Pope Eugenius III.

### CCCIX. Privilege for the monastery of Tolla.

*(A.D. 1148, July 7.)*

*[CAMPI, Hist. di Piacenza, I, 544.]*

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ALBERT, abbot of Tolla, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

Since without the worship of true religion neither can the unity of charity endure nor can service pleasing to God be offered, it is fitting for apostolic authority to cherish religious persons and to foster religious places in which they dwell by the protection of the apostolic see. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions and take the monastery of Tolla, in which you are devoted to divine service, under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves, strengthening it by the privilege of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions and goods it now justly and reasonably possesses, or may hereafter, through grants of pontiffs, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, obtain through God’s favour, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have considered it proper to specify by name: the place itself in which the aforesaid monastery is situated, with its parish and all its appurtenances; whatever [Col. 1356D] you possess at the castle of Arquata; the church of Mistriano, with its parish and all its appurtenances; the castle of Lavernasco, with the church of that place, its parish, and its other appurtenances; the new castle, with the church of that place, its parish, and all its appurtenances; the castle of Spelunca, and the church of that place with its parish and all its appurtenances; the castle of Molfaxi, with the churches of that place, its parishes, and its other appurtenances; the place of Rugarli, with the church of that place, its parish, and all its appurtenances; whatever you possess at Regianum with all its appurtenances; and the church of St. Dalmatius of Piacenza, with its parish and the other things belonging to it.

Upon the death of yourself, now abbot of the same place, or of any one of your successors, no one shall be set over it through any device of intrigue or violence, save one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren, shall provide to be elected from their own community, if a suitable person can be found, according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Benedict. We command that chrism, holy oil, the consecration of altars or churches, and the ordination of your clerics who are to be promoted to sacred orders be granted to you freely, without any improper exaction, by the archbishop of Milan. We grant that the burial-place of the monastery itself and of all its churches shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and final wish of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict; while preserving, nevertheless, [Col. 1357B] the rights of the churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may, in any way, on any pretext or under title of any writing, take away or diminish anything in property or in the liberty of that place from those things which have been granted by our predecessors or by the kings of the Italian realm. By the authority of the holy Roman see we forbid the bishops of the Churches of Piacenza and Parma, within whose dioceses the monastery itself or its properties appear to lie, and all others, whether nearby or distant, ever to presume to take anything except by their own right, or to claim for themselves the baptism of its parishioners—as appears in the charter of privilege formerly granted to that monastery [Col. 1357C]—or the tithes which you have possessed hitherto. If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly presume to act against it and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to make proper satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour, acknowledge himself or herself answerable before divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and our Lord, Redeemer Jesus Christ, and be subject at the last judgment to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve justice for the same church may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the severe Judge the rewards of eternal peace. [Col. 1357D] Amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Ubaldus, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Praxedes, have subscribed. I, Aribertus, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Anastasia, have subscribed. I, Ubaldus, cardinal-priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Hugo, cardinal-priest of the title in Lucina, have subscribed. I, Jordanus, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Susanna, have subscribed. I, Otto, cardinal-deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. [Col. 1358A] I, Octavianus, cardinal-deacon of St. Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed.

Given at Cremona through the hand of Guido, cardinal-deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the Nones of July, in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1148 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the fourth year of the pontificate of our lord Pope Eugenius III.

### CCCX. He declares that the church of Blessed Mary of Susa has been assigned to the Church of Ulx by himself.

*(A.D. 1148, July 7—at Cremona.)*

*[Ulciensis Eccles. Chart., p. 18.]*

### CCCXI. To the entire Roman clergy.—That chaplains should promise obedience to the rectors of the titles or churches.

*(A.D. 1148, July 15.)*

*[MANSI, Concil., XXI, 628.]*

[Col. 1358B]

EUGENIUS III, to the entire Roman clergy.

The deceitful and envious enemy of the human race, through the schismatic Arnold as though through his own limb, has brought it about that certain chaplains, insofar as lies in them dividing the unity of the Church, which admits no division, follow the error of Arnold himself and refuse to promise and render due obedience and reverence to their cardinals and archpriests. Therefore, lest by our silence we seem henceforth to give strength to the wicked acts of the aforesaid schismatic, we command and enjoin you by this present writing to avoid the aforesaid Arnold [Col. 1358C] in every way as a schismatic. But if any clerics, despisers of God and of the holy Church, should presume after receipt of this document to follow his error, we wish you to know that we shall render them utterly excluded both from ecclesiastical office and from benefice.

Given at Brescia, on the Ides of July.

### CCCXII. Bull for the church of St. Ambrose at Milan.

*(A.D. 1148, July 21.)*

*[GIULINI, Memorie di Milano, Probat., vol. V, p. 592.]*

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son MARTIN, provost, and his brethren in the church of Blessed Ambrose, devoted to divine service, present and future, in perpetuity.

[Col. 1358D] Whenever something is requested of us which seems fitting to reason and honour, it befits us gladly to grant it and to render suitable support to the desires of petitioners. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions and take your church, adorned with the relics of blessed Ambrose the confessor and of the holy martyrs Gervasius and Protasius, together with all possessions and goods assigned to your use, under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present document. We decree that whatever you now justly and canonically possess, or may hereafter obtain by grants of pontiffs, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or [Col. 1359A] other reasonable means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors.

Among these we have considered it proper to specify by name: the entire possession of the village of Axiliani, and half of the tithe with all honours belonging to that village; land at Cornaleto and Eburono; whatever you have from the share of Lauterius and his wife; fifteen solidi for the annual observance which you perform in the church of Blessed Celsus, and twelve candles—all of which are to be paid to you each year by the prelate of that church. Likewise, in the same church, three solidi which you are accustomed to have from ancient times; also the tithe which you possess at Vigonzono; and the customary refectory allowances assigned to you when the altar of Blessed Ambrose is opened on appointed occasions. We command that whatever right you have by ancient custom in the cemetery of your church and in the *cimiliarchia* [cemetery administration] be preserved to you. We also decree that your custom of carrying crosses in processions or for the burial of dead bodies, which you appear justly to possess, shall remain unimpaired. We likewise confirm to you the church of Blessed Mary the Greek, near the Cloister; whatever right you have in the church of St. George at Ponte Sesto; the hospital of St. James of Ristocano; and the refectory allowance which you have on the feast of St. Satyrus. Moreover, whatever has justly been granted, donated, or confirmed to you by authentic documents of bishops, kings, or other faithful of God, we strengthen by the protection of [Col. 1359C] our authority, and we take you yourselves under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves, without prejudice to the authority of the apostolic see and to the canonical right of the archbishop of Milan.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any other vexations; but that all things be preserved whole for the use and in every respect for the benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted. If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly presume to act against it and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to correct his or her offence by proper satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour, acknowledge himself or herself answerable before divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and our Lord, Redeemer Jesus Christ, and be subject at the last judgment to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve justice for the same place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the severe Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

Fare well.

In the circle and in the monogram:

> **MAKE FOR ME, O LORD, A SIGN FOR GOOD.**

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. [Col. 1360A] I, Hubaldus, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Praxedes, have subscribed. I, Hugo, cardinal-priest of the title in Lucina, have subscribed. I, Julius, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Marcellus, have subscribed. I, Jordanus, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Susanna, have subscribed. I, Oddo, cardinal-deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Octavianus, cardinal-deacon of St. Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed. I, John Paparo, cardinal-deacon of St. Adrian, have subscribed. I, Jacintus, cardinal-deacon of St. Mary in Cosmedin, have subscribed.

Given at Brescia through the hand of Guido, cardinal-deacon and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of August, in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1148 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the fourth year of the pontificate of our lord Pope Eugenius III.

### CCCXIII. He takes the nunnery of St. Maurice at Milan under protection and confirms its possessions.

*(A.D. 1148, July 29.)*

*[MURATORI, Antiq. Ital., V, 563.]*

[Col. 1360B]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ MARGARET, abbess of the monastery of St. Maurice Major, and her sisters, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetual remembrance.

A pious request ought to be fulfilled with effect, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth praiseworthily and the benefit sought may assuredly acquire strength. Therefore, beloved daughter in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests: we receive the aforesaid [Col. 1360C] monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service, under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions or goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, God being favorable, by grant of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and those who succeed you. Among these we have considered it proper to specify by their proper names: the church of Saint Mary at the Circle; the church of Saint Peter in the Vineyard; the church of Saint Quiricus; the church of Saint Valeria with its appurtenances; the estate of Aroxio with the church of Saint Nazarius and the church of Saint Peter; [Col. 1360D] the estate of Circlate; the estate of Purletia; the castle of Robiate with its appurtenances; the possessions which the same monastery has at Varedeo, Magnicago, Septimo, Baradaglo, Legniano, Arconate, Pistirago, and Fazione; the braida of Monte Vulpe; the braida called Ticinello; and the other possessions which the same monastery holds in Gardesana, in the Valley of Bubleidira, in Ulmeto, and in the Sarriana Valley, with their rights and all the other appurtenances aforesaid.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all shall be preserved whole [Col. 1361A] for the use, in every respect beneficial, of those for whose governance and support they have been granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the Archbishop of Milan. If anyone therefore in future, etc.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Hubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes, have subscribed. I, Hubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Aribertus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia, have subscribed. I, Jordanus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna, have subscribed. [Col. 1361B] I, Octavianus, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed. I, Johannes Papirio, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian, have subscribed. I, Gregorius, cardinal deacon of Saint Angel, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed. I, Jacintus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin, have subscribed.

Given at Brescia through the hand of Guido, cardinal deacon and chancellor, on the fourth day before the Kalends of August, in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1148 of the Incarnation of the Lord, in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### CCCXIV. Bull for the canonical community of Saint Antoninus of Piacenza. (1148, July 31.)

[CAMPI, *Hist. Eccl. Placent.*, I, I, 545.]

[Col. 1361C]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons, the canons of Saint Antoninus of Piacenza: greeting and apostolic blessing.

By these present letters we command your whole community, upon receiving this letter, humbly to request from our beloved son John, the elect, and from the church of Piacenza, within thirty days, chrism and oil for the use of the chapel of Roncalia. But if they delay giving these to you beyond the space of thirty days, then you shall have, by our authority, permission to receive these same things [Col. 1361D] from whichever Catholic bishop you prefer. Nevertheless, take the greatest care that on this account you do not rise in pride against the same elect or against the church of Piacenza.

Given at Brescia, on the second day before the Kalends of August.

### CCCXV. He confirms the privileges granted by Innocent II to the monastery of Saint Saviour and to the canonical order established there through the work of Bonifilius. (1148, August 20.)

[CORNELIUS, *Ecclesiae Venetae*, XIV, 93, from the autograph in the archive of Saint Saviour at Venice.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons BONOFILIUS and his brothers, professing the canonical life in the church of Saint Saviour situated at Rialto, [Col. 1362A] both present and future, forever.

It is fitting that we exercise watchful consideration on behalf of those choosing the religious life, lest any occasion of need make them indolent or—far be it—break the strength of their religious observance. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests; and, following in the footsteps of our predecessor Pope Innocent of happy memory, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid church of Saint Saviour, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present document. Since indeed you have resolved to observe the canonical order and live according to the Rule of blessed Augustine, willingly granting assent to your vows, we establish by apostolic authority that this [Col. 1362B] order shall remain inviolate in that church for all time. We decree that whatever possessions or goods the same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, the Lord providing, by grant of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. We likewise confirm to you the portion of the tithes from your parishioners which belongs to your church according to the sacred canons and enactments of the holy Fathers. We further forbid anyone to be set over that church through any deceitful contrivance or [Col. 1362C] violence, except one whom the brothers of that place collectively, or the sounder part of their counsel, shall canonically have provided to be elected.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb you personally or the church itself, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all shall be preserved whole for the use, in every respect beneficial, of those for whose governance they have been granted, saving the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. Furthermore, no one shall presume unlawfully to receive or retain parishioners of that church. If anyone knowingly attempts to violate this page of our constitution, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not [Col. 1362D] make amends for the offence by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor, and at the final judgment be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve their rights for that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Ubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes, have subscribed. I, Aribertus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Pastor, have subscribed. I, Bernardus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Clement, have subscribed. I, Jordanus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna, have subscribed. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. [Col. 1363A] I, Joannes Paparo, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed.

Given at Brescia through the hand of Guido, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of September, in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1148 of the Incarnation of the Lord, in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### CCCXVI. To Gerard, bishop of Bologna. (1148, August 24.)

[SAVIOLI, *Annal. Bologn.*, I, I, 216.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother GERARD, bishop of Bologna: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Because you have diligently undertaken, in accordance with our command, to admonish the consuls and people of Bologna [Col. 1363B] that they should effectively and commendably come to the aid of our faithful people of Nonantola against the attacks of the Modenese, we rejoice with paternal affection and thank your prudence. Therefore, that they may especially retain by this means the favor of blessed Peter and our goodwill, we ask, admonish, and exhort your brotherhood in the Lord not to desist from the good purpose which you have begun, but to endeavor, out of reverence for your mother, the Holy Roman Church, to afford the aforesaid faithful people of ours the timely assistance of your aid and counsel. We have indeed firmly admonished our beloved sons, the people of Reggio and Parma, by our letters not to provide the Modenese with any assistance, support, or counsel against the people of Nonantola. [Col. 1363C] Furthermore, we wish it to be known to your brotherhood that, by the common counsel of our brethren, both the cardinals and our brother Peregrinus, patriarch of Aquileia, and of very many bishops who had assembled, we have deprived the city of Modena forever of episcopal dignity, so that henceforth no bishop shall be established either in the city or throughout the whole diocese of Modena.

Given at Brescia, on the ninth day before the Kalends of September.

### CCCXVII. He confirms to the monastery of the Holy Saviour and the martyr Saint Julia, in the diocese of Brescia, of the Cassinese order, all its goods and complete exemption, and grants other privileges. (1148, September 8.)

[MARGARINI, *Bullar. Casin.*, II, 167.]

[Col. 1363D]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the daughter in Christ RICHELDA, abbess of the monastery of our Saviour and of Saint Julia, virgin and martyr, called the New [Monastery], situated in the city of Brescia, and to her sisters, both present and future, forever.

[Col. 1364A]

Though we consider ourselves debtors to all ecclesiastical persons by the office of the apostolate imposed upon us by God, it is fitting that we apply ourselves with a more earnest concern of charity to those whom we know to serve Almighty God in the observance of true religion and to reside continually in churches belonging to the right of blessed Peter. Therefore, beloved daughter in the Lord, Abbess Richelda, granting due and kindly assent to your reasonable requests, we strengthen by the privilege of the Apostolic See and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the monastery of the blessed virgin martyr Julia, entrusted, by the Lord’s gift, to your care, which is known to have been built within the city of Brescia by Queen Ansa of noble memory. We decree that whatever estates, possessions, or goods this monastery now justly and lawfully possesses from the munificence of the aforesaid queen, from the gifts of emperors of illustrious memory who undertook the governance of the realm after her, or from gifts conferred by other faithful persons—and whatever it may hereafter acquire, the Lord providing, by grant of pontiffs, generosity of kings or princes, [Col. 1364B] offerings of the faithful, or other just means—shall remain secure and unimpaired for you, your sisters, and those who succeed you in the same religious life. Among these we have considered it proper to specify by their proper names: Sermione, namely, with two churches, those of our Lord the Saviour and of the martyr Saint Vitus; Cervanica with the church of the martyr Saint Julia; Nubularia with the church of Saint Lawrence; Berciagum with the two churches of Saint Zeno and Saint Stephen; the village of Magone with the church of Saint Alexander; Thimolina with the church of Saint Julia; Barbada with the church of Saint Mary; Alfianum with the church of Saint Julia; Montecellum with the church of Saint Mary; Vovum with the church of Saint Peter and Saint [Col. 1364C] Lawrence; Calvatone with the churches of Saint Mary and Saint Julia; Genudolaria with the church of Saint Michael; Ciconiaria with the church of Saint Mary; Bontenagum with the church of Saint Martin the Confessor; Miliarina with the church of Saint Julia; and Sermida. Moreover, we likewise confirm to you all other estates, villages, castles, churches, and everything belonging to the same monastery. By the present decree we also establish that the aforesaid monastery, endowed with the protection of the Apostolic See and royal defence, shall never be reduced under the power or jurisdiction of any other person, so that no priest, unless invited by the abbess of that place, may presume to celebrate there the solemnities of Mass.

Therefore it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but all shall be preserved whole for the use, in every respect beneficial, of the handmaids of Christ, for whose governance and support they have been granted. Upon the death of you, the present abbess of that place, or of any of those who succeed you in the same office, no one shall be set over it by any deceitful contrivance or violence, except one whom the sisters by common consent, or the sounder part of the sisters’ counsel, shall, according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Benedict, provide to be elected. Moreover, we likewise confirm to you the church of Saint Peter in Solato [Col. 1365A] and the chapel of Saint Julia at Pradellis. We also grant the abbess of that place permission to build churches in honor of God, and likewise confirm the liberty granted to the aforesaid monastery by emperors and kings, both in establishing markets and in building castles, wherever she wishes, on the lands of that monastery for its benefit. Nor shall any bishop, duke, marquis, count, viscount, or any great or small person presume to exercise jurisdiction or render judgment in any places of the monastery, hold any court without the abbess’s permission, alienate in any manner its spiritual or temporal property, inflict injury upon it, or dare to exact fodrum, mansiaticum, ripaticum, provisions, [Col. 1365B] or any other dues. Furthermore, we confirm to you the tithes of newly cultivated land and the fruits of your labor, which you cultivate at your own expense, and jurisdiction over the servants and free persons belonging to your monastery. Chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars and churches, ordinations of the abbess, nuns, or your clerics who are to be promoted to sacred orders, and whatever pertains to sacred ministry, you shall receive from whichever Catholic bishops you prefer, provided that they grant these things to you without depravity or any reproach, as it is known that they were granted to your monastery, in consideration of the frailty [Col. 1365C] of the female sex, by our predecessors of happy memory, Paul, Calixtus, and Innocent, Roman pontiffs. We also confirm to you the port of Piacenza and its river-toll.

If in future any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly attempts rashly to violate this page of our constitution, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not make amends by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honor; let that person know that he or she is answerable before divine judgment for the wrong committed; let that person be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and at the final judgment let that person be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve their rights for that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action [Col. 1365D] and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Ubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes, have subscribed. I, Ubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Aribertus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia, have subscribed. I, Julius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus, have subscribed. I, Bernardus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Clement, have subscribed. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of the title of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Octavianus, cardinal deacon of the title of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed. I, Joannes Paparo, cardinal deacon of the title of Saint Adrian, have subscribed. [Col. 1366A] I, Gregorius, cardinal deacon of the title of Saint Angel, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of the title of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed. I, Jacintus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin, have subscribed.

Given at Brescia through the hand of Guido, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the sixth day before the Ides of September, in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1148 of the Incarnation of the Lord, in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### CCCXVIII. Privilege for the church of Blessed Mary of Brescia. (1148, September 9.)

[GRADONICUS, *Pontif. Brix. Series*, p. 305.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons, the canons of the church of Blessed Mary of Brescia, both present and those to be canonically appointed in the future, [Col. 1366B] forever.

The principle of equity and justice persuades us to preserve or confer upon churches enduring security for their property and safeguards of unshaken strength. For it is not fitting that clerics called to the Lord’s portion should be harassed by the perverse vexations of wicked people. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, following in the footsteps of our predecessor Pope Honorius of happy memory, we graciously assent to your just requests; and we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid church of blessed Mary, Mother of God and ever-Virgin, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions or goods you now justly and canonically possess, whether from gifts of Catholic bishops [Col. 1366C] of the city of Brescia or of other faithful of God, or may hereafter acquire, the Lord providing, by grant of pontiffs, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have considered it proper to specify by their proper names: the chapel of Saint Augustine; the chapel of Saint Faustinus in the Castle; the chapel of Saint Urban; the chapel of Saint Cassian; the chapel of Saint Margaret; the chapel of Saint Mary of Colcaria, with the *costa colcariae* and the other property belonging to that estate; the chapel of Saint Syrus; the chapels of Saint Clement and Saint Cecilia; the chapel of the holy [Col. 1366D] martyrs Marcellinus and Peter; the chapel of Saint Mary near Saint Euphemia; the chapel of the village of Calione; four chapels in Buticino and three chapels in the estate of Flere; the chapel at Castello Nuovo; the chapel in the castle of Capriano; the chapel at Uusado; the chapel of the holy martyrs Gervasius and Protasius at Pontecaralo; the chapels of Saint Mary and Saint Martin in the same place; the chapel of Virgiliano; the chapel of Saint Mary at Posterula; the monastery of Saint Peter at Flumicello; the chapel of Saint George at Scisciano; the chapel of Saint Mary at Urago; the chapel of Saint Emilian at Subvinea; the chapel of Saint George at Cellatica; two chapels at Salis, of Saint Thomas and Saint Stephen; the chapel of Saint Saviour in the castle of Nave; the chapel [Col. 1367A] of Saint Zeno at Andulo; the chapel of Saint Faustinus at Bareliaca; the chapel of Saint Michael at Nubilento; in the settlement of Maurus, two chapels, of Saint Stephen and Saint Quiricus; the hospice of Saint George at Sisinisco; the chapel of the settlement of Paulus; the chapel of Saint Philastrius in Casale; the church of Saint John at Ruvereto; the chapel of Saint Faustinus at Castroclare; the chapel of Saint Martin at Adro; two chapels in the estate of Casale, of Saint Mary and Saint Peter; at Castellione, two chapels of Saint Mary and Saint Emilian; at Mairano, the chapel of Saint Andrew the Apostle. Moreover, whatever Gerard Zanzulus and his wife Berta, and Richelda, widow of the late Gerard Bonizo, have reasonably bestowed from their own goods; likewise the diadem and *ingelenda* [uncertain term] of your church. [Col. 1367B] All tithes of the citizens, suburban inhabitants, and territory belonging to the city’s baptismal church, as they have hitherto been peacefully and reasonably possessed by your predecessors. The possessions which you lawfully hold for your support in towns, villages, or other estates, in woods, mills, or fisheries. Further, we decree that the possessions or houses of the clerics and the people of those possessions shall be free from fodrum and other public dues, as has been established by the emperors.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but all shall be preserved whole [Col. 1367C] for the use, in every respect beneficial, of those for whose support and governance they have been granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right and reverence due to the diocesan bishop. If in future any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly attempts rashly to violate this page of our constitution, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not make amends by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honor; let that person know that he or she is answerable before divine judgment for the wrong committed; let that person be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and at the final judgment let that person be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve their rights for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, [Col. 1367D] so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Hubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes, have subscribed. I, Aribertus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Pastor, have subscribed. I, Jordanus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna, have subscribed. I, Oddo, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Octavianus, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed. [Col. 1368A] I, Gregorius, cardinal deacon of Saint Angel, have subscribed. I, Joannes, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary Nova, have subscribed. I, Jacintus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin, have subscribed.

Given at the monastery of Leon through the hand of Guido, cardinal deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the fifth day before the Ides of September, in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1148 of the Incarnation of the Lord, in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### CCCXIX. He entrusts to Henry, bishop of Moravia, the affairs to be carried out by G[uidus], cardinal deacon and legate sent to Poland, both there and in the other land recently illuminated by the light of the Christian faith. (1148, September 13.)

[THEINER, *Disquis. critic.*, 211.]

[Col. 1368B]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable bishop of Moravia: greeting and apostolic blessing.

One who trusts in the charity of his brethren does not refuse to entrust to them what must be done. Since therefore we have great confidence in your person, by these present letters we command you diligently to assist our beloved son G., cardinal deacon, a prudent and honorable man, to whom we have entrusted our office in the regions of Poland, as vicar of the Apostolic See in the matters incumbent upon him both in Poland and in that land recently illuminated by the light of the Christian faith; and to endeavor to provide him with aid and counsel, so that, having obtained assistance through the support or favor of your discernment, [Col. 1368C] you may show how closely you are bound to the Roman Church by the bond of charity, and he may, through His mercy, accomplish things pleasing to God and fruitful for humankind.

Given at Parma, on the Ides of September.

### CCCXX. He praises Abbot Suger for having ordered the condition of the church of Saint Genevieve. (1148.)

[MANSI, *Concil.*, XXI, 640.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved son SUGER, abbot of Saint Denis: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since it belongs to the office of religious persons to love and defend religion and to endeavor with diligent [Col. 1368D] concern to advance it, we commend your discernment in the Lord, rejoice with you in the duty of paternal charity, and give you thanks because, through your care and labor, a religious observance pleasing to God is known to have been established in the church of Saint Genevieve and, by God’s grace, preserved. But since the affection of devotion in good sons is enlarged by paternal exhortations, we admonish and exhort your belovedness in the Lord diligently to assist the brothers of the aforesaid church, as you have well begun; so that Almighty God, who is the author of good will and the examiner of examination, may adorn your person in the present with good things pleasing to himself, make it rejoice with the saints in eternal joys in the future, and enable us to repay your care with worthy thanksgivings. [Col. 1369A] Furthermore, let your belovedness strive by every means to ensure that the treasure and instruments of that church, which are still held by secular canons, are assigned to the abbot and brothers residing in that church.

### CCCXXI. He confirms the monastery of Saint Mary in the Arena at Wrocław. (1148, October 19.)

[STENZEL, *Scrip. R. Sil.*, II, 164.]

### CCCXXII. To John, elect of Piacenza. (1148, November 9, note.)

[MURATORI, *Rer. Ital. Script.*, II, I, 208.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved [Col. 1369B] son JOHN, elect of Piacenza: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is not unknown to us, and we do not believe it has slipped from your [and from your] memory, that, both by our letters to the church of Piacenza and orally in your presence, we gave orders that on the feast of Saint Luke most recently past you should appear before us, answer our venerable brother Moses, archbishop of Ravenna, and prepare to carry out what justice should dictate . . . [having prepared]. But because you evaded appearing before us by the aforesaid date, or sending letters of response which might have shown some reasonable cause, after carefully examining the privileges and writings of our predecessors and our own, and having taken counsel with our brethren, [Col. 1369C] we have adjudged that you and your successors, the elect of Piacenza, shall receive consecration without contradiction from the archbishop of Ravenna as your proper metropolitan, and shall render him obedience and reverence without troublesome difficulty. Therefore, by these present letters [from us], we command and order that by the octave of Epiphany you go to the aforesaid brother, the archbishop of Ravenna, and receive consecration from him as your proper metropolitan; and if you do not do so, from this moment we suspend you from the administration of the church of Piacenza.

Given at Pisa, on the fifth day before the Ides of November.

### CCCXXIII. He orders the clergy and people of Piacenza to obey their metropolitan, the Archbishop of Ravenna. (1148, November 9.)

[Ibid.]

[Col. 1369D]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons, the clergy and people of Piacenza: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Just as one who obeys maintains the safeguard of virtues through obedience, so one who disobeys introduces an accumulation of sins through disobedience. For rebellion is as the sin of divination, and refusal to comply is like the crime of idolatry. Therefore, by these present letters we command and order that you render obedience and reverence [Col. 1370A] to our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Ravenna, as your metropolitan, lest an angry complaint concerning you come to our ears and we be compelled to punish your disobedience more strictly.

Given at Pisa, on the fifth day before the Ides of November.

### CCCXXIV. To Moses, Archbishop of Ravenna.—That the elect bishops of Piacenza shall receive consecration from him and his successors. (1148, November 16.)

[MANSI, *Concil.*, XXI, 665.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother MOSES, Archbishop of Ravenna: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1370B]

After the death of our venerable brother Arduinus, bishop of good memory, our beloved sons, the canons of Piacenza, elected our beloved son John, abbot of Columba, as their father and bishop; and, when we were at Auxerre, they humbly requested through their messengers that the election might receive the strengthening protection of our authority. But wishing to preserve its right to the church of Ravenna as to our special daughter, we did not then consider their petition admissible. Later, however, when these same sons appeared before us at Trier, they more insistently sought the same thing from us, asserting that unless the election were confirmed the possessions and goods of the bishopric would be excessively devastated [Col. 1370C] and consumed, and that there was no person who could answer you and the church of Ravenna on this matter, although they said they had many arguments why the elect of Piacenza should not receive consecration from the Archbishop of Ravenna. Therefore, wishing in the duty of paternal charity to provide for the needs of the church of Piacenza, we ordered by apostolic letters, with the right of the church of Ravenna reserved in all respects, that on the feast of Saint Luke most recently past he should appear before us, prepared to answer you and carry out whatever justice might dictate. But when we arrived at Pavia, you, brother archbishop, in the presence of our beloved son the elect and the clerics of Piacenza, humbly requested that we should hear more carefully the documents and arguments of the church of Ravenna and impose upon them a canonical conclusion. We deferred hearing them until the date appointed for both parties, [Col. 1370D] and gave orders both there and to the other party that, setting aside every opposition, you should come before us on the stated date. Since, therefore, on the appointed date the same elect had contemptuously failed to appear before us, either personally or through representatives able adequately to state his case, after carefully examining the privileges of our predecessors of happy memory, Gelasius, Calixtus, Honorius, and Innocent, Roman pontiffs, and their writings and our own, which contained commands that our aforesaid brother Arduinus of good memory should humbly obey the Archbishop of Ravenna as his metropolitan, and after taking counsel with our brethren, we have adjudged that the elect of Piacenza [Col. 1371A] and those who succeed him shall receive consecration without contradiction from you, brother archbishop, and your successors as their metropolitans, and shall henceforth render to them subjection, obedience, and reverence as to their proper metropolitan, without troublesome difficulty, saving in all things the authority of the Apostolic See. But if anyone knowingly violates this page of our determination, etc.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church.

I, etc.

Given at Pisa through the hand of Guido, cardinal deacon and chancellor, on the fourth day before the Ides of November, in the twelfth indiction, in the year 1148 of the Incarnation of the Lord, in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### CCCXXV. Privilege for the church of Saint Mary of Luni. (1148, November 11.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, I, 845.]

[Col. 1371B]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother GOTIFREDUS, bishop of Luni, and to his canonically instituted successors, forever.

Placed by the Lord’s disposal upon the lofty watchtower of the Apostolic See, and bound by the office of the apostolate entrusted to us, we ought to love our brother bishops and preserve to the churches committed to them by God their rights. Therefore, venerable brother in Christ, Bishop Gotifredus, granting with due kindness favorable assent to your just requests, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves [Col. 1371C] the church of blessed Mary, Mother of God and ever-Virgin, at Luni, over which you are known, God being the author, to preside, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions or goods the same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, the Lord providing, by grant of pontiffs, gifts of kings, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors.
