Concerning this we have sent letters to the count himself and have earnestly urged your brotherhood to admonish him to cease harassing the aforesaid brother of ours.

Therefore we command your brotherhood by these present letters that, if the aforesaid count, after being admonished by you, refuses to restore his men to the said brother and to desist from molesting him, you shall earnestly endeavour to punish such presumption against both the person and the land of that count. Moreover, since, as has become known to us from that brother’s own account, you love and honour him as the duty of your office requires, this is pleasing to us; and we earnestly request your brotherhood henceforth to love that same brother of ours still more warmly, for the reverence of blessed Peter and of ourselves and out of the affection of charity.

### DLXVI. To Guerric, abbot of St Vedast.—He exhorts him to obey Godescalc, bishop of Arras, and to pay ten solidi for Botelgeria.  
*(A.D. 1153, February.)*

[BALUZE, *Miscellanea*, Lucae edition, II, 169.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son GUERRIC, abbot of St Vedast: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1583D] The order of reason demands and the integrity of justice requires that we should strive to preserve our rights unimpaired in such a way that we are in no respect seen to deprive our brother bishops of their rights. Therefore, as our predecessor Pope Innocent, of blessed memory, is known to have commanded your predecessor, so we likewise command and order your devotion to promise obedience to the venerable brother Godescalc, bishop of Arras, and to show due reverence and subjection with regard to the things which you are known to possess from the Church of Arras.

Furthermore, that brother of ours complained that you unjustly withhold from him ten solidi which your predecessor is known to have paid every year to the predecessor of the aforesaid brother for Botelgeria. Therefore, by the authority of these present letters [Col. 1584A] we command you that, if what the aforesaid man has set before us is true, you restore them in full to that brother of ours.

### DLXVII. At Bishop Hermann’s request, he takes the Church of Verdun under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges.  
*(A.D. 1153, February 6, Rome, at St Peter’s.)*

[Unpublished.—See JAFFÉ, *Regesta Romanorum Pontificum*, p. 651.]

### DLXVIII. To Abbot Wibald.—He commends to him his envoys to Emperor Frederick.  
*(A.D. 1153, February 8.)*

[MARTÈNE, *Amplissima Collectio*, II, 558.]

[Col. 1584B] EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son WIBALD, abbot of Stavelot: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We more securely entrust to those in whose devotion and sincere charity we have greater confidence matters which must be advanced and directed for the honour of God, the Church, and the realm. Accordingly, we have thought fit earnestly to commend to your affection our beloved sons B., cardinal priest of St Clement, and G., cardinal deacon of St Angelo—wise and honourable men indeed—whom we are sending from our side into the presence of our dearest son Frederick, illustrious king of the Romans. By these present letters we command you to receive them honourably, treat them honourably, and diligently assist them, for the reverence of blessed Peter and of ourselves, in carrying out and completing the matters which we have entrusted to them for negotiation and arrangement with our aforesaid son. Thus, by the Lord’s bounty, the honour of God’s Church and the enlargement of the realm may result from your care and labour, and we may be obliged to thank you.

Given at Rome, on the sixth day before the Ides of February.

### DLXIX. To Bernard, archbishop of Tarragona.—He again orders him to obey the archbishop of Toledo.  
*(A.D. 1153, February 9.)*

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XXI, 675.]

He offends the clemency of the divine Majesty and the integrity of the heavenly Knower, who has been appointed Judge, if he abandons justice for anyone’s glory, regard for persons, [Col. 1584D] or humility. For the scales of justice are even. And we, established by the Lord’s ordering upon the lofty watchtower of the apostolic see and exercising Christ’s embassy, are debtors in their due rights to the greater and lesser alike, the wise and the foolish.

For we remember that already twice we commanded you by apostolic decree to obey the archbishop of Toledo, as your primate, with due humility; or, if you believed that you had some legal claim against him, to answer concerning those matters before our presence, at the Easter most recently past, either in person or through sufficient representatives, to the aforesaid brother, the archbishop of Toledo, or to his envoys. Yet you have hitherto taken care to put neither of these things into effect—a matter at which [Col. 1585A] we greatly wonder. Since the Church of Toledo therefore does not desist from its complaint, and we neither can nor ought to fail it in its right, we command and strictly enjoin you again by repeated letters, without delay, to recognize the venerable brother Ildefonsus, archbishop of that Church, as your primate and render him due obedience; or, at the next solemnity of the Lord’s Resurrection, to send sufficient representatives into our presence, setting aside every pretext. If you neglect this, then, with the Lord’s help, we shall by no means permit that aforesaid Church to be defrauded of its right.

Given at Rome, at St Peter’s, on the fifth day before the Ides [Col. 1585B] of February.

### DLXX–DLXXI. To John, archbishop of Toledo.—He confirms the primacy of Toledo.  
*(A.D. 1153, February 13.)*

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XXI, 670.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother JOHN, archbishop of Toledo, and to his successors canonically appointed, in perpetuity.

The Church recognizes that the power of binding and loosing in heaven and on earth was bestowed principally by the Lord’s authority upon blessed Peter and his successors in the words with which the same Lord addressed Peter: “Whatever you bind on earth shall be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven” [Matthew 16]. Likewise, the confirmation both of his own faith and of another’s faith is prepared for him by that same God when it is said to him: “I have prayed for you, Peter, that your faith may not fail; and when once you have turned back, strengthen your brothers” [Luke 22]. It is therefore fitting that we, although unworthy, who sit in the place of blessed Peter, should, insofar as divine clemency has granted us knowledge and ability, correct what is wrong, confirm what is right, and so order throughout the whole Church matters requiring arrangement according to the judgment of the eternal Judge, that our judgment may come forth from His presence and our eyes behold equity [Psalm 16].

Therefore, beloved brother in Christ, Archbishop John, we grant favourable assent to your just petitions; and, adhering to the footsteps of our predecessors of happy memory, Honorius and Lucius, Roman pontiffs, we decree by the authority of the apostolic see through this page of privilege that you shall hold the dignity of primacy throughout all the kingdoms of the Spains. You are to use the pallium granted to your charity by the apostolic see in the celebration of Mass only on the principal feasts: namely, on the three days at the Nativity of the Lord, at Epiphany, at Hypapanton [Hypapante; the Presentation of the Lord], on the Lord’s Supper, on Holy Saturday, on the three days of Easter, at the Ascension, and at Pentecost; on the feasts of blessed Mary, St Michael, and St John the Baptist; on all feasts of the apostles and of those martyrs whose relics [Col. 1586A] rest in your church; on the feasts of St Martin and St Ildefonsus, confessors; at the commemoration of All Saints; at the consecrations of churches, bishops, and clerics; on the annual day of your consecration; and on the feasts of Saints Isidore and Leander.

All the bishops of the Spains shall look to you as primate and shall refer to you anything arising among them worthy of dispute, saving nevertheless in all matters the authority of the apostolic see. We further strengthen the Church of Toledo by the stability of this present privilege, confirming to it the district of Complutum with its boundaries, as well as all churches which it is known to have possessed of ancient right. Moreover, we decree that the episcopal sees of Osma, Segovia, Sagunto, and Palencia shall be subject to the same Church of Toledo as to their metropolitan. The rest, however, which in ancient times were subject to it, when Almighty God in His merciful condescension restores them to the power of Christians, we decree by the authority of this decree shall be returned to their proper head.

Furthermore, we subject to your jurisdiction, on the following condition, the dioceses of those cities which, under Saracen invasion, lost their own metropolitans: so long as they remain without their own metropolitans, they shall be subject to you as to their proper metropolitan. But if any metropolitan sees are restored to their proper condition, each diocese shall be restored to its own metropolitan, so that it may rejoice under the rule of its own shepherd at the bestowal of God’s gift. If therefore in future any ecclesiastical [Col. 1586C] or secular person, etc.

Given at Rome, at St Peter’s, through the hand of the scribe of the Holy Roman Church, on the Ides of February, in the first indiction, in the year 1152 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the eighth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### DLXXII. To the bishops of the Spains.—That they obey the archbishop of Toledo as primate.  
*(A.D. 1153, February 13.)*

[Ibid., 675.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brothers, the bishops and archbishops established throughout the Spains: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The clemency of the apostolic see customarily preserves for each Church and ecclesiastical person its own dignity and right. Therefore we, to whom the care of all Churches especially belongs, received kindly the venerable brother Ildefonsus [John], archbishop of Toledo, when he came to us; and, having examined the privileges of our predecessors, confirmed to him the dignity of primacy throughout all the kingdoms of the Spains, according to the tenor of those privileges. Sending him back to his own see with the favour of the apostolic see and the support of our letters, we command and strictly enjoin your whole community to take care to show him, as your primate, canonical obedience [Col. 1587A] and due reverence without any contradiction. For it is fitting that one who rejoices to preside over many subjects should in no way be ashamed to be subject to his own prelates.

Given at Rome, at St Peter’s, on the Ides of February.

### DLXXIII. He takes the monastery of Ellwangen under protection and confirms its privileges and possessions.  
*(A.D. 1153, February 19—Rome, at St Peter’s.)*

[KHAM, *Hierarchia Augustana*, II, 32.]

### DLXXIV. To Hu., dean, and the canons of Toul.—That a canon of St Deodatus, who, while affected by illness and not in possession of himself, made a promise of “the religious life,” should not be compelled to fulfil the pledge.  
*(A.D. 1153, February 19.)*

[MABILLON, *Annales Benedictini*, VI, 523.]

[Col. 1587B]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Hu., dean, and the canons of the Church of Toul: greeting and apostolic blessing.

J., canon of the church of St Deodatus, the bearer of these letters, came to the apostolic see and stated in our hearing that his dean, A., [lacuna] maintains that he ought to enter religious life because he asserts that J., while suffering from illness, promised this in his presence. J., however, firmly asserts that he does not remember having made this promise; or, if he did promise it, he was, as he asserts, so far removed from his right mind that, because of the extreme severity of his illness, he did not know what he was doing. Nor was he tonsured, nor did he assume the habit of religion.

Certainly, if this man’s allegation is supported by the truth, it does not appear that he should be compelled to enter a stricter life on the basis of such a promise. We have referred the truth of the matter to your discernment for investigation, commanding you by these present letters, after summoning before you both this man and those who bring a claim against him in this matter, to examine it diligently. If you find his allegation supported by truth, decree that he is to be held released from the stricter life on the basis of that promise.

Given at Rome, at St Peter’s, on the eleventh day before the Kalends of March.

### DLXXV. Privilege for the monastery of Cantavensis.  
*(A.D. 1153, March 3.)*

[MANRIQUE, *Annales Cistercienses*, II, 195.]

[Col. 1587D]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons RADULPHUS, abbot of the monastery of Cantavensis, and his brethren, present and future, in perpetuity.

Whenever that is requested of us which is recognized to accord with honor and religion, it befits us willingly to grant it and to afford suitable support to the desires of petitioners. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, favorably assenting to your just petitions, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid church, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the protection of this present document [Col. 1588A]. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by the grant of pontiffs, the bounty of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, by the Lord’s favor, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these, we confirm expressly to you and to your church, through you, the grange called Horta with its appurtenances. Moreover, from the produce which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or from the sustenance of your animals, let no one presume to demand tithes from you.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions [Col. 1588B], retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; rather, let all things be preserved intact for the use and benefit in every respect of those for whose governance and support they were granted. If any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after a second or third admonition, unless he correct his presumption by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the rank of his power and honor; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the wrong he has committed; let him be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and at the final judgment let him be subject to stern retribution. But upon all who preserve their rights to that same place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ [Col. 1588C], so that here they may receive the fruit of good works and before the strict Judge find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Given at Rome, at St. Peter’s, through the hand of Boso, scribe of the Holy Roman Church, on the fifth day before the Nones of March [3 March], in the first indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1152, in the eighth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### DLXXVI. Privilege for the monastery of Bonneval, granted in precisely the same words, on the same day and in the same year as above.  
*(A.D. 1153, 3 March.)*

[Ibid.]

Given at Rome, at St. Peter’s, through the hand of Boso, scribe of the Holy Roman Church, on the fifth day before the Nones [Col. 1588D] of March [3 March], in the first indiction, in the year 1152, in the eighth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### DLXXV. To the canons of St. Peter’s, Rome.—Concerning the fourth part of the offerings granted to them.  
*(A.D. 1153, 10 April.)*

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 632.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons BERNARD, cardinal-priest of St. Clement’s and archpriest of the church of Blessed Peter, and to the other canons of the same church, present and future, canonically appointed, forever.

The partnership of the blessed Peter and Paul is so eminent and so glorious that, although both are teachers of the nations [Col. 1589A], authors of martyrs, and princes of priests, and although among all the apostles they excel by a certain special prerogative, they suffer no inequality in heaven according to their merits. To Peter, our Lord Jesus Christ himself, our Savior, entrusted the keys of the kingdom of heaven; Paul was chosen by God so that through his preaching he might fill the kingdom of heaven from the multitude of the nations. Peter is the rock and foundation of faith, and, lest we fall, sustains us firmly in its solidity. Paul, lest we be wounded by the perverse doctrine of heretics, arms us with the integrity of moral life and the invincible reasoning of faith. Peter, holding primacy, binds and looses by his authority. Paul, the diligent preacher, lest anything blameworthy or deserving of binding appear in us, fortifies us beforehand by his wonderful exhortation. Peter [Col. 1589B] is our support and house of strength, and we have been planted and rooted in his faith. Paul, the vessel of election, called those predestined and chosen by God with the sound of the heavenly trumpet; and, praying unceasingly for us that we may not stray from faith and truth, he protects us by interceding with God.

Therefore, since these two greatest seedbeds of God, illuminating the Church, shine forth with equal and friendly splendor and brotherly love, equity and justice urge that we, though unworthy, who perform Christ’s office on earth and are seen to sit in the chair of the same prince of the apostles, should love the household of Blessed Peter with paternal affection and assist it in its needs with pious provision. Moved, therefore, by the obligation of this consideration, beloved sons in the Lord, we grant to you, with the consent of our brother bishops and cardinals, by apostolic authority, and confirm by this present document, the fourth [Col. 1589C] part of all offerings which arise from the altar of the same Blessed Peter the Apostle, both from the chest and from all the ministries of that church, except the ministry of Blessed Leo. You shall always have full liberty, whenever you wish, to retain and keep these offerings in your own hands, or, with the consent of us and our successors, to sell them to whomever you wish—while in every other matter the free administration and custody of that church remain reserved in the hands of us and our successors.

[Col. 1589D] We have judged it fitting to do this so that you, laboring diligently day and night in the praises of God, both in celebrating Masses and in singing Matins and the other Hours with attentive care and fittingly, for the salvation of the living and the dead, may honor the aforesaid church of Blessed Peter with the service due to it; and so that the faithful of God, visiting the thresholds of the apostles with due devotion, may always hold that place in greater devotion and veneration. We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may presume, by rash audacity, to violate or in any manner disturb this page of our grant. If any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter should presume to attempt this, then, after a second or third admonition, unless he correct his presumption by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the rank of his power [Col. 1590A] and honor; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the wrong he has committed; let him be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and at the final judgment let him be subject to stern retribution. But upon all who preserve this our constitution for that same place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good works and hereafter find the rewards of eternal peace.

Amen, amen, amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Ymarus, bishop of Tusculum, have subscribed. [Col. 1590B] I, Hugh, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Callistus, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Chrysogonus, have subscribed. I, Hubaldus, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Praxedes, have subscribed. I, Manfred, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Sabina, have subscribed. I, Aribertus, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Anastasia, have subscribed. I, Hubaldus, cardinal-priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal-priest of the title of Pastor, have subscribed. [Col. 1590C] I, Astaldus, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Prisca, have subscribed. I, Gerardus, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Stephen on the Caelian Hill, have subscribed. I, John Paparo, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Lawrence in Damaso, have subscribed. I, John, cardinal-priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius, have subscribed. I, Centius, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Lawrence in Lucina, have subscribed. I, Henry, cardinal-priest of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus, have subscribed. I, Oddo, cardinal-deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal-deacon of St. Mary in the Portico [Col. 1590D], have subscribed. I, Hyacinthus, cardinal-deacon of St. Mary in Cosmedin, have subscribed. I, John, cardinal-deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Gerardus, cardinal-deacon of St. Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed. I, Odo, cardinal-deacon of St. Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed. I, Bernard, cardinal-deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian beside the Temple of Romulus, have subscribed.

Given at Rome, at St. Peter’s, through the hand of Boso, scribe of the Holy Roman Church, on the fourth [Col. 1591A] day before the Ides of April [10 April], in the first indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1153, in the ninth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

Place of the lead seal.

### DLXXVIII. Bull by which the monastery of Sarlat, founded by the princes Pippin and Charles, is received under St. Peter’s protection.  
*(A.D. 1153, 3 May.)*

[*Gallia Christiana*, new edition, Documents, II, 496.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son RAYMOND, abbot of the monastery of St. Savior at Sarlat, and to his successors canonically appointed [Col. 1591B] forever, etc.

Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Raymond, favorably granting assent to your just petitions, we receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves the monastery of Sarlat, over which by God’s appointment you preside, and fortify it with the privilege of this present document. We decree that the same place, as it was established by its founders, the princes Pippin and Charles of noble memory, shall remain forever undisturbed and free from every exaction or burden. Moreover, whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by the grant of pontiffs, the bounty of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, God being favorable, shall be kept secure [Col. 1591C] and unimpaired for you and your successors.

Among these, we have judged the following to be stated by their proper names: namely, the church of St. Mary of the Market, with its tithes and appurtenances; St. Martin of Campaignac; St. Leontius, with their appurtenances; St. Mary of Montignac, with the chapel situated within the walls of that castle; St. Riberius with its appurtenances; St. Peter of Corn; St. Mundana, with the courts of Marciliac and Calabro; St. Simeon of Gordonio; St. Peter of Cador; the chapel of St. Mary of Carlux; the churches of St. Amand of Symeyrols; half the revenues of the church of St. Mary of Pratis; St. James of Trapa with its appurtenances; the estates of Syourac; the church of St. Mary of Moncuq; St. Mary of Capella with many churches and lands situated in the vicariate of Cauves; the churches of St. [Col. 1591D] Hilary of Doissac and St. Mary of Sales; the church of St. Sacerdos of Aurenca with its appurtenances in the churches of St. Vincent, St. Avitus, St. Martin of Drot, and St. Peter of Auvert; the church of St. Mary of the Valley; St. Martin of Claviac with their appurtenances; the church of St. Desiderius; St. Saturninus; St. Martin of Causac; the church of St. Martin of Pertus; St. Martin of Lenvilla; St. John of Podio Girolmi with the chapel of St. Mary Magdalene; the churches of St. Martin of Saussignac, St. Saturninus of Annac, St. Stephen of Borchet, and St. Avitus of Balares; the church of Somensac; St. Julian; St. Peter of Roqueta; the church of St. Sulpicius of Pico; the church of St. Michael of Lantes; the churches of St. Germanus of Ravanella with their appurtenances; [Col. 1592A] St. Peter of Nessa with its appurtenances; half the revenues of the church of St. Amand; the church of St. Christopher with its appurtenances; the monastery of Sigiac with its appurtenances; the churches of St. Mary of the Market, St. Mary of Aurevilla, St. Severinus, St. Fronto, St. Peter of the monastery of Holy Cross, St. Perdulphus, and St. Eulalia; the chapels of St. Mary of the Mount, St. John of Agen, and St. Martin of Gardelus; two parts of the revenues of the church of St. Mary of Monsaguel; likewise the monastery of Fita with the churches of St. Faith, St. Mary of la Esterna, St. Maurice, St. Damian, St. Mary of Borbel, St. Mary of Rocella, and St. Mary of Berrat, with their tithes and appurtenances and with half the revenues of the church of St. Peter of Toules. All these we confirm to you and, through you, to the monastery of Sarlat [Col. 1592B]: the churches of St. Peter of Caviac, St. Martin of Genebredo, and St. Mary of Sergiac, with their appurtenances.

In the parish churches which you hold, you shall elect priests and present them to the bishop. If they are suitable, the bishop shall commit the cure of souls to them, so that they may answer to the bishop concerning the care of the people, but render to you due subjection in temporal matters belonging to the monastery. Upon the death of you, the present abbot of the same place, or of any of your successors, no one may be placed over it through any deceitful contrivance or violence, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the majority of the brethren of sounder counsel, shall provide to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict. We also decree that the burial-right of your monastery and the places belonging to it [Col. 1592C], which you have hitherto enjoyed according to ancient custom, shall remain free and undisturbed. No archbishop or bishop may presume to place under interdict or excommunicate either the monastery of Sarlat itself, or the monasteries of Fita and Issigiac, or the person of the abbot. Let no one support disobedient monks against the abbot, and let no one presume to found new churches near your churches or monasteries more closely than customary.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations. Rather, let all things be preserved intact for the use and benefit in every respect of those for whose governance and support they were granted. As a token of this liberty received from the apostolic see, you shall yearly pay to us and to our successors one gold coin from the aforesaid monastery of Sarlat, another from Fita, and another from Issigiac [Col. 1592D]. If any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after a second or third admonition, unless he makes amends by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the rank of his power and honor; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the wrong he has committed; let him be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and at the final judgment let him be subject to stern retribution. But upon all who preserve their rights to that same place [Col. 1593A], may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good works and before the strict Judge find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Odo Dircardus [formerly cardinal-deacon], of St. George at the Golden Veil. I, Hyacinthus, cardinal-deacon of St. Mary in Cosmedin. I, G[regory], cardinal-priest of Callistus. I, Guido, cardinal-priest of St. Chrysogonus. I, Ismarus, bishop of Tusculum. I, Hugh, bishop of Ostia.

Given at Rome, at St. Peter’s, through the hand of Boso, scribe of the Holy Roman Church, on the fifth day before the Nones of May [3 May], [Col. 1593B] in the first indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1153, in the eighth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### DLXXIX. To the abbots of St. Pons and Cruas.—That they observe the decree of Urban II at the Council of Clermont.  
*(A.D. 1153, 12 May.)*

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 678.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the abbots of St. Pons and Cruas: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is exceedingly serious to resist the commands of the apostolic see with stiff neck and to seek to render its constitutions void. For in other letters we instructed your care not to receive those excommunicated by our venerable brother Peter, archbishop of Narbonne, and firmly to observe, concerning the appointment of priests in the parish churches which you possess in his province, the decree of our predecessor of holy memory, Pope Urban. This decree is as follows: “Since certain monks seek to take away from bishops their right, we decree that they shall not place priests in the parish churches which they hold without the counsel of the bishops; rather, bishops shall, with the abbots’ consent, commit the care of the parish to a priest, so that such priests may answer to the bishops concerning the care of the people, but render to the abbot due subjection for temporal matters belonging to the monastery [Col. 1593D], and thus each party’s rights may be preserved.”

But you, as we have learned from the repeated complaint of that same brother of ours, have been wholly unwilling to observe either his interdict or the decree itself. Therefore, by repeated letters, we instruct and command you: entirely to abstain from the society of persons excommunicated by our aforesaid brother, and not to appoint priests in the churches which you have in his bishopric without his consent. Otherwise, we have granted him authority both to excommunicate the priests themselves and to impose an interdict upon the churches.

Given at Rome, at St. Peter’s, on the fourth day before the Ides of May [12 May].

### DLXXX. To the monks of the archbishopric of Narbonne.—That they observe Urban II’s decree at the Council of Clermont.  
*(A.D. 1153, 12 May.)*

[Ibid., 679.]

[Col. 1594A]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, abbots, priors, and other monks established throughout the bishopric of Narbonne: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since certain monks seek to take away from bishops their right, our predecessor of venerable memory, Urban, decreed at the Council of Auvergne that in the parish churches which they hold they should not appoint priests without the bishops’ counsel; rather [Col. 1594B], bishops should, with the abbots’ consent, commit the care of the parish to a priest, so that such priests may render account to the bishops concerning the care of the people, but render to the abbot due subjection for temporal matters belonging to the monastery. Since, therefore, the order of justice and reason teaches that one who wishes his own commands or institutions to be observed by successors ought to preserve the will and enactments of his predecessor, by this present document we command you to present to our venerable brother Peter, archbishop of Narbonne, the priests whom you appoint in the parish churches in his diocese, so that, if they are suitable, they may receive from him the cure of souls, as has been decreed.

Likewise, by the authority of this document we command you [Col. 1594C] to pay him without any contradiction the portion of offerings and tithes that comes from the people and is recognized, according to the enactments of the canons, as belonging to the archbishop’s right—excepting those matters therein which have been specially granted to you by the apostolic see. Moreover, since it has been reported to us that some of you presume solemnly to baptize infants and, contrary to the rule of your profession, to give penances and the Eucharist to laypeople, we strictly forbid, by the authority of this document, any further presumption to do so. Otherwise, we have granted our aforesaid brother, your archbishop, authority to exercise the censure of ecclesiastical severity against such offenders.

Given at Rome, at St. Peter’s, on the fourth day before the Ides of May [12 May].

### DLXXXI. Privilege for the Church of St. Mary of Asti.  
*(A.D. 1153, 16 May.)*

[UGHELLI, *Italia Sacra*, IV, 363.]

[Col. 1594D]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother ANSELM, bishop of Asti, and to his successors canonically appointed forever.

Established, by the Lord’s disposition, upon the lofty watchtower of the apostolic see, we ought to love our brother bishops with fraternal charity and preserve for the churches in which they are known to serve the Lord their rightful claims. Therefore, venerable brother in Christ, Bishop Anselm, we graciously assent to your just petitions and receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves the Church of Blessed Mary, over which [Col. 1595A] by God’s appointment you are known to preside, fortifying it with the privilege of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by grants of pontiffs, the bounty of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, by God’s favor, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors and, through you, for that same church.

Among these, we have judged the following to be stated by their proper names: the abbey of St. Dalmatius of Pedona, with the castle, court, and the Gesso Valley as far as the *fenestrae*, and the parish church of that place with all churches belonging to it; the abbey of the Holy Apostles with all its appurtenances; the abbey of St. Anastasius [Col. 1595B] with all appurtenances; the abbey of Azano, with the castle, chapels, and all its appurtenances; the abbey of St. Christopher; the parish church of Quadrigentina, with the castle, court, and churches belonging to it; the parish church of Onville, with all churches belonging to it; the parish church of Montalto, with all churches belonging to it; the parish church of St. Mary in Grana, with castle, court, and churches belonging to it; the parish church of Pizenzana; the parish church of Meirade; the parish church of Bagnasco; the parish church of Duodecino; the parish church of Musantia, with all churches belonging to it; the parish church of St. Julius of Lavegia, with court, castle, and churches belonging to it; the parish church of St. Vincent of Marcelengo; the parish church of Predocha; the parish church of Canali [Col. 1595C], with all possessions and churches belonging to it; the parish church of Novello, with churches belonging to it; the parish church of Vitia, with churches, castle, court, woods, and all its appurtenances; the parish church of Garena, with hospitals, churches, and its appurtenances, and the wood called the Island of St. John; the parish church of St. Peter of Publico, with court and all churches belonging to it; the parish church of Manchiano, with churches belonging to it; the parish church of Lavaldesio, with court and churches belonging to it; the parish church of Bagenne, with castle, court, wood, banality-right, and all churches belonging to it; the parish church of St. Peter in Grado, with court, the castle of Earcuo, chapels, woods, and all its appurtenances; the parish church of Carazone, with castle [Col. 1595D], court, and churches belonging to it; the parish church of St. Peter of Vico, with court, chapels, and the hermitage of St. Ambrose called Mons Altus, with an ironworks, the valley of Causalia, and the castle of Rivoburente as far as the Alpine summits; the parish church of Predolense, with court, castle, and churches belonging to it; the parish church of Upper Bagenne, with court, castle, chapels, woods, and the castle of Forfice as far as Bisimalta, and with the church of St. Stephen near the spring of Brobius, with its appurtenances; the parish church of Moroxina, with all churches belonging to it; the parish church of St. Alban, with castle, court, churches, mills, and woods; the castle called Altavilla, with court and its appurtenances; everything that you possess in Monte Magno [Col. 1596A]; the castle of Contansteris with its appurtenances; Caprile with its whole *comitile* [county or comital estate]; the county called Serralonga; the wood called Populare, with the castles and villages contained within it; Ceresolas with its castles and appurtenances; the castle of Sommariva del Bosco with its appurtenances; the castle of Sommariva Perno with its appurtenances; Cajarasco with all its appurtenances; the castle called Montaldo; the county and refuge of Pollenzo; the county of the city and of the whole bishopric, with public revenues, and all that is known to have been lawfully bestowed upon the Church of Asti by imperial grants.

Furthermore, we decree that all tithes in your bishopric, except those granted by the apostolic see to monks from their own labor, which they cultivate with their own hands or at their own expense [Col. 1596B], shall, according to the provisions of the sacred canons, remain under your administration without anyone’s opposition. If disputes concerning tithes arise through feudal custom, they shall be decided only by ecclesiastical judgment. You may also remove from churches exactions imposed by laypersons under the pretext of a fief or on any other ground. In the parish churches held within your bishopric by monks or regular canons, in accordance with the decree of our predecessor, Pope Urban of blessed memory, they shall elect priests and present them to you. If these are suitable, you must commit the cure of souls to them, so that they may answer to you concerning the care of the people, but render due subjection to those religious houses in temporal matters [Col. 1596C] belonging to them, without prejudice, of course, to the privilege of the apostolic see.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations. Rather, let them be preserved intact for the use and benefit in every respect of those for whose governance and support they were granted. If any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after a second or third admonition, unless he makes amends by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the rank of his power and honor; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment [Col. 1596D] for the wrong he has committed; let him be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Redeemer Jesus Christ; and at the final judgment let him be subject to stern retribution. But upon all who preserve what is just for that same place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good works and before the strict Judge find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, Oddo, cardinal-deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, John, bishop of Tusculum, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal-deacon of St. Mary in the Portico, have subscribed. [Col. 1597A] I, Oddo, cardinal-deacon of St. Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed. I, Hugh, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, W[?], cardinal-priest of the title of St. Callistus, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal-priest of the title of B. Chris[ogonus], have subscribed. I, Ubaldus, cardinal-priest of St. Praxedes, have subscribed. I, Manfred, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Sabina, have subscribed. I, Aribertus, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Anastasia, have subscribed. I, . . . ., cardinal-priest of the title of St. Pastor, have subscribed.

Given at Rome, at St. Peter’s, through the hand of Roland, cardinal-priest and chancellor, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of June [16 May], in the first indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1153, in the ninth year of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### DLXXXII. Privilege for the convent of Othmarsheim.  
*(A.D. 1153, 21 May.)*

[SCHOEPFLIN, *Alsatian Diplomatic Records*, I, 480.]

[Col. 1597B]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ, EVANCHILDIS, abbess of the monastery of St. Mary at Othmarsheim, and her sisters, present and future, professing the regular life, forever.

Whenever royal decrees concur with sacerdotal judgments in preserving what has been piously done, and things religiously enacted are fortified by privileges both of sacerdotal authority and royal dignity, they ought to receive all the greater firmness through the work of piety, inasmuch as a twofold authority has more carefully opposed the attacks of the wicked lest [Col. 1597C] they be able to disturb them. Coming before us, beloved daughter in the Lord, Abbess Evanchildis, you explained in our hearing that Rudolf of noble memory had built, at his own expense, upon his estate a monastery in honor of St. Mary, Mother of God, for the salvation of his soul. When Pope Leo VIII, our predecessor of holy memory, was passing through those regions, Rudolf offered it, subject to an annual payment of one white garment and one shoulder-cloak, to him and through him to Blessed Peter, prince of the apostles; and with due devotion requested to receive its consecration from that predecessor’s hand. Having at last attained the fulfillment of his wish, he endowed the place from the abundance of his property. By the privilege of that predecessor, who exempted it from every molestation and claim of the successors of Henry, then illustrious king of the Romans [Col. 1597D], he retained no custom or right whatsoever for himself or his successors in the same place, except that he ordained that its advocacy should remain with his heirs after his death. Thus, if there were several heirs, the one whom the abbess and sisters of that place should freely determine to elect as their advocate was to administer the office of advocacy by right of that advocacy.

Moreover, lest whoever might be advocate should have any occasion or pretext for plundering the Church’s property or hindering the sisters in divine worship, it was established and confirmed by the privilege of the aforesaid predecessor and king [Col. 1598A] that the advocate should receive absolutely nothing from property then possessed; rather, only from what should be acquired thereafter. That is, if there were twelve *mansi*, one was to fall to his use, of such kind as the abbess might wish to grant him; but if there were not so many *mansi*, he should wait until the number of twelve was completed, and then receive one of the twelve according to the abbess’s choice. For the greater security of that same place it was also established and put in writing that, should the advocate perhaps presume to destroy or despoil the monastery and, after admonition by the Roman pontiff, disdain to render the satisfaction due, the Roman bishop should remove him from the office of advocacy, and the abbess and her sisters should have entirely free power to elect another advocate for themselves.

Therefore, beloved daughter in Christ, Abbess Evanchildis, since you requested that this church, belonging in a special manner to the right of Blessed Peter, be fortified by our privilege, we confirm the matters written above. Following the example of our aforementioned predecessor, we receive it as belonging to the right of the most holy Roman Church under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves and fortify it by the protection of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire through grants of pontiffs, the bounty of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, God being favorable, shall remain secure [Col. 1598C] and unimpaired to you, beloved daughter in Christ Evanchildis, abbess, to the other sisters, and to those who shall succeed you.

You shall receive the consecration of altars, the blessing of nuns, and other ecclesiastical sacraments from the diocesan bishop, provided that he enjoys the favor and communion of the apostolic see and is willing to confer them freely and without impropriety. Otherwise, you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer, who, supported by our authority, shall grant what is requested. Upon the death of you, beloved daughter in the Lord Evanchildis, now abbess of the same monastery, or of any woman who succeeds you, no one may be placed over it by any fraudulent contrivance or violence, except one whom the sisters of the same place, or the majority of the sisters of sounder counsel, shall judge according to God to be elected, and who is to receive the grace of blessing from the Roman [Col. 1598D] pontiff.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations. Rather, let all things be preserved intact for the use and benefit in every respect of those for whose governance and support they were granted, without prejudice to the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If any ecclesiastical or secular person hereafter, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after a second or third admonition, unless he corrects his guilt by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the rank of his power and honor; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment [Col. 1599A] for the wrong he has committed; let him be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and at the final judgment let him be subject to stern retribution. But upon all who preserve what is just for that same place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good works and before the strict Judge find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

Given at Rome, at St. Peter’s, through the hand of Roland, cardinal-priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of June [21 May], in the first indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1153, in the ninth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III.

### DLXXXIII. He grants in emphyteusis to Count Vincio of Montumano the fourth part of the fortress of Tranianum, given to the Roman Church by that count.  
*(A.D. 1153, 3 June.)*

[UGHELLI, *Italia Sacra*, III, 638.]

[Col. 1599B]

In the name of the Lord. In the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1153, the ninth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Eugenius III, the first indiction, on 3 June.

I, Eugenius, bishop, servant of the servants of God, and third pope in the most holy see of the blessed apostle Peter. In the presence of my brethren the bishops, the chancellor, and the cardinal, on this very day, of my own free will, I lease and grant to you, Wicio, count of Montumano, and to your heirs and successors in perpetuity—that is, one whole fourth part [Col. 1599C] of a fortress called Tranianum, together with a whole fifth part of the houses and farmsteads, lands, arable fields, vineyards, woods, meadows, marshes, and swamps, with springs, streams, waters and watercourses, mountains, hills, slopes, and plains; together with a whole fifth part of all pleas and *bundi* [jurisdictional dues], and with a fifth part of the entire honour and jurisdiction, and with all things generally and wholly belonging to the said castle, situated in the territory of Chiusi, as it is bounded by its neighbours—property of the right of blessed Peter and of the holy Roman Church—to hold, use, enjoy, improve, and, as has been said, possess in perpetuity. Just as it belongs to blessed Peter and the holy Roman Church by the donation made by you [Col. 1599D] to me and my successors, so I lease and grant it to you and your heirs and successors in perpetuity. Each year, in the month of May, you shall pay to us, our successors, and the sacred Lateran palace, as rent, half a morabetin; and should it happen that for three years you or your successors fail to pay us or our successors the said rent, then, when required in the fourth year, double shall be paid to us and our sacred palace. Therefore I, together with my successors, promise to defend you and your heirs and successors against all honours, should need and necessity require it. But if any party should attempt to act contrary to the faith of this lease, and should in any way fail to observe all that has been stated, or [Col. 1600A] if you, the lessee, or your heirs or successors fail to pay and observe what has been stated to us and our sacred palace, then the said unfaithful party shall pay to the party keeping faith, as a penalty, ten pounds of fine gold; and once the penalty has been paid, these two charters of lease, drawn up in identical terms by the hand of Andrew, notary of the holy Roman Church, in the above-mentioned month and first indiction, shall remain valid according to their tenor.

I requested the mark of the hand of the above-named lord Eugenius, supreme and universal pontiff and third pope in the most sacred see of the blessed apostle Peter, for this charter.

Centius Frajapanis, consul of the Romans. Hyacinth, lord pope’s dapifer [steward]. [Col. 1600B] Peter, prefect of the City. Maximus Guitianus. Oddo, son of Franco. Assalitus, son of Conrad of Guito. Guivad of Radicofani. Salac, his son. Mirus, son of Massinellus. Ardimanus of Castellione in the valley of the Ove. Gerard, viscount of Civitella. Peter of Aseja. Benedict, son of Zeno. Blasius of Macello. Orlandinus, son of Bometto. Bevarsus of Caviano. Cossivallus of Mejola. [Col. 1600C] Arnolsinus of Castellione in the valley of the Uvae.

And I, Andrew, notary of the holy Roman Church, completed and authenticated it.

DLXXXIV. Privilege for the monastery of Tournus. (A.D. 1153, June 6.)

[JUENIA, *History of the Royal Abbey of Tournus*, Proofs, p. 164.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son PETER, abbot of Tournus, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We desire that those things which are done by our brethren the bishops with reasonable foresight should remain stable, and that they may be observed in future times we wish to strengthen them by the safeguard of our confirmation. Therefore, beloved son in [Col. 1600D] the Lord, graciously granting assent to your just petitions, we confirm to you, and through you to the monastery itself, by the authority of the apostolic see, the donation of the church of Moncellis which Peter, of good memory, and Hubert, archbishops of Lyons, are known to have made to your monastery and confirmed by the text of their document; and we decree that it shall remain valid hereafter, saving the canonical right and due reverence of the Church of Lyons. Let no person whatsoever therefore be permitted rashly to infringe this page of our confirmation or in any manner disturb it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

[Col. 1601A] Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, on the eighth day before the Ides of June [6 June].

On the lead seal: EUGENIUS POPE III.

DLXXXV. Privilege for the abbey of Conques. (A.D. 1153, June 6.)

[MABILLON, *Benedictine Annals*, VI, 724.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son ODO, abbot of the monastery of Saint Faith of Conques, and to his successors regularly appointed in perpetuity.

It is fitting readily to grant assent to religious desires, so that faithful devotion may obtain a swift effect. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Odo, abbot of Conques, we graciously [Col. 1601B] assent to your just petitions, and, following the example of our predecessors of blessed memory, the Roman pontiffs Urban and Calixtus, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves, and fortify by the privilege of this present writing, the monastery of the blessed virgin Faith, who is said to rest there, over which, with God’s help, you preside. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, God being favourable, by concession of pontiffs, gift of kings or princes, offering of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names: namely, the churches of Grandinabro, Montiniaco, Saunas, Saint Cyprian, [Col. 1601C] Nota-villa, Marciliaco, Saint Marcellus, Bella-calma, and Manso Bosonis; and in the church of Prunsologio, five solidi of annual rent; the church of Campaniaco with the whole village; the churches of Cauniaco, Pricio, Pratis, Trebes, Monteroserio, Persia, Speleu, Anadiliaco, Curedis, Saint Felix, Orgagneto, Albiniaco, Bromme, Brommat, Barro, Camporerio, Goliniaco, Spayraco, Balsiaco, and Riniaco; and what you hold in the church of Firminihio; the churches of Vivario, Flaniaco, Lemniaco, Claniaco, Malavilla, Pervenqueriis, Croso, Gasanguas, Bellomonte, Monte-Aldone, Rodolayguas, Seyraco, Borno, Monte-Acuto, Sepedo, [Col. 1601D] Pino, and Castello-Mauron; the churches of Saint Faith of Vauro and Perairorio, and Salvitate Armandi; the churches of Molendino Pizino, Tavanella, Avarolago, Ussello, Alavastria, Montebruno, Saint Mamet, Saint Romanus, Auriaco, Castelletto above the Loire, Saint Victor, Chavannico, Columbario near Visternum; the church of Saint Faith; and the churches of Pallatio, Vayraco, Celliano, Lecaraco, Manabello, Lareriis, Cailla, and Plancas. In the diocese of Albi: the churches of Saint Felix and Fontelupino; the church of Cullas; the churches of Vinairolio, Exculto, Podio-palenoso, Carzag, Castaneo, Embaisso, Cambone, Saint [Col. 1602A] Christopher of Murello, Caparosso of Callitone, Baracz, Barbasta, the Holy Sepulchre, Saint John of Estecestat, Horson, and Hosforda.

Upon the death of you, the present abbot of that place, or of any one of your successors, no person shall be placed over it by any artifice of intrigue or violence, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren, shall elect according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Benedict. The person elected shall receive blessing from the diocesan bishop, provided that he is Catholic, enjoys the favour and communion of the apostolic see, and is willing to confer that ordination freely and without improper exaction; otherwise he may have leave either to appeal to the apostolic see or to approach whichever Catholic bishop he prefers, who, supported by our authority, shall grant what is requested. We grant the same also concerning the consecration of altars or churches and the ordination of monks to be promoted to sacred orders. We add further that no bishop may, without the permission of the Roman pontiff, subject your house or monks to interdict or excommunication; nor, because of a general interdict upon the diocese, shall the aforesaid monastery cease from the divine office. Rather, with the doors closed and excommunicated and interdicted persons excluded, you may celebrate the divine offices in a subdued voice. Moreover, no bishop or provost [Col. 1602C] may prevent you from receiving for conversion free laymen or clerics fleeing from the world, unless they are excommunicated. We also decree that the burial-place of that house shall be entirely free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and final will of those who decide to be buried there, unless they happen to be excommunicated or interdicted, while the right of the mother church is nonetheless preserved. We forbid, moreover, that irregular custom from being practised any further: namely, that the relics of the saints of the same monastery be carried to public assemblies against the will of the brethren serving God there. We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole [Col. 1602D] for the benefit in every way of those uses for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the canonical right of the diocesan bishops in the aforesaid chapels. If therefore any ecclesiastical or secular person [this our …, etc.].

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina. I, Ymarus, bishop of Tusculum. I, Hugh, bishop of Ostia. I, W., cardinal priest of the title of Calixtus. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Chrysogonus. I, Jordan, cardinal priest of the holy Roman Church, of the title of Saint Susanna. [Col. 1603A] I, Odo, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, Hyacinth, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin.

Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, through the hand of Roland, cardinal priest and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the seventh day before the Ides of June [7 June], in the first indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1153, in the ninth year of the pontificate of lord Pope Eugenius III.

DLXXXVI. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Benedict of Saxo on Mount Laterone. (A.D. 1153, June 13.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, III, 631.]

[Col. 1603B]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son ACTO, abbot of the monastery of Saint Benedict of Saxo Laterone, and to his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life.

It is fitting readily to grant assent to religious desires, so that faithful devotion may obtain a swift effect. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves, and fortify by the privilege of this present writing, the aforesaid monastery in which you are devoted to divine service. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly [Col. 1603C] and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, God being favourable, by concession of pontiffs, gift of kings or princes, offering of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: the churches of Saint Blaise of Bellicione; Saint Saviour of Strata; Saint Leonard, in which is the hospital of the beam of Donatus; Saint Christopher at Serrasicca; and Saint Saviour of Schifia.

We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole for the benefit in every way of those uses for whose governance [Col. 1603D] and support they were granted, saving the canonical right of the diocesan bishops. If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our grant, should rashly attempt to act against it and, after a second or third warning, fail to make suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and honour, recognize that he or she is guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed, be cut off from the most holy body and blood of God and our Lord Jesus Christ, and be subject at the last judgment to strict vengeance. But may the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all who preserve justice toward the same place, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, through the hand of Roland, cardinal priest and chancellor, on the Ides of June [13 June], first indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1153, in the ninth year of the pontificate of lord Pope Eugenius III.

DLXXXVII. Privilege for the Camaldolese congregation. (A.D. 1153, June 16.)

[MITTARELLI, *Camaldolese Annals*, III, Appendix, 464.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son RODULPH, prior of the Camaldolese, and to his brethren, present and future, professing the regular [Col. 1604B] life, in perpetuity.

It is fitting readily to grant assent to religious desires, so that faithful devotion may obtain a swift effect. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions; and, adhering to the footsteps of our predecessor Pope Paschal of blessed memory, we command and establish by the authority of this present writing that no person whatsoever—cleric, monk, or layperson, of whatever order or dignity, in present or future times—may in any way divide from its subjection and unity the congregations and places which have received the discipline and order of the Camaldolese hermitage or cenobium and which today are under its rule. For the preservation [Col. 1604C] of unity, the following places and congregations have been considered worthy of being recorded by individual names: in the diocese of Arezzo, the monastery of Saint Saviour of the Berardinghi; Saint Peter at Rota; Saint Mary at Agnano; Saint Quiricus at Rosa; the hermitage of Fleri; the monastery of Saint Virianus; Saint Bartholomew at Anglare; near Balmo, the monastery of Saint Mary at Trivio; at Galrata, the monastery of Saint Mary on the Island. In the diocese of Montefeltro, the monastery of Mount Hercules; in the diocese of Forlì, the hospital of Almericus; in the diocese of Pesaro, the monastery of Saint Decentius and the hermitage of Fajoli; in the diocese of Bologna, the monastery of Saint Michael the Archangel near the castle of Britti, and Saint Felix; in the diocese of Florence, the monastery of Saint Peter at Luco and Saint Saviour [Col. 1604D] near the city; in the diocese of Fiesole, the monastery of Saint Mary at Poplena and the church of Saint Margaret; in the diocese of Volterra, the monastery of Saint Peter at Fontiano, Saint Mary at Puliciano, Saint Peter at Cerreto, and Saint Justus near the city; in the diocese of Pisa, the monastery of Saint Mary of Morrona, the monastery of Saint Stephen at Cintoria, and Saint Sabinus at Cerasolo; in the city itself, the monasteries of Saint Michael and Saint Fridianus; in the diocese of Lucca, the monastery of Saint Saviour at Cantiniano and Saint Peter at Puteoli. Likewise in Sardinia, in the archdiocese of Torres, the monastery of the Holy Trinity of Saccaria and the church of Saint Peter of Scanno. Likewise [Col. 1605A] in Tuscany, in the diocese of Chiusi, the hermitage of Vivo on Mount Amiata, with all appurtenances of the aforesaid places. We establish, therefore, and sanction by the authority of the apostolic see, that all these things, with everything belonging to the said monasteries, shall remain for ever, as one body under one head—that is, under the prior of the Camaldolese hermitage—and shall continue in observance of that discipline under the prior, namely, who shall, by God’s grace, be regularly elected by the abbots or priors and hermits of that congregation.

Furthermore, we decree that the congregation itself shall be perpetually fostered under the protection of the apostolic see in such wise that no bishop may excommunicate any of these monasteries or prohibit it from divine offices without the prior’s consent or the permission of the apostolic [Col. 1605B] see. The brethren themselves may receive the sacraments of consecration and ordination from whatever Catholic bishop they prefer. We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may, etc. If anyone therefore, etc. But to all, etc.

“MAKE FOR ME, O LORD, A SIGN FOR GOOD.” SAINT PETER, SAINT PAUL, EUGENIUS POPE THE THIRD.

I, Eugenius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, GG., cardinal priest of the title of Calixtus, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Chrysogonus, have subscribed. I, Manfred, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Sabina, [Col. 1605C] have subscribed. I, Arimbert, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia, have subscribed. I, Julius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus, have subscribed. I, Ubald, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Octavian, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia, have subscribed. I, Gherard, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill, have subscribed. I, John Paparo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Damaso, have subscribed. I, Oddo, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed. I, John, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Gerard, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed.

[Col. 1605D] Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, through the hand of Roland, cardinal priest and chancellor, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of July [16 June], in the first indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1153, in the ninth year of the pontificate of lord Pope Eugenius III.

DLXXXVIII. To Bernard, archbishop of Tarragona—That he acknowledge the primacy of Toledo. (A.D. 1153, June 29.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 674.]

Whoever wishes that others should be subject to him [Col. 1606A] ought not to disdain that he himself should likewise be subject to others. For it is most unworthy and blameworthy that what we know to be observed by the angelic spirits themselves should be despised by men. We read and believe that archangels preside over angels and, as over subjects, command them in divine service. Therefore, concerning your honour and religion, we can scarcely sufficiently wonder that you have neither rendered to the archbishop of Toledo, as we commanded you by apostolic sentence, the obedience which he claims is owed him by your brotherhood, nor appeared before us, at the fixed term, prepared to give a sufficient answer to him or his envoys, either personally or through your representatives. By repeated letters we again command you, and in commanding order you, that either you render, without hindrance or contradiction, obedience to our venerable brother Ildefonsus [corrected: John], archbishop of Toledo, as to your primate; or that on the first Sunday of the coming Lent, on which *Invocavit me* is sung, you present yourself before us, prepared to answer him sufficiently concerning this matter. If you neither render him obedience nor come before us at that term to answer him, from that time forward we utterly prohibit your use of the pallium.

Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, on the third day before the Kalends of July [29 June].

DLXXXIX. To John, archbishop of Toledo—He informs him what he wrote to Bernard, archbishop of Tarragona. (A.D. 1153, June 29.)

[Ibid.]

[Col. 1606C]

We love your person with true charity in the Lord, and desire that the honour and dignity of the Church of Toledo entrusted to you be wholly guarded and preserved, insofar as reason and propriety allow. Therefore, by repeated letters we command and in commanding order our venerable brother Bernard, archbishop of Tarragona and legate of the apostolic see, either to render obedience to you without hindrance and contradiction, or to appear before us on the coming Sunday of Lent, [Col. 1606D] on which *Invocavit me* is sung, prepared to give you a sufficient answer concerning this matter. If he should take care to fulfil neither alternative, from that time forward we have altogether forbidden him the use of the pallium. Moreover, in the presence of your envoys, we orally commanded our venerable brother Ildefonsus, archbishop of Braga, that he render to you and your successors due obedience and reverence as to his primate.

Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, on the third day before the Kalends of July [29 June].

DOUBTFUL DOCUMENTS.

[Col. 1607]

DXC. He confirms a spurious diploma which King Conrad III is said to have granted to the Church of Utrecht. (A.D. 1145, March 18.)

[COCQUELINES, II, 284.]

[Col. 1607A]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the dean and chapter of the Church of Utrecht, grace, glory, and apostolic blessing.

The petition of our dearest son in Christ, Conrad III, illustrious king of the Romans, conveyed to us through his beloved son Conrad, his brother and provost of your Church, sent for this purpose by the same king to the Roman curia [addition: “sent”], requested that we would deign by apostolic authority to confirm the privileges granted to your Church by the kings and emperors of the Romans, his predecessors, and also the privilege [Col. 1607B] granted by himself to your aforesaid Church, whose text is as follows:

> “In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity. Conrad, by favour of divine clemency, third king of the Romans.
>
> “If we enlarge the churches of God and protect and confirm their rights by royal authority, we imitate the examples of our predecessors, the pious kings and emperors; and we do not doubt that this will be beneficial to the exaltation of our kingdom and especially to the salvation of our soul. Therefore let the diligence of Christ’s faithful, both future and present, and of our kingdom know that, while we were residing in the city of Utrecht and deliberating concerning the peace and condition of the kingdom, our faithful servant Hardbert, venerable bishop of that place, our brother Conrad the provost, and the dean and chapter of the major church of the said city came into our presence, entreating our highness that, just as our predecessors, the pious kings and emperors of the Romans, endowed the Church of Utrecht itself with many honours and privileges, so our royal excellence, following in their footsteps, might deign to grant that church some prerogative of honour. We therefore, considering that it befits royal excellence to honour with a fuller prerogative those whose devotion we experience in continual services; considering also that we and our predecessors, kings and emperors, have from its foundation held the first place among the canons in the said church [Col. 1607D] and that two priests serve our prebend there, praying God for our salvation and for the tranquillity and peace of the kingdom; and considering the faithful service of the said venerable bishop Hardbert, and the welcome services and frequent devotion of the dean and chapter, dear to us, by which they greatly honoured our royal excellence and our beloved consort, Queen Gertrude, while she resided for some time in that city; and therefore wishing to exalt the same major Church of Utrecht by a special prerogative of honour, for the remedy of our soul and of the souls of our grandfather Emperor Lord Henry III—whose entrails are buried in that church as a pledge—and our uncle Emperor Henry IV, and through the intervention of our aforesaid beloved consort the queen and our dearest brother Conrad, provost of the same church, we grant and give, as a perpetual gift, by royal magnificence, the right of electing and instituting a bishop in that church—which right is known to belong to the kings and emperors of the Romans, and has descended and been transmitted from our predecessors, kings and emperors, down to our own time—to the aforesaid provost, dean, and chapter of the church of Saint Boniface of the same place, joined from their foundations, as we have learned, in a special brotherhood with the same major Church; and we grant them our full authority, never to be infringed by any of our successors, so that, whenever the aforesaid bishopric falls vacant, the said provosts, deans, and chapters of the major church and of Saint Saviour of Utrecht aforesaid—and no others save the fellow-canons of their churches—shall have full power to elect another bishop. That this our donation, gift, and privilege, voluntarily and freely granted by royal magnificence, may be perpetual for them, be deemed valid by all, and remain unshaken for all time to come, we have ordered it to be written in this charter, confirming it with our own hand as is seen below; and we have caused fit witnesses who were present to be subscribed, whose names are these:
>
> “Anselm, bishop of Navelburg; Albero, bishop of Liège; Werner, bishop of Münster; Nicholas, bishop of Cambrai; Udo, bishop of Ossenburg; Duke Walram; William, Count Palatine; Henry, count of Zutphen; Arnold, count of Cleves; Adolph, count of the Mount; Henry, count of Guelders; Conrad, provost of Utrecht; Emo, provost of Saint Boniface; Conrad, provost of Tiel; Lambert, provost of Saint Peter; Godfrey of Rhenen; Alard of Megene; Otto, prefect of Utrecht; Egbert of Anestelle; Berthold of Aldenseele; James of Saterfole.
>
> “Mark of lord Conrad III, king of the Romans.
>
> [Col. 1608D] “I, Arnold, chancellor in the place of Henry, archbishop of Mainz and archchancellor, have verified this, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1145, eighth indiction, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of November [18 October], in the eighth year of the reign of Conrad, third king of the Romans.
>
> “Issued at Utrecht, happily in Christ.”

Therefore, moved by reverence for our Church and by the earnest request of the said king, and considering also the devotion of the king toward your Church, by which he has honoured it favourably and splendidly with royal magnificence, we confirm by apostolic authority the aforesaid privilege—whose text has been inserted word for word in these our apostolic letters—and all privileges granted to your Church by the kings and emperors of the Romans for the honour of Christ and the exaltation of the Church. Under the bond of anathema we forbid any imperial, royal, episcopal, clerical, or lay person, of whatever rank or condition, ever to harass the Church of Utrecht contrary to such privilege and to the tenor of our confirmation, or to dare to undertake anything in the aforesaid matters to its prejudice. We decree null and void anything done by anyone to the contrary. Let no person whatsoever, therefore, be permitted to infringe this page of our confirmation or rashly oppose it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he shall incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of April [18 March], in the first year of our pontificate.

DXCI. He confirms the possessions and privileges of the monastery of Ilsenburg. (A.D. 1148, March 23.)

[*Neue Mittheilungen aus dem Gebiete historisch-antiquarischer Forschungen*, II, 300.]

EUGENIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son SIGEBODO, abbot of Ilsenburg, and to his successors regularly appointed in perpetuity.

Since it belongs to apostolic solicitude to promote and defend in every way religion pleasing to God, therefore, most beloved son in the Lord, Sigebodo, abbot of Ilsenburg, we graciously assent to the most humble petitions of you and your brethren. According to the tenor of the privilege which our predecessor Pope Innocent II of blessed memory granted to your monastery, whatever he established and confirmed for you by apostolic authority, we also establish and confirm by that same authority; what he prohibited we prohibit; and what he granted we also decree shall remain firm and unimpaired for you, under threat of perpetual anathema. Namely, from the donation of Bishop Arnold, who was a most devoted founder of your monastery: tithes at Bernerdiggerode, Suthseauno, Bireslove, Thiderziggerode, Gulisbere, Winitherode, Brodesende, Luttherigerode, Boviggerode, Emmenrode, Geschenrode, Eggerziggerode, Backenrode, Beneziggerode, and Waliggerede. From the donation of Burchard II, bishop beloved of God: tithes at Iggenlove, Bareleslove, Roresheim, Thrubike, Aldenrode, Thurwardiggerode, Gunderaderode, Ezerdiggerode, and Werslove. From the donation of Bishop Heriard, who was also called Stephen: donations at [Col. 1610A] Dannenstide and Suthlochtenheim; and also all the holdings enumerated in order in the aforesaid privilege of our predecessor. From the donation of Bishop Reinhard: tithes from newly cleared lands in all places where you appear to hold tithes; likewise estates at Papesthorpe and Wochkenstide, paying annually a rent of eight talents, which Bishop Otto granted and confirmed to your monastery in exchange for Gedenhusem and Alerstide. Therefore we confirm to you, in the manner of our predecessors and under threat of anathema and eternal damnation, these things and everything which you now canonically possess through the effort of yourself or your predecessors, and whatever you may hereafter obtain by just means alone: male and female serfs, lands, cultivated and uncultivated plots, buildings, fields, meadows, pastures, open fields, woods, hunting rights, [Col. 1610B] waters and watercourses, streams, fisheries, mills, millworks, tolls, roads and trackless places, issues and revenues, holdings and tithes, things acquired and to be acquired. By apostolic authority we likewise forbid anyone to exact tithes or any payments from the estates which you cultivate for your own use; and we forbid any advocate to seize or usurp anything for himself beyond the right and benefice established of old. In the power of the Holy Spirit we command that subadvocates and their collectors be removed and restrained by bishops from every harassment of your church. But if anyone should hereafter presume to undertake anything against this our command or prohibition, as a violator of an apostolic decree, unless warned he comes to his senses, let him be deprived of Christian burial.
