EUGENIUS III, ROMAN PONTIFF.

Historical Notice. 1003  
Booklet concerning the miracles of Pope Eugenius III. 1010  
Preliminary Observation. 1010  
Here begins the account of miracles at the tomb of Lord Eugenius III, Roman pope. 1010  
Diplomatic Notice on the letters of Eugenius III. 1011  
LETTERS AND PRIVILEGES OF EUGENIUS III. 1013  

I.—Informs P., prior of the church of St. Frigdianus at Lucca, that, Lucius II having died on 15 February, he has been elected pope in the church of Blessed Caesarius; he requests that prayers be offered for him. 1013  

II.—At the request of Bishop Dodo, confirms the possessions of the Church of Huesca. 1015  

III.—To the abbots and provosts of Prémontré.—That they are to assemble at Prémontré once a year for a general chapter. 1017  

IV.—Takes the monastery of the Holy Trinity of Curba Fossa (in the diocese of Lucerne) under protection and confirms its property. 1017  

V.—Privilege for the monastery of St. John at Kattenborn. 1018  

VI.—To Alvisus, bishop of Arras. 1020  

VII.—Confirms the privilege of the brethren of St. Frigdianus at Lucca: that cardinal-deacons of St. Mary the New are to be chosen from their number. 1020  

VIII.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Mary of the Prison. 1020  

IX.—To William of Montpellier. 1022  

X.—A privilege confirming the liberty and all the property of the Church of Marmoutier. 1022  

XI.—Orders Alvisus, bishop of Arras, to decide concerning the marriage of Baldum of Rispens and Matilda of Albiniac. 1026  

XII.—Grant of privileges to the monastery of St. Saviour in the diocese of Pavia, of the Cassinese order, which is declared subject to the Holy Roman Church alone. 1026  

XIII.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Peter at Perugia. 1029  

XIV.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Bertin at Sithiu. 1031  

XV–XVI.—Confirms the privilege of the monastery of St. Bertin at Sithiu concerning the exchange of Thierry, count of Flanders, from Henchin to Berquarium, and concerning the election at Alchias. 1032  

XVII.—Takes the monastery of St. George at Prague under the protection of the apostolic see and confirms its possessions. 1032  

XVIII.—To Bartholomew of Laon and Ursio, abbot of St. Dionysius at Reims. 1033  

XIX.—Replies to Louis, king of the Franks, that he received his letter “with due kindness” and satisfied his wishes. 1034  

XX.—Confirms donations made to the monastery of Scheyern in Bavaria by German magnates, bishops, and others. 1034  

[Col. 1670] XXI.—To Rotrod, bishop of Évreux.—That he is to grant to the nuns of Fontevraud the church given to them by the abbot of Conques. 1036  

XXII.—To John, archbishop of Braga.—That he is to acknowledge the primacy of Toledo. 1036  

XXIII.—Privilege for the nunnery of Fontevraud. 1037  

XXIV.—Privilege for the church of St. Mary at Verona. 1038  

XXV.—Confirms the peace between Theobald, bishop of Verona, and Albert, abbot of Nonantola, made on this agreement: that one should possess “parochial right,” and the other “right in the land,” in the parish of Nogara. 1040  

XXVI.—Grants Otto, provost, and the brethren of Cappenberg, together with the nuns of Wischlingen of the same congregation, immunity from tithes. 1041  

XXVII.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Mary of Columba. 1041  

XXVIII.—Informs Otto, bishop of Prague, and Vladislaus, duke of the Bohemians, that certain persons have been excommunicated for invading the property of Henry, bishop of Moravia. 1044  

XXIX.—Orders the abbots of Gradice and Třebíč, together with Otto, duke of Moravia, to join the duke of Bohemia in compelling Dukes Conrad, Wratislaus, and Theobald and their accomplices to make satisfaction to the bishop of Moravia. 1044  

XXX.—At the request of Henry, bishop of Moravia, takes the monastery of Litomyšl under the protection of the apostolic see and confirms its possessions. 1045  

XXXI.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Saviour of Monte Acuto. 1046  

XXXII.—Privilege for the Church of St. Peter at Guastalla. 1048  

XXXIII.—Privilege for the abbey of St. Mary at Castellone. 1050  

XXXIV.—Bull in favour of Albert, abbot of St. Theodard. 1051  

XXXV.—To Otho, bishop of Lucca. 1052  

XXXVI.—To G., abbot of St. Nicholas of Vedogio. 1053  

XXXVII.—Orders Alvisus, bishop of Arras, to judge between the abbot of St. Nicholas of Vedogio and the priest of Baptalmes. 1053  

XXXVIII.—To Theobald, bishop of Verona. 1054  

XXXIX.—Orders Wido, cardinal-priest, to settle a dispute concerning a certain castle which had arisen between the canons and certain nobles of Verona. 1054  

XL.—Privilege for the Church of Reggio. 1055  

XLI.—Privilege for the Church of Berchtesgaden. 1057  

XLII.—Takes the monastery of SS. Peter and Paul at Hadmersleben under protection and confirms its privileges and possessions. 1059  

XLIII.—Entrusts to Aribert, cardinal-priest, Gregory, bishop of Bergamo, and the abbot of Astino monastery the hearing of the dispute between the canons of St. Alexander and St. Vincent. 1059  

XLIV.—Confirmation, or renewal and new grant, of privileges to the monastery of St. John the Evangelist in the diocese of Parma, of the Cassinese order. 1039  

XLV.—Confirms the possessions and privileges of the monastery of Molesme. 1062  

XLVI.—Commands the bishops of Sens, Volterra, Florence, Lucca, and Luni not to permit impediment of those who resort for prayer to the altar of Blessed James the Apostle, who works miracles in the church of Pistoia. 1062  

XLVII.—Grants an indulgence to those devoted to Blessed James. 1063  

XLVIII.—To Louis, king of France.—Concerning the undertaking of an expedition to the Holy Land. 1064  

XLIX.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Stephen at Freising. 1066  

L.—Privilege for the monastery of the Restored Place. 1067  

LI.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Remigius at Reims. 1069  

LII.—Privilege granted to the Carthusians of Mont-Dieu. 1071  

LIII.—Privilege for the monastery of Belleval. 1072  

LIV.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Mary at Cuissy. 1074  

LV.—Orders archbishops and bishops, without delay, to bless as abbots the elected provosts of the Premonstratensian order. 1076  

LVI.—Privilege for the church of St. John the Evangelist at Ravenna. 1077  

LVII.—Takes the church of Blessed Peter at Regensburg under protection and confirms its possessions.  

LVIII.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Mary at Springiersbach. 1080  

[Col. 1671A] LIX.—Commands Bernard, bishop of Hildesheim, and his successors not to alienate Wincenburg Castle; forbids the Goslar men, who had usurped a certain provostship, to be left unpunished. Recommends Provost C. and Canon R. 1082  

LX.—To Gregory, bishop of Bergamo. 1082  

LXI.—To P., prior, and the brethren of St. Frigdianus at Lucca. 1083  

LXII.—To the abbot and brethren of St. George at Lucca. 1083  

LXIII.—Privilege for the church of St. John at Rattenborn. 1084  

LXIV.—To Peter, bishop of Reggio, and Bertrand, bishop of Fréjus. 1085  

LXV.—Intercedes with Henry, bishop of Moravia, for brethren who departed without permission from the monastery on Mount Strahov. 1085  

LXVI.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Mary in Regola. 1085  

LXVII.—Takes the monastery of St. Peter at Ghent, or Blandinium, under protection and confirms its property and privileges. 1087  

LXVIII.—Privilege for the nunnery of Fara. 1089  

LXIX.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Lambert at Suben. 1091  

LXX.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Michael at Berg. 1092  

LXXI.—Confirmation of all the property and privileges granted to the monastery of Trinorc by the supreme Roman pontiffs. 1093  

LXXII.—To the bishops of Angoulême and Limoges.—That they are to settle by a canonical decision the dispute concerning Rocabovis-curtis between the Cluniacs and the clerics. 1095  

LXXIII.—Bull confirming the property of the monastery of Crisenon. 1096  

LXXIV.—Bull in favour of the monastery of St. Martin. 1097  

LXXV.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Zeno at Reichenhall. 1099  

LXXVI.—Informs St. Alexander of Bergamo of the definitive judgment rendered by him upon several points of dispute. 1100  

LXXVII.—Privilege for the monastery of La Chaise-Dieu. 1102  

LXXVIII.—Privilege for the monastery of Nantua. 1103  

LXXIX.—Privilege for the monastery of Mortemer. 1104  

LXXX.—Privilege for the monastery of Cluny. 1105  

LXXXI.—To H., prior, and the brethren of St. Marcellus of Salsets.—Confirms for them the gift of the church of Savatia, made by Eustace, bishop of Valence, before he became disobedient to the Roman Church. 1106  

LXXXII.—Grants Odo, prior, and the brethren of St. Martin-des-Champs that, when the canons of Blessed Gervasius at Énery die, monks may be substituted there. 1107  

LXXXIII.—Privilege for the church of St. Martin at Buron. 1107  

LXXXIV.—Bull for St. Evurtius at Orléans. 1109  

LXXXV.—Privilege for the church of St. Mary at Parma. 1111  

LXXXVI.—Privilege for the church of St. Andrew at Rochester. 1113  

LXXXVII.—Commends the establishment of regular canons in the church of Tarentaise. 1113  

LXXXVIII.—Confirms the rights and possessions of the regular canons of the church of St. Peter at Tarentaise, and decrees that the regular order according to the Rule of St. Augustine is always to be observed there. 1114  

LXXXIX.—Exhorts all the faithful of God established throughout Gaul to undertake the holy war. 1115  

XC.—Privilege for the monastery of SS. Peter and Paul at Westminster. 1115  

XCI.—To the chaplains of the church of Piacenza. 1117  

XCII.—To Abbot Suger.—That he is to assist before the king the monastery of Blessed Medardus, burdened by the count of Soissons. 1118  

XCIII.—To Bishop Egelbert and the canons of the church of Bamberg.—Concerning the sanctity, miracles, and canonization of Emperor Henry. 1118  

XCIV.—To Peter, archbishop of Bourges.—Concerning the primacy over the provinces of Bourges and Bordeaux. 1119  

XCV.—Bull confirming the property and immunities of Tongerlo. 1120  

XCVI.—To the clergy and people of Tournai.—Sends them a bishop, restored to the Church of Tournai after return from exile and consecrated by himself. 1122  

[Col. 1672] XCVII.—To Louis VII, king of the Franks.—Commends Anselm, bishop of Tournai, consecrated by himself. 1122  

XCVIII.—To Alvisus, bishop of Arras, and Milo, bishop of Thérouanne.—That they are to ensure that Anselm, consecrated by himself as bishop of Tournai, is received by the king of France and the count of Flanders. 1123  

XCIX.—To Bernard, abbot of Clairvaux.—Informs him that at his insistence he has consecrated Anselm bishop of Tournai, and orders him to labour diligently for Anselm’s peace. 1124  

XCIX bis.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Peter at Salzburg. 1125  

C.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Nicasius at Reims. 1127  

CI.—To Samson, archbishop of Reims.—Rebukes him because he presumed, contrary to the right of the archbishop of Bourges, to crown the king of the Franks in the city of Bourges, and therefore forbids him the use of the pallium. 1128  

CII.—Writes to the consuls of Lodi that “it is manifest that the document which the bishop of Lodi, under the name of Robaldus, archbishop of Milan of blessed memory, produced in the presence of his predecessor Lucius concerning the cause being litigated between himself and the brethren of Correto, was rejected by that pope.” 1129  

CIII.—Grants privileges to the monastery of Fleury. 1129  

CIV.—To Henry, bishop of Moravia.—Concerning a certain task entrusted to him for the sowing of peace. 1129  

CV.—To R., bishop of Bazas, concerning the abbey of St. Fremier. 1130  

CVI.—Privilege for the nunnery of Blessed Mary in the Wood of Nid-de-Merle. 1130  

CVII.—To the bishops of the province of Bordeaux.—Concerning ecclesiastical and canonical liberty. 1132  

CVIII.—Privilege for the canons of the church of St. Ursus at Aosta. 1135  

CIX.—Privilege for the monastery of Reichersberg. 1134  

CX.—Privilege for the monastery of SS. Peter and Paul at Paderborn. 1137  

CXI.—Commends the writings of Gerhoh, provost of Reichersberg, “against the most wicked innovations,” and exhorts him to perseverance. 1139  

CXII.—Privilege for the church of St. Lawrence at Clarholt. 1139  

CXIII.—Confirms in the church of St. Wigbert at Quedlinburg the canonical order established by Thomas, cardinal-priest and legate of the apostolic see. 1140  

CXIV.—To Henry, bishop of Moravia.—Consoles him, afflicted by adversity. Recommends Theobald, brother of Duke Vladislaus, released from excommunication. Announces the deposition from office of certain priests because they had conducted sacred rites for payment in the land of the excommunicated Conrad. Permits him to absolve Vladislaus. 1140  

CXV.—Confirms the rights of the monastery of Varlary concerning the election of an abbot and the bestowal of the advocacy. 1141  

CXVI.—Takes the church of St. Mary and St. Blasius at Fridesel under protection and confirms its possessions. 1142  

CXVII.—To Villanus, archbishop of Pisa, confirms with renewed liberality, in the year 1146, on the Kalends of June, in the eighth indiction, all the grants which Innocent II had formerly made to Baldwin. “Given at Viterbo through the hand of Robert, cardinal-chancellor of the Holy Roman Church.” 1142  

CXVIII.—Exhorts Henry, bishop of Moravia, Otto, bishop of Prague, Duke Vladislaus, and all clergy and people established throughout Bohemia and Moravia to restrain clerical incontinence. 1142  

CXIX.—Praises Vladislaus, duke of the Bohemians, as zealous for ecclesiastical affairs. Sends greetings to his wife Gertrude. Recommends Henry, bishop of Moravia. 1143  

CXX.—Privilege for the monastery of Stavelot. 1144  

CXXI.—Orders Henry, bishop of Moravia, to admonish Vladislaus, duke of Bohemia, to make satisfaction for damage done to the Church of Regensburg. 1145  

CXXII.—Takes the Church of the Holy Sepulchre at Jerusalem under protection and confirms its possessions. 1145  

CXXIII.—Commends Bishop Theobald because, on account of the property of the canons seized by citizens, he had forbidden the celebration of divine offices in his city. Orders him to ensure observance of the sentence of excommunication pronounced for the same cause against certain nobles by Guy, cardinal-priest. 1149  

CXXIV.—Orders Arnold of Trent, Lothair of Vicenza, Bellinus of Padua, bishops, to compel certain nobles to sell the property of the canons of Verona which they had seized. 1150  

CXXV.—Assures the canons of Verona that Cereto Castle was adjudged to them by Wido, cardinal-priest. 1151  

CXXVI.—At the request of Bishop Anselm, confirms the bishopric of Tournai, exempted from the authority of the bishops of Noyon. 1151  

CXXVII.—To Raymond, bishop of Périgueux, that he is to compel the clerics of Rocabovis-curtis by excommunication to restore that church to the Cluniacs. 1153  

CXXVIII.—Bull for the monastery of Gellone. 1154  

CXXIX.—Privilege for the church of St. Zeno at Hall. 1156  

CXXX.—Privilege for the church of St. Donatian at Bruges. 1158  

CXXXI.—To the abbot and monks of Bec. 1159  

CXXXII.—Privilege for the monastery of Peterborough. 1160  

CXXXIII.—Privilege for the same monastery. 1163  

CXXXIV.—To Theobald, bishop of Verona.—Warns him to order the excommunication pronounced against the enemies of the canons by the priests of Runchen and others to be observed. 1164  

CXXXV.—To Lothair, bishop of Vicenza.—That he is to punish the archpriest of St. Boniface, who communicated with excommunicated persons. 1165  

CXXXVI.—Privilege for the monastery of St. George in the diocese of Prüfening. 1165  

CXXXVII.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Margaret at Osterhofen. 1167  

CXXXVIII.—Privilege for the monastery of Windberg. 1168  

CXXXIX.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Mary at Abingdon. 1170  

CXL.—The regular order of Canons of St. Augustine established at Klosterneuburg, together with all its other privileges and immunities, temporal as well as spiritual, is confirmed by apostolic authority. 1172  

CXLI.—Grants Eberhard, bishop of Bamberg, the right to the pallium and other privileges. 1175  

CXLII.—Commends and entrusts Henry, bishop of Moravia, to Conrad, king of the Romans. 1175  

CXLIII.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Nicholas at Sept-Fontaines. 1176

CXLVIII.—To Louis, king of the Franks.—On the same matter. 1180  

CXLIX.—To the same.—On the same matter. 1181

CLXXXVII.—To Humbert, archbishop of Besançon.—That he is to assist the Cluniacs in reforming the church of Baume. 1228  

CLXXXVIII.—Bull in favour of the monastery of Tiron. 1228  

CLXXXIX.—Privilege for the church of St. Mary at Brane. 1231  

CXC.—Privilege for the monastery of Jandun. 1233  

CXCI.—Privilege concerning the churches subject to the bishop of Paris; concerning the agreement between Bishop Stephen and King Louis; concerning the prebends of canons who become bishops; and, further, concerning the levy which the king was accustomed to impose upon the bishop’s lands, remitted by King Louis. 1234  

CXCII.—Confirms the agreement between Stephen, formerly bishop of Paris, and Theobald, archdeacon, made through Matthew, bishop of Albano, John of St. Chrysogonus, and Peter of St. Calixtus, cardinal-priests. 1236  

CXCIII.—Bull for the nunnery of St. Dionysius at Montmartre. 1236  

CXCIII bis.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Martin-des-Champs. 1239  

CXCIV.—Bull concerning the dedication of the church of Montmartre. 1242  

CXCV.—Confirms the agreement made by Giraldus, bishop [of Limoges], between the monasteries of Uzerche and Meymac. 1242  

CXCVI.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Heribert at Deutz. 1244  

CXCVII.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Quentin at Mont. 1245  

[Col. 1675A] CXCVIII.—Bull to Ivo, abbot, and the monks of Redon, confirming their privileges. 1247  

CXCIX.—To Stephen, king of the English.—That he is to receive Robert, bishop of London, into his favour. 1248  

CC.—To Matilda, queen of the English.—That she is to urge her husband to love the aforesaid bishop. 1249  

CCI.—To Theobald, archbishop of Canterbury.—Concerning the dispute between the archbishop of Canterbury and Bernard, bishop of St. David’s, over metropolitan right. Orders both to come before him “on the feast of Blessed Luke in the following year.” 1250  

CCII.—Fragment of a privilege for the monastery of St. Martin-des-Champs. 1250  

CCIII.—To the priests of the churches of the monastery of Baume.—Relaxes the interdict by which he had justly punished the churches belonging to the monastery of Baume. 1251  

CCIV.—Orders Henry, bishop of Moravia, to exhort Conrad, king of the Romans, to devote attention to the union of the Church of Constantinople with the Roman Church. 1251  

CCV.—Privilege for the church of St. Saviour at Saragossa. 1252  

CCVI.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Mary at Lucelle. 1253  

CCVII.—Privilege for the church of St. Mary of the Place of God. 1254  

CCVIII.—To the consuls of Lucca.—On behalf of the brethren of the church of St. Frigdianus. 1256  

CCIX.—To [Gregory], bishop of Lucca.—On the same matter. 1257  

CCX.—Takes under protection the abbey of noble Benedictine nuns at Messines, in the diocese of Ypres, enumerates and confirms its possessions. 1257  

CCXI.—Privilege for the monastery of Tronchiennes. 1259  

CCXII.—Grants a bull to Nicholas, abbot of Corbie, given at Auxerre through the hand of Guy, cardinal-deacon and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the third day before the Kalends of August (30 July), in the tenth indiction, in the year 1147. 1260  

CCXIII.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Mary of Vallis Christiana. 1260  

CCXIV.—To Henry, bishop of Moravia.—Says that it would have been more pleasing to him had he gone to the Holy Land rather than against the Slavs in Pomerania. 1262  

CCXV.—Takes the monastery of St. Mary of Neuburg into the protection of the apostolic see. 1262  

CCXVI.—Bull confirming the Church of Ilbenstadt. 1263  

CCXVII.—Takes the monastery of Aldersbach, of the Cistercian order, under the protection of the apostolic see. 1265  

CCXVIII.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Mary at Huntingdon. 1266  

CCXIX.—Bull confirming the possessions of the abbey of St. Mary of Bertin-court, or Moncel. 1268  

CCXX.—Privilege for the monastery of Rigny. 1269  

CCXXI.—To the bishops of Mâcon and Chalon.—That they are to compel Jocerannus Grossus, lord of Brancidun, to make satisfaction for injuries done to the monastery of Cluny, in accordance with the decision of the archbishop of Lyons. 1271  

CCXXII.—Asserts to the monastery of Cluny the holding of Baerne-Monteria, granted by William, count of Mâcon. 1272  

CCXXIII.—Bull confirming the property and immunities of the Church of Stivagium. 1274  

CCXXIV.—Privilege for the monastery of Yergua. 1278  

CCXXV.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Mary of Nienzabas. 1279  

CCXXVI.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Vitus at Prüfening. 1280  

CCXXVII.—Bull to the Savignian brethren.—Confirms their union with the Cistercian order. 1282  

CCXXVIII.—Charter concerning the recognition of the right of St. Mammetus in the territory of Dijon. 1282  

CCXXIX.—To Abbot Suger.—Asks which bishops refuse to give him aid for the defence of the realm; a definite place is appointed for the council; concerning the excommunicated duke of Lorraine; concerning the church of Buxis. 1283  

CCXXX.—Fragment of a bull by which he confirms the property and possessions of the monastery of St. Lambert at Laeti. 1284  

CCXXXI.—Summons Henry, bishop of Moravia, to the council of Trier and commends to him John, his legate. 1284  

CCXXXII.—To H. [Eberhard], archbishop, [Col. 1676] and the bishops and abbots established throughout the province of Salzburg.—On the same matter. 1284  

CCXXXIII.—Privilege for the monastery of St. John at Réome. 1285  

CCXXXIV.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Mary at Jette. 1285  

CCXXXV.—Privilege for the nunnery of Helder. 1287  

CCXXXVI.—Privilege for Christ Church, London. 1289  

CCXXXVII.—Asserts certain tithes to the church of St. Mary and St. John, situated above the river Marne near Gournay Castle. 1291  

CCXXXVIII.—Privilege for the nunnery of the Holy Spirit, the Paraclete. 1291  

CCXXXIX.—To the abbot of Cluny.—Decrees that henceforth the abbot of St. Germanus at Auxerre is to be elected with the counsel of the abbot of Cluny, and that the elect is to receive blessing from the bishop of Auxerre. 1294  

CCXL.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Augustine at Thérouanne. 1295  

CCXLI.—Releases Henry, bishop of Moravia, from the summons to the council of Trier. 1296  

CCXLII.—Takes the church of St. Alban at Basel under his protection and confirms each of its possessions by name. 1297  

CCXLIII.—Rebukes T[heobald], bishop of Verona, because, without restoration of the canons’ possessions, he had released the city from interdict. Orders him to ensure their restoration. 1298  

CCXLIV.—Writes to P[eregrinus], patriarch of Aquileia, that he wonders why he had absolved certain knights excommunicated for occupying the possessions of the Church of Verona. Orders him to induce them to restore what they had taken. 1299  

CCXLV.—To Henry the Younger, king of the Romans.—Praises his zeal for the Church and wishes him all prosperity. 1299  

CCXLVI.—To Anselm, bishop of Havelberg.—That he is to ensure restoration of estates of Corbie which his own men had usurped. 1300  

CCXLVII.—To Reinher, canon of Havelberg.—That he is to restore twenty holdings (*mansi*) which he had taken from the monastery of Corbie. 1300  

CCXLVIII.—Privilege for the monastery of Laach. 1301  

CCXLIX.—Takes the monastery of St. Peter in the Black Forest under protection and confirms its property. 1302  

CCL.—Takes the monastery of Heilsbronn under protection and confirms its possessions. 1303  

CCLI.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Eucharius at Trier. 1303  

CCLII.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Mary at Lonnig. 1304  

CCLIII.—To priests, clerics, and laypersons established throughout the parishes of Archa and Zülpich. 1305  

CCLIV.—To the monks of Corbie.—Exhorts them to show humble reverence to Abbot Wilbald. 1306  

CCLV.—To Henry, bishop of Liège.—That he is to restrain those who plunder the property of the monastery of Stavelot. 1306  

CCLVI.—To the abbot and brethren of St. Benedict above the Po.—Orders them to show obedience and reverence to the abbot of Cluny, and forbids them to elect an abbot for themselves without his authority, command, counsel, and consent. 1306  

CCLVII.—Takes the monastery of St. Disibod under protection and confirms its property and privileges. 1307  

CCLVIII.—Privilege for the monastery of Bonifaget. 1307  

CCLIX.—Bull to the captains, vassals of the monastery of Nonantola.—That they are to defend the monastery against enemies. 1309  

CCLX.—Privilege for the church of the Holy Apostles on Monte Cornelio at Liège. 1309  

CCLXI.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Mary of Longpont. 1311  

CCLXII.—Confirms the property and privileges of the monastery of Benediktbeuern. 1312  

CCLXIII.—Confirms the judgment pronounced by certain bishops between Henry, abbot of Hersfeld, and Otto, bishop of Halberstadt, concerning tithes. 1314  

CCLXIV.—To Moses, archbishop of Ravenna.—Concerning his right regarding confirmation of the election of the bishop of Piacenza. 1314  

CCLXV.—Privilege for the monastery of Lorsch. 1314  

CCLXVI.—Mandate to archbishops, bishops, etc., concerning restitution to be made to the monastery of Lorsch. 1316  

CCLXVII.—Confirms the privileges and possessions of the monastery of Maulbronn. 1316  

[Col. 1677] CCLXVIII.—Privilege for the monastery of Helmershausen. 1317  

CCLXIX.—Privilege confirming all the property of the monastery of Altach, or Lower Altach, in the diocese of Salzburg. 1318  

CCLXX.—Orders P[eregrinus], patriarch of Aquileia, to command certain counts to pay the three hundred pounds owed to T[heobald], bishop of Verona, and to restore to the canons of Verona the estates taken from them. 1319  

CCLXXI.—To Henry the Younger, king of the Romans.—Promises that he will provide for his aunt, the duchess of Poland. 1320  

CCLXXII.—To the German prelates.—That they are to assist the younger King Henry and help him with their counsel and actions. 1320  

CCLXXIII.—Privilege for the church of St. Mary at Cambrai. 1321  

CCLXXIV.—To Odo, duke of Burgundy.—Charges him with hostility toward the Church of Vézelay. 1323  

CCLXXV.—To I., countess of Nevers.—Rebukes her because she harasses those travelling to Vézelay. 1323  

CCLXXVI.—Privilege for the monastery of Affligem, in the diocese of Cambrai. 1323  

CCLXXVII.—Confirms the altars, possessions, and privileges of the abbey of Ename, of the Order of St. Benedict in the diocese of Mechelen. 1325  

CCLXXVIII.—Takes the Church of Włocławek into his faith and protection, and confirms the boundaries of the bishopric and the limits of the diocese of Włocławek established by Giles, bishop of Tusculum, and Bolesław, duke of Poland. 1328  

CCLXXIX.—Confirms to St. Martin a perpetual prebend in the church of Amiens. 1331  

CCLXXX.—To A., archbishop of Bremen, H., bishop of Minden, and T., bishop of Verden.—That they are to ensure the restoration of estates of the monastery of Kammin which had been usurped by various persons. 1331  

CCLXXXI.—To the monks of Corbie.—Confirms the deposition of Abbot Henry. 1332  

CCLXXXII.—Takes the monastery of SS. Facundus and Primitivus at Sahagún under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. 1332  

CCLXXXIII.—Bull for the abbey of St. Mary of Flavigny-sur-Mont. 1332  

CCLXXXIV.—To the people of Fulda.—Declares void the election made by them against his command, and orders them, in the presence of certain abbots whom he names, to elect an abbot from another monastery. 1334  

CCLXXXV.—To the abbots of Ebrach, Eberbach, Hersfeld, and Corbie.—That, on going to Fulda, they are to ensure the election of an abbot from another monastery. 1335  

CCLXXXVI.—Privilege for the nunnery of St. Andrew at Göss. 1335  

CCLXXXVII.—Takes the monastery of St. Giles of Canawella under his protection. 1336  

CCLXXXVIII.—A letter of like tenor to the Gallican bishops, defining the rights of Marmoutier in the parishes subject to it. 1337  

CCLXXXIX.—Orders the deans established throughout the archdeaconry of the Church of Bonn to obey Provost G. 1338  

CCLXXXIX bis.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Thierry at Reims. 1338  

CCXC.—Privilege for the abbey of St. Dionysius at Paris. 1339  

CCXCI.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Remigius at Reims. 1342  

CCXCII.—To the abbess and nuns of St. Peter at Reims.—A safeguard for the abbess and nuns of St. Peter at Reims against the abbot and monks of St. Nicasius, concerning the paved road of Turnus. 1342  

CCXCIII.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Mary at Bas-Fontaine. 1343  

CCXCIV.—Bull confirming the substitution of Premonstratensians at Bucilly. 1344  

CCXCV.—Takes the monastery of Thelon under protection and confirms its Premonstratensian discipline and property. 1345  

CCXCVI.—To A. [Alfonso], king of Spain.—Confirms the primacy of Toledo. 1345  

CCXCVII.—To Abbot Suger.—Concerning the placement of monks in the church of St. Geneviève. 1347  

CCXCVIII.—To the canons of St. Geneviève.—That they are to receive honourably the monks whom he is about to send to their monastery. 1347  

CCXCIX.—Brief letter to Hugh, bishop of Auxerre. 1348  

CCC.—Privilege for the Church of the Holy Sepulchre at Jerusalem. 1348  

CCCI.—Privilege for the church called the Parish [Col. 1678] of the Martyrs [at Ulc]. 1350  

CCCII.—Privilege for the monastery of Bellelay. 1352  

CCCIII.—To Humbert, archbishop of Besançon, etc.—That they are to punish fittingly the contempt of the Roman Church in the priest who had transgressed an excommunication pronounced by him and had stolen the revenues of the monastery of Baume from the Cluniacs. 1353  

CCCIV.—Takes the monastery of Rüeggisberg under protection and confirms its possessions. 1354  

CCCV.—To Abbot Suger.—Having changed his plan, he no longer wishes to send monks to the church of St. Geneviève, but regular canons. 1354  

CCCVI.—The possessions of the monastery of Clairvaux at Milan.
confirmed. 1354. CCCVII.—To Albero, archbishop of Trier, Albero, bishop of Verdun, and the archdeacons of the Churches of Metz and Toul: he commands them, under pain of excommunication, to admonish Duke Matthew to destroy the castle built near Toul. 1354. CCCVIII.—He orders the churches of the bishopric of Cremona to obey Bishop Oberto. 1355. CCCIX.—Privilege for the monastery of Toul. 1356. CCCX.—He attests that the church of St Mary at Susa has been assigned by him to the Church of Ulci. 1358. CCCXI.—To all the Roman clergy.—That chaplains shall promise obedience to the rectors of the titular churches, or churches. 1358. CCCXII.—Bull for the churches of St Ambrose at Milan. 1358. CCCXIII.—He takes the convent of St Maurice at Milan under protection and confirms its possessions. 1360. CCCXIV.—Bull for a canon of St Anthony at Piacenza. 1361. CCCXV.—He confirms the privileges granted by Innocent II to the monastery of St Saviour and to the canonical order established there by the worthy undertaking of Bonfilius. 1361. CCCXVI.—To Gerard, bishop of Bologna. 1363. CCCXVII.—He confirms all the property and complete exemption of the monastery of the Holy Saviour and the martyr Julia, in the diocese of Brescia, of the Cassinese order, and grants other privileges. 1363. CCCXVIII.—Privilege for the church of Blessed Mary at Brescia. 1366. CCCXIX.—He entrusts to Henry, bishop of Moravia, the affairs to be accomplished by Guy, cardinal-deacon and legate sent into Poland, both there and in that other land newly illumined by the light of the Christian faith. 1368. CCCXX.—He praises Abbot Suger for having regulated the condition of the church of St Geneviève. 1368. CCCXXI.—He confirms the monastery of St Mary in the Sand at Wrocław. 1369. CCCXXII.—To John, bishop-elect of Piacenza. 1369. CCCXXIII.—He orders the clergy and people of Piacenza to obey their metropolitan, the archbishop of Ravenna. 1369. CCCXXIV.—To Moses, archbishop of Ravenna.—That the bishops-elect of Piacenza shall receive consecration from him and his successors. 1370. CCCXXV.—Privilege for the church of St Mary at Luni. 1371. CCCXXVI.—Bull confirming to the Camaldolese hermitage the donations of Jerome, bishop of Arezzo. 1372. CCCXXVII.—Bull for the convent of St Hilary situated in the bishopric of Fiesole. 1373. CCCXXVIII.—Bull for the monastery of nuns of St Martin of Agello. 1375. CCCXXIX.—To the bishops of Auxerre and Soissons and Abbot Suger.—Concerning the election of the bishop of Arras. 1376. CCCXXX.—Bull for Guy, abbot of the monastery of St Mary of Morrona. 1377. CCCXXXI.—Papal protection granted to the monastery of the Scots at St James’s, Regensburg. 1378. CCCXXXII.—To the lord Abbot Suger.—Concerning the affairs of the church of St Geneviève. 1379. CCCXXXIII.—To Abbot Suger.—Concerning the affairs of the church of St Geneviève. 1380. CCCXXXIV.—To Abbot Suger.—That he provide Hugh of St Victor with expenses for a journey to Rome; and concerning the affairs of the church of St Geneviève. 1380. CCCXXXV.—To Abbot Wibald and the brethren of Corvey.—That the deposed Henry find no place among them. 1380. CCCXXXVI.—He adjudicates the disputes between Ralph, bishop of Orta, and the canons of that cathedral church. 1381. CCCXXXVII.—To Hugh, abbot of the monastery of St Augustine at Canterbury. 1382. [Col. 1679] CCCXXXVIII.—Bull for the hermitage of Fonte Avellana. 1383. CCCXXXIX.—Privilege for the monastery of St Peter at Modena. 1384. CCCXL.—He congratulates Henry, bishop of Moravia, on the return of the people to obedience. 1385. CCCXLI.—To Henry, bishop of Moravia.—That he absolve Wladislaw, duke of Poland, from excommunication. 1385. CCCXLII.—He orders the clergy and people of Lemos and other peoples to obey the bishop of Lugo, to whom, by command of the apostolic see, their churches had already been restored, having previously been occupied by the bishop of Oviedo. 1386. CCCXLIII.—He commends a certain person to Henry, bishop of Moravia. 1386. CCCXLIV.—To the archpriests of the diocese of Modena. 1387. CCCXLV.—Privilege for the monastery of St Peter at Salzburg. 1387. CCCXLVI.—He exhorts Guy, abbot of Bonneval, to admit the monastery of Grandval and its monks among the brethren of the Cistercian order. 1390. CCCXLVII.—To the abbots of Cuxa, Bisuldun, and others.—That they obey G., abbot of St Victor at Marseilles, upon whom he has conferred the office of blessing. 1390. CCCXLVIII.—To Conrad, nobleman and margrave. 1390. CCCXLIX.—To [Hugh], archbishop of Sens, and [Hugh], archbishop of Rouen.—He warns them to compel their parishioners, who had inflicted losses and injuries upon the Church of Paris, to make satisfaction to that Church. 1391. CCCL.—To H. [Hugh], archbishop of Vienne, to whom is entrusted the investigation of the controversy between Henry, bishop of Autun, and Peter the Venerable, abbot of Cluny, concerning ownership of the churches of Poligny. 1391. CCCLI.—To Hugh, abbot of the monastery of St Augustine at Canterbury. 1391. CCCLII.—Rescript to Theobald, archbishop of the Church of Canterbury, concerning the absolution of Prior Silvester. 1392. CCCLIII.—To the archbishop and chapter of the Church of Tours.—He refuses to write to the people of Dol and Saint-Brieuc, as being excommunicated. 1392. CCCLIV.—To Conrad, king of the Romans.—He consoles him on his return from Jerusalem, because of the tribulations inflicted upon him and his army. 1393. CCCLV.—To H., archbishop of Sens, and his suffragans.—On the same subject. 1394. CCCLVI.—To Abbot Suger.—Concerning disturbers of the kingdom of France. 1395. CCCLVII.—To Abbot Suger.—Concerning the return of Louis VII, king of France, from lands overseas. 1396. CCCLVIII.—Letters concerning the election of Matilda as second abbess of Fontevraud. 1396. CCCLIX.—To King Conrad.—He confirms for his chaplain Theobald the provostship of Xanten, provided that he resign the other provostship which he formerly possessed. 1397. CCCLX.—To Bermond, bishop of Béziers.—He commands him to permit Trencavel, viscount of Béziers, to construct a chapel in his palace. 1397. CCCLXI.—To Serlo, abbot of Savigny.—That he and all subject to his monastery live according to the Cistercian rule. 1398. CCCLXII.—He grieves over the health of Henry, bishop of Moravia, and consoles him. 1398. CCCLXIII.—To Henry, archbishop of Mainz.—He commands that “both personally and through his suffragan bishops he give careful and diligent attention to the wanderings of false messengers, who travel about in his name and presume to harass the faithful of the Church with unlawful exactions; and, if any should fall into his hands or those of his suffragans—especially Ildebrandinus, formerly servant of Jacintus, cardinal-deacon—he shall have them arrested.” 1399. CCCLXIV.—To all the brethren of Fontevraud. 1400. CCCLXV.—Privilege for the monastery of St Lucius at Chur. 1400. CCCLXVI.—To Abbot Suger.—That he decide, by judicial process, the case of two excommunicated clerics. 1401. CCCLXVII.—To Emperor Conrad.—At his request he again confirms the election of the provost of Xanten, and postpones the deposition of the archbishop of Cologne. 1402. CCCLXVIII.—Bull to Oberto, archbishop of Milan. 1403. CCCLXIX.—Concerning the annual celebration of the dedication of the church of Blessed Frigidianus at Lucca. 1404. CCCLXX.—To the archbishop of Braga.—He suspends him from episcopal office unless he render obedience to the archbishop of Toledo. 1405. CCCLXXI.—To Alfonso, king of Spain.—Concerning the primacy of Toledo. 1405. CCCLXXII.—To Abbot Suger.—That he investigate the case of a priest excommunicated by the archdeacon, and excommunicate those who assaulted the priest. 1405. CCCLXXIII.—To H., archbishop of Sens.—On the same subject. 1407. CCCLXXIV.—To Abbot Suger.—He appoints him judge in another ecclesiastical case. 1407. CCCLXXV.—He confirms the canonical discipline of the brethren of St Laud at Rouen. 1408. CCCLXXVI.—To the prelates of Poland.—He rebukes them because they have not observed the sentence of interdict issued by his messenger G., and, that they may repent, confirms the same sentence. 1408. CCCLXXVII.—Privilege for the monastery of St Martin at Anhausen. 1409. CCCLXXVIII.—To the bishop of Castello [Venice]. 1411. CCCLXXIX.—Bull for the monastery of St Benedict at Piacenza. 1411. CCCLXXX.—He grants to Guibert, provost, and the canons of St Lawrence at Genoa a broad confirmation of all their goods and rights, including the donation of Count Raymond. 1411. CCCLXXXI.—Privilege for the church of Fontevraud. 1413. CCCLXXXII.—To Abbot Suger.—Concerning King Louis’s plan for an overseas expedition. 1414. CCCLXXXIII.—To Abbot Suger.—That he cause the treasury of the church of St Geneviève, pledged as security, to be redeemed. 1415. CCCLXXXIV.—He confirms the goods, possessions, and privileges of St Mary of Reno. 1415. CCCLXXXV.—Bull concerning the transfer of the monastery of Middelburg. 1417. CCCLXXXVI.—To the canons of the church of Orléans.—On behalf of Lord Philip, concerning the church of St Leta, which he asserts belongs to his deanery. 1418. CCCLXXXVII.—To Abbot Suger.—That he decide the ecclesiastical case concerning which letters 372 and 373 have already been issued. 1418. CCCLXXXVIII.—To Peter, provost of Ulci.—He commands that henceforth no one shall ever be ordained or received in the church of St Mary at Susa, nor shall food or a gift of clothing be granted to anyone, unless, having first taken the regular habit, he has professed the canonical life. 1419. CCCLXXXIX.—He takes the monastery of St Nicholas at Angers under protection. 1419. CCCXC.—To Abbot Suger.—Concerning the Eastern Church; the conference held between the pope and king; and the Church of Compiègne. 1419. CCCXCI.—To Abbot Wibald.—That he excommunicate Godebold, canon of Minden, unless he restore the church of Hemeringen, taken from Everard. 1420. CCCXCII.—To Abbot Wibald.—He praises his zeal for the Roman Church and, in his favour, writes to the bishop of Minden and the archbishop of Bremen. 1420. CCCXCIII.—To Henry, bishop of Minden.—That the church of Kammin, because of the unforeseen accident and death of a certain monk, has no need of reconciliation; and that he cause what was taken from that church to be restored. 1421. CCCXCIV.—To Hartwig, bishop of Bremen.—He commends Abbot Wibald to him and asks that the estates taken from the Church of Kammin be restored. 1421. CCCXCV.—To King Conrad.—He gratefully receives his embassy, through which the affairs of Church and kingdom are strengthened. He has entrusted the matter of the monastery of Morbach to the bishop of Lausanne; and concerning Otto, who had cut off a cleric’s nose. 1422. CCCXCVI.—He takes the monastery of Ebrach under protection and confirms its goods. 1423. CCCXCVII.—He takes the convent of Wechterswinkel under protection. 1423. CCCXCVIII.—To Pontius, abbot of Vézelay.—On the same subject. 1423. CCCXCIX.—To the duke of Burgundy.—He rebukes him because he is hostile to the monastery of Vézelay. 1423. CD.—To Henry, bishop of Autun.—He rebukes him because he is hostile to the monastery of Vézelay. 1424. CDI.—To Hugh, bishop of Auxerre.—On the same subject. 1424. CDII.—He confirms all the goods, donations, and exemptions of the monastery of St Quirinus at Tegernsee, which is declared subject to the ordinary bishop in spiritual matters. 1425. [Col. 1681] CDIII.—To Eberhard, archbishop of Salzburg.—That he compel Otto, son of Otto, count palatine, to make satisfaction to Otto, bishop of Freising, for the injury inflicted; or, if unwilling, excommunicate him; and that he hold the brethren of Tegernsee monastery commended to his care. 1427. CDIV.—To P., prior of the church of St Frigidianus at Lucca. 1427. CDV.—He confirms the privileges and immunities of the canonical church of St Mary of Montbellet. 1428. CDVI.—Privilege for the church of the canons of Blessed Mary at Raitenbuch, in the diocese of Freising, under the Rule of St Augustine. 1429. CDVII.—He enumerates the possessions of the abbey of Lobbes, of the Order of St Benedict, in the diocese of Liège, and confirms and enlarges its privileges. 1431. CDVIII.—To the abbot and convent of Lobbes.—That they no longer sit in the refectory with the canons, nor be in a single choir with them. 1434. CDIX.—Privilege for the monastery of St Mary at Compiègne. 1435. CDX.—Privilege for the Church of Penn, at the request of Bishop Grimald. 1437. CDXI.—At the request of Bishop Michael, he confirms the possessions of the Church of Monopoli. 1437. CDXII.—He congratulates Godescalc upon his appointment as bishop of Arras. 1438. CDXIII.—To Eberhard, bishop of Bamberg, etc.—That he restore monks to the church of Heidenheim, after expelling the secular clerics from it. 1439. CDXIV.—To Henry, archbishop of Mainz.—On the same subject. 1440. CDXV.—To Goswin of Cîteaux and all the abbots assembled at Cîteaux.—He writes that, had duties not prevented it, he would gladly have attended their assembly. 1441. CDXVI.—To Abbot Suger of St Denis.—Concerning the violence of the count of Anjou against his brother Robert. 1441. CDXVII.—To the same.—He commends Mo., a subdeacon. 1441. CDXVIII.—To Abbot Suger.—He consoles him over the death of his nephew. 1442. CDXIX.—He confirms the privileges and possessions of the monastery of the Saviour and St Boniface at Fulda. 1442. CDXX.—Privilege for the monastery of Weissenau. 1444. CDXXI.—He confirms the churches and goods, extensively enumerated, of the abbey of St Saviour of Majella; protects its rights and vindicates its liberty. 1444. CDXXII.—To the archbishop of Sens.—That he judge the controversy between the bishop of Orléans and the abbot of Vézelay. 1449. CDXXIII.—To M. [Manasses], bishop of Orléans.—On the same subject. 1449. CDXXIV.—Bull for the bishops of Orléans. 1449. CDXXV.—To Pontius, abbot of Vézelay.—Concerning the controversy which he had with the bishop of Autun. 1451. CDXXVI.—Privilege for the monastery of the Holy Trinity and St Michael at Miletus. 1452. CDXXVII.—To Louis, king of France.—For the Church of Beauvais. 1454. CDXXVIII.—To Henry, bishop of Beauvais.—Likewise on the same subject. 1455. CDXXIX.—To Hugh, bishop of Auxerre, and Bernard, abbot of Clairvaux.—For the reconciliation of the king with the bishop of Beauvais. 1456. CDXXX.—To Hugh, archbishop of Rouen.—Likewise concerning the harassment of the Church of Beauvais. 1457. CDXXXI.—To G., rector, and the people of Bologna.—That they defend the inhabitants of St Cassian and Rudolph, bishop of Imola, against the injuries of the people of Imola. 1457. CDXXXII.—Privilege for the Church of Beauvais. 1458. CDXXXIII.—To Henry, bishop of Beauvais.—He responds to Henry’s letters requesting release from the burden of episcopal dignity; neither Eugenius nor Adrian IV, who succeeded him after Anastasius IV, had been willing to grant that request. 1459. CDXXXIV.—To Hugh, archbishop of Rouen.—For Hugh of Gournay. 1460. CDXXXV.—To Henry, bishop of Beauvais.—He refuses permission to lay down the episcopal office. 1460. CDXXXVI.—Privilege for the monastery of Michaelstein. 1460. CDXXXVII.—Bull for Guarin, abbot of St John in the Valley (Chartres). 1462. [Col. 1682] CDXXXVIII.—Bull for Theobald, abbot of St Caraunus. 1463. CDXXXIX.—Confirmation of the privileges granted by Pope Innocent II to the monastery of Rott, Order of St Benedict. 1464. CDXL.—Bull for the monastery of St Quiricus of Rosis. 1466. CDXLI.—He confirms the metropolitan rights of Robert, archbishop of Acerenza, and grants him the pallium. 1467. CDXLII.—He takes the convent of St Cyriacus at Gerndorf under protection and confirms its possessions, imposing upon the sisters an annual rent of one mark of silver. 1469. CDXLIII.—To the abbots of St Pontius and Crass.—That they observe the decree of Urban II at the Council of Clermont. 1469. CDXLIV.—He consoles the nuns of St George at Prague over the death of Heinec, bishop of Olomouc, their greatest benefactor, and gives thanks for the ornaments sent. 1470. CDXLV.—He confirms the privileges of the hospital of St Blaise. 1470. CDXLVI.—He confirms the goods and privileges of the convent of St Peter Major at Florence. 1471. CDXLVII.—To the archbishop of Tarragona, legate of the apostolic see.—That he acknowledge the primacy of Toledo. 1472. CDXLVIII.—Privileges for the church of Imola. 1473. CDXLIX.—He adjudicates the controversy between the clerics of St John and St Sabina among the Marsi concerning the consecration of oil. 1474. CDL.—To Raymond, archbishop of Toledo.—He congratulates him because the archbishop of Braga has subjected himself to his primacy; he rebukes him because he invaded the latter’s territory and treated him too harshly. 1475. CDLI.—He confirms the possessions of the monastery of St Mary on Pongartenberg and takes it under his protection. 1476. CDLII.—To [Eberhard], archbishop of Salzburg.—He commands him to judge between the abbot of Baugarten and [Conrad], bishop of Passau, disputing certain possessions. 1477. CDLIII.—To the bishop of Passau.—He informs him of the mandate given to the archbishop of Salzburg. 1478. CDLIV.—He takes the convent of St Zacharias at Venice under the protection of the apostolic see and confirms its goods. 1479. CDLV.—He confirms the possessions of the monastery of Altenberg. 1480. CDLVI.—Privilege for the canons of Pistoia, from their archive. 1480. CDLVII.—Protective bull issued for the monastery of Esrum. 1482. CDLVIII.—To Theobald, archbishop of Canterbury.—That he consecrate [Silvester], abbot-elect of the monastery of St Augustine. 1483. CDLIX.—To Otto I, bishop of Freising.—That in the case concerning an estate to be restored by Otto, count palatine, he favour the monks of Tegernsee. 1484. CDLX.—To Eberhard, archbishop of Salzburg.—That he keep Count Otto excommunicated until he make satisfaction to Tegernsee monastery for the tithes taken from it. 1484. CDLXI.—To [Andrew], archbishop of Ragusa. 1485. CDLXII.—To P., prior of the church of St Frigidianus at Lucca. 1485. CDLXIII.—To Conrad, vicar, and all the Roman clergy. 1486. CDLXIV.—To Arnold, archbishop of Cologne.—Concerning confirmation of the many rights and privileges long ago granted to the archbishop and to the priests and canons of the metropolitan church of Cologne. 1486. CDLXV.—To the people of Cologne.—He sends back to them Archbishop Arnold, consecrated by his own hand and adorned with the pallium, commanding them to obey him, etc. 1488. CDLXVI.—To King Conrad.—That he honourably received his ambassadors and complied with all his wishes. 1489. CDLXVII.—To Henry, bishop of Liège.—That he compel the counts of Loon and Montaigu to restore what they took from Stavelot monastery. 1490. CDLXVIII.—To Hartwig, archbishop of Bremen.—That he ensure restoration of the estates taken from Kammin monastery by his parishioners. 1491. CDLXIX.—To Henry, archbishop of Mainz.—That he procure restoration of what his parishioners took from Corvey monastery. 1491. [Col. 1683] CDLXX.—To Bernard, bishop of Paderborn.—That under the rigour of anathema he compel Widikind to restore what he took from Corvey monastery. 1492. CDLXXI.—To Herman, bishop of Utrecht.—That he preserve the estates of Corvey monastery situated in his diocese. 1492. CDLXXII.—To Ulrich, bishop of Halberstadt.—That he restrain his parishioners who trouble the brethren of Corvey. 1493. CDLXXIII.—To Henry, duke of Saxony.—He commends to him Wibald, abbot of Corvey. 1493. CDLXXIV.—To the bishop of Verden.—He complains that his brother and other parishioners are invading the goods of Kammin monastery. 1493. CDLXXV.—To the bishop of Minden.—That he continue to benefit Corvey monastery. 1494. CDLXXVI.—To the abbot of Lüneburg.—That Henry, abbot of Corvey, deposed from his office, has not been restored. 1494. CDLXXVII.—He commands the abbot of Lüneburg not to allow Corvey monastery to be harassed by Henry, the deposed abbot. 1495. CDLXXVIII.—Bull for the monastery of Waldsassen. 1495. CDLXXIX.—He confirms the privileges of the Church of Aosta [in the province of Tarentaise]. 1496. CDLXXX.—To Henry, bishop of Beauvais.—Concerning the case of Master Peter. 1498. CDLXXXI.—To the same.—For the nephew of the abbot of St Denis. 1499. CDLXXXII.—Rescript to Hugh, abbot of St Remigius, that he provide for the needs of the Carthusians of Mont-Dieu. 1499. CDLXXXIII.—Fragment of a privilege addressed to William, dean, and the canons of Vienne in the land of the Allobroges.—He confirms to them all the privileges and goods of the church of Vienne, enumerating among other things “Pupet with its appurtenances; a third part of the coinage of Vienne; the municipality called Conveniacum, with its church and appurtenances; Charentoniacum; Chomondum; the borough called Villa; the estate of St Clarus; the church of Reventin; St Victor’s, St Peter’s of Sessiacum; the estate of Faramundus; the church of St Genesius; Mount Solomon.” 1500. CDLXXXIV.—To the prelates, counts, and barons established throughout Germany.—That they assist Emperor Conrad in the Italian expedition. 1501. CDLXXXV.—To the abbot of Reigny.—He appoints him judge in the controversy mentioned in the preceding letter. 1502. CDLXXXVI.—To the abbot of Chora.—Concerning the tithe which he had usurped at Vézelay, and the money which he had borrowed. 1502. CDLXXXVII.—To the bishop of Langres, etc.—Concerning the controversy of the abbot of Vézelay with the bishop of Autun. 1502. CDLXXXVIII.—To G., bishop of Langres.—That he excommunicate the count of Nevers unless he repent. 1503. CDLXXXIX.—Privilege for the monastery of Bremet. 1504. CDXC.—He receives the monastery of Heidenheim under his protection and grants it various privileges. 1507. CDXCI.—He commends Adalbert, abbot of Heidenheim, to Eberhard of Bamberg and Burchard of Eichstätt, bishops, that they assist him in every way. 1508. CDXCII.—He earnestly commends Abbot Adelbert of Heidenheim and his brethren to Gerhard, count of Eichstätt. 1509. CDXCIII.—He commands Adelbert, advocate of Heidenheim monastery, to support Adelbert, abbot of that monastery, and protect him from attacks. 1509. CDXCIV.—To the archbishops of Rouen, Reims, and Sens, etc.—For the Church of Beauvais. 1510. CDXCV.—To Henry, bishop of Beauvais.—For the church of Ruricourt. 1511. CDXCV *bis*.—Confirmation of all the goods and liberties of Ror monastery of Regular Canons of St Augustine, in the diocese of Regensburg. 1511. CDXCVI.—Privilege for the Church of Coventry, at the request of Bishop Walter. 1513. CDXCVII.—To Bernard, bishop of Saintes.—That he permit a new church to be built. 1514. CDXCVIII.—Privilege for the monastery of Silviniac. 1515. CDXCIX.—To Peter, abbot of Cluny, and the monks of Cluny.—He accuses them of ingratitude and [Col. 1684] negligence because they did not restrain the monks of Gignac, who were violently hostile to the brethren of Mirat. 1517. D.—To Hugh [Humbert], archbishop of Lyons.—That, under threat of excommunication, he ensure restoration to the brethren of Mirat of the things taken by the people of Gignac. 1518. DI.—Privilege for the Church of Treviso. 1520. DII.—He grants privileges to the monastery of Fitero. 1522. DIII.—He confirms certain possessions of Heilsbronn monastery. 1522. DIV.—To Emperor Frederick.—He congratulates him on his election, hoping that he will complete the exaltation of the Church begun by Conrad. 1522. DV.—To Stephen, bishop of Metz.—That he compel Count Henry of Salm to restore the cell of Asmingia, which he had taken from the abbot of St Michael on the Moselle. 1523. DVI.—To Henry of Salm.—He orders him to restore to the abbot of St Michael the cell of Asmingia, which he had taken, or else be punished by canonical vengeance. 1524. DVII.—To the bishops of Metz, Verdun, and Toul.—He commands them to keep Count Rainald of Bar from harassing the church of St Michael and to compel him, under penalty of ecclesiastical censure, to restore what was taken. 1524. DVIII.—Privilege for the Church of Trier. 1525. DIX.—Privilege for Hemmerode monastery. 1527. DX.—Privilege for Wadegozing monastery. 1529. DXI.—Privilege for Springiersbach abbey. 1532. DXII.—Bull by which the controversy formerly conducted before the bishop of Reggio by the abbess of the Brescian monastery of St Julia against the bishop of Cremona concerning the church of Cicognara is finally settled. 1533. DXIII.—Confirmation of the advocacy of the abbey of Niederaltaich, transferred from the Empire to the bishop of Bamberg. 1536. DXIV.—To Henry, bishop of Autun.—That, when summoned, he attend Bishop G[odefrey] of Langres to render account concerning the losses inflicted upon Vézelay monastery. 1537. DXV.—Bull for St John at Sens. 1538. DXVI.—To all the faithful. 1539. DXVII.—Rescript to Silvester, abbot-elect of the monastery of St Augustine at Canterbury. 1539. DXVIII.—To Theobald, archbishop of Canterbury, that he consecrate [Silvester], abbot-elect of the monastery of St Augustine. 1540. DXIX.—To the convent of St Augustine at Canterbury.—That they obey Abbot Silvester, even if the archbishop should refuse to consecrate him. 1540. DXX.—To Moses, archbishop of Ravenna.—That he treat the bishop of Piacenza kindly. 1541. DXXI.—To the Cistercians.—Confirmation of constitutions. 1541. DXXII.—To the chapter of Magdeburg.—That they not favour the bishop of Zeitz, invader of the Church of Magdeburg. 1543. DXXIII.—To the bishops of Germany.—He disapproves the transfer of the bishop of Zeitz to the archbishopric of Magdeburg. 1544. DXXIV.—To Abbot Wibald.—He commends to him the case of A. [Adelgot], bishop of Chur, and asks him to defend ecclesiastical immunities against laymen. 1545. DXXV.—Bull for the canonical church of Blessed Mary at Fano. 1546. DXXVI.—Bull for the monastery of St John in the valley of Tura (near Toggia). 1548. DXXVII.—To Raymond, master of the Hospital of Jerusalem. 1550. DXXVIII.—To Odo, duke of Burgundy, and the Burgundian nobles.—That the burghers of Vézelay be regarded as excommunicated. 1550. DXXIX.—To Hugh, archbishop of Sens; G. [Godfrey] of Langres; T. [Theobald] of Paris; and Henry, bishop of Troyes.—That the burghers of Vézelay be regarded as excommunicated. 1551. DXXX.—Privilege concerning all the properties of the monastery of St Mary at Bozavy. 1551. DXXXI.—To [Peter], abbot of Cluny.—That he grant the monastery of Silviniac to the exiled abbot of Vézelay. 1552. DXXXII.—To Arnold, archbishop of Narbonne.—That he restrain the bishop of Maguelonne and Peter of Verona, hostile to the Cluniacs living near Montpellier. 1553. DXXXIII.—Privilege against the archdeacons of Paris, for the authority of the bishop. 1554. [Col. 1685] DXXXIV.—To Raymond of Maguelonne and Adelbert of Nîmes. 1555. DXXXV.—Privilege for the monastery of Saints Lawrence and Hilary. 1555. DXXXVI.—Bull for the Church of Constance. 1557. DXXXVII.—To the clergy and people of Toledo.—That the Mozarabs obey the archbishop of Toledo and not differ from him in ceremonies. 1559. DXXXVIII.—He receives into apostolic protection the church of St Rumbold at Mechelen, formerly collegiate and now metropolitan, with all its possessions and tithes. 1559. DXXXIX.—He confirms the possessions and privileges of the abbey of St Cornelius at Ninove and receives it into the protection of the apostolic see. 1561. DXL.—Privilege for the church of St Lawrence at Genoa. 1562. DXLI.—To Villanus, archbishop of Pisa. 1563. DXLII.—To the archpriest of the title of St Mark. 1564. DXLIII.—To Ardition, subdeacon of the Roman Church, and Master Omnibonus. 1564. DXLIV.—To Aesculapius, priest. 1564. DXLV.—To all the clergy.—Concerning robbers and violators of churches, and when, after penance has been performed, ecclesiastical burial must be denied unless they give security for restitution of the damage. 1564. DXLVI.—Concerning witnesses to be employed in a case of separation because of closeness of kinship. 1565. DXLVII.—He decides the dispute between Theobald, bishop of Paris, and the canons of St Geneviève concerning the parish of the church of St John. 1565. DXLVIII.—To Abbot Bertold and the brethren of the cell of Würzburg. 1566. DXLIX.—He reproves Hugh, archbishop of Vienne, because he inflicts injuries upon the Cistercian and Cluniac brethren. 1567. DL.—To John, bishop of Padua.—Concerning usury. 1567. DLI.—Privilege for the monastery of St Silvester on Monte Suave. 1567. DLII.—To the bishop of Langres.—That he judge those who communicated with the excommunicated people of Vézelay. 1568. DLIII.—Privilege for the church of St Mary at Capenberg. 1568. DLIV.—At the intercession of Rainald of Dassel, provost, he confirms Ringelheim abbey to the church of Hildesheim. 1570. DLV.—To Peter, archbishop of Bourges.—He commands him to restore to the monastery of St Denis the church of Mont-Major and the goods of a deceased priest, wrongfully taken. 1571. DLVI.—Bull for the convent of the Holy Saviour at Évreux. 1572. DLVII.—To Henry, bishop of Autun.—He rebukes him because he is hostile to the monastery of Vézelay. 1575. DLVIII.—Privilege for the Church of Arras. 1575. DLIX.—He exhorts the canons of Arras to safeguard ecclesiastical offices. 1578. DLX.—To the clergy and people of Arras.—He declares that he approves beforehand the sentence which their bishop shall pronounce against heretics of his diocese, and decrees that they too must obey it. 1579. DLXI.—To the nuns of Digne.—He announces that he has entrusted their reform to the bishop of Arras. 1580. DLXII.—To the people of Douai.—That they render due obedience to the bishop of Arras. 1580. DLXIII.—He exhorts Theodoric, count of Flanders, to restore to Godescalc, bishop of Arras, the men of the town of Marœuil. 1581. DLXIV.—To Sibylla, countess of Flanders.—That she dissuade her husband, the count, from injuries against Godescalc, bishop of Arras. 1582. DLXV.—To Samson, archbishop of Reims.—That he withdraw Theodoric, count of Flanders, from inflicting losses upon the bishopric of Arras; and, if he does not desist, punish him and his land. 1583. DLXVI.—To Guerric, abbot of St Vaast.—He exhorts him to obey Godescalc, bishop of Arras, and to pay ten solidi for Botelgeria. 1583. DLXVII.—At the request of Bishop Herman, he takes the Church of Verden under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. 1584. DLXVIII.—To Abbot Wibald.—He commends to him his ambassadors sent to Emperor Frederick. 1584. DLXIX.—To Bernard, archbishop of Tarragona.—He again commands him [Col. 1686] to obey the archbishop of Toledo. 1584. DLXX–DLXXI.—To John, archbishop of Toledo.—He confirms the primacy of Toledo. 1585. DLXXII.—To the bishops of Spain.—That they obey the archbishop of Toledo as their primate. 1586. DLXXIII.—He undertakes the protection of Elwangen monastery and confirms its privileges and possessions. 1587. DLXXIV.—To Hu., dean, and the canons of Toul.—That a canon of St Deodatus, who, overcome by illness and not in possession of himself, made a promise of “religious life,” not be compelled to fulfil that pledge. 1587. DLXXV.—Privilege for Cantav monastery. 1587. DLXXVI.—Privilege for the monastery of Vallis Bona, granted in precisely the same words, on the same day and in the same year, as the one above. 1588. DLXXVII.—To the canons of St Peter’s, Rome.—Concerning the fourth part of offerings granted to them. 1588. DLXXVIII.—Bull by which the monastery of Sarlat, founded by the princes Pippin and Charles, is received under the protection of St Peter. 1591. DLXXIX.—To the abbots of St Pontius and Crass.—That they observe the decree of Urban II at the Council of Clermont. 1593. DLXXX.—To the monks of the archbishopric of Narbonne.—That they observe the decree of Urban II at the Council of Clermont. 1594. DLXXXI.—Privilege for the church of St Mary at Asti. 1594. DLXXXII.—Privilege for the convent of Othmarsheim. 1597. DLXXXIII.—He grants by emphyteusis to Count Vincione of Montumano the fourth part of the Rocca of Trani, which that count had given to the Roman Church. 1599. DLXXXIV.—Privilege for the monastery of Tournus. 1600. DLXXXV.—Privilege for Conques abbey. 1601. DLXXXVI.—Privilege for the monastery of St Benedict of the rock of Mount Laterone. 1603. DLXXXVII.—Privilege for the Camaldolese congregation. 1604. DLXXXVIII.—To Bernard, archbishop of Tarragona.—That he acknowledge the primacy of Toledo. 1605. DLXXXIX.—To John, archbishop of Toledo.—He informs him what he has written to Bernard, archbishop of Tarragona. 1606. DXC.—He confirms the spurious diploma which King Conrad III is said to have granted to the Church of Utrecht. 1607. DXCI.—He confirms the goods and privileges of Hillesleben monastery. 1609. DXCII.—Bull confirming the Premonstratensian institute at Rott and the possessions of that monastery. 1611. **LETTERS OF VARIOUS PERSONS TO POPE EUGENIUS.** 1613. **LETTER I.**—From Emperor Conrad to Eugenius.—He requests confirmation of the election, in his absence and despite his reluctance, of Abbot Wibald to the abbacy of Corvey, and of the union of Keminada and Visbika with Corvey monastery. 1613. **LETTER II.**—From Eberhard, bishop of Bamberg, to Eugenius. 1615. **LETTER III.**—From Emperor Conrad to Eugenius.—He informs him that his son Henry has been elected king of the Romans by the common acclamation of the princes, and that he himself, having taken the cross, is preparing for the Jerusalem expedition.—He complains of Henry, archbishop of Mainz. 1616. **LETTER IV.**—From Hugh, archbishop of Rouen, to Eugenius.—He asks the pope to uphold the liberty of the monastery of Vézelay. 1617. **LETTER V.**—From Henry, king of the Romans, to Eugenius.—He excuses the archbishop of Mainz for not having attended the Council of Reims, and commends him to the pope as he sets out for him.
commended. 1618

**EPISTLE VI.**—Of the same [writer] to the same [recipient].—He implores the pope’s protection. 1619

**EPISTLE VII.**—Of the same to the same.—[He asks] that he receive graciously Henry, archbishop of Mainz, and the others going to the pope; absolve the duchess of Poland from excommunication; and hold Abbot Wibald in his favor. 1619

**EPISTLE VIII.**—Of Henry, duke of Saxony, to Eugenius.—He extols the merits of Wibald, abbot of Stavelot, and asks that the pope ratify the union of Kaminada with the monastery of Corbie. 1621

**EPISTLE IX.**—Of Henry, count of Namur, to Eugenius.—[He declares] himself ready to observe the measures ordained at Trier in the pope’s court concerning the case pending between himself and the archdeacon of Verdun. 1622

**EPISTLE X.**—Of Emperor Conrad to Eugenius.—[He asks] that he deign to confer the provostship of Xanten upon his chaplain Thiebald, canonically elected. 1623

**EPISTLE XI.**—Of the same to the same.—He writes on behalf of Thiebald, provost of Xanten, and of the cleric Otto. 1623

**EPISTLE XII.**—Of the same to the same.—[He asks] that he receive Arnold, archbishop of Cologne, graciously and send him back restored to his see. 1625

**EPISTLE XIII.**—Of the same to the same.—He commends to him the bishop of Regensburg, who is making his way to Jerusalem. 1625

**EPISTLE XIV.**—Of the same to the same.—He sends envoys to him and asks that Eilulf, abbot of the monastery of Murbach, be confirmed by him, and that the cleric Otto be absolved. 1626

**EPISTLE XV.**—Of the same to the same.—He commends to him Peter, archbishop of Capua, through whose assistance he had recovered his health. 1627

**EPISTLE XVI.**—Of the same to the same.—He sends to him as envoy Master Henry, notary of his court. 1628

**EPISTLE XVII.**—Of Baldwin, bishop of Noyon, to Eugenius.—He recounts how, amid troubles and reproaches, he introduced religious monks into the Church of Compiègne in place of canons of scandalous life. 1628

**EPISTLE XVIII.**—Of Emperor Conrad to Pope Eugenius.—[He asks] that he confirm the election of Hermann, bishop of Utrecht, and absolve the count of Are from excommunication. 1630

**EPISTLE XIX.**—Of Henry, bishop of Liège, to Eugenius.—He requests confirmation of the election of Arnold, archbishop of Cologne. 1631

[Col. 1688]

**EPISTLE XX.**—Of the Church of Cologne to Eugenius.—Concerning the election as archbishop of Cologne of Arnold, provost of the greater church of St. Peter. 1632

**EPISTLE XXI.**—Of Emperor Conrad to Eugenius.—Concerning the election of Arnold, archbishop of Cologne, which he requests be confirmed. 1634

**EPISTLE XXII.**—Of the same to the same.—He states that he is preparing an Italian expedition for the benefit of the Church, and commends the archbishop of Bremen and Abbot Wibald. 1635

**EPISTLE XXIII.**—Of Emperor Frederick I to Eugenius.—He informs the pope of his election and coronation. 1636

**EPISTLE XXIV.**—Agreement of Emperor Frederick I with Pope Eugenius III. 1638

**EPISTLE XXV.**—Letter of Cardinals Bernard and Gregory to Eugenius.—They commend to him the bearer of this letter. 1640

**EPISTLE XXVI.**—Of Robert, bishop of Exeter, to Eugenius.—Against Hugh de Cotes, who had abandoned the order of Regular Canons. 1640
ULGERIUS, BISHOP OF ANGERS.

Report for the Monastery of Roten. 1649  
Letters. 1655  
Ulgerius’s Testament. 1655

OGERIUS, ABBOT OF LUCEDIO.

Notice. 1657

ARNULF OF BOERIES.
